Libertarian Institute

click here

title: Parasitism
text:
The Communists (now I mean the officially recognized and declared ones) decided to be bombers to the end and came to the House with an old hit - the anti-parasitism law, yes indeed! It hasn't been here for a long time. The chairman, Comrade Filip, justifies it as follows: "This is a simple amendment to the Criminal Code, which introduces a new criminal offense that responds to a serious problem in society." Politicians from other parliamentary parties (led by Kalousek) laughed at him. And you know what's the saddest part? That Philip is consistent and logically right; unlike those who laugh at him. separation of the state from the social security system

title: The state recorded BTC
text: The state has noticed that there are cryptocurrencies; and reacted classically in his own way - the first regulation regarding their purchase and sale. Exchange offices and other service providers that can be paid for with virtual currencies (there are over 80 places in Prague, where you can buy food, accommodation, school fees or veterinary treatment with bitcoins) are now obliged to find out the identity of those with whom they trade in cryptocurrencies. The next planned step is to make the buyer (!) responsible for VAT if he bought in cryptocurrency and the seller did not pay the tax. Bitcoin and other virtual currencies are, of course, a pain in the ass for the tax office, because they can be used to easily mask a financial trace and the state no longer has all the property of its subjects in the palm of its hand; and the more popular these currencies become, the more they will become resisted. So let's get ready to present Bitcoin as the currency of child porn traffickers and the like; we will still enjoy it.

title: Attack in Quebec
text:
Although most of the recent terrorists profess Islam, this time a (literal) Islamo-killer attacked – he shot up a mosque in Quebec, Canada; it shows the quite unsurprising truth (which Breivik also showed some time ago) that a terrorist does not have to be a Muslim (although the lying president claims the opposite and many idiots repeat it after him). Most people just aren't totally deranged dorks who would be satisfied with shooting innocents, but every now and then there is a flawed piece like that; he then looks for all sorts of convenient excuses to do it - and Islam is one of them. But those who do not have Islam can do otherwise; someone attacks an abortion clinic, another sets fire to a police car, another throws a Molotov cocktail at a baby, finding an enemy is so easy when you have it in your head and you're hungry for blood... and whoever doesn't even have enough invention to create an ideological enemy, he just shoots up a school... or a pub.
The stupid thing is that, like the Islamobites, they tend to be ecstatic about every Muslim attack and many are almost happy about it, mainly because it supports their worldview, now one can observe again in the camp of the sun-lovers the association of terrorists with DJ Trump and Marine Le Pen, whom the person admired; yes, this terrorist was anti-immigrant and shot up a mosque, but neither Trump nor Le Pen are really responsible for that (and I say that, even though I loathe both of them). Responsibility for actions rests with the one who commits them; when someone presents me with evidence that DJ Trump helped him with this, I will be the first to condemn him, but the reality is that he probably didn't even know the young man, so it's hard to blame him for looking up to the fool in him. Dangerous rogues were, are and will be; luckily there aren't many, but there are a few, so let's put up with it, be ready to defend ourselves, but let's not make up nonsense and limit freedom in their name.

title: School funding
text:
Until now, Czech schools were financed according to the number of students; however, the deputies voted that from September the money would be distributed according to the lessons learned (by the way, the presentation of the law was accompanied by hysteria, which included topics such as the tradition of humanism, the genocide of the Indians, European values, the Thirty Years' War, the atrocities of Christianity, the harmfulness of multicults and chocolate - the papalists took it from the ground). What will this change bring? Does anyone know? No. Everyone has an opinion, but real results are unpredictable; it can help and harm, probably one way for some and another that way. The declared goal is to help rural schools with few pupils, which will probably happen, but if costs are maintained, quite logically at the expense of schools with a large number of students (extra money for small schools will be missing somewhere). The question, of course, is: Is it desirable? And the answer? Unfortunately, no one can even know this; and what's worse, we won't even know in the future.
the only way
how to find out what is desirable
, consists in leaving people a free choice - let everyone decide which school to go to (and if to school at all; we also have
unschooling
) wants to send his child and how much he wants to pay for it; until we leave these things to the free market, where everyone can best decide how they want their resources to be used, we are completely blind, unable to perform an effective economic calculation. Not to mention that funding is one of the smallest problems in the case of education; the state education system primarily deforms our children through indoctrination, exposes them to massive pro-state propaganda and instills in them from an early age the feeling that
submission to imposed authority is desirable
. If someone wants to educate in an authoritarian way, that's basically their business, but let them do it through the schools
he doesn't even expose the children of the rest of us
.

title: Police harassment first hand
text:
With her friend Teresa, who you may know from
our videos

However, I generally do not talk to the police, I do not pay them anything, I do not sign and I want to go to administrative proceedings; that didn't smell good to them, so there was the usual buzz - all kinds of drug tests with a long wait (all negative), mandatory equipment check (okay). At this point the average monkey capitulates and withdraws; however, I had to deal with some kind of aggressor who started yelling at me, violating my personal zone and behaving rudely, which also happens sometimes and is solved by recording (you have the right to do that by law), which is why bengas usually start behaving decently on camera. recording here
).
Although the laws give the uniformed monkeys enormous power, there are ways to fight back a little; recording is one of them - if you are dealing with an official, make a recording. The problem arises when, on the one hand, the bitch enjoys the benefits that the law gives her, but on the other hand, she has no problem breaking the same law (for example, by banning recording); then suddenly you find yourself in a situation where you are being bullied by someone who you cannot realistically resist. For even if you overcame him on the spot, you will go grumbling; and if you want to avoid that, you have to let yourself like everything... I wouldn't wish that feeling on anyone. title: Twenty-two years since the death of Murray Newton Rothbard
text: Today is exactly twenty-two years since one of the greatest thinkers, economists, philosophers and geniuses - Murray Newton Rothbard, the "father of anarcho-capitalism" left this world at the age of 69; his life's work was a consistent and logical introduction to the consequences of two trends that were seemingly not very related: anarchism and the Austrian school of economics. Anarchists were often wrong in economics, and the proponents of the Austrian school of economics did not apply their (correct) conclusions to the state; Murray Newton Rothbard corrected both and came to a brilliant conclusion: "Capitalism is the fullest expression of anarchism, and anarchism is the fullest expression of capitalism. Not only are they compatible, but you can't really have one without the other. True anarchism will be capitalism, and true capitalism will be anarchism." This knowledge and full understanding of it changed my life greatly; Thank you, Mr. Rothbard.

title: Go elsewhere!
text:
I have a hospital not far from where I live; this hospital is famous for how bad it is, not to mention the personal experiences of my loved ones suggest that (visibly drunk doctors and such). Fortunately, I personally rarely use the services of doctors, but recently I found myself in a condition (poisoning) where a visit to the hospital was necessary; for obvious reasons, my girlfriend drove me about 30 kilometers to a better hospital (which is almost every one). It took the doctors about eight hours to fix me, so there were quite a few medical staff around me; however, without exception, their first question after looking at the card was not about my health, but about why I'm not in the hospital where I live (I don't think they always ask, but this time they couldn't catch up). Each time, I was told that not like this, and they wrote (with exclamation marks) in my discharge papers that I should go to the place of residence for the inspection.
Can you imagine this in a private company? Can you imagine employees who reproachfully ask customers why they didn't go to a competitor? Understandably difficult; entrepreneurs are passionate about customers, they fight for them, they try to please them, and when they have a lot of them, they do everything to keep them. Hospital
in our socialist healthcare system
however, they do not have this motivation; the boys represent nothing but the current and the necessity to do something. I believe that the repeated calls for me to go to the competition vividly illustrate and symbolize something much deeper, the whole attitude is reflected in them; if you tell a businessman that his competition has disappointed you, you go to him, he will typically be happy, but a socialist thinks differently. And now consider what pervades the effort to discourage customers; unfortunately, it's not the doctors' fault, they act rationally, the whole state juggernaut that more or less forces them to act like that is faulty.

title: Unfreedom or status quo?
text:
In my efforts to show people the benefits of a free society and the inherent evil that lies in states as such, I mainly come across propaganda and indoctrination on the subject of "the state is necessary", where this firmly rooted thesis often completely overwhelms any logical arguments, which are then swept off the table a priori; however, there is also the popular and ubiquitous "it wouldn't work" argument, which I have mentioned many times before and would now like to discuss in a little more detail.
Before I get into that, I can't help but mention one observation I've made over the years of debates about freedom: Against the general distrust of people in freedom in the real world stands a fairly significant confidence in the freedom of the Internet in the virtual world by the same people. Did you notice that? When politicians come up with regulations outside the Internet, they are often supported in activities that limit freedom of expression (and not only that); however, when it comes to Internet censorship, most people are far more sensitive. Why do you think this is so?
One explanation occurred to me - while the real world is so over-regulated that no one can even imagine it without regulations, the Internet is currently quite free and everyone can see that there is no doom and things work even without a central authority. The amount of regulation outside the Internet has exceeded all limits, so that people have been forced to integrate it into their lives, which the majority of the population can no longer imagine well enough without them; rather, it requires a huge amount of imagination and the necessity to accept the fact that the outcome cannot even be predicted well enough, because the free market is unpredictable, so the most daring ideas will be just one of many hypothetical versions of the future.
In connection with this, an urgent question arises: How much do people fundamentally reject freedom and how much change as a result of state propaganda? In an unfree world, these two things can merge - the one who is an enemy of change can appear to be an opponent of freedom, which of course also applies vice versa. What role does fear of the unknown play? Everyone can see that a free Internet does not mean the end of civilization; however, many are convinced that a stateless society would bring about the end of civilization. Do you think that if these people were able to imagine some alternatives, that would change their attitudes?

title: Murray Christmas 2016!
text:
So, year after year has come together again and we have Christmas here; holidays that almost everyone celebrates, they like them in their own way, but at the same time they also very often curse them (complaints about consumerism, haste, hecticness, etc.). I personally - as a Christian and an anarcho-capitalist - love Christmas because I appreciate the spiritual and material aspects of these holidays; and I always, without exception, enjoy them as much as possible without stress. How to do it? Well, I'm spending the holidays with my family and loved ones, and we're discussing what "should" be done for Christmas; no one is forced into anything. Whoever wants to go get a tree, it will happen; whoever wants to bake cookies, bakes; whoever wants to cook dinner will cook; whoever wants to buy gifts, will buy them; most of it is usually done by someone... and what does no one do? We just don't have that this year; but we always meet, everyone is happy, loving and loved. I can only recommend it xD
Even this year, I don't want to forget to give (us) libertarians an example in the field of PR: Christmas was apparently originally a pagan holiday, which Christians managed to turn into a day when we commemorate the birth of the Lord Jesus, whom the Lord sent to this world to redeem us from sin through the suffering he had to undergo for our sins - at least that's what I believe and I am extremely grateful to him for this help on the way to salvation; regardless of what you believe, isn't such an act fascinating? And now I am not talking about the sacrifice of Jesus, but about changing the meaning of pagan holidays to Christmas despite the fact that all the interesting astronomical phenomena around the year zero that could be the Bethlehem comet, whether it was 1P/Halley or not, did not take place in winter; that's something like changing Czech Statehood Day to Tax Abolition Day... and there's still a long way to go.
I also like the "consumer" part of Christmas - tinsel, debauchery, good food and other pastimes; moreover, during them there is a huge amount of voluntary exchange, which symbolizes capitalism. Of course, the great thing about it is the volunteering; don't you want to participate in Christmas consumption? So just don't do it. Instead, you can play for example

title: The spirit of freedom
text:
I thank the libertarian Robert Higgs for the inspiration to write this text.
Dear readers, have you ever heard or used any of the following arguments?
1/ Look around you, there is a state in every society; Do you know of one that isn't there?
2/ The state is a thousand-year-old institution, it has existed since time immemorial; if it's so bad, why aren't stateless societies emerging?
3/ Without states, people would behave like animals, be dangerous and unable to take care of themselves; they need their rulers!
4/ Without states, economic collapse would occur; the economy stands and falls by laws.
5/ The abolition of states would cost great bloodshed; then they would still spawn again at the cost of more blood.
6/ Free people in various parts of the world are even worse off than the citizens of our state; and they should be happy for what they have.
7/ Conditions in the States may improve; rather than abolishing states, let's try to reform them.
8/ A world without states is nothing but a utopia; it can never work, which is clear to all but a few naive fools.
Let's go back in time a few hundred years and look at a few arguments against the abolition of slavery:
1/ Look around you, there is slavery in every society; Do you know of one that isn't there?
2/ Slavery is a thousand-year-old institution, it has existed since time immemorial; if it's so bad, why don't neo-slave societies emerge?
3/ Slaves would behave like animals without their masters, would be dangerous and unable to take care of themselves; they need their slavers!
4/ Without slavery there would be an economic collapse; the economy stands and falls with slavery.
5/ The abolition of slavery would cost great bloodshed; then it would still spawn again at the cost of more blood.
6/ Free people in different parts of the world are even worse off than our slaves; and they should be happy for what they have.
7/ The conditions of slaves may improve; rather than the abolition of slavery, let us try to improve their living conditions.
8/ A world without slavers is nothing but a utopia; it can never work, which is clear to all but a few naive fools.
These are real arguments of real people (A. Lincoln, G. Washington, T. Jefferson, G. Fitzhugh, T. Carlyle and many others).
How "strong" does the first eight arguments appear compared to the second? And how many more years will pass before people find them just as absurd?

title: Benga and fast driving
text:
If you drive more slowly, you have more time to react to the situation around you; this is definitely true if you are going that way by your own decision. But what if you are forced to do so under the threat of a fine? An Australian study led by Dr. Vanessa Bowden shows that volunteering matters here too; eighty-four drivers (who did not know what was being tested on them) were allowed to drive in a simulator where they had to drive through places with a speed limit of 50 km/h - while they knew once that they would be fined for exceeding the limit by 1 km/h, the second time by 6 km/h and finally by 11 km/h. Result? Well, the more restrictive limits forced the driver to watch the speedometer more and less of the surroundings, ergo they were demonstrably more likely to overlook what was happening around them; and what's the use of a shorter braking distance if you can't see that you have to brake? However, the uniformed monkeys don't care; their job is to collect dashes for fines...
The order was clear: He must not pass at any cost!

title: What definitely wouldn't work?
text:
The focus of most debates on anarchy tends to be a discussion of what could or could not function without state power; anarcho-capitalists try to predict (although they themselves admit that it is impossible to say with certainty) how the free market could theoretically replace individual functions of the state, while statists bring various objections as to why this would not actually be possible. However, I believe that the world (and the free market) works in a much more fascinating way than anyone could ever imagine (including anarchists who are aware of it); I would like to give two examples here.
Let's imagine that there was a law according to which a policeman would have to be present in every restaurant to make sure that someone does not run away without paying, or refuses to pay after a meal; how would statists defend such a law? Well, they'd probably argue that if it wasn't there, everyone would definitely be abusing it, doom would ensue and all the restaurants would go out of business; the guests would leave in droves without paying, after the meal they would pretend that they didn't have money, or they wouldn't take it with them on purpose - and then what would the poor waiters do about it? And now anarchists, hand on heart: How many of you would invent some complex construct, how the market would solve this "problem"? I certainly do; I would argue, for example, that restaurants could require a deposit from unknown customers, while only regulars would pay after the meal. Still... realistically, it's simply not necessary; except for exceptional excesses, it works even without any special measures.
Now suppose the Internet were not anonymous; anyone's online activity would be publicly traceable to their true identity. E-shops would definitely start using something like this to verify the identity of their customers. How would statists defend this? Here they would most likely come up with the fact that an e-shop simply cannot work on the anonymous Internet, because anyone could order goods on delivery in a foreign name, shops would be spammed with orders and would have to start demanding payment in advance; but then again everyone would start setting up fake e-shops en masse, cashing money, but never sending the goods. So it would be "clear to everyone" that no one would simply ever sell or buy anything on the anonymous Internet, because users would not be able to trust each other; and now - in the world of the non-anonymous Internet - try to refute those statists (or e-shop owners)!
I believe that many of the problems for which we are currently struggling to imagine how they might be solved without the state actually have far more straightforward and incredible solutions than we would ever imagine.

title: State versus landowners
text:
The agrarian lobby is trying to push through a law that would prevent the owners of farmed agricultural land from freely disposing of their property; specifically, the person who rents it should first have the right of pre-emption to such land, then the state, and only then the owner could sell it to whoever he wants. If such a law were to actually pass, it would be a huge intrusion into the property rights of many people; after all, they own the land, so they should also be able to use it as they see fit, perhaps sell it to anyone, not be
forced by force
favor certain buyers in the name
further protection of Czech farmers
. The owner will be harmed by this law, as he will not be able to sell his property to whoever he wants (typically to the highest bidder; instead, he must prefer a worse buyer for him); so let's sound the alarm, spread the word, and make it harder for the lobbyists to inform as many people as possible of their disgusting intentions.

title: No reincarnation?
text: Did you know that the Chinese government has been regulating reincarnation for several years? I didn't until recently; and when this news reached me I couldn't believe it, however after about an hour of googling it appeared to me that this is most likely the case. In China there is a "State Administration for Religious Affairs" (which is terrible enough in itself) without whose permission reincarnation is prohibited; or rather, if a monk wants to find out who he was in a past life, before meditation and all those religious procedures, he must first fill out a form, go to the office and wait for approval, otherwise he is acting illegally. The substance of the law will probably be the buzz of the Tibetans, because reincarnation is important to their culture; nevertheless, this is one of the most absurd laws I have come across so far (next to, for example, Iowa, where kisses longer than five minutes are prohibited, or North Carolina, where the only legal sexual position was missionary).

title: The town of Cherán
text:
In the Mexican state of Michoacán lies the town of Cherán, which has about thirteen thousand inhabitants; these residents are characterized by the fact that they definitely have balls (although most of them are women xD), which they proved in 2011 when they kicked out the mafia from their town, however, they really took it from the ground up, because it was not only the illegal mafia in the form of drug cartels, but also the local politicians and police - they simply drove them out of the town by force. Political parties were abolished, each of the city's four districts now elects its representative to the city council. The city is now protected from outside invaders by a militia made up of townspeople who originally didn't even know how to hold a gun, but now can defend themselves against both legal and illegal criminals; even internal security is (almost) ensured by the residents themselves - petty criminals are fined or forced to serve time for misdemeanors, while those who commit something serious are handed over to the central government.
Crime in Cherán has dropped significantly since then; for example, there has been no murder or kidnapping there in the last year, which would not be unusual for a town of 13,000 people, but in Michoacán (where there are not even four and a half million inhabitants) over a thousand people are murdered every year (in the entire Czech Republic with ten million people, we don't even have a fifth of their murders, so we don't even kill ourselves a tenth as often), so according to the average there, statistically, Cherán should also happen every year there have been several murders (and there used to be). I don't claim that they have it directly in Cherán
anarchy
, after all, they still cooperate to a certain extent with Michoacán, however, with the expulsion of the representatives of state power, more peace, tranquility and order came to the city than there had ever been before; so there is only one question left - what do you think, if it came down to it, would the people of Cheran even be able to build roads?

title: Fidgeting for 300 megs
text: Deputies are discussing an amendment to the law, according to which the military intelligence should receive three hundred megabytes for spoofing Czech citizens, but what's worse, one more nice power: All telephone operators and Internet providers would be obliged to allow the Military Secret Service to put their devices working on the man-in-the-middle principle on their lines, which in practice means that the state will have access to all electronic communications of all citizens who pay for it.
