title: Heroes of Parallel Polis
text:
Ludwig von Mises' motto was: "Tu ne cede malis sed contra audentior ito."
This translates to: "Do not retreat from evil, but fight against it even more courageously."
I am deeply convinced that the greatest sources of evil in the present world are states; it is difficult to fight them, because they are powerful monopolies of violence with amazing PR and persistent propaganda. Nevertheless, there are people who, for various reasons, wage their battles with them in many ways: gray economy, civil disobedience, spreading enlightenment and breaking myths, but also trying to change the state from within... whatever I think about the individual methods of struggle, I am grateful to everyone who does something against the state. However, few will stand up to him directly...
...and that's why I call the libertarians of the Parallel Polis heroes; those in question have defied state coercion through the EET, a disgusting and immoral system designed to make the state's plundering of citizens more efficient, and which is defended by the absurd rhetoric that whoever refuses to be robbed by the state is himself a thief, and
they told Babiš their NO
: "Parallel Polis does not accept and will never accede to EET rules." They simply won't record their sales electronically; they don't hide behind anything, they don't hide anything, they have declared it publicly and they simply refuse to bow down to a stronger tyrant. How will the state react to this? I'm a little afraid that I own the way; however, the question is how long it will take... but before that happens, you have a chance
in Holešovice to go for coffee and dessert or something to eat for bitcoins
(if you don't have them, you can buy them on the spot) without your purchase being registered by the Ministry of Finance. >

title: Mother Dating Son - Public Matters
text:
Thirty-six-year-old Monica Mares, who is the biological mother of nineteen-year-old Caleb Peterson, found herself passionately loving her son like a woman to a man; he reciprocates her feelings, so they start dating. Well, it's weird, but their thing; unfortunately, this view is not shared by the courts in New Mexico, where they both live. In addition to the fact that the state has banned Monica from contact with all (!) of her children, both lovers are in danger of going to bed; however, they want to be together despite the oppression and are determined to find a new home somewhere where they won't be persecuted for their relationship... this shows the meaning they probably have for the incest
punish - who does it help?
Absolutely no one, they don't plan to break up because of it anyway, besides, they don't hurt anyone with the relationship; and their prison will have to be paid for by the taxpayers on top of everything, not to mention the destruction of that family whose mother was taken away by the state.
It does not surprise me how many people are able to condemn such a thing, for I understand that they find it disgusting; however, I find it remarkable how few of them say, "I'm sick of it, so I don't wish them well," but try to rationalize this feeling with arguments like, "It's unacceptable, because if they have a retarded child, the taxpayers will pay for it." Well... yes, that's true, but if this were the real reason, then those in question would also have to be supporters of banning sex for anyone with a genetically transmitted disease; if they aren't, then obviously it's for them
not a sufficient reason
and they want to ban incest for other reasons. Personally, I find the whole thing to be absolutely disgusting state intervention and destruction of people's lives, who have not been guilty of anything other than loving each other; although the relationship between the two is highly non-standard and deviant, I wish them good luck, understanding from the environment and peace from the state.

title: Urza in Polis: The state is immoral
text:
A fortnight ago I you all
invited to Parallel Polis
to his lecture - and above all the subsequent discussion - Fr
anarcho-capitalism
; since D-day has arrived, I remind you of the invitation again. And if you have someone around you who is perhaps not an anarcho-capitalist or libertarian, but whom you think might be interested in why the state is a bad servant but a bad master, bring them along.
Today's lecture is entitled "The State is Immoral"; it will be about the ethical aspects of the state's existence.
And I cordially invite everyone to the next lecture in two weeks (December 14 at 8 p.m.), where we will look at how anarchy is related to the Austrian school of economics.
I'm looking forward to seeing you tonight at 8 p.m
Parallel Polis
.

title: "Exceptional" condition
text:
In November 2015, terrorists attacked in Paris
; the French government then declared a "state of emergency", meaning a (theoretically temporary) police state. We were able to convince ourselves of the effectiveness of this measure
in July in Nice
; benga failed, a magora with a truck would probably be stopped by an armed populace, but the guns are bad (and therefore regulated), ugh. While the "state of emergency" continues to be extended (always by several months), French Prime Minister Manuel Valls has hinted that it will be extended again by several months in January 2017, because (I quote): "It is difficult to end the state of emergency now. Especially in a presidential campaign with meetings and public gatherings. We have to protect our democracy. The state of emergency allows arrests and searches, which is effective. So we will no doubt to live with this condition for a few more months.' And so freedom dies; who remembers what benjamin franklin said about exchanging liberty for security?

title: Babiš's brain processes
text: About a week before the launch of the first wave of EET, Babiš proposed unexpected changes: He wants to exempt e-shops and small entrepreneurs (natural persons with a flat tax and income up to a quarter of a million per year) from the obligation to record sales; as far as I'm concerned, the more people that are taken out the better, but an interesting question arises: Why is he doing this? He is said to have officially heard the proposals and blah blah blah blah; no, no one is perhaps naive enough to believe that. So why? Does he want the outcasts to be relieved and to like him? If so, why would he announce it until after they had already acquired the software? Or is he counting on the fact that his coalition partners will reject it and he will then be able to blame them ("I wanted to exclude e-shops, but Sobotka blocked it.")? Alternatively, Babiš has information that the system will not be able to handle it technically, and is trying to reduce its load so that it does not fall down? I don't know myself; and I'm happy to read every opinion in the discussion, because that is the main point of this text, so please contribute!

title: Murderous monkeys in uniform
text:
Two bengs from Pilsen, and I will name the pigs - Jan Pergl and Lukáš Zahradník, were sent in October 2012 to deal with a serious situation: A homeless man was knocking on the window of a hostel. When they arrived, he was no longer knocking, but the lawmen found him and beat him to death; what about the courts? The municipal court acquitted them, the regional court gave them eight years, the high court then four, and finally the supreme court six and a half years.
For many reasons
I consider imprisonment to be pointless, counterproductive, unfair (especially to those who pay for it) and stupid; however, leaving that aside, let's look at the amount of punishment and compare it to other murderers... but what about murderers, even Smetka got double for H-System! Well, either a homeless person is a subhuman in the eyes of the courts, or a uniformed monkey is a superhuman, or both. By the way, if
private arbitrator
tried a murder committed by his employee, anyone would call it a farce; why is it so cool on the part of the state?

title: Ritual burning of ivory
text:
The head of the royal zoo, Přemysl Rabas, will spend millions on bonfires; in 2014 he organized the ritual burning of horns in Dvór Králové, this year the boys (accompanied by Jan Stejskal, head of foreign projects) flew to Vietnam to fool around in the same way. Too bad they didn't read (or didn't understand)
my article, which I published on this topic back then
; then maybe they would know that by burning tusks and horns, this raw material becomes rarer, i.e. more expensive, thus increasing the motivation of poachers to hunt elephants and rhinos. In addition... if they sold them, in addition to the decrease in rarity (and therefore also the price, thus also the efforts of the poachers), they would get enough money to protect those animals (the Royal Court's potion cost a hundred mega at the time); not to mention poaching issues are best dealt with by option
private farms (without them, for example, bison would have died out long ago)
, which is also not allowed with protected species. However, mindless activism is unfortunately more popular than thinking.

title: Hole in EET
text:
EET needs no introduction, we all know this Babiš system of streamlining state robbery; however, as part of my work, I had the opportunity to get to know it in detail, as I implement the interface into our customers' system, through which they will send receipts. In addition to the technical aspect of EET directly radiating as it is a state project, it also has holes; what kind? So, firstly, it does not limit transactions "without a receipt" in any way; where the receipt is present, it is not a good idea to falsify it, because EET has a bonus system where everyone will be able to verify the receipt and then punish the merchant. Yes, that's exactly how Babiš imagines "justice", people will beat each other up; after all, what else can you expect from agent Bureš 007... in addition to this, of course, massive propaganda creates an underworld for swindlers so that they can excuse the inexcusable by saying that they are actually doing a good thing (because those who don't let themselves be robbed are actually stealing... and so on).
But what is no less interesting? The transaction for EET is defined by: TIN, establishment ID*, cash register ID*, receipt ID*, amount and time (items with an asterisk are generated by the merchant himself); and now let's imagine that in some hypothetical pub or hotel, it happens by chance that more things start to be sold for the same price (lunch menu, room...), or the items are divided into receipts in such a way that, by coincidence, more receipts with the same amount start to appear at the same time, and just like a monster, a regrettable mistake happens that several guests receive a receipt with identical identifiers... they have no chance to know and even if they check the validity of the receipts in the bonz system, it will tell everyone that it is OK. Wouldn't that be a disaster? In conclusion, I would like to add that I am only warning entrepreneurs about this potential mistake, so that they can beware of it and avoid it (if anyone doesn't understand it, get in touch, I'll be happy to explain); there is definitely no public incitement to break the law!

title: Liquidation of gaming rooms
text: The state regulates gambling, which the businessmen in the given field avoid in various ways, for example, they make their casinos officially private clubs and the like; however, the Ministry of Finance is after them like a chicken, recently it had a court cancel the Pilsen-Prague network of gambling houses with the funny name "Hrou pro stresu" and the official status of a private club. Some might say that eliminating gambling is beneficial, but this has two hooks, moral and practical (as usual): The moral is that it is offensive violence against free people by the state; and from a practical point of view it is dysfunctional as usual - the customer will ultimately pay the additional taxation, and limiting the number of gaming rooms only distorts the competitive environment, which is also paid for by the player, who, however, will not get rid of the addiction, he will only make money faster. Gambling addiction is stupid and bad, but the state is seriously not helping it.

title: Urza in Parallel Polis
text:
For many years (actually, it will be eight years already) I wrote a lot and personally did not visit libertarians that often; however, times change and I accepted the invitation from
Parallel Polis
, where every second Wednesday (starting on the thirtieth of November, i.e. exactly two weeks from now) I will talk (and then discuss with interested parties) about
anarcho-capitalism
. I will be very happy to see you all there; especially, of course, those who more or less vehemently disagree with my views so they can counter me (or at least quietly disagree and think if they don't feel like getting involved). If you have someone around you who may not be a libertarian, but might be interested in the topic, don't hesitate to bring them along; the more diverse the range of opinions among the discussants, the better.
I look forward to seeing you on November 30 at 8 p.m. in Paralelní Polis!

title: The government will close the pig factory in Lety
text:
More than a year ago I did
in Stoká wrote about a place in Lety
, where the concentration camp stood and today they have a piggery there; I am personally satisfied with the situation, because I like products from pigs - unlike concentrates - very much. There are people, however, who do not mind the pork there for pious reasons; I don't really share this view, but fine, we all have our priorities, I don't necessarily need the pork loin right there for my pork chops, actually I don't care at all. The shareholders, who already own pig farms, have a similar view on this, they also would not mind raising pigs elsewhere; such a situation clearly gives room to
voluntary exchange
: Let the people who are bothered by the pig farm in Lety, buy it from the shareholders and build a monument there, for example; great solution, but... but they would have to sacrifice something for that, which of course they don't want. So the government approved the proposal to force all of us (including, for example, me, who is comfortable with pork) to pay them.
Why is this wrong? Simply because the resources that need to be expended to move the piggery would benefit the people more if they were expended differently. How do I know? Well, very simply - it follows from the very fact that people did not voluntarily agree to buy back the pork; by that
demonstrated their preferences
the necessary resources should be used differently, for something that will bring them more benefit. There is no way to "measure" whether it is better to have a monument in Lety or to spend the money in another way, because the benefit from both is subjective; but this can be ascertained quite easily by letting free men act: If they voluntarily spend enough money on the monument, then it means that it is more beneficial to them; otherwise, it is not and should remain pork. This choice has already taken place and people have clearly demonstrated their preference not to spend on moving the piggy bank; then came the government and
forced them to waste resources
and do it anyway.

title: Rebirth of Mithras
text: Mithra is a very old god, so old in fact that he was a celebrity almost two thousand years ago; back then, people worshiped him and built temples for him (not always voluntarily) out of their precious resources. Now history is essentially repeating itself – the European Union subsidized the study of this god with a generous sum of twenty-seven million crowns; again, these are resources collected involuntarily (through taxation) under the threat of violence. And how were these precious resources handled? What was the output of the project? What benefits did we get for our money? Tereza Fojtová, spokesperson for Masaryk University, which received the grant, said: "The biggest success was the publication in the prestigious journal Nature about why people were afraid of gods." And judge for yourself - could you have bought something better for that money? Well, blood does not flow from a stranger; and if someone spends money that doesn't belong to him, he doesn't have to think carefully about it... so why not try to restore the past glory to a long-forgotten god?

title: DJ Trump wins, PvČ aftermath
text:
DJ Trump won
big fight PvČ
, and the US has a new president; it's a horror, of course, but we can take solace in the fact that Hillary wouldn't be much better. What happens? When the shitstorm dies down and DJ Trump takes office, we'll find out which of his campaign promises he really meant; I'm afraid we'll see him renege on issues like tax cuts while he revels in the protectionism he promises. Time will also show what his supporters, who glorified him before the election and made him a hero who would bring freedom, hope and "finally a change for the better" really wanted; it is more than evident that DJ Trump will not provide any of this... the question remains whether or not he will be a disappointment to his fans; I hope so, because the opposite would mean that they were not so much about freedom, but mainly about protectionism, which is probably the only thing their candidate will be able to push through.
It is also worth noting all those articles praising DJ Trump as a savior, savior, change and fighter against the establishment, which sound absolutely absurd, which is why when someone points it out and brings some counter-arguments, their authors or promoters suddenly switch from "the divine Trump" (which I criticized) to the "lesser evil" (which I do not agree with, but I understand); another logical bomb is the voices that are now celebrating the victory of a man from the people and an outsider, because a billionaire with connections to politicians and money for a massive campaign, he is a typical underdog without a chance, who won only thanks to God's providence and the alert mind of the American people (who elected Obama four years ago, which often made the same people crazy), something like Babiš in our country (many point to the similarity with Zemanem, but note that Babiš fits much better). Well, let's hope DJ Trump hits us as little as possible.

title: Cunt versus pee
text: Americans have a big day today - the presidential election; unlike the Czech presidential election, where there was absolutely nothing to choose from, in the US there is at least one candidate that I can imagine I would vote for, and that is Gary Johnson. However, the person in question does not stand a chance, and a real fight "cunt versus pee" will take place between a disgusting socialist and a totalitarian populist; and where is the lesser evil? Hillary is a classic statist, DJ Trump something like an American Babe; both have the remarkable quality, in my opinion, that if elected (and unfortunately one of them will), the United States will have the worst president ever (not that Obama is much better). What do I say to that? I would probably mind Hillary's victory a little less, DJ Trump disgusts me far more as a human being (not the rioting, but the evil totalitarianism); I fully understand the opposite opinion, but the articles that glorify one of the candidates creep up my neck.

title: The Prague municipality broke its teeth
text:
We were able to meet some time ago
read bad news in Stoké
about how the pigs from the Prague municipality liquidate Uber drivers; now I bring good news - the municipality lost the court case with the first Uber driver. The effort was to make the person in question lose fifteen thousand crowns for illegal taxi driving; However, the Municipal Court in Prague canceled this fine, stating that Uber is not a taxi service, but a paid carpooling service (on the grounds that, by law, a taxi service is for everyone, while Uber only provides services to a narrow circle of people who have installed the mobile application). I congratulate the driver and welcome the court's decision; worse, however, is that in the justification of the judgment, one can read, among other things, that the use of the Uber mobile application was not prohibited by any legal regulation - let's hope that no one will take this as a guide. For this time, however, the municipality got away with it; I hope (although I don't really believe) that this is the end of the Uber drivers' rant.

title: No sleeping in the car
text:
There is some kind of honking law that mandates truck drivers a forty-five hour break every week; in belgium they have upgraded this nonsense to a state where drivers are fined if they decide to spend this time in the truck. And to make matters worse, the French and Belgian governments have agreed on a common course of action where they are trying to push through the EU a regulation according to which drivers should not even spend this break in a hotel; the aim is apparently to send the concerned 'homes'. This is typical protectionism, the senselessness of which
wrote Claude Frédéric Bastiat almost two centuries ago
, but who would bother reading when they have the force of the state on their side in the form of an armed police fist; in the light of such measures, it seems paradoxical and absurd to talk about how we need the European Union for the sake of an open market, when its own bureaucracy only binds the market and does everything to distort it.

title: Pumpkins laugh at patriots
text:
Yesterday was All Souls Day, Halloween two days earlier; and the Internet is full of pseudo-patriotic articles and thoughts about "our All Souls" and "that American holiday of Halloween", which we should not let the All Souls "squeeze out". A typical response to this is the objection that Halloween is actually a Celtic holiday and All Souls' Day is not originally "ours"; however, as it happens, the defenders of traditions are very often those who do not bother to find out anything about them, the main thing is to defend something "ours". Personally, All Souls is stolen from me, and so would Halloween, but I really like those smiling pumpkins, so I'm a fan of that Celtic holiday; on the other hand, I fully understand that some people prefer Dušičky (and others like both for a change, others nothing). But I don't understand the constant talk about "our traditions" and how we shouldn't let others push them away... why not?
I fully understand that someone prefers All Souls, perhaps because they like visiting their relatives at their graves, or they just don't like Halloween (for example, those wonderful pumpkins); however, completely beyond my understanding lies the attitude that we should somehow "protect" the Souls just because they are "ours". In what way is "our" tradition better than "foreign" tradition? Personally, I don't think it matters; I like some customs, others don't interest me, but I definitely don't care what their roots are or whether they are traditional enough here. I always judge the thing itself, not its origin; anything Czech is (only because of its origin) any better than anything (perhaps) Slovak or German. Only patriots have a constant need to push "their own" everywhere, but above all to define themselves against "the foreign"; I find the "Halloween vs. All Souls" feud pointless and his
patriotic
downright absurd.

title: Chargers of all countries, unite!
text: I'm browsing the Internet like this when an advertisement from the European People's Party in the European Parliament suddenly jumps out at me: "Do you also mind that different brands of mobile phones use a different charger? Thanks to EU regulation, phone manufacturers sold in the EU will have to offer customers universal chargers that can be used for all smartphone brands from 2017. No more annoying searching for your charger and less electronic waste!" I don't want to completely solve why it's an absolute hogwash again, probably everyone understands that, but what's the point (!) of it now, when manufacturers have finally united in principle on USB chargers through the market? Besides, I can very well imagine how our reality will be presented when it becomes history: Each type of phone had a different charger when the EU came and finally unified it; what about the fact that the chargers first unified the market, so that the EU came and issued a meaningless bureaucratic regulation.

title: Archmage Babiš
text: You may have already heard Babiš shouting that the national debt fell for the first time under his government and that we are borrowing less than before; I admit that technically speaking this time (exceptionally) he is not lying. But if we look at the budget deficit, we will find that it is still bats like a cow; how is that possible you ask? Can Babiš do magic? Well, let the fact that, for example, in 2012, the national debt increased by (very roughly) two hundred billion crowns, while the deficit amounted to "only" about one hundred; yes, Babiš is such a financial magician, he can leave the borrowed money in the account for a few years, then use it and pretend that he is not in debt - well, tell me, who among us can do this? In addition, we have cash-pooling - the state has by law granted itself the option to simply dispose of the money of some (also non-state) institutions (for example, health insurance companies), which, although they must be returned, are not included in the state debt; so what do we say to Babiš about his debt reduction bullshit? "Shit!"

title: Let's celebrate violence with violence!
text: Today, October 28, the state declared a holiday to mark the day of the establishment of the independent Czechoslovak state; and how do we celebrate the creation of a state, that is, an organization based on coercion and robbery? Well, stylishly – with more violence, of course; politicians recently passed a law forcing big box stores to close on holidays. The Chamber of Commerce is protesting... um, against what? That against threats of violence from the state to those who do not close and refuse to pay fines for it? No; the complaint is aimed at the fact that the big ones close, while the small ones don't - or if it's terror, then for everyone! And people find it perfectly normal to discuss it, or even feel right to respect it; why is it that if I walk up to a shopkeeper and tell him to either close shop today or pay me a hefty fine or physically attack his property, everyone condemns that behavior, but when parliament does the exact same thing, it's okay? How can it be?

title: Babiš's whimper
text:
While I program connections to EET servers for a lot of money into various information systems (by the way, the interface is technically also... how could I say... state quality), Babiš travels around the Czech Republic and explains to people how EET will cost entrepreneurs almost nothing; the promotional tour is going great, according to his own words: "In Mikulov they even wanted to beat me up, elsewhere they shout at me. I try to explain everything to them; in some places they can explain it, in others they don't want to talk at all." Despite the "explanation", I would like to set the record straight:
That's how the state works
, that he takes most of the fruits of their labor from people under the threat of violence, from which Babiš, among other things, rakes a part; and he not only brazenly calls those who do not let themselves be robbed by the state thieves, but also comes with EET, which is not free and makes the state robberies (called taxes) even easier... no wonder this is hard to "explain".

title: Freedom of speech according to Pelikan
text:
We could meet in August
in Stoká to read about the pelican's roaring
, which gave rise to a draft law that was already approved in the first reading in the Chamber of Deputies - according to it, terrorism, its planning, financing, material support, cooperation with terrorists, as well as crimes resulting in the facilitation of a terrorist attack will be more severely punished; so be it... unless it would be Pelikán and his melody boys from ANO, so that they wouldn't push some more hogwash into it as a bonus, in this case up to twelve years imprisonment for the person who publicly approves of a terrorist attack (even if he has nothing to do with it), for example on a social network - you simply write a status on the topic that Osama was a fighter and he did it well (either because you are idiots, or maybe you are just joking) and off you go grumble - long live freedom of speech. Now we can only hope that the senate will throw it on their heads...

title: Inmate's Ministry of Truth
text:
The Minister of the Interior, Milan Chovanec, decided to become the Minister of Truth at the same time; he had a survey done (for our money) from which it came out that a quarter of people trust the "alternative media" more than the state media, and in addition, half of us hold "bad" (that is, different from Chovanec's) views on some war conflicts in the world. What about that? Well, if you don't have to pay for the propaganda yourself, there are plenty of options; So the inmate creates the SJJP (Special Unit of the Only Truth; which is not an official name, so I named it myself) in his ministry, whose task is to prevent the spread of "false or misleading" information and propaganda (that is, other than the most massive - the state one), because he says: "We have to set the rules so that people have the opportunity to find true information in a matter of minutes or a few hours."
And how does he want to achieve this? SJJP will have about twenty people (because we pay few officials), some of whom will be professional paid Internet trolls, because they will be tasked with refuting "bad" opinions on social networks and in comments wherever possible, the task of others will be to train civil servants in the "correct" truths, while the majority will be engaged in browsing the Internet and cracking (to the idiots, secret services and other state authorities) what they found there and did not like; after all, which state goon would be interested
freedom of speech
, when his own propaganda is in jeopardy? Incidentally, the entire SJJP is part of the new Counter-Terrorism Center; remember this if you ever think of applauding when the state fights against terrorism, immigrants, islam and everything - for the money they rob us of, they will also start censorship and paid trolling against us.

title: A ban on internal combustion engines?
text:
The Bundesrat (German federal government) is asking the European Union for regulation that would ban internal combustion engines across the board from 2030; German politicians are already trying hard to push electric cars through financial incentives to the companies that make them, but we can see the effect of this waste of money ourselves - how many cars with an alternative drive are driving on the roads around us? And what does not follow evil will follow even worse; when emission regulation and pointless subsidies are not enough, the ban kicks in. I do not think that it will be possible to establish it within fourteen years, but we can see where the will of the socialists is heading; of
my beloved Elise
I hope to become a veteran by then and not have to worry about it. At the end, I will add one more postscript for all environmentalists who are already excited about the idea, because electric cars emit almost no emissions - that is true, but someone has to produce the electricity somewhere... and solar panels and windmills will not cover that.

title: French plastics
text: The French government passed another law; all sellers and businesses will have to gradually reduce and by 2020 completely stop the sale, distribution and use of plastic bags and plastic dishes (cups, cutlery, plates, ...) unless they are made from biodegradable substances, which is of course significantly more expensive. So everyone will have to pay extra for (not only) beer in a cup and many other items; instead of people deciding for themselves what is a priority for them, whether to save money or not to leave indelible traces, the government ordered it for them, because of course the politicians know better (after all, they have the money for it - looted from the pockets of taxpayers - and no one else's blood flows). Also noteworthy is the fact pointed out by the secretary of the Pack2Go organization (representing packaging manufacturers): There is no evidence that biodegradable materials are more beneficial to the environment.

title: Electronic elections?
text:
In response to the low voter turnout in recent elections, there have been voices calling for electronic voting again, so that even people who do not want to go to the polls can vote; the most common objection I have noticed is the possibility of manipulation of such elections, when a person is not responsible for the crime and the like. In my opinion, this is not such a problem, because the phenomenon of someone forcing someone to vote will be minimal (not to mention that the entire state apparatus is about coercion, so this is not so contrary to the spirit of the state xD). That voter turnout would increase is probably true, which I consider (ceteris paribus) as an anarcho-capitalist to be bad, although it is not very clear what kind of increase would actually occur; from the available data it follows that more young people should then vote, which is generally considered an advantage, but I personally see no reason why a young voter should be any better than an old one.
Most e-voting promoters assume that the higher the turnout, the better; in my opinion, this assumption is nonsensical not only from the point of view of an anarchist, but also from the point of view of most of those people themselves, if only they would think about it a little more. The results of democracy do not depend on the quantity of the electorate, but on the quality (which I do not dispute that democracy will be crap anyway, but even crap can take different forms and measures); and what will happen to quality if we introduce electronic elections? A person who is not interested in politics needs dozens or hundreds of hours to make an informed decision about who to vote for (or not to vote for); those who don't vote because they don't want to spend ten minutes walking to the polls (which isn't a bad thing at all), certainly don't spend that much time getting information (which is fine) - but do we really want these people at the polls to throw in whoever's billboard they saw last?

title: State versus Doginni, Airbnb...
text:
Yesterday I got angry at here
by the Prague municipality's crackdown on Uber drivers
; however, due to the popularity of the Internet, there are many other similar services, such as Airbnb, where people can rent apartments to each other, or Doginni, where interested parties can let their dogs walk, or earn extra money by walking them. These are all services that no one is forcing anyone to use, and those who do are definitely benefiting from it (otherwise they wouldn't); however, the state cannot help but stick its greedy claws into it, demand protection money and bully decent people. In addition to trying to collect taxes, the officials here even ask for trade licenses for dog walking (this is again a genius invention xD); and the result? Well, Doginni is thinking about moving abroad, where the parasites won't bother them so much; good job bureaucrats, abolish the service, surely you will best benefit the people you are parasitizing on.

title: Crackdown on Uber; who is harmful
text:
Uber is familiar to just about every libertarian and many others; it is an application for smartphones, with which you can either offer someone a ride in a car for money, or order this service. Practically everyone can easily become a taxi driver without unnecessary paperwork (and taxes xD) and Uber also offers passengers various advantages compared to a standard taxi service, so its popularity is growing; understandably, this pisses off all sorts of state peeing regulators and other parasites, because it's hard for them to get a kick out of it. So a couple of goons from the Prague municipality started to spend a long time ordering Uber drivers, which they let drive them to Podolská Street, where shitty monkeys in uniform were already waiting for them; all those caught in the trap now face at least fines, some even worse, since none of them at least had a taxi driver's license.
Now seriously... how can anyone defend these mafia practices!? One wants to drive people for money, another wants to be driven somewhere for money, another writes an application for them; everyone is happy, no one is forcing anyone to use the services, so what the fuck is the problem!? A few uniformed monkeys and scumbags from the municipality, disgusting parasites living off protection money called taxes, simply decided in their "working" time to harm decent people who voluntarily exchange their services with each other; they defend it with some screwed-up customer protection, that one would be screwed - after all, whoever is interested in such protection does not need to use Uber at all! And now to the rotten lobby of classic taxi drivers, who are trying to ban it in every possible way; so damn, if you can't compete with it, start running it yourself and don't force people to use services they themselves consider inferior (if not, you can compete).

4,882,098 people (more than 65?%) did not come to the regional elections; this means that Babiš, the winner of the election, who received twenty-one percent of the votes of those who voted, was actually elected by only seven percent of all the people who could vote. What about the others? In the media (especially on the Internet) they are spoken of rather pejoratively; I have heard more than once that they "didn't bother" to come to the polls and are basically thought of as ignorant (especially some Islamophobic parties who constantly claimed to speak for ordinary people, unable to accept their mistake and defeat, so they insult non-voters). Of course, it is more convenient for politicians to declare that some ignorant people do not vote than to admit that many of those who do not vote are expressing their disapproval; it is difficult to estimate how many there will be in total, but in my area it is the overwhelming majority of non-voters (it is true, I am surrounded by libertarians xD).
Personally, I always choose - not that I think it is possible to fight my way to freedom, I completely agree with the opponents, but if I get an opportunity from the aggressor to improve my conditions a little, I will use it (I will discuss this in more detail
he wrote on the Mises
); moreover, I know a political party that can be used as a platform to spread libertarian views towards the public, so the more visible the better. I also vote because I don't think the following attitude is reasonable: "I don't vote to express my disapproval." Why? Well, if I want to express something, I should do it in such a way that my message is understood; and non-voters tend to be seen by the majority as ignorant, not informed dissenters. When a non-negligible part of the people will understand this message, I will also stop voting; for now, however, I'm just preparing the ground for it with, for example, this very text.

title: Marx and pensions
text:
Minister Marksová has become a celebrity in Stoké during her tenure; not even because of his name, but for
unbelievably
dull
or
dangerous
proposals
laws
... and the last one is also a delicacy. According to Marks, to make the pension system "fairer", the childless should pay more social insurance than people with children; at first glance it sounds quite logical, if a little monstrous - whoever raises more taxpayers should pay less. Such reasoning would perhaps even make some sense if social insurance had at least some characteristics of insurance (apart from the name) and was not simply just (another involuntary) tax; the amount of the social "insurance" payment does not depend on the risks or the amount of performance, but on the income of the person who pays it, which lacks any meaning from the point of view of any theoretical "justice" (especially because people with higher incomes statistically less often need the "performance" of that "insurance" from the state).
If we completely ignore the moral side of the matter, i.e. that the whole social insurance is legalized robbery, and we will assume that it is a legitimate system (which is not true by any chance, but let's assume it), then it is true that people with children "produce" additional payers, thus they actually "deserve" benefits, but according to this logic, when we are not dealing with needs, but merits, it makes exactly the same sense to benefit people with very above-average incomes, because they themselves (not perhaps once their children) contribute far more money to the system than most; to ensure "fairness" in such an inherently unfair system by disadvantaging the childless is about like ensuring "fairness" to bullied schoolchildren by padding classroom walls. So why does Marks do this? Well, either she's seriously that limited, or she's coughing up some justice and trying to score political points; I would almost like the second option more.

title: Without the EU, we would starve
text: Karel Schwarzenberg let himself be heard that our survival is only possible within the EU, without which we would (I quote) "starve", and states like the Czech Republic or Austria should (I quote again) "shouldn't rant" against the EU; the old man is solidly pearling and probably suffers from delusions, according to which European bureaucrats and politicians most likely feed entrepreneurs and their employees, who would starve without them, while completely ignoring who actually creates values and who is a parasite on them. That the insolence of politicians knows no bounds is not so surprising; the sad thing (although for me - unfortunately - less and less surprising) is that it doesn't even touch the majority of those who comment on that statement - they often curse the EU and Schwarzenberg because of migrants, but there was no storm similar to the one that followed when Mládek called entrepreneurs parasites, although what Schwarzenberg said basically means the same thing, he just cleverly covered it with statist rhetoric.

title: Pako Pavel Kočiš
text: Pathetic, your name is Pavel Kočiš (hereafter referred to as Pako)! At the age of seventeen, he wallpapered his room with eight hundred and ninety photographs and pictures of Václav Klaus, the then president; now, at the age of twenty-two, he has decorated his room with more than five thousand photos and pictures of Miloš Zeman for a change (and complains that he is slowly running out of space). But that's not all; Pako sends various gifts to his favorite presidents (candy boxes, pickles, hand-painted pictures and the like) and, like a true stalker, tries to get a job at the castle (unsuccessfully) and bombards his idols with letters. So far, he has earned the attention of Zeman's spokesman Ovčáček, who visits him to support his psychosis a little and get a piece of gossip; so the next time you hear about a secular state somewhere, don't forget that the harshest religion is statism - and whoever falls for it particularly badly, the priests from the president's office will come to praise it.

title: Generating Generals
text:
The actor Stropnický, at the time the Minister of Defense, probably likes watching porn from a military environment, because he came up with the idea of a special forces unit made up of all women; the first thing that came to my mind when i read this was "dude why!?" I mean, apart from porn. Not that I'm a principled opponent of women in the military - let everyone do what they want (although I'd prefer not to pay it, but neither do the guys), but why make a unit entirely female? What is it good for? And I find it especially bizarre at a time when the state spends a lot of money promoting gender correctness; why is it that a private company is not allowed by law to discriminate on the basis of sex, while the Secretary of Defense can build special forces modeled after Charlie's Angels for no relevant reason except, presumably, his masturbation fantasies?
Another invention similar to Stropnický's angels is also the minister's desire to have a woman in the rank of general; he confided his plan to the media with these words: "I believe that we will have our general in the foreseeable future. [...] I would like to make it before the elections next year." Seriously? I mean... sure seriously, he's a politician, so he naturally thinks like that; but that he still has the audacity to brag about it in the media and no one finds it strange? Would Stropnický "like to make it to the elections"? The Army now has four female colonels, which basically means the goal is to promote one of them within the year, so congratulations in advance to the future general on her new rank, which she qualified for primarily by virtue of having a vagina; and she didn't even have to use it. I probably shake my head the most at the fact that most people don't even think there is anything strange about how the state is opposed to discrimination based on gender, but intends to practice it on a more than huge scale.

title: Venezuela: EET, level grandmaster
text: Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro Moros has ushered in rigid socialism in his country; the results were not long in coming. Although there are rich deposits of oil in the territory of Venezuela, poverty reigns everywhere, because no one is able to extract it properly; the situation is so serious that the people there have been thirsty and hungry for a long time. Whenever the market comes up with a solution, Maduro does not hesitate to stop it; it's been about a year since the law limited the price of bottled water - and what a surprise, there was a shortage of it. Now people stand in line in front of supermarkets all night long; even that is already illegal. State militias are criss-crossing the country, arresting thousands and thousands of people en masse; for what So, for example, when someone is caught with food for which they do not have a receipt, or when someone sells food, or just stands in line overnight to get it; because, of course, the traffickers are to blame for everything, with whom it is necessary to turn around. Doesn't that sound familiar?

title: Washing dirty laundry in court
text: Once upon a time, a guy in Germany was deciding whether he was the biological father of his child about a year ago; there would probably be nothing so strange about that (although I personally believe that blood ties are overrated xD), but the person in question handled it like a demented person in court... and so this extremely important case went all the way to the Constitutional Court at the expense of the German taxpayers' money, which decided that there is no law according to which the mother should be obliged to state the names of her lovers - potential fathers, however, he would welcome such a law. Minister of Justice Heiko Maas immediately seized on this statement, proved his "usefulness" and rushed through the law; if it passes the House (and so far it looks like it might), it opens up another uncharted territory for the state to stick its nose into with taxpayers' money - a public matter: Who fucked who!?

title: State liquidation of companies
text: Babiš's Pelican of Justice wants to liquidate companies that do not deposit their financial statements in time in the Collection of Documents of the Public Register; such a company, according to Pelikan's bluster, should simply be abolished, deleted from the commercial register and trashed. Even now, a fine of up to one hundred thousand crowns is threatened for this, which, however, is a punishment that our fair minister of justice finds too lenient; it is better to simply cancel those companies (and people). And freedom of business? Well, that's good, but only to a certain extent; simply, the freedom of business ends where the will of the politician begins. The state can simply do whatever it wants, now including disrupting companies for not handing over some potentially sensitive information; How would people react if a private entity acted like that? That would be a blast; if it's because of a scumbag from the private sector, it's terrible, but it's something completely different from a scumbag in the service of the state.

title: By banning trucks for a better tomorrow
text: Prague councilors banned the entry of excessively large (that is, longer than twelve meters) trucks into Prague from the beginning of 2017; Minister of Transport Ťok justified this by saying that trucks do not belong in Prague, which, by the way, is a sentence with which every socialist or green jubilant idiot will enthusiastically agree. Why? Well, especially because they don't think about... for example, the fact that the trucks are not there to drive around, but to transport goods; and few will send a thirteen-meter truck to bring in one loaf of bread. So what will those who need to get so many goods to Prague, that they are now loading them into such large cars, do? Most likely, they will send more smaller ones, which will be more expensive as a result (and this will be reflected in the price of the goods), it will produce more stench and noise, and it will worsen the traffic situation; but otherwise bravo, comrades, good job, the world will be a slightly better place to live with this ban.

title: Regulation of leaflet printing
text:
The Slovak government once again threw the local entrepreneurs
another one
a stick under the feet; anyone who wants to print (advertising) flyers, brochures, business cards (!) or catalogs intended for customers becomes a manufacturer of unpackaged products and must register with the Ministry of the Environment (although this registration will require some paper for letters, envelopes, letterheads, but what wouldn't we do for nature). Unfortunately, it doesn't end there, because when the print actually happens, the person still has to pay protection money to a waste-recycling company; of course, not just any company, but one of the few that have a paper for this from the ministry. So, in reality, waste disposal will be paid twice – once by the person who gets rid of it, and the second time by the person who produced it. I wonder when the Czech politicians will come to something like this; for example, such a Babiš could certainly run one of those certified waste recycling companies.

title: Expensive paper? Let's ban buyout!
text:
Among other things, also as a result of the constant increase in the frequency of purchases via the Internet, the price of low-quality paper (cardboard boxes and the like) is increasing, as a result of which collection centers increase the purchase prices; there is more interest in paper, so people's motivation to recycle is growing, the world keeps turning and
the market is working great...
however, there are also non-leavers, who already take paper from containers for sorted waste and sell it, which the municipalities do not like, as they lose their profits from the sale. And the solution? Typically political – the Union of Towns and Municipalities of the Czech Republic (such an association of mayors) pressures the state to ban the purchase of paper (just as the purchase of iron was already restricted); Fortunately, the Ministry of the Environment rejected it. However, the fascinating thing is that someone was able to seriously come up with it; it's roughly the same as if someone stole my watch and I demanded that the state ban people (who had nothing to do with it) from selling watches.
By the way, how the rising price of paper motivates people to recycle shows one more interesting thing: Recycling as such is not automatically "right" (as some try to tell us; but it's not "bad" either), it simply has some benefits, but it also costs something (time, comfort, place...); but how do you determine if the benefits outweigh the costs? Everyone has to decide for themselves (no higher authority knows better), and the incentive to do so is increased by the market depending on how much is needed - higher paper consumption causes higher prices, which in turn increase people's motivation to sort and recycle. Of course, this issue includes a whole range of aspects – economic, ecological, social, logistical and so on; it is not possible to say unequivocally which of the above is actually more important, but it is possible to let people act and
not regulate the market
, which alone can provide acting individuals with the necessary inputs for their decisions.

title: Spy or Pay!
text: Fico enforced an absolutely crazy law in Slovakia: An entrepreneur to whom a supplier delivers a service performed by someone who works illegally will pay a fine of fifty-five thousand to five and a half million crowns; yes, you read that right - it's not at all a question of whether the recipient knew about it, because he becomes automatically guilty just because he didn't take enough care of his supplier. The quite interesting question is whether Slovak officials will enforce this law across the board, or only in the cases of selected individuals who will need to be eliminated for some reason; not that the result wasn't terrible either way. If we consider that to employ someone illegally means only to refuse to pay protection money to the state, we arrive at the fact that not even the mafias have the audacity to punish someone who takes services from someone who has not paid them; However, Fico is a flaming hammer of people's democratic justice that will happily crush any businessman.

title: Marine Le Pen's yarmulke
text: France's most famous Islamophobe, Marine Le Pen, had a fit of consistency in which she made it known that if Muslims are banned from headscarves and burkinis, logically yarmulkes should be banned as well; however, she did not carry her idea through to the very end, because then she would have to forbid Christians with crosses, Buddhists with dharma chakras and statists with flags (the paradox of the whole thing lies, among other things, in the fact that Le Pen herself is a member of the most brutal religion of today, which has taken it so far with propaganda that it is no longer even called a religion, even though it exhibits all its signs). Of course, banning symbols of Islam won't help anything, and their motivation could be expressed roughly like this: "We have to give it to those bastards." Stupid and primitive, but understandable. "People insist that we only ban Muslims, so let's ban something else," that already requires a significant amount of stupidity or malice.

title: Year Stock
text:
Today is exactly one year to the day
opening Stok
; I let my libertarian friends know about it at the time, so 152 of them (unique IP addresses) took a peek, only to have only a few dozen of them return in the following days. It took about a month or two for at least a hundred people a day to open Stoky; currently, their traffic is in the hundreds of unique IP addresses per day, sometimes over a thousand, almost never under five hundred. Although these numbers do not make Stok a wildly read website, I am very happy that hundreds of people read what I write every day; and it makes me no less happy that others took advantage of this opportunity at the same time as me, so that we now have twenty-one authors in Stoká.
My thanks go to all these authors; I will be happy for your next text. I also thank the debaters, whose ideas inspire further writing, and last but not least also the readers, especially those of them who spread libertarian ideas further into the world. Share xD
The purpose of Stok is to provoke discussions on libertarian topics under short and easily digestible texts, which may be inaccurate or incomplete in favor of brevity and easy readability; in a way, this is a "libertarian boulevard" - the goal is not theoretical and academic analyzes of the given topics, as these can come up in the discussion, or in an article that will be inspired by them. So the sewers are going in about the direction I intended; however, I am not satisfied with one thing: Although - as the creator of most of the content - I am a very positive person in life, the texts here are too often very negative, because they discuss politicians, socialism, restrictions on freedom and other unpleasant topics; in connection with this, I would like to ask all current and future authors to definitely not hesitate to come up with positive things that can be related to freedom, the market, capitalism and good news for example xD

title: Redistribution? Simply disproved in 150 words!
text:
A few days ago I had the opportunity to discuss with a socialist who defended redistribution with a sentence that I realized is at the beginning of most egalitarian ideas: "If you take from a really rich person such a small part of his property that it has almost no effect on him, and give it to a poor person, it will help him far more than it hurts the rich." People familiar with the Austrian school of economics see from the perspective that, with regard to the interpersonal incomparability of utility, the statement does not make sense; we could close the polemic with that, but not everyone has read (or will ever read) Mises, that's why I'm coming up with an argument understandable to anyone (although it's not a completely general argument and universally valid always and everywhere, it's enough for Europe of the twenty-first century).
If you claim that an extremely rich man should be forced to give his wealth to the poor
, because it will help them more than it will harm him, but at the same time you have, for example, designer clothes, a mobile phone, possibly a computer or a car or maybe even a house,
you are hypocrites
! If you really believed what you claim, you would have sold your belongings long ago and donated them to the starving poor in Africa or Asia,
because compared to them you are extremely rich people
- the personal property of most of those reading this text could save many lives; or perhaps you are not willing to sacrifice your comfort to save another's life!? Fine, me neither. But I don't want to hear a word about redistribution for the sake of greater benefit for the recipient. Never! And no buts!
Because it's either true, then donate everything but one set of clothes to charity and pay for the hostel, or it's not true
, so whoever said that should shut up, shuffle their feet, and be very careful not to preach any similar socialist crap next time.

title: Czech goods
text:
The President of the Agrarian Chamber, Miroslav Toman, made it known that he would like more protectionism - according to him, eighty percent of goods in Czech stores should be made up of Czech products; Sobotka also responded to it, according to which more Czech goods can be forced on the counters through stricter controls. Oh yeah. What does supporting Czech products mean for consumers? That instead of "the best" winning the free competition based on market mechanics (according to the customer's standards, be it quality, price, or any other indicators), "the Czech" is favored; as a result, this means that some worse alternatives of the best customer choice are forcibly artificially preferred over worse ones (if this were not the case, there would be no need to order anything and Czech goods would be found in supermarkets purely on the market).
For those who are interested in a more detailed justification of why the artificially forced preference for Czech (or any other) products ultimately harms the customer, I recommend the first parts of my
series about anarcho-capitalism
; For those who would prefer a very good analogy, I offer this one: Imagine that, for example, you, as a Pilsen resident, decided that you would only buy goods from Pilsen in order to "help your city" (or if, perhaps, Pilsen shops were obliged to offer eighty percent of Pilsen products); here it is suddenly obvious that your shopping will be greatly limited and you will find it harder to buy. The same applies to purchases of "Czech goods", only it will not be so drastic, the restrictions will be smaller, but still not zero. What about that? Personally, in the case when I choose between products, one of which is foreign and the other Czech, while the other parameters are the same for me, I take the foreign one, because I am trying to compensate for the purchases of patriots.

title: First day of school
text:
In primary and secondary schools, another school year starts today, first-year students are often excited, which is often due to the fact that they do not know what awaits them, while older children already do, which moderates their enthusiasm; I would like to take this opportunity to point out again something obvious, but which is often completely ignored: What is compulsory schooling? We've all gotten so used to it that most of us have developed Stockholm syndrome, so we tend to ignore the obvious fact that it's a violent ultimatum from the state that we either let our children be indoctrinated and taught as the state official sees fit, or they're kidnapped (by force if necessary) and eventually indoctrinated by the state; Does this claim seem too harsh and exaggerated? Well, on the factual side it is a simple description of the current state; on the emotional side it may seem absurd... why? Precisely because you also went through that indoctrination.
The school system serves not only to brainwash even the smallest children and spread state propaganda (every one of us is taught from a very young age that we need the state and that it is necessary, the police are good, and democracy is synonymous with good, without any discussion about it - just imagine the uproar if such massive advertising was forcefully imposed on children by some private entity), but also to inculcate conformity in our children and suppress their individuality (with this aim it was even designed a school system for the Prussian army; and we still use it, we just pretend that it is not the goal, many even believe it). Although this topic touches me very much, there is unfortunately not enough space in Stoky for its detailed analysis; I therefore allow myself to recommend it to the reader
another text I wrote about education
, or refer to
website of the "Freedom to learn" initiative
. I wish the students good luck then; and don't let yourself be shaped too much.

title: Marks has another idea
text:
Star Stok, my favorite Michaela Marksová,
whose
ideas
here
sometimes
I'm taking it apart
, comes with an amendment to the Labor Code, in which, in addition to clouds of other bullshit, I was interested in the protection of mothers after maternity leave (of course, protection from employers - how else); for example (but not only) they should be entitled (!) to the same job content as they performed before. For now, let's put aside the impracticality and buzz potential of this law and assume that it will actually have the desired effect; what happens then? Well, logically, the motivation of entrepreneurs to employ women will decrease a little more, because their "protection after maternity leave" costs something; the result will be another "problem" to solve for Marks - the inequality of men and women in the labor market. The person in question will then once again get the opportunity to be "useful" and invent another regulation that will "solve" the situation; that too will understandably have negative effects, so hooray – another opportunity for a “solution”!

title: EU wants to regulate messengers
text: The European Commission came up with another saving proposal - applications in which users chat (such as Skype and the like) should now be subject to the same rules (which in practice means regulations and restrictions) as telecommunications operators; this primarily means that their operators will be required by law to cooperate with the fizles and release sensitive data and conversation history of their users to them upon request. Officially, of course, it is the fight against terrorism, so any true Islamo-killer can applaud; unofficially, I would like to know whether this is another classic expansion of state power, or whether telephone operators have lobbied in an attempt to torment the competition a little (the technical solution of that cooperation with uniformed monkeys will cost something, especially for those applications that do not save the history of conversations on their servers). In any case, the result will be the same – yet another step towards unfreedom by the EU.

title: Hot topic: Burkini
text:
Some Muslim women have a problem with exposing themselves too much in public, so they choose to bathe in pajamas called burkinis; and some idiots have a problem with insufficient exposure of those concerned in public, that's why they decided to ban them from such bathing. Manure to the ground; so a perfect political topic - in France they already have decrees for it and uniformed monkeys enthusiastically booing scantily clad women. Islamobies rabidly applaud this because anything that is even remotely anti-Muslim is for a greater good - no matter how incredibly pointless bullshit it is; politicians have a harvest, because they can be "useful" once again - this time it's not just Le Pen, but the burkini ban is also supported by Valls and Sarkozy, because why not join the people, there are few boozers, they practically can't defend themselves and they won't find support in a democratic society.
I'm certainly not saying that there shouldn't be beaches where the owner bans the burkini, any more than I have anything against the existence of nudist beaches where the owner decides he doesn't want people in swimsuits there; such prohibitions are perfectly fine if the legitimate owner decides on them - let everyone decide on their own beach under what conditions and who can and cannot visit it, which, by the way, is the only reasonable way to solve the whole situation, or rather not to solve and create problems where there are none. Anything else means both the initiation of offensive violence, but also from a purely human point of view, it is nothing more than an outpouring of frustration; the various efforts to ban face coverings are at least excused by some wannabe security risk, while in the case of the burkini, there's really nothing close to a reason other than the good old desire to boo someone and poke their nose into nobody's business.

title: Endorsement of terrorism
text: Politicians need to define themselves harshly against terrorism, so the government proposed an amendment to the law, according to which approving a terrorist attack, even just by a status on a social network, should now be punishable by three to twelve years in prison; that's more than you can get for rape, by the way. This is certainly not to say that endorsing terrorism is not idiocy, on the other hand I am very much against initiating violence against someone just because they are an idiot; not to mention that putting people in jail is probably the dumbest form of punishment in itself. It is also remarkable how many constantly swear by freedom of speech, but when it comes down to it, they do not hesitate to persecute people for their opinion in the interest of hysteria; not to mention the fact that the real benefit of such a measure in the fight against terrorism is undoubtedly zero, perhaps slightly negative in the end.

title: Local minimum wage
text:
The European Commission (again and again) comes to save the world, again quite surprisingly with decrees, regulations and boozer laws, this time about the minimum wage (although now the promised paradise on earth will seriously come with them); what is it about Well, employees working abroad are supposed to receive the minimum wage (and be subject to other collective bargaining agreements) of the country where they work, not where they are employed; in practice, this means that drivers traveling through multiple states will have their minimum wage and other working conditions change during the trip, depending on what the unions have agreed upon. Good luck. I can completely see how it will not cause any problems and complications for anyone, whether it is the financial side of things, when companies from poorer countries will have to pay employees the minimum wage from richer countries, or the bureaucracy associated with the whole process of continuous changes to working conditions.
Fortunately, this whole genius idea is still only in the design stage, so there is a real chance that it might not be implemented; in any case, it is defended by typical protectionism - the protection of domestic employees so that foreigners do not "take their jobs". Claude Frédéric Bastiat already showed more than two hundred years ago that such an approach does not make sense, does not bring anything good and is only harmful; because customers always choose the services that suit them best in the market, so any state intervention that causes them to reconsider their choice means that instead of the best option, they were forced to settle for the second best. However, this quite obvious truth has been skilfully disguised by various socialists, so that no one really cares anymore; because it was replaced by annoying populist propaganda on the topic of protecting "ours" from "foreigners", regardless of the fact that in the end the customer... "ours" will pay for it anyway.

title: Sanity in Texas
text:
In Texas, someone had a bright idea...and lo and behold, suddenly people over the age of twenty-one are allowed to carry guns on college campuses; of course, a number of professors and other left-wing intellectuals, who predict bloodbaths and student massacres, railed against the law. This change is the second reasonable adjustment to the laws regulating firearms in Texas in recent times; you could talk about the first one
read in Stoky in June
. Now let's keep a close eye on the long-term trend of crime in this American state, how many people will die in college massacres in the coming years compared to the past, and what all these deregulations in the field of weapons will bring to the residents there; if it turns out (which I strongly believe) that the situation is improving, hopefully it will lead to further loosening of unnecessary - and not just gun - laws - not just in Texas.

title: Collective guilt versus logic
text:
Recently, the frequency of terrorist attacks in Europe has increased dramatically; most of them are quite undoubtedly Islamic radicals, and I find it ridiculous to suggest that their motivation has nothing to do with the religion they profess. Most recent terrorists are Muslims, the ratio of terrorists among Muslims is higher than among followers of any other faith, and of course we have no reliable way to distinguish someone who just privately believes in Allah and doesn't bother anyone with it, from someone who intends to use their faith as an excuse for sadistic murder; what about that
Before you answer this question, please consider the following: Since ancient times, everywhere in the world, not only in Europe, there has been a significant frequency of rape; most of them are undoubtedly men, and I find it ridiculous to suggest that the motivation for these acts has nothing to do with the sexuality of the perpetrators. title: Theory and practice
text:
Anarcho-capitalism is often the target of statist ridicule, according to which it is only a theory that cannot be put into practice; if you start talking in front of them about private courts or something similar to the police, they usually react by pointing out the fact that nowhere is the law handled completely privately, because the state can do it better and it "wouldn't work" at all.
The typical answers of anarcho-capitalists then mostly consist of a theoretical (and mostly absolutely correct) explanation of why and how it could work; however, any such speculations are often dismissed by simply pointing out that nothing of the sort is currently being implemented anywhere, resulting in a debate in which the libertarian defends something and the statist scoffs at it, automatically putting himself in a much more advantageous position.
As things really stand, I find this mode of debate quite absurd; why?
Well, in recent history we got a look at what a centrally controlled economy looks like - and it was appalling. We were also able to see in various states that any economic segment that any state allowed itself to leave to the market began to function better than before; on the contrary, it has probably never happened that the state stopped managing something, which would lead to the fulfillment of all those catastrophic statist predictions about market failure.
Imagine knowing two fundamentally different ways of solving problems; you first try to solve everything with one and it's not very good, then you start to solve individual things with the other and you always get better. Will you then try to maintain the status quo at all costs, or will you try for (further) improvement?
There are essentially two ways to control the course of things: Either let free people act, or have their lives centrally planned by force from the position of the state. So far, central planning has always failed; and each time it was replaced by free market principles, there were positive changes.
So what actually works and what fails? Who should question and who should defend? On whom should the burden of proof lie? So what is theory and what is practice?
The reality is that there are a huge number of industries where the state has failed across the board while the private sector has succeeded; on the contrary, there is probably no industry that thrives in private hands and only begins to flourish thanks to the state.
So based on what empirical experience can anyone claim about something that we need the state to do it because the free market "wouldn't work"?
In a rational discussion uninfluenced by state propaganda, the statist should, on the contrary, explain to the anarchist why this or that sector should be the rare exception that requires a central plan for its functioning.

title: EET options
text: Croatian Finance Minister Boris Lalovac boasted about how great EET they have there; the state can see how much money entrepreneurs have, how high sales, daily turnover and even what they buy with their money. The tax office watches it all and looks for anomalies, which he then eliminates; the Croatian Finance Minister even boasted that since they know absolutely everything about entrepreneurs (they say they also monitor the physical movement of cash registers, if it occurs), they can manage not only taxes, but even economic activities, i.e. the entire economy - and all this with the help of information obtained from EET. title: For safe roads
text:
Viktor Tolar, with thirty years of driving experience, lost his driver's license for more than a year, after which he had to take driving school again to get it back at all; why? In three years, he exceeded the speed limit three times in the Strahov Tunnel by less than twenty kilometers per hour, and four times he drove less than sixty in the fifty; add to that "he found it indecent to haggle with the police" and also the merging of the offenses for discussion, which effectively slows down the disappearance of points, and we're painted, well... in this case, scored. I can very vividly imagine all the comments about how stupid the person was acting; and I admit his approach wasn't exactly the height of prudence, on the other hand... is this really the point? Such laws are always defended with talk of safety, but when they are then used to bully, it is so often excused that the bullied did not defend themselves when they could; but do we really want it to be necessary?
In my opinion, the most important question is not at all what most people start to solve in connection with the issue, i.e. whether the revocation of the driver's license in the given case is in accordance with the law, whether any of the officials or police officers made a mistake, or how unwisely the victim of state bullying proceeded, but whether it is okay for the person in question to lose his driver's license for what he committed; and this is not just some anarchist view, here I am talking about the spirit of the law and the alleged reasons why it applies, which should be an argument for statists as well. The question is: On the basis that someone, after thirty years of driving, over the course of three years exceeded the speed limit three times by less than twenty kilometers per hour and four times by less than ten, can it be concluded that the person in question is socially dangerous as a driver and this problem will be solved by a year without a driver's license and driving school? If not, then it just shouldn't happen; regardless of "the law is the law" and the like.

The state took property from the church, which after many years was finally recognized as a mistake, as a result of which the decision was made to return the looted property; however, the state wants to take a part of this transaction by force (taxation of restitution), which it creatively justifies by collecting protection money from other transactions as well - this is the first degree of this insolence.
