The worst thing about the whole thing is that the absurdity of the whole thing does not occur to the person in question, because in her eyes robbery is not robbery if it is legislated, and whoever organizes the concert must not deny entry to anyone, because discrimination (it's bad, yes) and also "it's just not done".

title: Insolence beyond the grave
text:
Ever since the results of the referendum on the (non)remaining of Great Britain in the EU are known, political negotiation dances have begun on the topic of who needs mutual trade more, the British or the rest of Europe; there are various statements and speculations about what the EU will "enable" for British citizens in terms of trade, which is also related to various pro-Union arguments on the topic of how, thanks to the Union, we can move goods and people very freely. Nothing but shit, I tell you! The reality is that one gang of thugs from national governments has set up absolutely senseless barriers to free people to trade, while another – transnational – gang has changed them to make them a little more tolerable; then we have to pay all these robber clans under the threat of violence from our own resources in the form of protection money - called taxes.
So, the next time you hear from some moron in a tie, whose paycheck you're trying to parasitize, about how European officials will "allow" us to trade and how we need some bureaucrats and politicians to remove barriers to free trade, remember that there are naturally no such barriers here, because when two people want to exchange goods, they would just naturally do so; the reason why it sometimes presents a problem is definitely not the people, but the politicians, who already feel that they have the right to a commission from the trade that they did not deserve and are only complicating it, so the solution to such a situation is clearly simply to stop messing with it, but certainly not to establish another apparatus of exactly the same profiteers, which will mitigate the effects of what the first ones did, at the cost of clouds of bureaucracy and other regulations. The claim that these bureaucrats are "enabling" us to trade is absolute bullshit.

title: The EU is also against weapons in the Czech Republic
text:
As probably most readers are well aware, gun legislation in the Czech Republic is less terrible and disgusting than in most European countries; some even euphemistically describe this state of affairs by saying that we have good gun laws. I personally do not agree with such an assessment, because until weapons are sold without registration, permits, restrictions and in anonymity, this is repression and the initiation of violence by the state; pseudo-arguments based on catastrophic scenarios, that in such a case people would kill themselves en masse, do not stand up primarily because if people really wanted to kill themselves, they could do it without legally regulated firearms. No one, except a few deranged individuals, wants to risk their own life so that they can kill the people around them; but when such a person is found and acquires a weapon (which he can do even now, only more difficult), he does far more damage in an unarmed society than in an armed one.
To my considerable surprise, it seems that Czech politicians don't even have extremely pro-prohibition appetites regarding gun legislation (that is, compared to the politicians of other European countries); I have no doubt that if voices could be raised from it, opinions would be easily corrected, but so far this is not happening. However, where there is no fuss at the national level, the EU will push it; and it seems that it will be exactly the same with weapons: the new directive regulates weapons with magazines, revolvers with non-removable magazines less strictly; and although the Czech politicians are quite dismissive of this invention, it will probably not be of any use to them, as the other member states are playfully overriding them... in other words, exactly what the propagandists constantly told us before joining the EU will happen - we will lose absolutely basic freedoms from above.

title: Freedom of speech or not?
text:
The European Commission, together with Internet giants such as Google, Facebook and Twitter, published a code of conduct on the Internet, the aim of which is to prevent hate speech; if it was a voluntary action on the part of those companies, it is of course only their business how they handle their business and who they give space to express their opinions, but if it was coercion under the threat of sanctions from the European Union, it is
gross suppression of freedom of speech
. Since many do not see a very significant difference (in both cases it is censorship), I will explain it: If a private media owner censors his content, he is only deciding on something that is his (just as everyone decides who to let talk in their living room at home) and customers can reject it; if this censorship is carried out by the state, it is a violent intervention in someone else's property and typically global oppression, since the laws usually apply generally to everyone (that is, all the media, and competition does not work).
So the very fundamental question is: How did the negotiations between the European Commission and the aforementioned corporations take place? I can imagine the pressure, because in the past we have already been able to verify that the EU can throw legislative rubbish under the feet of even big giants; on the other hand, I wouldn't even be surprised if the management of those corporations was made up of indoctrinated people who simply accepted European propaganda as their own - after all, there are not a lot of such people in the world. I also wouldn't be shocked by a scenario where the European Commission would offer some benefits to those big players, but I don't think it's very likely; in such cases, the state typically offers to suppress competition, which is not very effective in the web environment, moreover, it does not bring political points, as people are quite adamant about restricting the freedom of the Internet. Which option do you think is the most likely, dear readers? Leave your opinions in the comments.

title: Smarter than the market?
text:
Although libertarians usually do not call for the expansion of the state's powers, in the case of closing borders to refugees, I see relatively many exceptions around me, justified approximately as follows: "If we had more freedom (the legal possibility to effectively defend our property, privately discriminate on the basis of religion, etc.), we could afford to let refugees into the territory of the Czech Republic; however, since we do not have these freedoms and, moreover, redistribution is raging, the state should close and guard the borders, possibly ban Islam.” What is pernicious about this thinking? Instead of calling for a reduction in the power of the state, we want to strengthen it so that the government can repair the damage it has caused through its regulations; this is a notorious statist trap that we can see everywhere - for example, the creation of the unemployed through increasing the price of labor (various employee protections, the minimum wage, etc.) and the subsequent "fight against unemployment" by further distorting the market.
Another logical flaw in this argument should be seen better than anyone else by libertarians; it is indeed possible (and I also assume it) that in a free society people would currently cope with the situation surrounding the immigration crisis by natural free market discrimination (whether at work, in the provision of services, or in closed communities, the possible form of which can be found in the works of Hans-Hermann Hoppe), but we cannot know for sure, because
the market would perhaps come up with a different solution
. So when we want the state to keep refugees outside the borders, we are actually predicting the behavior of free people in the sense of: "They would deal with immigrants one way or another, so let's simulate it with state interventions." In essence, it is like declaring that if there is likely to be some charity and solidarity in the free market, then state redistribution is perfectly fine, because it actually simulates these free market mechanisms.

For a limited time, there will initially be an exemption for menthol cigarettes; however, even these will disappear from the shelves over time. Since the law passed both houses of parliament very smoothly, I do not think that the situation can be expected to improve in the foreseeable future.
The purpose of this measure should, in theory, be to protect the health of the population, which is why absolutely barbaric interventions in our freedoms are so often excused lately. Many people object that the state should and must take care of the health of its citizens, because we have socialist health insurance, as a result of which one's health is another's business. However, such an argument should not be used to defend an even greater amount of state intervention, because its consistent application leads to complete absurdities, for example, that the state should decide on the diet of each of us with regard to his health; the only reasonable solution, of course, is to abolish forced health care cost-sharing once and for all and move smoothly to

title: You shouldn't steal, but...

However, even if they were indeed individuals already starving, approving their thefts sets a dangerous precedent; every homeless person can then get rid of some begging and just start stealing, if the court acquits him anyway. It can be assumed that if this practice grew to mass proportions, the courts would probably begin to decide differently, but it would be difficult to compensate for the damage that will occur in the meantime (starting with this small theft). title: Public transport in Blanca? Not by chance; people would go there!
text:
What does a market entity do when it finds an opportunity to satisfy the needs of a large number of people? He rejoices, grabs her by the scruff of the neck and earns. How will a public administration with a monopoly in a given industry react in the same situation? He starts looking for reasons not to do anything. How is that? Well, he'll get his money anyway (people will be forced to pay protection money), so why do the extra if there's no profit? It is quite logical that whoever gets more money the better he serves people has a great incentive to provide the best possible service; however, those who receive money regardless of what they actually do for others are mainly motivated to do as little as possible. Despite how obvious these principles are, masses of people can pretend they don't exist under the influence of state propaganda; I would therefore like to give an example from practice that clearly shows how things are.
Do you remember how, before the opening of Blanka, politicians promised that public transport would run there? Well, Blanka has been standing for some time and still nothing; Why not? The transport companies came up with a surprisingly honest rationale: If public transport buses started using the tunnel, these lines would become very popular and a huge number of people would want to ride them; but the operation of so many buses is simply too expensive, so as part of public transport savings, they will not run through Blanka. Yes, you read that right, public transport doesn't go through Blanka because it would just be too good. By consistently applying this logic, we end up canceling the most desirable lines and opening up some obscure ones that no one wants to ride; on the contrary, a consistent rejection of such an approach means a free market – entrepreneurs will be motivated to operate exactly those lines for which people are willing to pay, which are precisely those that
they cost less resources than they benefit

title: About attitudes towards refugees
text:
My opinion of immigrants is currently very "out"; because I think roughly this: "No one should force anyone to feed refugees. No one should prevent anyone from feeding refugees." As it happens, when I present some of my opinions in this sense (basically I always say the same thing - laissez faire, let everyone take care of themselves on their own and for their own, let others do the same and don't get involved on either side), everyone always chooses the part of it that irritates them (while some interpret it as alibi xenophobia, others as alibi treason) so that they can bash me over the head; neither side typically takes the napkins, as they - despite my futile protests - automatically classify me as their opponents, because I do not share a single opinion with them.
Why am I even writing about this? Lately, I've often seen various Islamoboes label public speaking out against refugees as heroic; as someone who constantly enjoys criticism from both sides, I can state that the opposite is the case (if we are talking about speech within the limits of the law; when the ideology police start dealing with it, the situation is reversed). If any public opinion on immigration approaches heroism, it is standing up for refugees; on the one hand, the overwhelming majority of the population holds a more or less opposite opinion, which increases the risk of conflict, but above all Islam killers are far more feared than sun worshippers. While the disapproval of the sunnies is typically manifested (either virtually or in person) by some chatter, the Islamobies can be much sharper (from their side I have been addressed with many insults and threats, virtually and in person, a few times bordering on physical insults).
I wouldn't like this text to sound like the sunnies are the good guys - they are the ones who typically use all kinds of subsidies, collaborate with the state and try to censor their opponents, which I consider much more rubbish. I'm only talking about the courage needed to express one or another opinion: With my (anti-state) opinions, I usually annoy both sun worshipers and Islam killers; and I know from my own experience that the latter is worse. The point of this treatise is to point out that speaking out against refugees in public is not brave (unless you break the law) because most people will applaud anyway; on the other hand, expressing yourself in the opposite spirit is far from such fun and you have to reckon with the consequences.

title: Are you a good taxi driver? This will be assessed by the official.
text:
Liberec businessman Pavel Svoboda has a problem - although he found fifteen people who wanted to work as taxi drivers for his company, not one of them received a permit from the authorities, because none of them passed the topography exam; even Mr. Svoboda signed up for the exam himself, because he couldn't do it - and he also flew out. Where is the buried dog? Well, there are errors in the test, so the correct answers are evaluated as wrong (and this is not a word game, for example, an adept taxi driver is given the task of listing all the streets that cross another; and the only "correct" answer is to include a parallel road that does not cross it). So Pavel Svoboda asked the municipality to cancel this absurd test, but the answer was: "Conducting the test is the only option established by law to ensure qualified drivers offering taxi services." So the one who answers the questions wrongly is qualified.
We can, of course, speculate whether the errors in the test were caused by clerical shenanigans, or were there on purpose so that the only way to pass the test was to buy the "correct" answers from someone at the municipality; in any case, the biggest screw-up in the whole thing is the very fact that there is any mandatory quality control of taxi drivers by the bureaucracy. The whole idea is completely wrong, because the only person who would do such a thing is the customer, since the clerk simply cannot know what is important to whom - how important is it for the driver to be nice? Handsome? Verbose? Silent? Cheap? Familiar with geography? Who else but the customer can decide how important it is for him whether the taxi driver knows the city by heart or follows the GPS? Of course, the biggest crap lies in state coercion, when a group of people force some individuals to provide their services to others only under certain conditions.

text:

Interestingly, the public mostly takes it and finds it reasonable, even prudent; and I ask all those people: How much of your time, money and land have you already invested in figuring out procedures for what to do when a large part of your family suddenly dies? Absolutely nothing, I suppose; because you feel sorry for wasting precious resources on preparing for scenarios that may occur with minimal probability. But neither they nor the officials do it for free (in addition, those places can be used in other ways).
This is another rather widespread paradox: Public administration often wastes resources on preventing all sorts of unlikely disasters, and people accept it with gratitude only because they do not see the resources it cost as their own; typically, none of those who praise officials for foresight willingly deprive themselves of their own funds to insure themselves against such eventualities. And it's not just about disasters, in general "planning ahead" (mainly in the field of ecology) is perceived as positive, because people intuitively feel that it happens for free; if such planning were really worth the resources used for them, they would do it for themselves, on their own and for themselves, which typically does not happen. Because everyone intuitively solves the costs of sacrificed opportunities in his life, but as soon as it comes to public affairs, he ceases to perceive them; after all, we took something away from those (state) schools.

title: Warning for drivers: There is no roundabout like a roundabout!
text:
Ťok and his minions from the Ministry of Transport, be it again
they eat hell
, or just the comrades made a mistake and did not think much when writing other laws, in any case the result is the same, once again something
redefined
: The classic roundabout, as we know it, must from now on be mandatorily marked with both a roundabout sign and "Give way", which is quite OK; the problem is that now the law also allows a "roundabout" that doesn't have "Give way", which is why in that case approaching cars have priority over those circling - in other words, the right-of-way normally applies there, which would apply even if there were no signs at all (so their function is only to confuse the enemy - the driver - to give the impression of a classic roundabout). I don't know if the goal was to cause more accidents, to collect more fines, or if the law was simply written by some demented person, in any case, watch out!

title: News from Liberland
text:
I assume all Stok readers know what Liberland is; whoever doesn't, let them google this libertarian mini-state founded by Vít Jedlička. Although the president of Liberland has still not managed to convince the other states (especially Croatia, which Liberland has surrounded with a wall and arrests its citizens) to recognize Liberland's sovereignty, the first company was registered in the new state, which, by the way, undertook to pay voluntary taxes; another novelty is that Liberland already has its own currency called Merit, which in my opinion is a bit unluckily tied to the US dollar. Whatever my reservations about Víto Jedlička's steps (and I have a few), I'm happy for his activities - although I don't really believe that the Liberland project could be successful, but even if it wasn't,
means a huge promotion of libertarianism
in the Czech Republic and abroad; and if he happens to succeed, more than a tax haven will be created. What do you think?

title: Hundred year weather forecast
text:
According to a new study by the University of Oxford (!) climate change may cause a shortage of fruit and vegetables by 2050, resulting in hundreds of thousands of people dying from cancer and cardiovascular disease; crop-devastating heat waves, which so far occur about once every hundred years, could (!) occur every four years from 2100. What to say to that? Well, according to Urza's new study, the Klingons may (!) arrive tomorrow; not that I've seen their ships anywhere, but the Oxford scientists can't even predict what the weather will be like in a month, but they know what it'll be like in a hundred years? Well, how can (!) it be, which is not too different from my prediction of the Klingons. Are you arguing that weather forecasting is different than climate change? So be it. Show me someone who flawlessly predicts climate trends (heat waves, harsh winters, droughts, rains...) ten years in advance; until then, I refuse to take seriously those who predict heat in 2100.
Not to mention that if it was just fortune telling itself, I have nothing against it, I don't mind card readers either (although I don't believe in them); however, the problem lies in the fact that the charlatan predicts the future cheaper (and to the customer who voluntarily paid for it, not from money stolen by the state), but above all in the fact that the consequences of various climate studies are devastating even for those who do not want to have anything to do with it, however, governments create various laws and regulations on the basis of climate fortune telling, which on the one hand cost crazy money and on the other hand have no effect at best, at worst lead to social engineering and the buzzing of citizens. And when time proves the charlatan's mistake? Never mind, another "expert" will be found; just look at the case of global warming - when it turned out that the top "scientists" were manipulating the data, the fight against global warming was renamed the fight against climate change, and it goes on.

title: The state is me
text: To amuse himself, the ruler invited actors to the city to perform a play; however, he didn't like her, so in the middle of the performance he sent a maid right into the middle of the ongoing performance, who ended it - the actors leave humiliated, the audience disperses, the ruler shows his displeasure. A scene from a fantasy or historical book? Not; Slovakia, Brezno, 2016. Starring Marián Kotleba, the mayor of the Banská Bystrica Region, and Marianna Kemková, an official from the Department of Education; normally on fair play: "End the game or we'll have the curtain drawn." And as she said, it happened. Is there anything else that needs to be added? In my opinion, not.

title: Babiš, ruler of the virtual world
text:
Together, ANO and ČSSD are pushing another law through parliament (and sweeping all amendments off the table), which will give Babiš even more power; specifically, the Treasury Department should have the legislative power to block any website. And the reason? Combating illegal gambling on the Internet; not that such a fight isn't already a huge piece of crap in itself, however this upgrade is that the decision as to whether a given site is illegal gambling is made by Treasury officials whose word will be the law, ergo this means in practice the possibility of unlimited virtual censorship. Therefore, when a Babiš website messes up, it will simply be cut; that "he couldn't get away with it"? But come on! A stork's nest? It's a completely obvious scam, from which everyone just gets their ass, but in reality nothing major is happening; and the people will re-elect him anyway, he's a crowd pleaser - and that's everything in a democracy.
Defense of the Ministry of Finance? Quite funny: "But we will not abuse it. Blocking will be applied only as a last resort." Well sure, we all believe it, it makes sense; that is why ANO and the ČSSD are throwing off the table all amendments that would prevent this abuse, at least legislatively. Not to mention that there is already a law by which the MF can block incoming payments to an illegal gambling house, which in reality means shutting it down completely; with this crap, they can already destroy any virtual casino today, but it's not so sexy for Babiš, because they can't block the websites of inconvenient people, or blackmail them with the threat of blocking. I really wonder what all those big "right-wingers" who voted for Babiš in the last elections say about this, because he is a businessman, he will lead the state as a company and so on; probably nothing, because such people are not interested in actions, only bullshit.

title: Whoever doesn't close on holidays, I'll close him and he'll be closed
text:
Unions are trying to push through a law on the mandatory closing of large stores on holidays. I started the program You have a word... on this topic, and dear friends, I would like to; not only from the amendment, but the "arguments" there, that was extreme. Right at the start, someone explained the obvious (because unfortunately it had to be) that store employees' salaries come from the money customers spend there; to which a kind of affected saleswoman replied: "That's not true! The reality of chain stores is that we employees don't get anything from those sales." At that I stared open-mouthed; I get it, she's completely stupid, but this is bordering on unreasonableness. All the socans there had their mouths full of bullshit about Western countries, because if they introduce totalitarianism in Germany, we have to too; and some folk started talking about national values... I regret that I wasn't there to metaphorically piss his ass off about those national values!
But on the other hand, the arguments of their opponents... I was also scratching my head, because there was hardly anything substantial, only surveys, Western countries (evergreen; when they ban reading in Germany, books will be burned in the Czech Republic), statistics, urban life; but for anyone to say anything about coercion, property rights, freedom, voluntary exchange, at all... the maximum was, "It's social engineering; why should the state educate the citizens when to shop?" Damn yes! But it would be more appropriate to ask: "Why should anyone be forced to not trade their wares with others on certain days? Why is it that a herd of demented or violent bastards - including that blunt saleswoman - initiates offensive violence against vendors while the general public pretends it's legitimate?" If someone ripped the beads off the cow's neck during the show, it would be a hoot; but robbing someone of millions by force? All right.

title: Landfills and presumption of guilt
text:
Do you know what amendment to the law is proposed by Marks? No, I'm kidding, this time it's not Marks, but Environment Minister Richard Brabec; and what is he going to enrich us with? People who already have black dumps on their land must prove in court that they did not put the waste there, otherwise they will have to clean it up; and those who fail to do so will pay a fine of up to a million. The first and obvious absurdity of that law probably hits everyone in the eye: How do you want to prove that you didn't make a mess somewhere (anytime) in the past!? One of the main reasons for the existence of the presumption of innocence is precisely the practical impossibility of proving that you did not commit something, if the act was supposed to happen over a long period of time; on the other hand, after the Esenbäck Huml wiped his ass with this principle by asserting the objective responsibility of the vehicle operator, the other goons cannot be left behind.
However, I consider the fact that the state interferes at all with whoever creates a landfill on their land to be a far more poignant aspect of the whole thing; in general, the term "black dump" should evoke that someone is dumping garbage on someone else's property, but this is not the case, it also applies to the owner, if he does not have a permit from the appropriate authority. And there is no talk of any radioactive or extremely toxic waste, or anything that can endanger health or even smell too much in the surroundings - there are other sections for all of this that have nothing to do with landfills; the state simply decides whether you are allowed to have your landfill on your property even if it does not pollute the surroundings in any way. Now it's just upgraded the already existing crap so that the owner of the land will be punished even if someone else brings the mess there, but he is unable to prove it; and thus, serious friends, the state protects our property and property rights.

title: Marks vs. stress
text:
I thought I had enough about the person in question, but he won't let me; guess what novel she came up with again! Employers are now legally obliged to provide their employees not only with safe working conditions, but also to actively protect them against stress; as? By introducing "anti-stress rooms", "anti-stress corners" or mandatory breaks at work, it is said to be at the discretion of employers; which is also related to the funniest part of the whole proposal - there are no penalties for violating this law. Are you rolling your eyes? Comrade Marksová explains it as follows: "We rather want to say that the employer should not forget about it. We imagine it as a dialogue between the labor inspectorate and the company. When the employer forgets about it, we will remind him of it. [...] I don't understand why it should be missing from the modern labor code." In other words, anyone can give a shit about it.
Unlike the topics I discussed here for the last three days, this is rather a laugh, you can see it as a light point behind the other horrors; in any case, in my opinion, it represents a beautiful probe into the thinking of the person in question: "I don't understand why it should be missing from the modern labor code." Marx simply has a certain obsession that can be found in some socialists discussing on the Internet - they need to have absolutely every fart treated by law; the only difference is that while they are spamming us with posts, the comrades are straight with the laws. Why else – other than out of compelling need – would anyone enforce a law that carries no penalty for breaking it? Some readers of the D-FENS weblog call me a graphomania because I enjoy writing; Marks will be in a similar situation, only she doesn't do it in her free time, but with the looted money of the citizens, moreover, her creations usually can't be ignored... but luckily, this one can.

title: Marksová versus apartment owners
text:
Marksová, a hot topic in Stoky for the third day in a row; the earliest
home office

pay inequality

The so-called "poverty merchants" (that's what the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs calls them) are said to buy apartments, which they then rent to the socially weak, who make a mess in the houses and devastate them, which of course bothers the neighbors. In this way, you will get rid of the "poverty merchants" and the uncontrolled demolition of houses by ungrateful people in one fell swoop, and you will also save money; but that would also show how useless Marks is with the whole famous ministry, so a tried and tested tactic was preferred: The state created a problem which it can then "solve".

title: Marx versus the labor market
text:
Yesterday we were in Stoky
were dissecting

She found out that Czech women take 22 percent less than men, which of course she evaluated as an opportunity to raise the profile and report some of the activity; and what would you say he will do with it? title: Marksová versus home office
text:
The Minister of Labor and Social Affairs - the socialist Marksová - is once again behaving as if she knows better than us what is best for us; I know, it's in the job description to act like that, but that doesn't change the annoyingness of such behavior. This time, she came up with another amendment (how else) to the Labor Code (which would be best simply repealed), which sets employers some additional obligations towards employees working from home; of course, those duties are nothing but a huge pile of crap (ensuring contact with the team, paying for internet connection, etc.), led by the biggest bastard – training on work safety and ensuring a safe working environment (yes, at the employee's home; a dangerous slob doesn't matter, as long as you don't want to program for an employer there, then doom would happen)! I really don't know if I should laugh at the cow or go cry in the corner.
The ramifications of this law for employee protection are likely to be similar to any time someone comes up with something like this, meaning it will primarily harm the very ones it was designed to protect; shit? Sure. I can quite well imagine employers who will not be interested in dealing with the whims and caprices of Marx, so they will simply stop providing home offices to their employees so that the goddamn state can't sniff them out for someone harming themselves during working hours in their own home, where the proper Marxist working conditions were not provided. Another possibility is that the restriction of working from home is not a side effect, but the goal of this amendment; the person in question allegedly (I only heard about it indirectly) expressed that the home office causes inequality in the labor market, because companies operating in fields where the presence of employees in the workplace is not required, thus gain an advantage over the others.

title: Chinese "Miracle"
text:
The Chinese comrades built the Pentagonal Mart - a giant mall in the shape of the Pentagon; if you google it, you will find that the image is quite accurate and it is an interesting idea at all - that the state would ever do something good? No; it also has its "flies". Such details... for example, the whole building cost over two hundred million dollars, it was completed already in 2009, but because of its shape it is completely confusing inside; but that is still not the main problem - the mall is located in a place where no people live, ergo no one goes there, which means that no one sells anything in it, since its opening it has been a ghost shop, which is only dilapidated and waiting for potential customers to start living around it. It is precisely for this reason that indicators such as GDP are completely misleading; the construction of a completely unnecessary and expensive building clearly did not help anyone, on the contrary, it cost resources and has been completely useless for years, yet it increased GDP.
And not only that - it is an illustrative example
inefficiency of central planning
, for it clearly demonstrates that even if money is spent on something, it may not be useful; however, it is important to realize that absolutely all state projects suffer from this ailment, it's just that it may not be visible as much. If the state subsidizes something (absolutely anything) because it would not otherwise earn for itself, it means that the benefit from the given thing is less than its price (
if it were the other way around, it would pay for itself
); it's basically the same case as Pentagonal Mart, it's just different in scale. If the subject of subsidies is something that at least partially works, someone goes there, but does not earn money to operate it, people often tend to evaluate the project differently, because at least it brings something to the customers; that's true, but the costs add up to more than anyone gets out of it (otherwise, people would be willing to pay full price voluntarily).

title: The earth is round, we need a state
text:
"Members of The Flat Earth Society are all around the globe." Wittily? Yes; and true. Seriously. Even the most absurd conspiracy theory has its supporters; moreover, they were recently made visible by the rapper B.o.B. in a debate with astronomer Neil deGrasse Tyson, so iDnes and other Czech media also came with a report on The Flat Earth Society (TFES), which of course sparked discussions, which I like, because in them you learn a lot of interesting things (rather about people than about the topic itself). But why am I writing about it? What interested me? Far more interesting than the arguments of TFES, I find the reactions to them; the most common was, of course, ridicule, but it often came from individuals who, in the discussion, proved that they actually know nothing about physics and not only can't disprove the TFES theory, but also don't understand the arguments why the Earth must be round - they simply believe the opposite, because some authorities say so and they don't want to be idiots.
Anyone who believes in some (albeit flawed) theories that they may have thought about is considered an idiot and ridiculed by people who have simply accepted the "correct" view of authority without bothering to understand it at all; how many mockers know kepler's laws, or can explain why a full moon can be observed during the day (one of the main arguments of TFES)? TFES cannot convince such people of anything - not because they are wrong, but because their opponents are right only by chance (in the Middle Ages, the same natures burned for the opposite) and it is not possible to debate with them, because they know absolutely nothing about the issue and do not even try to understand anything, because there are many of them and instead of thinking, they just assure each other that they are "right", which "everyone knows, after all, except for those idiots from TFES". What libertarian does that not remind you of anything? The good news is that even on the question of the shape of the Earth, the truth has come out; the bad one though, that it took centuries.

title: "Shocking" in the queue
text:
Every once in a while something comes along in the world that makes some people worth standing in, say, an all-day line; it may be the sale of some long-awaited game titles (or data discs), possibly new iPhones. Who are waiting? Well, especially enthusiasts who just can't wait - they have to have their desired hobby as soon as possible; they could easily buy in a few days without waiting, but that wouldn't be it, they would also lose the opportunity to chat with other people about a shared hobby. When selling the iPhone 6, queues were significantly shortened or even eliminated thanks to the registration system. Queues for those who want to buy them, free sale a little later for all other interested parties, everyone gets it, because that's how capitalism works; unlike the queues for meat or bananas in the past... but also for kettle subsidies in the present!
What are boiler subsidies? Well, the state has decided to subsidize people who want to upgrade their boiler in the direction that the powers that be in the current mood have recognized as correct. And what about those who don't want to wait? Can they also come in a few days to have it without waiting? Of course not, are you out of your mind, needy subjects!? A limited number of applicants will be accommodated, so bad luck; fall nicely into the queue, dig with your finger and be grateful to the state that you will get back at least part of what you were robbed of before, because that is the essence of subsidies. Already the old expropriator and socialist Masaryk uttered this pernicious sentence: "In the Czechoslovak Republic, there will be no more place for the old charity, which was always considered a grace, which always humiliated the poor recipient and dulled his human consciousness. Today, we put social duty in the place of humiliating grace." And this is it!

title: A fee for not having money
text:
The robbers from the Ministry of Environment have teamed up with their cronies from the Ministry of Industry and Trade in a common interest, which is, unsurprisingly, the pursuit of loot; this time they came up with an additional tax for owning a car that is too old and an increase in a similar tax already existing (owners will now pay five thousand for cars meeting the EURO2 standard, three thousand for EURO3). The official justification for this particular robbery expedition is the alleged effort to rejuvenate the vehicle fleet; and I first of all ask myself whether seriously rejuvenating the vehicle fleet is desirable in all cases, since this tax will, for example, also apply to
my love
, which I keep for a considerable amount of money in better technical condition than the vast majority of newer cars, not to mention the fact that its driving characteristics make it an even safer car.
Okay, I'll admit, most people don't own a car over ten years old because they fell in love with it (not that that gives anyone the right to tax me for it), they just probably don't have a new one; so a heroic state comes on the scene, which will give these people the missing money... no, sorry, a bug crept in, it won't give them anything... it will take (...and it's not a giant, it's Prince Jason). Logical. The non-functionality (or even negative functionality) of such a measure must be obvious at first glance to anyone who is not completely demented, but even if it is not, we can look at how the same action turned out last time - the car fleet did not get younger, on the contrary, it got a little older (so that poor people with old cars had to pay a tax due to their poverty); so are our robbers from two ministries mentally disabled? Well, it probably won't be any kind of genius, but they're not that stupid either; but canis lupus defecates on the age of the fleet, the main one is another cinder block for the state.

title: About freedom and necrophilia
text:
Last month you could read in Stoké
» About freedom and incest «
i
» About freedom and zoophilia «
; to complement this unplanned miniseries, we look to Sweden, where Liberal People's Party politicians are proposing to legalize necrophilic sex, provided that the dead gave written consent to it while they were still alive. Of course, this proposal outraged the Czech "respectable citizens", according to whom the Swedish politicians behind the attempt to legalize necrophilic appetites have gone completely crazy, they are sunbathers and they are leading our civilization to ruin; but I wonder what's wrong with that? If two people make an agreement that one can have sex with the other after death, isn't that entirely their business? Why should anyone else interfere, least of all legislators? Unlike zoophilia, where one can argue (albeit weakly) about the suffering of animals, in the case of necrophilia nothing of the sort makes sense.
The whole transaction typically has two participants: One dead person who, for some reason during his lifetime, consented to his future corpse being used for the sexual gratification of another person; whether he agreed because he's weird, for money, or for a completely different reason, he obviously gained some benefit (material or otherwise). The other alive, who is most likely excited by sex with a corpse, so he too will get his way; this transaction clearly enriches both parties, otherwise they would not voluntarily enter into it. Why defend a treaty that will undoubtedly help all concerned (otherwise they wouldn't have agreed) and hurt no one? And why are so many Czechs outraged that somewhere in Sweden, a necrophiliac whom they do not even know will enjoy the corpse of a person who agreed to it and whom they also do not know? Well, in accordance with their demented religion, it is their business; and what kind of religion is that? Well, the biggest and most dangerous - statism and democracy.

title: Ministry of Transport versus boaters
text:
Probably every boater has noticed that, although some dangerous weirs are marked with a no-floating sign, there is almost no floating sign; therefore, most weirs are not marked in any way, which for many years meant that the law did not prohibit floating. However, the Ministry of Transport
it's going to hell
,
redefines brands
and Minister Ťok behaves as if he is off the chain, so their next demented decree prohibits the floating of unmarked weirs; this creates a paradoxical situation where, for example, a weir with a sluice (a channel intended for navigation) cannot be legally crossed if there is no sign (although the very existence of the sluice speaks for itself). And the fine? Well, up to two hundred thousand crowns; yes, you read that right, Ťok has gone completely crazy. For all the so-called "right-wing" ANO voters, I just add that they can congratulate themselves on the election of such an individual (and of course it's not just about weirs, the Ministry of Transport has been kicking it up a notch lately).
What are the likely practical consequences? Those who have moved among boaters can certainly imagine that the majority of them will not even register this decree and the remaining minority will typically ignore it; and that the police would build fences at the dams? I'm not ruling it out, but I'm not assuming either. The biggest problem will be the leaders of children's boating groups, who, for peace of mind, will most likely call the dam managers (if they can get contacts) and request an individual permit (which the law has always allowed); anyway, it will just be another springboard for everyone involved, which Ťok has as much up his ass as he can have. And the reason for all this? Well, most likely the implementation of the good old "ordnung muss sein" to Czech conditions; or the official simply needed to report activity; or some benga really ordered it to be able to cash out (I doubt it, but who knows); or... the state, government, officials, Ťoku, do you know what you can do for me?

title: Fidgeting in Germany
text:
The German government gave its goons the green light to use malware (viruses, trojan horses) to track suspects; so, apart from many other pests, the biggest one - that is, the state - will start to spread this crap over our networks. And when I say "us", I'm referring to the fact that the Internet knows no national borders; that the government has legalized actions for which it punishes others is nothing new in the world (wars, taxes, propaganda in schools and the imprisonment of those who do not obey), so I don't want to dwell on it that far, because I find the technical implementation of the whole thing more interesting. Because how does malware spread? Well, viruses can replicate themselves and spread through, for example, various files, worms do so over the network; trojans are programs with some declared functionality (for example, a screen saver, but not limited to that) that the user downloads for himself, but they secretly do something else (for example, play tricks on the government).
So the logical question is how will government malware locate its target; Do they infect fake clouds of computers before they get the real one? After all, we can trust them not to misuse the data obtained from other machines, right? And when this kind of fiddling becomes the norm, will antivirus manufacturers be accused of obstructing the investigation? And no, it's not meant entirely ironically considering that
Apple was already forced by the US government to implement a backdoor in iOS
for the FBI and ISPs are also required to snoop on a court order, just as the owners of various servers are forced to provide snoopers with their user data; is there any reason why it should be any different in the context of anti-state malware fighters? I personally don't see any... so I ask myself when and where will it end? But in addition to asking, I also give
some advice
in conclusion...

title: Public matter: raising children
text:
Who knows best what is best for children? Their parents? But anyway, that's a long-ago idea; the Ministry of Education will best take care of our children (for our money). And of course, Minister Kateřina Valachová knows this best, because she decided to implement the inclusion of disabled children; the social engineer in question decided that too many pupils were going to special schools, so she and her officials came up with a "solution" (to a problem of her own making): A school counseling facility recommends to individual disabled children whether they should attend a regular school or a special one; if the parents decide to send their child to a standard school, even if he was recommended a special one, everything is fine, but the opposite is no longer the case - whoever sends his child to a special school despite the recommendation of the license plate number, the social worker can boo him to his heart's content, in extreme cases until the children are taken away completely.
Even the well-worn - and completely demented - argument that parents are not "experts" in education, while some civil servants have the paper to do so, can no longer be used here; social workers do not have to be (and typically are not) experts in special pedagogy, so it makes no sense at all. The whole measure is nothing but the unbridled will of the state, which no longer has any inhibitions at all, and whose politicians, officials, bureaucrats and all the other instigators now consider it completely normal that they can decide on whatever they like; some motherfucker from the ministry just makes up her mind and another willing motherfucker from the socialite does not hesitate to destroy families just to satisfy her whims. Don't get mad at me, but this is just so close; and I don't care if the person in question is completely stupid and means well, or if she is simply bored or needs to show activity -
the consequences tend to be dire
in any case.

title: Nanny state, version 2016
text:
It was not. Behind nine mountains and nine rivers in the town of Sonnino in Italy, the land of the best cars, lived an absolute madman who didn't like how his wife (didn't) take care of the household and his family; and because he was an extra mean whiner, he was going to turn her in to the fiddler's shop. There were uniformed monkeys sitting in the gymnasium who weren't able to drive their service Alphas, so they were probably bored, which is why they didn't send the bonzak to the proper limits, but instead charged his wife with "domestic abuse", for which she faces two to six years behind bars; whether the court finds her guilty or not (probably not), she will at least be inconvenienced by having to show up and deal with it. And for what!? That she didn't clean, cook and fuck? Seriously? Where are we?
The Italian media accuse the whole case of being sexist because we have equality between the sexes and taking care of the household does not have to be exclusively a woman's job; but is this really the focus of the problem? Is it really an absurd idea today that it would work in every household as its members agree without having a tax-paid arbiter at their disposal? And if someone is relieved that the incident did not take place in the Czech Republic, don't be too happy - according to the new Civil Code, it is illegal to hide affairs from your partner; a 40-year-old woman from Pardubice is already suing her husband on this topic - she found his mistress and the state is now supposed to force him to provide detailed information about her, including their joint plans. In connection with this, I ask: Who can wipe his ass without the assistance of the state? And who doesn't?

title: French government versus property rights
text:
Many supermarkets in France have been honoring such a custom for years: The food they don't sell, they give it to people for free in the evening to take apart; it's usually nothing fresh, but homeless people (or poor Czech students xD) won't look down on it, and supermarkets will save some money on hauling away and getting rid of leftovers. Some time ago I received information that the French parliamentarians are trying to eliminate this custom (due to some hygiene standards), but in practice they probably did not succeed; and because the state simply can't let anything go, everything must be banned, or at least ordered, now it has imposed on French supermarkets the obligation to donate all the food that they would otherwise throw away or give away to charities (transportation costs apparently fall on the donor). President Hollande is so enthusiastic about the regulation that he wants to apply it to restaurants and canteens as well; also pressures Juncker to introduce it in the entire EU, i.e., of course, including the Czech Republic.
Why is this completely wrong? Well, firstly because property rights should be inviolable; it's simply not moral to force someone to give something to someone if they don't want to - after all, how would the supporters of that law like it if they had to obligatorily sort their garbage and transport some of it somewhere at their own expense? This is said to solve the problem of supermarkets wasting food; but what increases their motivation to waste? Yes, that's right, subsidies artificially reduced the purchase price of food; how about stop subsidizing farmers and give space to the market? A frequent criticism of food waste also completely ignores the costs (such as transport) that must be incurred in order to make use of this food; however, these costs (among other things due to pointless subsidies) are often higher than the cost of wasted food. However, it is best to limit waste
free market
, as there is no better way to allocate resources;
every deformation of it
is the road to hell.

title: Equality, even if there was no bread
text:
Socan Jiří Dienstbier, the minister without portfolio (but she is an official), who is in charge of human rights and equal opportunities, found that only thirteen percent of the 250 companies with the largest turnover in the Czech Republic have women in their management; since the person in question is a social engineer to the core, he decided that wasn't enough - and how did he find that out? This whole idea is based on the assumption that the most successful companies are not able to select people for their management so well,
as Dienstbier would do

Maybe those companies didn't choose the best people

For a long time no one prevented women from pursuing a career, but in our society we have more families where the man earns while the woman takes care of the household than families where it is the other way around; it is not relevant why this is so - it could be tradition, genetic predispositions, whatever - however it follows logically that there are more men (than women) willing to devote their whole lives to a working career, ergo more of them will succeed. Trying to use state violence to force companies to choose other people for their management, before they decide for themselves, only
reduces their effectiveness
and deforms
the market

title: Apple to the US government: Shit!
text:
Well, for diplomatic reasons, it wasn't straight up shit, but something along the lines of "We have no sympathy for terrorists, we respect FBI professionals, the government has good intentions, we'll cooperate... but we won't give them access to iOS." title: Another police whip on decent people
text:
The Ministry of Transport has redefined the "No Truck Entry" label; it no longer applies only to vehicles over three and a half tons, but now also to light vans, pickups or station wagons with a partition. From the clouds of quite logical restrictions, which were typically the restriction of the entry of excessively heavy cars to the infrastructure, which is not intended for this, with the stroke of an official's pen became a beautiful buzzing instrument, the dream of every uniformed monkey. In addition to bans on entering certain areas, this also applies to faster lanes on some roads where overtaking of trucks is still prohibited; now, even those who have a normal station wagon with a cargo space separated by a grid are not allowed to overtake there, which of course makes a lot of sense, because such a grid in the interior will do wonders for the driving characteristics of any car!
The Ministry of Transport no longer even pretends that the signs should be beneficial, because if they were, it can hardly just redefine their meaning and declare that wherever it was until now "correct" not to allow vehicles over three and a half tons, today even lighter ones are not allowed, depending on how they have separate personal space from cargo space; the real purpose of such nonsense is police buzz and the issuing of fines for actions that do no harm to anyone -

(especially some completely demented traffic lights, for example in Kralupy I drive past one every week whose contribution to safety is negative, so drivers tend to ignore it, which is why monkeys in uniforms are constantly patrolling there and cashiers), but they will of course welcome any other benga to be able to defend their numbers (in the concentration of scumbags - one per 250 people - the Czech Republic is one of the world's best, only a few totalitarian regimes compete with it).

title: EET approved
text:
For about a week now, I've been working on nothing but VAT control reports for our Czech customers; in addition to me, there is another programmer, financial analyst and designer flying around - the price of the work of the four of us just for a week for those few companies is about two hundred thousand crowns wasted because of the state because we extinguish their problems with control reports (most of our customers are abroad, where Babišova does not have much reach). text:

In this text, I don't want to decide where the truth is - I do apply George Carlin's first rule: "I don't believe anything the government tells me," but this does not mean that I should blindly believe the opposite, so in principle I admit that the truth can be both (although after a thorough study of the available information, one of the versions seems more likely to me); however, the public's reactions to this case are much more interesting: I have read the opinions of dozens of Islamo-killers who "know for sure" that the woman in question was raped; but also the opinions of many sun lovers, they already "know" that she made it up. The catch is that from the information available, neither can be said with certainty; and the sad thing is how a huge number of people do this just because it fits their worldview - unfortunately most debates on this topic show that there is no logic or arguments at all anymore, because discussions about migration are already conducted almost exclusively emotionally.

title: Opencard, Lítačka, money and politics
text:
We all probably know the magic trick of the former mayor of Prague, Pavel Bém: "I'll make seven hundred million disappear and guess which card you're thinking of." A few years have passed since then, and to the already brutal purchase price (less than three quarters of a billion), another more than a billion was added for operation. And remember that crap about how it's going to be a multi-functional card that can be used everywhere? Well, "surprise," that was a lie; in practice it is a tram for almost two gigabytes. What did not happen, however, was that the political leadership of Prague changed, so a new card called Lítačka enters the scene; on the one hand, it costs ten million, on the other, of course, the question is how it will work (not that there are no problems with Opencard). In any case, it is remarkable how the same service can be obtained two orders of magnitude cheaper; imagine that in life you are deciding whether to pay ten thousand or a kilo for something... such a common situation, right?
This whole affair shows the absurdity of the management of public funds in so many ways as to be ridiculous; for example: Mass transport is subsidized, individual transport is taxed, yet politicians constantly solve the problem of "too many cars" - what does this say about the quality of public transport? There is a project that can be purchased for billions, but also for tens of millions; what will be the difference in quality? Even if there was one, has anyone asked the people of the city of Prague which option they prefer? Why do some have to pay for the transport of others? For what reason does DPP have to be subsidized by ten billion annually from public budgets, although it practically has a monopoly on public transport in a city of more than a million people? Who is responsible for this limitless waste? How would the managers of a private company who managed in this way fare?

title: Fidgeting for a better tomorrow
text:
The master of scumbags Babiš and his slimy scumbag padawan Sobotka eat hell together; their government approved another law "against tax evasion" - the CNB will introduce a central database of accounts of legal and natural persons and financial movements on these accounts. And since we already have a law from above limiting the amount of payment in cash, it will definitely be possible to bend it further and tighten it; the right to "have an account" has already been recognized by the EU, so it is only a matter of time before it becomes an obligation, which is only a step away from the ban on cash payments and the transfer of all legal transactions to Babiš's database. The advantage is that introducing something like this in the Czech Republic without other countries doing it is probably not politically feasible enough; the disadvantage is that when they do it, the argument will come again: "It works in developed Western countries, so we must have it too."
The government will ban Bitcoin as the currency of pedophiles and mafias
at the moment when it gains a little popularity, like all other alternative currencies, they can then be liquidated as a means of bypassing the CNB account register, since these will then be taken as
a given without which the world simply could not function
and doom would ensue; how about it worked for thousands of years?

title: Consistent gunban in Denmark
text:
Today we look at Denmark again - in Sonderborg, a 17-year-old girl was attacked by a sexual assailant (media reports say it was a foreigner, some suggest it was an asylum seeker; given today's political correctness, I think it's likely that it was, they just don't want to write it in full), knocked her to the ground and started taking off her pants; the person in question has my respect twice – firstly she defended herself and secondly she did so with pepper spray, the possession of which is illegal in Denmark. I'd consider it an adequate defense if she pulled out a quiver and shot him with balls, but if she did, she'd be in even more trouble than she is now; yes, you read that right, the person in question has a problem. Danish police spokesman Knud Kirsten reported that the person was charged with illegal weapons; what kind of stomach does a person have to announce this to the public and continue to work on behalf of the criminal organization that punishes the victims?
What's sad about the whole thing (besides the fact that it happened at all) is the reaction of people, many of whom are calling for more police and a tougher approach to immigrants; how does that make sense in the context of this case? After all, the person in question defended herself! Of course, the attacker can do it again, but he couldn't if the girl had used a deadly weapon instead of a pepper spray; the police do not deal with such a thing, because they either lock him up (at the taxpayers' expense) and release him again, or deport him, which will prevent him from raping again in Denmark, but not elsewhere. State repression has never been as effective in the fight against crime (which is often committed by state forces) as an armed society; the attacker's fear of an armed victim also works as a prevention (not to mention that armed victims reduce the number of attackers over time). However, due to massive state propaganda, this obvious logic is not available to most people.

title: No more buffets in schools
text:
The Ministry of Education proposed a decree that specifies the foods that may be sold (even in vending machines) in schools (the list of what is prohibited was no longer enough here, now we have a list of what is allowed and everything else may not be sold); this regulation is so harsh that even fruit yogurts, milks, creams (not to mention sweet lemonades, baguettes, chips and the like) do not pass. The dobrosers' idea of the practical impact of the decree is that children will eat healthier; and to some extent this is no doubt true... but what will the other effects be? Well, when we ran out of baguettes in the school vending machine, we went to the store across the street to buy them (it's true, not all of them, but a significant part); therefore, in addition to the intended impact, the decree gives students one more reason to leave school during breaks... will we solve the increase in traffic accidents in the vicinity of schools in a few years? And who will associate it with the regulation of vending machines and buffets?
Far more interesting, however, is the widespread support of similar initiatives by the public (the lobby to ban the sale of junk food in schools has existed for years; and when I occasionally spoke against them in some discussion, it always caused a huge wave of resentment); not that I don't understand parents' efforts to provide their children with healthy food, but... is this really the right way? How about putting that energy into raising children? Quite possibly then these children would not even have the need to stuff themselves with chips outside of school. And if you're going to ban something, why not go to the school principal (who can decide what's sold in the school) and convince him? It is also noteworthy that local bans of this type were at an absolute minimum, because no one really cared about them; however, as soon as it comes to a blanket ban on something by law and further restrictions on freedoms (even "private" schools), everyone is immediately enthusiastic, full of support and energy... do you really think that we are banning ourselves to a better world?

On a related note, I'd like to post some behind-the-scenes information that has come my way; I have no guarantee that this is true, nor have I confirmed anything from two independent sources, I am only relaying what I have learned: Babiš is said to be buying a majority stake in Ahold (Albert, Interspar, Hypernova), which would make him the owner of the largest retail chain in the Czech Republic, which plans to supply Agrofert. How does this relate to EET? I don't have any evidence for such a claim, nor do I know for sure if it's true, but I trust my source more than Babiš (well, probably everyone) and it definitely makes sense to me.

title: Wealth inequality
text:
Oxfam, which constantly supplies us with studies on the topic of how much of the world's wealth is owned by what percentage of people, has come up with the fact that a long-daunted line has been crossed: The richest one percent now own more than the rest of the world. They added a call for politicians to fight it. Oxfam's conclusions were opposed by economists from the Deloitte Group; as? Well, they challenged the methodology that defines a person's wealth as the value of assets minus the value of debt, which makes a fifth of Americans and Europeans living on welfare and with, say, student loans, poorer people than starving children in Africa who are on zero; in addition, they acknowledge that wealth inequality is too high and "something needs to be done about it".
That's what I call argumentative bullshit: getting bogged down in details and approving demented conclusions. So what is the main problem with such studies? First of all, the constant emphasis on inequality in ratio and total ignorance of the fact that
absolute wealth continues to increase at a rapid rate
; even the poor get rich, so what about the rich getting richer faster? It is constantly presented as if the rich are getting richer at the expense of the poor; in fact, it is a reciprocal process (someone produces something, thereby becoming very rich; but also everyone who buys from him raises his standard a little). Furthermore, it is forgotten that the groups of "rich" and "poor" are not constant, but people migrate between them (so it is not always the same individuals). But most importantly: Taxation may reduce relative wealth differences, but
the overall growth of wealth is clearly inhibited by redistribution
!
So what might help today's poor, harms tomorrow's.

title: Dividing the spoils
text:
Imagine an organized group that works by scouting out a rich businessman, liquidating him and disposing of his assets; what doesn't suit them, they simply auction it off. Reprehensible, isn't it? Would you buy from them? Now imagine living in a society where something like this happens quite openly and openly; wouldn't that be bad? Well, I have bad news for you: You live in such a society. Benga hit a Chomut drug maker, jailed him and took his cars (Ferraris, Hummers and some others) which are now up for auction; since they had no luck shooting hummers for 850k last time, now they're trying again for half meg. Everything takes place in public, the actors are clearly not ashamed of their actions, on the contrary, they even brag about it; and most people don't even blink, they don't find anything objectionable about it.
Why? Because it was a drug manufacturer? So what? That he made things that could harm people? Well, of course it is, but that does not differentiate it from manufacturers of clouds of other (state-authorized) things that can also destroy lives (for example, alcohol, cigarettes, knives, ropes...), but above all, the person in question does not force them on anyone, he just produces and offers them; the decision to buy and use is up to each individual. However, the state has decided to persecute some manufacturers and destroy their lives just for offering their product to others; and what is he actually going to do with them besides just plain robbing them? He will shut them up in prison; which is a euphemism for medieval torture where someone is placed in a small cell and held there against their will, often for years. How does society view deviant sadists who lock someone in a basement and keep them there? Horrible, appalling! But when the state does it? All right!

title: Freedom of speech in ruins
text:
Some time ago you could

title: What is capitalism?
text:
Yesterday I wrote about what capitalism is not; and he did not miss the opportunity to refute some of his delusions
critics
. Today I would like to write a few lines about what capitalism is; To begin with, I would like to quote a man whom I consider to be the greatest thinker of the twentieth century and probably of all time - Murray Newton Rothbard:
Capitalism is the fullest expression of anarchism; anarchism is the fullest expression of capitalism. The true anarchism will be capitalism; and the true capitalism will be anarchism.
If by chance someone longed for a translation, then a capitalist creation
Google Translate handles it quite well
(with narrowed eyes).
So what does the term capitalism mean? It is a free market in which the state does not interfere. Yes, sure, capitalists can be ruthless entrepreneurs motivated by their own selfishness and greed, which is a big problem in conjunction with the state - corruption, laws tailored to their companies, subsidies, monopolies (which by the way
they do not arise without the state
); however, in a free market environment, the same profiteering and avarice lead those same people to satisfy the needs of others - how else can they get money without the state, other than by convincing people to use their services and buy their products?
And what is the best way to convince someone to buy something from you? Of course, in the way that you offer him the thing that the person needs! Maybe some people think that this is a beautiful theory, but in practice it works completely differently; yes, of course, you are right, it works differently in practice, but why? Well, because of the state, of course. In the free market, it really works just as I describe; just look at places where the state doesn't interfere so much - Singapore, Hong Kong and others - how are they flourishing? But what about socialist Sweden? Isn't there another way? No; just look at the history, Sweden got its wealth in the days of wild capitalism, socialism was installed only after the country was extremely rich (and this growth was also significantly retarded).
Capitalism is freedom and abundance; capitalism means the free market, which has taken us from carriages to cars, from typewriters to computers, from empty pantries to full refrigerators, from toil in the fields to the possibility of choosing a career in countless fields, from the huge price of food to the negligible, from the occasional wash in the stream to luxurious bathrooms, from one outfit per person to full closets, from a box to a flush toilet, from days or weeks needed to travel to hours, in short, from poverty to riches! Make no mistake, this is not the work of an official, behind it is still greed, personal gain and the pursuit of mammon... the same qualities that turn the state into a disaster, the market can exploit for our good.

title: What is not capitalism?
text:
In recent years, I have observed around me that criticism of capitalism is becoming extremely fashionable and popular, especially among young people (but by no means only among them); what about that, let everyone define himself against what he himself deems appropriate. However, I find it very sad and alarming that the vast majority of those who rail against capitalism typically have no idea what capitalism is; and the problem is not that they simply "define it differently", which in itself wouldn't matter if they stick to such definitions consistently, but they, in their majority, criticize a kind of mischief, but they want to restrict real capitalism by law.
First of all, I would like to give a few examples of what capitalism is definitely not: Capitalism is definitely not Agrofert and Babiš, it is the products of socialist subsidies and regulations (biofuels...); capitalism is not private schools absolutely limited by state regulations; capitalism is seriously not private health insurance companies when health insurance is compulsory; capitalism is definitely not even a (non-state) company that the state will grant a monopoly on anything (water supplies, for example). Where there is no free market, there cannot be capitalism; and if the state interferes somewhere, then it is not a free market.
Some people argue that it is not the state's fault that large companies have non-market privileges, but the corporations' fault, because they bribe state officials and politicians; regardless of the outcome of the academic debate on the topic of who is more to blame, it is quite evident how the problem cannot be solved - giving more power to the state. Even if it were perfectly true that it is only the fault of large corporations that paid politicians create laws tailored to them, it cannot be argued that the state will solve it (because the problem arose precisely because it did not); if states are corrupted by big players in the market, then regardless of who is to blame, the consequence of increasing state power can be nothing but more corruption!
You can blame businessmen for corrupting politicians; but as long as there are entrepreneurs in a market environment and politicians with the power to distort this environment, corruption cannot naturally not occur (by the way, the records of it are thousands of years old, obviously it has never been different; nor could it be). Therefore, the only solution is to either take away entrepreneurs the opportunity to do business, or politicians the opportunity to make decisions; and perhaps everyone who either remembers the first version, or at least
theoretically understands
, why it is a road to hell, he should at the same time realize that the problem cannot be solved other than by removing political power (adding it will achieve the opposite). And for those who still don't realize it, I have one of those

title: Who is the real threat?
text:
I keep hearing around me that immigrants are the biggest threat to us that needs to be "done" urgently; when I keep asking, in 99% of cases, "it is necessary" means that the politicians, the government, the police, or simply the state should act. Although direct statistics cannot be obtained due to political correctness, in many countries it is possible to observe an increase in crime correlated with the arrival of migrants, which in my eyes is a sufficient argument (further strengthened by hiding direct statistics) for stating that immigrants are a statistically more dangerous group in our society. But are they really what threatens us the most?
An incomparably more dangerous group that initiates an order of magnitude more violence than all migrants combined are our nation states and the European Union; not citizens, not ordinary people, not "all of us", no "society", but states, which are politicians, officials, policemen and other parasites living off our money, which they take from us under the threat of violence and call it taxes. These people rob us, impose their will on us, and if we do not submit, they take us by force and lock us up in prison (even if we do not harm anyone; for example, only because we refuse to pay them or do not want to let them interfere with our transactions); they are people who commit more violence every day than immigrants do in a whole year. I'm not saying that mass migration is not a threat, I'm just calling for reflection on whether it's reasonable, as part of the solution to this problem, to strengthen the powers of a state that generates more evil and violence than all immigrants combined.

This complete toothlessness is not accidental, it is a common feature of many modern fairy tales - mainly not defending yourself, the fight of good against evil is "out", courage or solving problems is like a broom; the main character must not show initiative and influence things that simply flow around him (for example, Harry Potter - something is happening there, but
the main character shows no foresight or effort to take matters into his own hands
, rather the opposite), because we have to protect children from getting the impression that each of us is the engineer, engineer and driver of our own happiness - things just happen that way regardless of our actions. Those who do well are "lucky", otherwise "bad luck" is to blame, especially not the person concerned. The motto of many modern fairy tales is: "He who does nothing, spoils nothing; so above all, don't stand out." How will such stories influence the generation that grows up with them? In comparison, the Black Prince is seriously a completely unproblematic character.
