title: Murray Newton Rothbard; requiescat in pace
text:
Today it is exactly twenty-one years since one of the greatest thinkers, economists, philosophers and geniuses of the twentieth century and, in my opinion, of all time left this world at the age of 69 - Murray Newton Rothbard, the "father of anarcho-capitalism"; the importance of his work lies in the incredibly consistent unification of two seemingly unrelated trends: the Austrian school of economics and anarchism. His teacher, the outstanding economist Ludwig von Mises, proved the impossibility of economic calculation in central planning, thus proving beyond doubt the superiority of the free market economy over the socialist one, he still assumed that the free market would be ensured by the state; on the other hand, various anarchists pointed to the ethical indefensibleness of the state as a monopoly on violence, but their solution was typically various communist utopias lacking economic foundations.
In his life's work, Murray Newton Rothbard consistently combined these two directions into a consistent anarcho-capitalism, because he understood that the obstacle to anarchy and the free market is the state, while the absence of a monopoly on violence means anarchy and a free market, which he expressed as follows: "Capitalism is the fullest expression of anarchism, and anarchism is the fullest expression of capitalism. Not only are they compatible, but you can't really have one without the other. True anarchism will be capitalism, and true capitalism will be anarchism." He was a man of sharp analytical mind with an absolute sense of logic, but at the same time very emotional; an implacable hatred of evil, whose greatest contemporary embodiment is the state, permeated his entire work. He died when I was not yet ten years old; however, later on, what he created greatly influenced my life and opened my eyes. Thank you, Mr. Rothbard.

title: China, 1984: Sesame Credit
text:

Registration is not yet mandatory, however the comrades plan that it should be by 2020; according to available information, the goal is for everyone to have an account established at birth and remain with them throughout their lives.
From the sources I've gone through, I haven't been able to figure out exactly how the point system works; rather, the result of my search was finding contradictory information (according to some, the application will monitor practically anything, including activities on social networks - by sharing pro-government materials you gain points, by sharing anti-government materials you lose them; however, the creators of the application deny this). Be that as it may, the introduction of such a system means laying the foundations for absolute totalitarian control; over time, it will seem completely normal to people, similar to, for example, the Czech census has clouds of supporters. And just as Babiš argues when introducing EET that they also have it in Croatia, I wonder if I will live to see the first Czech politician start justifying the introduction of Sesame Credit by saying that it brings great results in China.

title: The worse the better?
text:
Not only from libertarians, I occasionally read arguments in the sense of "the worse, the better", which generally reckon that the current establishment (the rotten state, the EU) must soon collapse under its own weight, because what the politicians are presenting is unsustainable; yes, that's right, it's not sustainable, and if socialism continues to grow, over time, it will not only hinder the prosperity of our society, it may even stop it, so we will start to become poorer, which will eventually lead to a fall. But when? It took the Soviet Union almost three generations, and it still had much better conditions to fall than what we have here now. Why? First, it was seriously completely centrally planned, we are only partially so; secondly, the overall level of wealth was then lower, ergo the path to absolute poverty was shorter; thirdly, the degree of personal freedom (words, confession, ...) was lower; fourthly, there was a positive example of "the West" (even if it was not allowed to be talked about).
The power of the market is fascinating; despite all the regulations and the huge ball on the foot in the form of the public sector, the private sector still manages to generate wealth. There is a historical example that tells us that even after this is not the case, it may take three generations for a change to occur; counting the time before we even start to get poor, we are at best talking about our great-great-grandchildren, who might be affected. This is not to say that the EU cannot fall sooner, on the other hand, it will be replaced by another socialism without any problems. That's why I wouldn't get too attached to the motto "the worse the better"; it's another thing to support things that ridicule or divide the establishment, but their real danger is minimal (now, for example, the best Czech clown named Zeman). So what is our only - albeit meager - chance? Let us tirelessly explain to the people the benefits of freedom; here is another year and with it new armies of indoctrinated statists... so we have work xD

title: Helping and protecting... and tearing down
text:
In 2014 (we don't have this year's statistics yet), 1,327 official vehicles of monkeys and 84,532 cars driven by normal people were involved in traffic accidents; in total, 8,282 monkey cars and 7.8 million human cars were registered at the beginning of the same year. It follows that during the period in question about 1% of humans and 16% of apes were felling, which were supposed to help and protect those humans; can the sixteenfold accident rate be explained by the greater number of kilometers driven? The average human car travels fifteen thousand kilometers a year, the police do not have exact statistics, but in order to balance the above disparity, the apes would have to drive a quarter of a million a year, which would actually mean an annual replacement of the vehicle fleet - and according to the financial reports of the police, this does not even happen by mistake.
Not to mention that even if mileage explained such a huge number of accidents, according to the state's own logic, it does not excuse anyone - or does the point system somehow take into account who drives more kilometers? One might argue that the uniformed monkeys are involved in so many accidents because they chase criminals and "pirates"; But does chasing give them the right to threaten others? title: Is multiculturalism the root of evil?
text:
Especially recently, especially in connection with the migration crisis, we can read from many authors that multiculturalism is evil, it fails, it has never worked and it will lead us to destruction; and I can't disagree that if the politicians keep pushing multiculturalism to us like they have been doing so far, nothing good will really come of it. However, I have a bit of a feeling that among the authors of similar texts there is often a rather fatal misunderstanding of the cause of the real problem, which in my opinion is simply not multiculturalism; it is state-enforced multiculturalism.
What would multiculturalism look like without state support? Well, Rooster-type lunatics would probably continue to go to the ghetto to kiss gypsies, all sorts of left-leaning students would still stuff it for us, write articles about it, and a few of them might even move some refugees into their homes; and I personally guess that with this step some of them would cure themselves of multiculturalism. But what would be the real impact on a normal person? Practically none, we can all ignore the rooster and the numbers of #accepted refugees would most likely be in the units or small tens.
So why is multiculturalism a problem? Because the state imposes it on us under the threat of violence; we don't suffer because of idiots kissing gypsies, but because of anti-discrimination laws, because of mandatory EU refugee quotas, because of expensive detention camps, because of mandatory integration, because of non-profits connected to state money pipes, in short because of politicians and people paid with public money who need to defend their existence. Multiculturalism by itself, without state support, would be nothing more than a fairly harmless pastime for a few coffee shop leftists (and without the connection to public money, there would be even fewer of them).
So we have two problematic factors here: the State and multiculturalism. What would a state do without multiculturalism? Bureaucrats would simply find another excuse to prey on decent people. And what would multiculturalists do without a state? At most, they would arouse sympathetic smiles from those around them. Unfortunately, I therefore come to the same conclusion as I have done so many times - the primary cause of the problem is once again the state; and as many times before, the situation appears different at first glance, so many even see the solution in further state interventions (only on the opposite side), while it would be more than enough if the government gave the people a break.

title: A few tweaks for Stoky
text:
I've made a few changes to the Stok code, but I've already had a few additional or confused questions about what's going on, so I'll allow myself to briefly comment on them - firstly, I added an RSS feed, there's probably nothing to explain, anyone who uses RSS readers can add my channel; secondly, I've made a few changes regarding the appearance that may not be entirely clear at first glance. Unregistered visitors have it easy, a new item has been added to the menu (» appearance «), where they can choose how Stoky should look for them; the settings will be stored in browser cookies. Registered users have it a bit more complicated; in addition to the »appearance« item, they also have the »change account data« option, where they can choose the same, however, this setting will not be stored in cookies, but in the database of their user accounts.
What is the difference? Whatever you set in the » appearance « menu will be saved only in the browser where you set it; on the other hand, via »change account data«, you can set the form that Stoky will have wherever you log in from. In case of a conflict between the settings, the user "wins" (» change account data «), however there is an option (the very first one) that can reverse it (ie the user's appearance will correspond to what he chose in the menu » appearance «); you can use this to turn off Stok sounds at work (the black-and-white appearance without images is also without sounds), which some readers have asked me to do. And as I just verified the theory in practice, changing the coat of the website is very easy thanks to CSS, so if anyone has an idea or wish in the form of another appearance, do not hesitate to write; if more similar proposals come together, or if I like something, I will implement it.

title: Merry Capitalist Christmas 2015!
text:
I don't celebrate Christmas in the traditional sense of the word (with my family, we typically have a nice day characterized by good food, visits and playing computer games together, but we don't stress about cleaning, sweets, "obligatory" buying of gifts and the like), but as an anarcho-capitalist and a Christian, I think they are God's; why?
Christians were able to use this originally pagan holiday for their PR and turn it into a commemoration of the birth of the Lord Jesus, whom God sent to redeem us from sin and suffer for our sins, for which I personally am infinitely grateful to him (despite the light tone of the whole text, I mean this sentence completely seriously), although apparently he was not even born in winter (all the interesting astronomical phenomena around the year zero, which could be by the Bethlehem Comet, whether it was 1P/Halley or not, they come out to different seasons); libertarians should take a cue from Christians regarding their approach to PR xD
In modern times, moreover, Christmas has become a very consumerist pastime (and I will also make money from this year's holidays, as I will celebrate all the holidays, including today, with a well-paid job), which is very good, so many voluntary shifts will probably never take place at any other time of the year; I make a living, among other things, by programming ERP systems for giant retail and wholesale chains, some of which are able to realize up to 80% (!!) of their annual sales in December. So to people who complain that the spirit of Christmas has been replaced by consumerism, I say: Even the original purpose of Christmas was to celebrate (even those that had nothing to do with Jesus), so don't be smart and enjoy it; and if you lack spirituality, pray - I personally do so not only at Christmas and I can warmly recommend it.
Well, for those who don't want to pray, I want them not to come too soon, at least

a Christmas song from the best band that ever was, is and will be
(the endless visual kitsch is of course not their work, but it probably belongs to Christmas), in connection with which I have to mention

(can't help but Chloe Agnew is irresistible); and so that not only the majority heterosexuals, but also the minority heterosexuals, who unfortunately many of my brothers and sisters in Christ cannot (despite the officially declared tolerance) come up with a name for, I am also sending

(in case anyone hasn't noticed, this is instrumental singing with no musical instruments involved; yes, that's right, they are fighters).
However, if there is still someone among the readers whom I have not infected with the Christmas spirit and convinced them that Christmas is God's (which perhaps everyone must see clearly by now), for that I can lovingly rummage
the last remnants of dark humor
; and if that doesn't help either, then maybe just (at your own risk, because the gentleman apparently has a problem; and whoever clicks on the following link may have it too)

, which I absolutely do not share with the person in question, but when it's the holiday of love and understanding, I decided to publish it, because it was censored in Český slavík and even went to court because of its work, which is disgusting (well, it's also the work, but no one has to listen here), so I dedicate this Christmas memory to him at least xD

title: Social dynamics
text:
As one calls to the forest, so one calls from the forest; and this is doubly true of collective guilt: If we divide people into "us" and "them" (according to anything other than the actions of specific individuals) in order to restrict the freedom of "the others" based on how some of "them" have transgressed, we give great arguments to "their" populists who also preach collective guilt; and the more we behave like that, the more "they" will perceive it as well, which will again confirm the words of "our" populists, and everything can escalate to absurdity. If we apply this to refugees, we find that by curtailing their liberties we are seriously driving them into the arms of various terrorist organizations; but watch out! There is no good idea that cannot be twisted and abused; and this, unfortunately, is demonstrated by the sun-lovers: They divide society into "us" and "them" exactly the same, but they limit "our" freedoms in favor of "them" and even brazenly argue that if they don't do so, "they" will become radicalized.
Do you know what the German sunshine politicians are calling for now? They want to ban New Year's Eve fireworks so they don't traumatize the refugees, because the fireworks could remind them of the war; and the curtailment of our freedoms are defended by saying that we must step back so as not to radicalize anyone. But don't they realize that's what they're doing? After all, the principle applies to both sides, and it is completely irrelevant who started it; by restricting the freedoms of the local residents, they will understandably begin to feel threatened and more and more of them will insist on dividing "us" versus "them", which will lead to the same thing on the other side. How is it possible that this principle is well understood by the sun worshipers in one direction, the Islamobies in the other, while neither is able to consider that there is not the slightest reason why exactly the same should not apply to both sides? Well, collectivism has never been very logical. So when will politicians ban fireworks?

title: Social networks are not for minors
text:
Bureaucrats in the European Union are preparing a law according to which social networks should be banned for those under thirteen, while young people between the ages of thirteen and sixteen should only be allowed to go there with parental consent; what to say to that? Firstly, perhaps we can all see what rubbish this is, as the state once again declares its intention to raise children instead of parents, and if this continues, in a few generations it will be the norm that raising children is the domain of the state, and if anyone dares to say that parents should do it, they will be branded an extremist; and secondly, I hope that it is also clear to all of us how incredible this piece of shit is, because we can imagine how such a law can be enforced in practice.
There are two possibilities how the whole thing can turn out if the law passes (it hasn't been approved yet): Either there will be some kind of state consent database or similar madness, or the law can be skillfully used as a stick to beat inconvenient dogs - then (in both cases) it will be a mess; or, in practice, it will end up with a parental consent checkbox being added to the checkbox for agreeing to the terms and conditions - then it will be comically toothless and it will be even more experienced that breaking the law is the norm, which would be nice. So we have three options: (a) The law will not pass, (b) the law will pass and someone will actually start enforcing it, or (c) the law will pass and it will be a joke to the rabbits; option (b) is scary, but I find it unlikely, personally I guess (a) is more likely. Reader tips are most welcome in the discussion.

title: Compulsory elections?
text:
I recently heard Miloš Zeman speak again on the topic of mandatory elections, of which he is a great and long-term supporter. Since only about half of the voters participate in this democratic process, it is not enough for the rulers and they would like more; and when they want something, there is nothing easier than simply ordering people to do it. Here, however, the situation is that only the president really wants it, who in turn lacks the power to enforce it, ergo we will most likely not see mandatory elections in the foreseeable future; however, it is not completely excluded in the future, as there are countries in which citizens have this obligation (if they do not want to participate, they pay a fine).
At first sight, of course, such an idea struck me as monstrous, for such a law is morally unjustifiable; the question is what would be the practical effects? In the first place, it would no doubt incite the people against the authorities, which is always a good thing. Furthermore, in my opinion, a similar law would provide room for more effective mockery of democracy; for example, in Germany there is a political party called "The Party" (in the original "Die PARTEI"), which has only one point in its program: "We will do nothing," for which it understandably does not have much support, but which mandatory voting could change.
Not to mention the fact that something could possibly be gained from compulsory voting by founding a party that will, first of all, promise to abolish compulsory voting; in addition, she could still come up with a libertarian program, ideally smuggled in Trojan style – the official program will only abolish the voting obligation, but in case of potential success she could still liberalize a little in the parliament, or at least use the attention of the media to spread libertarian ideas. The question, of course, is how many of the approximately half of non-voters do not vote simply out of laziness and how many out of some principle, which would greatly influence who these people would be willing to vote for in the event of an election.
So although we can certainly be glad that voting is not compulsory here (less potential buzz), personally I would not be so worried about its introduction, because our situation cannot deteriorate that much (except, of course, another demented state regulation), on the other hand, perhaps such a law could result in some liberalization or at least a weakening of the state in the eyes of its voters and their further annoyance; the question, of course, is to what extent this would affect anything. What do you think about it, dear readers?

title: Political correctness sucks
text:
Exactly one month ago I published a text here
»Political correctness like a cow«
, which now turns out to be a hasty title, as it no longer gives much room for gradation of the titles of other posts; but who could have known then that it would be even more correct in a month? Yes, you are right, everyone could have known. And what happened now? The Rijksmuseum (Reich Museum) in Amsterdam renamed historical works of art whose names were now deemed politically incorrect; for example, "Mohammedan" became "Man with a beard", "Hottentot whore" will now be "Smoking woman from the Khoi tribe", "Head of a Moor" is in newspeak "Head of a man", "Negro servant" was renamed "Young servant" and more than two hundred other works were similarly defaced... do you think that in the next upgrade we will see interventions in the skin color of the depicted persons so that the ratio of blacks and whites between the rich and the poor is balanced?
So the state finances culture from the pockets of taxpayers in order to take care of it better than terrible private individuals, but apparently it does not understand what every barbaric math physicist Urza does, that is, that part of the work of art is also its name, the change of which changes the artist's message; or is someone seriously going to tell me that if the painting "Hottentot Whore" is renamed "Smoking Woman of the Khoi Tribe" by a callous kokot, the information will not be lost and with it part of the author's statement? And what's worse - the historical connections and the spirit of the time from which the works originate are disappearing; however, it is "necessary" to indicate to the students who are required to visit the museum that political correctness has always been here. I recently saw a joke with a picture of Parliament and the caption: "You idiots, Orwel wrote 1984 as a warning, not a manual!" But it's slowly becoming less funny, because renaming those works of art is exactly the activity Comrade Winston Smith had in his job description...

title: The Future of Bitcoin?
text:
Bitcoin probably needs no introduction here; what libertarian wouldn't be excited about a currency that isn't controlled by the state? A huge number of texts have already been written on this topic, the authors of which not only describe Bitcoin, but at the same time venture into various predictions of the future of this virtual currency, with regard to the economic and technical side of the matter; although I share their enthusiasm to a large extent, I also believe that one extremely important factor is often neglected within it - the fucking state. Even if several politicians have not already declared their intention to ban Bitcoin in case it becomes widely used, this step is more than expected from the state - after all, what government will voluntarily give up a monetary monopoly?
Creating a social demand for a ban will be a completely trivial task - it will be enough to find and thoroughly investigate in the media a real or fictitious network of pedophiles trading for bitcoins (it doesn't even have to be true, just fill the media with it); subsequently, a bag of various "experts" will be torn open, confirming that bitcoin is not only the currency of pedophiles, but also of terrorists, thieves and tax evaders. And law enforcement? Well, some will argue that due to decentralization, it is practically impossible to effectively take bitcoins from people, which is true, on the other hand, it is very easy to ban sellers from accepting bitcoins; and anyone who will accept this currency in the online store will complain. Crap? Sure, but who cares but libertarians? Of course, it is right to keep trying to resist, but I fear that Bitcoin will suffer the same fate as Bernard von NotHaus. Does anyone have a more optimistic view? Please share it in the discussion.

title: How do we lose our freedom?
text:
Some time ago I poured into Stok
comment
, which in turn several people wrote to me that I should insert it as a standard "article"; since in my opinion it is long enough for Stoky, here (a little more generally) I describe its point - how we lose our freedom.
Phase One:
We have some freedom (speech, movement, business, arms, ...); people are not willing to give it up (yet) and anyone who would try to limit this freedom because of some bureaucratic bullshit will be sent somewhere, he will start losing voters and all his colleagues will give up on him. If, by chance, someone just passes a law that cancels this freedom, everyone who promises to repeal this legislation will do better in the next election.
Phase Two:
Prohibitionists present a strong emotional reason to limit this freedom (terrorist attack, mass-raped children, radioactivity, biological weapons, and so on, just about anything that evokes strong feelings, even though it may be only marginally related to the freedom in question); if it is a major intervention in our lives, he promises that it is a temporary change. I assume that we are all familiar with such arguments on the topic that during war one is allowed or does this and that (giving war as an example of moral heights is also laughable). The hysteria will completely overshadow any reasonable debate on the subject, so the ban will pass.
Phase Three:
As soon as people have become accustomed to the fact that the given freedom is already somewhat restricted, the social engineers will come up with a proposal to reduce the number of murders, rapes, robberies, and the like, if this freedom is suppressed a little more; these efforts sometimes fail, but after a while they still succeed (note that once a regulation is in place, it is virtually never repealed). When that happens, that freedom will begin to be restricted without the interest of the public, even because of every fool and bureaucratic whim; although it was a no-brainer at first, it leaves practically everyone (except a few crazy libertarians) cold at this point.
Phase Four:
Processes (within the public and private sectors), services, goods and norms arise, which are based on the fact that the given freedom is somehow limited; these are then used as arguments why that freedom must remain suppressed. Even if the original reason disappears, or turns out to be pointless from the very beginning, it really doesn't matter anymore. No one is interested in this freedom anymore, moreover, "it is clear to everyone" that it must be limited, because otherwise "it wouldn't work" (because of all the processes that count on that limitation).

title: Gasoline, alcohol and a weak acid? Only from eighteen!
text:
The Ministry of Health changed the law on the protection of public health (yes, we also have such a law, because our bodies belong to the state) so cleverly that in schools, students are not allowed to come into contact with fuels (the health of young car mechanics) or with weak acids or alcohol (be healthy, chemistry students), so even the chemistry olympiads have an impact; the Ministry of Education promised to fix it, but it turned a blind eye, so nothing. Taking the professionals at their word, Minister Němeček and Minister Valachová are first and foremost trying to figure out who is to blame - according to Valachová, Němeček messed it up with an idiotic change to the law, while the latter defends herself by saying that the amendment was available to her in advance, so she should have been reminded of it; as for the problem itself, it can of course wait, because it is always possible to establish an interdepartmental commission, come up with a proposal and send it to the hygienists, who also have plenty of time. Can you imagine doing this at work?
However, this tragicomic incident is only the tip of the iceberg, a symptom of something much deeper. In addition to the existence of such an obvious piece of crap as the law on public health undoubtedly is (the state declares that our health - and therefore not even our bodies - belong to us, but to politicians who usurp the right to decide), we face one more problem - the whole concept of our legislation is turned on its head: A law has come into force that is clearly wrong, everyone knows it, including those who proposed it; nevertheless, everyone must follow it, because if any teacher now experiments with prohibited substances (the same ones that were allowed only a month ago) with students, they will complain. Someone could argue that it has to be, because otherwise, in the case of every illegal behavior, it would still have to be assessed whether the law that was accidentally broken is not meaningless in the given situation. And what do I answer to such an objection? "Well, that's how it should be!"

title: Gulm, Erdogan and freedom of speech in Turkey
text:

Bizarre? Indeed.
I assume that the vast majority of Czechs will consider the case completely absurd and the question of Gollum's goodness as marginal compared to the absolutely fundamental suppression of freedom of speech, because that is what really matters; on the other hand, exactly the same people are then able to completely ignore the crucial trampling of the owner's freedom to decide about his premises in the discussion about smoking bans in restaurants and instead get bogged down in the debate about the harmfulness or stench of cigarettes, which is just as irrelevant as the analysis of Gollum's character. How is that possible? Well, although these people have already graduated from the state foundry on the topic of regulation of entrepreneurs, but not on the social harmfulness of insulting a public official; but be sure that if it becomes a topic, someone pushes it into the school curriculum and indoctrination takes place within the educational process (where does the media dig into this), within a single generation, the character of Jabba, to whom Zeman is fondly compared, can begin to be seriously addressed in the Czech courts.

title: Misguided debate
text:
Sometimes I play the talk show "Máte slovo" on the second monitor (more like a background sound) (if there is a political topic in the given episode); today, an amendment to the already totalitarian "Act on Significant Market Power" was discussed, which further tightens the Act. The hot topic of the show was supermarkets, which, based on their strong market position, get discounts from manufacturers; however, the law says that an entity that is a "significant market power" cannot demand a lower price without a "just cause" (that's seriously there). The debate then takes place in the spirit that the supporters of the regulations accuse the retail chains of buying food at low prices from the position of a strong player in the market, while the representatives of the supermarkets reject this; and everyone implicitly assumes that is wrong.
Why is this appalling? Well, for the same reason that there was a terrible debate about banning smoking in restaurants, the focus of which was whether cigarettes are harmful to health and how bad the smoke stinks (the absolutely key takeaway from that debate, which I still remember to this day, is that smoke in a pub spreads like urine in a swimming pool); and this is exactly how practically everything is discussed (far from only in that talk show) - if the acceptance or non-acceptance of the regulation of anything is discussed, basically the debate is reduced only to whether it is harmful or not, while if the first variant occurs, the regulation is automatically considered justified, ergo correct. And that is why, dear libertarians, we must tirelessly point out the essence of things, which is freedom, property rights and the real cost of regulation laws (not only economic, but above all moral); because no one else will do it for us.

title: Don't want to pay your quirks? Force others!
text:

Sunbathers and their holy #acceptance. Why? The sunbathers obviously benefit from material aid to the refugees (to what extent it actually helps them, let's leave aside), while the Islamo-killers benefit from a sense of security (to what extent closing the borders will ensure safety, let's also leave aside). Each of us is made happy by something different - some want a multicultural society and going to kiss gypsies in the ghetto (which is not a metaphor, but the Rooster - just to be clear), others want closed borders and Czech flags as proof of their annoying religion in the name of patriotism, while for example I like whores, good wines, bloody steaks and my convertible, but in my life I would never think of forcing someone to pay me for it (because then she would probably pass me the taste); on the other hand, Islamophile and Islamophobic totalitarians directly crave for it: "Stop, close the borders!" "Stop, close the Kettle!" "Wait, I have an idea to make everyone pay for it!" On the other hand, I, a free-market anarchist, am commonly labeled an extremist because all I want is: "Leave me alone..."

title: State like a house
text:
In connection with the issue of migration, we often hear the comparison that a state is like a house; just as the owner decides who to let home and who not, the state should supposedly decide who to let across the border and who stays outside. Although such a comparison may seem logical at first glance, it is actually one of the most false analogies I have ever come across; what I find very unique about it is that the compared statement denies the one to which it is compared.
As? Well, if the state decides who is allowed to cross the border, it also prevents me from inviting home whoever I see fit (because in some cases it leaves him completely out of the state). Isn't that paradoxical? The analogy is based on the fact that it is good to be able to decide for myself who I let into the house, but this principle that she uses as a model would be canceled by the principle that she is trying to enforce; it's hard for me to let whoever I want into the house when the person in question doesn't even have to cross the border.
Another problem with this analogy is that while a house typically has an owner who legally makes decisions, the state does not. A far more accurate analogy would be with the apartment building in which I own an apartment: Can the neighbors, by majority vote, ban me from inviting a visitor they don't like? Um... suddenly it's not so clear anymore, huh? Not that they couldn't make such an agreement in advance, but if it doesn't apply at the moment when I bought an apartment in that building, it suddenly becomes a rather tricky matter, and I quite doubt that anyone would still use the analogy like that (although it is more accurate in every way).
But the city resembles the state even more than the house; and here we are already on downright thin ice, because it is quite unheard of for the citizens of the city to vote on who can come there for work, for example. Do not take this text as a defense of any European Union quotas for refugees, because it would be even more absurd than my neighbors forbidding me who can visit me, if they ordered me who I must accept into my home; I'm just pointing out that the analogy of state borders with land borders makes practically no sense, and even contradicts itself.

title: Pimps versus taxi drivers
text:
We've had such trouble here - the Prague scumbags are bragging to the media about how they caught evil taxi drivers after several months of action; and what did these evil sons do? Well, they dared to arrange a voluntary transaction with the customer before the ride (two kilometers per liter, which corresponds to about a 98% margin) and then not turn on the taximeter; however, the state forcibly forces all shifts to take place according to the (demented) rules it has set. The accused are six taxi drivers and one official, who covered the person in question from the checks, while the uniformed monkeys also boasted that they were all watching them non-stop, which is why ten detectives and dozens of extras were needed for each one to prove that each victim broke the law for a total of five thousand crowns, because below this threshold it is only a misdemeanor, not a crime (and not every attempt was successful, the taxi drivers offered the above agreement only rarely).
Even if we leave aside the moral side of the matter, i.e. that it is rubbish when the state intervenes in voluntary exchanges, then what actually happened? A detective (let's count a complete newbie) takes about 25k a month, events lasting several months or two months, extras should work for free, let's ignore the costs of equipment and taxi trips; and we find out that the state blew 3.5 megs (lower estimate) just on detective salaries so that, dude, what!? To convict six people of offering someone a ride at a pre-agreed (albeit high) price, and one of covering for them in the process. Bravo! Three and a half million for charging seven people with a victimless crime; and those whores are still bragging about it in the media!? Do you think they probably screwed up at the cinema? Well, google it and read how journalists are licking their asses for it; and below that the enthusiastic comments of demented idiots... because why wouldn't we throw away millions so that someone can't have a 98% margin; and that is, dear children, democracy, the government of the people!

title: Minimarx
text:
Minister of Labor and Social Affairs Marks lives up to her name - the minimum wage, which will already rise from 9,200 to 9,900 in January, wants to increase it by another liter the following year and up to 12k the year after that; the explanation is as follows: "If people go over the income threshold even a little bit today, they lose housing benefit. It's quite a lot of money, it's not worth it to them." On the one hand, it is nice that she noticed the inverse relationship between social benefits (also from her ministry, by the way) and people's willingness to work; on the other hand, I can't help but wonder how much stupidity or crap it takes for someone to propose raising the minimum wage as a "solution" instead of reducing those benefits.
I don't know what Ms. Marks thinks the minimum wage is, but it's certainly not a wage-raising or even welfare law; the minimum wage simply means that the state prohibits people from working for less than the politicians determine. The state does not thereby create anything, it does not protect anyone, it simply prohibits work below a certain price; whoever cannot earn that much (plus all taxes) for the employer, simply no one will employ him, because he would lose out. Setting the benefit level so that people don't want to work much is silly; but to "solve" the situation by banning work under certain conditions... that's completely pathetic. So, I ask: Does Marks know what she's doing (which would make her a pretty bitch), or is she just plain dumb? What do you think?

title: Quo vadis, ODS?

title: I'll read it
text:
The perennial comparison of Islam to Nazism and Muslims to Nazis is among the most popular Islamophobic arguments; not that such an analogy does not make sense in certain special situations, it is generally used meaningfully by some of the smarter fighters against Islam, but in the vast majority of cases it is nothing more than a dull parroting of these views by the dumber ones who can do nothing but rewrite completely random texts in such a way that they simply replace the occurrences of the corresponding words in it, for which even software could be written in half an afternoon handled automatically, while the output would be about as stupid. So how do such comparisons fail?
In the first place, although Islam has some features in common with Nazism, it also has a number of features that are quite different; the main difference lies primarily in the fact that, while Nazism is a very young and concrete ideology, Islam is nothing but one big mess, a big hundred-year-old religion that has countless interpretations and a holy book with many translations (of which the six "main" ones and many others). Islam actually has a number of different currents (from aggressively totalitarian Salafists to benevolently frivolous Sufis), which Nazism simply does not have; for that reason, for example, it is completely absurd to compare "moderate Muslims" with "moderate Nazis" (because in reality there were no Nazi currents proclaiming something diametrically different from the teachings of Hitler himself; if they existed, then such a comparison makes sense).
Moreover, even in cases where the comparison makes sense, abominations sometimes flow from it; typically this applies to situations where someone tries to enforce a ban on Islam by arguing that Nazism is also banned. The problem here lies primarily in the fact that banning a totalitarian ideology is itself a totalitarian practice; totalitarianism simply cannot be defended with totalitarianism (so Nazism should not be banned either). If we sacrifice freedom of speech, expression, press or religion, we ourselves become the ones we want to ban! The argument that prohibitions of totalitarianism are not in themselves totalitarian practices is completely absurd; for there is no objective measure to determine what is to be forbidden, ergo there must be someone to decide about it - and that is exactly what totality consists of.
I am certainly not saying that comparing Nazism and Islam must always be wrong under all circumstances; for example, political Wahhabism does resemble Nazism. But it is not possible to suddenly claim that it is one and the same thing in all circumstances without thinking, because that is simply not true; the differences are sometimes negligible, other times huge, so before comparing one to the other it is advisable to think about what the result should be and whether the comparison lacks all meaning in this particular area. Please, let's not close our eyes to logic in the name of fanaticism.

title: Illegal home pig-slaughters
text:
Based on a few years old regulation from the EU, the Czech state forbade its subjects to hold traditional pig-slaughters unless they have a special permit; unfortunately this permit doesn't seem to be obtained by going to the office, rather you more or less need to own a slaughterhouse. The usual neighborhood pig-slaughters are simply a thing of the past; and commercial pig-slaughters organized by pubs as well. However, the whole thing has its bright side - the state does not have enough resources to actively control compliance with this law, so the only way to screw someone up is if someone informs them beforehand.
The dark side then consists in the fact that even such whores can be found among us; in 2014, the state collected one hundred and twenty thousand crowns in fines, all from natural persons (legal persons most likely did not dare, because it is necessary to advertise it, which increases the risk of disclosure), who were probably swindled by their neighbors. Shame on them! Shame on any motherfucker who is able to beat up his neighbor for killing his own pig; this can no longer be excused with any nonsense about the social danger of such behavior, this is pure unadulterated crap for which the person in question deserves the utmost contempt.
On the other hand - although I did not manage to track down the number of such crackers - considering that one fine for an illegal slaughterhouse can reach up to three hundred thousand and the state collected one hundred and twenty thousand for the whole year, it can be assumed that it was most likely a few (or small dozen) cases; even if the average fine was only ten thousand, that would be twelve people, that is, one per month, which is not so much for a population of ten million. Overall, I like the certain indifference of people to breaking the law in this country, because although they generally consider taxes to be correct in general, tax evasion and undeclared work are not socially condemned on a personal level (perhaps compared to Germany, where it is perceived similarly to robbing a neighbor).
In any case, similar laws that are not enforced by the state are downright a shame to follow; it is enough to convince crackers not to crack. So if you know any such human waste, be mean to him, ostracize him, convince others to do the same, just teach him a lesson to change his mind next time; and the less people who collaborate with the police the better, so spread the word about all the bad things the police have done or caused (for
examples
no need
walk far
). The state is evil; and whoever is willing to do crap for him, let decent people show him that this is not the way to go.

title: The war on drugs is (always) failing
text:
The War on Drugs is (always) failing; Murray Newton Rothbard and other brilliant visionaries predicted this long before this war really started, people resistant to the prohibitionist state propaganda realized it within a few years, others understood it after a few decades, and today everyone knows it, including small children, even the former powerful already admit it. I'm sure even the modern ones know it, but they do it for a living, so it's easier for them to pretend it makes sense; after all, what would all those poor drug squad cops do?
The Global Commission on Drug Policy assessed the situation in a report in which it was surprised to find that the anti-drug policy at the cost of millions of dollars from the taxpayers' pockets has failed because it is not effective, but it creates organized crime and causes the death of thousands of people; members of this commission are, for example, former UN chief Kofi Annan, former NATO secretary and former EU high representative for common foreign and security policy Javier Solana, former US foreign minister George Schultz, and former presidents of Mexico, Brazil, and Colombia. The former powerful, whose power does not depend on the drug war, have no reason to lie anymore...
The very opening of their report states: "The global war on drugs has failed with devastating consequences for individuals and societies around the world." It also says: "Political leaders and public figures should pluck up the courage to say out loud what many of them admit in private: The evidence clearly demonstrates that repressive strategies will not solve the drug problem, the war on drugs has not won, and cannot win." The important thing is that those past leaders, who are criticizing today, took that courage; I would also like to know how they estimated what the contemporaries say to themselves in private - that they have rich personal experiences? xD
The whole matter belongs to a vast group of those which would be laughable, if they were not, of course, to cry; one thing is that decades ago there were strictly logical explanations why the war on drugs simply wouldn't work, but it didn't fit, so it was quite understandably ignored, but we have a completely different situation today, where, in addition to those explanations, there is also empirical evidence that this war will do more harm than good - yet the politicians continue this activity, because the real goal is not the declared results, but more power, the expansion of the state and, last but not least, an amazing source of income from taxpayers' pockets.

title: Minus and minus gives a plus, so banning banners... no, unfortunately!
text:
When I last wrote in Stoká about Pelikan's Ministry of Justice, which is fighting against it really persistently (against whom? Well, that justice xD), I had no idea that I would be here again in just two days to rant about Pelikan; on November 18, the person in question tweeted the following message: "Whoever publicly incites hatred of any (...) religion (...) will be punished with imprisonment for up to two years." And exactly on that day - what a coincidence - Konvička was charged with the crime of incitement to hatred. Of course, it does not appear at all that the Minister of Justice had any personal interest in the matter, let alone boasted of it publicly; He wouldn't do that, would he?
What does Kettle say today? "There is an obvious effort to criminalize political opponents of the government, and that effort is evident in the date the indictment was written."
What did Konvička say a while ago? "The only thing that will help is the pressure on politicians, representatives, journalists to do everything to stop Islamic expansion. Even at the cost of overturning laws, closing borders, militarizing society and yes, even depriving the civil rights of the 12-16 percent of the population who sympathize with Islam."
If the situation wasn't so serious, I would have laughed heartily at the irony. The problem is that banning banners doesn't get us freedom, so it just doesn't work; prohibitions always constitute totality, never freedom. The bottom line is that there is no universally accepted method for deciding who is "right" (after all, if there was such a method, the dispute would disappear), so the only way to determine what will be forbidden is for the one in power to decide. "He who sows the wind reaps the storm," is a wise proverb, but for the conditions of a democratic state it must be modified to: "He who sows the wind reaps the storm; and everyone else with him." By calling for the banning of any opinion, we are simply creating a society where instead of free discussion, we simply silence our opponents by force; and only a fool would think it would never backfire on him (not to mention the ethics of the whole thing).
Martin Konvičko, although you are in my opinion
manic
a sadist
, who wants here
to introduce totality
, I have my fingers crossed for you in court! Not only because if they convict you, it would be another step towards totalitarianism, but above all because you were just expressing your opinion and trying to convince others of it, which is a completely legitimate action and you should not be punished for it in any way - regardless of what I or anyone else thinks about that opinion.

title: Police scares: alcohol goggles
text:
Benga launched another campaign against drunk drivers; it is hard to say what the purpose is this time, it could be a media artillery preparation for tightening the legislation or another hype event, or simply someone needed to report activities for taxpayers' money. Anyway, the whole thing was done by having the uniformed monkeys get the so-called "alcohol glasses", which cause people to see double or triple, they called some servile journalists, put the glasses on them and let them drive between the cones, so that they would then write articles on the topic of how terrible it would be if the cones were replaced by pedestrians.
I assume the vast majority of readers know what it feels like to be drunk; and who thinks the only problem in that condition is vision? Of course, I am not saying that it is not possible to get drunk in such a way that one slowly becomes blind, on the other hand, the loss of motor skills, slowing down of reflexes and other problems come much earlier, which will affect the ability to drive very fundamentally; hence the nonsense of the police statement that the glasses allegedly simulate 1.5 per thousand - most likely they will simulate much more in terms of vision, while far less otherwise (or simply just 1.5 vision and nothing more).
So the result is that both the whole test and the "alcohol glasses" are simply a lie; they do not simulate what they are supposed to simulate. Yes, of course, it is possible to get into a state equivalent to some kind of drunkenness by blurring the vision, but this is highly individual, because even that alcohol affects people differently; apart from the hooray event and scaremongering in the newspapers, the informational value of such a bag is practically non-existent. And I ask: Who paid for it all? But most importantly... who among these payers, taxpayers, would pay such crap even voluntarily if they didn't have to? Imagine how absurd it would be if someone asked people for money to buy "alcohol goggles" and put them on journalists and let them drive between cones... but why ask when there's another way, huh?
And finally, just on a side note, I'm wondering if it's illegal to drive with "alcohol glasses". Does the applicable legislation forbid me to wear glasses behind the wheel that significantly distort my vision? Of course, in case I crash because of it, it's clear; but as long as I drive without an accident, can a monkey in uniform slap me with a fine? If not, why not? If it really is as equivalent to drunkenness as the buffoons claim, why is one forbidden and the other allowed? Does it even make sense? I am afraid that it is again some purely arbitrary decision of politicians with a patent on what is best for us.

up to five years before (sic!) the theft. You simply receive an expensive gift from someone, the person in question steals something in five years - and lo and behold, a bailiff out of nowhere! title: Forests of the Czech Republic in Nicaragua
text:
I read about another amazing project on which the state lost "only" twenty million crowns - this corresponds to two crowns per citizen, which is little enough so that we don't have to cry and make an ass out of it; so what funny happened? The state company Lesy ČR (!) about ten years ago bought a teak plantation in Nicaragua (you dude xD) with the justification that it is a lucrative commodity, so they will start a profitable business (cinder block xD); we saw what it looks like when the state gets into business here in vivid colors before 1989, but apparently some still haven't learned their lesson.
Daniel Szorád, the head of Lesů ČR, said: "People who were at the birth claim that it could have succeeded. That it was supposed to be a printing press for money, it just didn't catch on."
Well, it happens; here and there someone "gets something wrong", but while in the private sector they also pay for it themselves, in the public sector the main thing is that no one else's blood flows. For example, I really liked the idea, when Greece once sold some tiny islands, that I would buy one and build a tower on it; yo-yo, if someone was paying me, I would dare to do it, at worst I could say that I "got it wrong".
And how did that money printer turn out? It has never been in the plus side, just for the protection there, Lesy ČR pays about half a million a year, so far about twenty million crowns have been spent on the entire project. By the way, I would be very interested in what kind of work those guards do there, they already take around 40k a month for it; how many security guards can be bought for that in such a shitty world? Ten rangers and one to watch over them? Or they simply dig into it, since no one from here has any way to control them anyway and no one bears any responsibility anyway; and if they happen to find out that, as they all knew, someone cut down half of the forest, they will simply set fire to the rest and it will be lost in it, absolutely no one will care.
So Daniel Szórád decided to get rid of this "money printer", but hey, nobody wants it (surprise); and such a lucrative business plan it was! The employees of Lesů ČR (including the boss) will solve it by taking a vacation to Nicaragua (with our money, of course), where they will try to convince someone to buy the teak forest below the price. Of course, this is just a demented comedy with a cost of crowns per head; however, it illustrates very accurately what happens when the state gets into business - utterly pathetic and utterly boundless waste...

title: Political correctness as a cow
text:
The Chicago Blackhawks hockey club and the Washington Redskins American football club have a common problem; what? Well, they have a picture of an Indian in their emblem, which, for example (and far from only) is racist according to Obama and shows disrespect for the original inhabitants of North America; so I don't know, I don't have the schools for this, nor the "correct" political mindset, but how can disrespect for someone be expressed by someone putting it in a club emblem or naming their sports team after it? I have no connection to American football, but if someone founded, for example, "Washington Anarchists" and put a yellow-black anarcho-capitalist flag in their emblem, I would think of many things, but hardly anything related to disrespect...
However, the American Indians are said to see it differently, they are said to be offended by it; I believe that someone like that can be found, but is it really such a topic among them? We probably won't find out through the media mask of political correctness. But even if it offends everyone, what right do they have to ban the owners from naming the club as they see fit? Limiting someone's freedom on the basis that their speech "offends" someone is a road to hell, because anything can offend anyone, so applying this principle we would probably end up having to seriously ban everything; not to mention the fact that assessing what offends whom and how much is not realistically possible in practice.
Daniel Snyder, the owner of the Washington Redskins club, first sent the politically correct activists to the appropriate places, now he has to defend himself against them in court; however, I find the arguments of his lawyers a bit hot and maybe a bit dangerous - they argue that the Washington Redskins should not be renamed because there are even more racist or offensive trademarks, for example Baked By a Negro Cookie Company (cookies from a Negro), or Dirty Whooore Clothing Company (clothing for dirty girls; I really like this, because I like light girls - even those that at least they dress) - I'm a little afraid that it won't end up with a ban not only on redheads, but also on all whores and blacks...
Political correctness is spreading everywhere like a plague, some time ago it was found officially offensive (and therefore prohibited) to display the confederate flag, so nothing stands in the way of banning Native American motifs in the logos or names of sports clubs; basically, the comrades in the USA have reached a point (and not that we are any significantly different) in which bans on activities that offend someone are considered correct, so freedom itself is not so much discussed anymore (they wrote it off a long time ago; and it was such a land of freedom), but the debate is only about what and how much offends how many people.

title: Freedom of speech in Britain
text:
BBC presenter Ursula Presgrave is unlikely to be a fragile soul who loves sick children; on her Facebook profile she posted a controversial (and in my opinion quite demented) opinion about the uselessness of some of them: "Anyone born with Down syndrome should be euthanized. It's just cruel to let them lead a useless vegetable life." People reacted quite logically to this with many comments to the effect that she was just trying to get attention and that she was disgusting; I quite agree with the second conclusion, in the case of the first I have my doubts, as the person in question has more than enough attention as a BBC star.
Domenica Lawson, Princess Diana's goddaughter with Down syndrome, feels offended by this statement because she says she lives like normal people (which I also have some doubts about; on the other hand, it's purely her business); and many other famous people experience it too, I'm not famous personally, so I'd just conclude that Ursula Presgrave is probably a cow. It is understandable that it will most likely cost her her job, but what is much worse is that someone sued her, the court recognized her guilt, and the person in question will go sulking for six months; and that's much closer than the whole famous statement about children with down syndrome, because it was just talk.
Before the court, of course, the person in question was indirectly forced to pour ashes on her head, apologize, take back her statement, bitterly regret it, and the like; I don't believe in the sincerity of such behavior, but I don't condemn it in any way, because nothing like this would most likely not have happened at all if the person in question had not tried to accept a lesser punishment. But how can anyone believe in freedom of speech in a society where people are sent to prison just for expressing stupid and callous opinions in public? Of course, freedom of speech is not just about letting people express reasonable and emotionally mature opinions; for real freedom is when everyone is allowed to show himself as an insensitive fool without being penalized for it.
Fortunately, we are not that far in the Czech Republic, although our comrades
trying their best to get closer to the British ones
; where will it all end? We will see the creation of a Ministry of Truth, which will approve which views are the "correct" and permissible, and no one will be allowed to publicly hold otherwise; eventually maybe not even privately. However, I am sure that even if something like this happens, we will still live in a declarative free speech society; and just like today, even in that case we will of course have that freedom, but it will be clear to everyone that it cannot be unlimited - exactly as the state propaganda is currently serving it to us.

title: Massacre in Paris
text:
Last night there were several coordinated massacres in Paris where a handful of terrorists opened fire on crowds of people; the number of dead is tentatively estimated to be in the tens (allegedly there are more than a hundred victims). Although there were also bomb attacks, according to the available information, it seems that the vast majority of those murdered were shot (that is, they did not die in the explosion). The terrorists attacked several places at the same time (a full concert hall, a football stadium, a restaurant, generally places where people go for entertainment); by the shouts of "Allahu Akbar" it can be judged that these were Islamic radicals.
The reactions of politicians and the public are quite predictable - the French government has declared a state of emergency, closed the borders (both ways) and is preparing "further steps"; the public (mainly the Czech one) defines itself against Islam, for Konvička and Hample it will be a real feast, I assume that they are both happy without each other. From the opposite camp, the following thought came to me in particular (paraphrasing freely): "There are 6M Muslims living in France; if a tenth of them were radical jihadists, we would have 600k attackers; if only one percent of them were radicals, 60k people would attack; and even if it was only a tenth of a percent, it would mean 6k attackers."
The problem is that even those few terrorists were enough; and no matter how many measures we impose at the borders or anywhere else, we will never be able to eliminate them all. The only way to defend yourself is to increase the ratio of terrorists needed to murder a person; Yesterday, a group of goons attacked and killed dozens of people. Why? Because they had nothing to fire back. If nine out of ten people had one arm long, I expect the casualty-to-terrorist ratio would drop pretty damn low; quite possibly by order of magnitude - after all, the attacks took place in a place where the police were more or less around, under "more favorable" conditions, Breivik achieved an appalling ratio of 77:1 (these terrorists are around 10:1; and I am convinced that in an armed society they would not get past 2:1 in the long term).
Now around us we will hear calls for the banning of Islam and other totalitarian measures, which in the long run prove to be not very effective (often completely counterproductive); the only meaningful solution is an armed and free society, in which everyone can bring anyone they see fit to their land, but no one will be obliged to take care of them, give them anything, employ them, serve them in their business, etc., weapons will be freely available without state permission and ammunition will be freely available. Even in such a society, of course, there are goons who will go shoot people at a concert, but they simply don't kill that many.

title: Attacker with knife at school
text:
In Merced, California, another tragedy occurred at a school marked with a gun free zone sign; one of the students ran there in the morning with a knife (ergo he even respected the ban on firearms), stabbed five people, after which the police arrived and shot him dead. I have no reservations about the work of the police here, shooting the attacker is of course perfectly fine; but the question is, of course, why did he manage to attack five people? Benga had to get there first, obviously they can't be everywhere (and that's actually a good thing, as they usually do more harm than good; this example was an exception).
But what if the school was not a gun free zone? What if students or teachers could be armed at school? How many people would the attacker manage to stab? He only had a knife! One can certainly imagine that the first victim will be stabbed so suddenly that no one has time to react; before anyone recovers, perhaps the predator will attack someone else, maybe a third person at the most, if he chooses a great position to attack and everyone will be shocked. However, if almost everyone had a thunder stick at their waist, I can't imagine how a student could stab five people at school; quite possibly they would have stopped him before or after the first victim.
Uniformed monkeys with the best training simply must naturally react an order of magnitude (!) slower than armed humans on the spot; even most superheroes, if they existed, wouldn't be able to intervene in time! The attacker typically does not respect the gun free zone, but even if he accidentally does (perhaps this one was exemplary and only took a knife), the consequences are dire. The only real effect of a gun free zone is to disarm potential victims; it is something like a henhouse secured in such a way that, although no hen could escape, every marten had convenient access inside.
So why do gun free zones even exist? I'm afraid that the only reason is some kind of reality-detached dreams of prohibitionists, who imagine the functioning of the world in such a way that whatever the state prohibits, everyone will automatically respect it; these people absolutely do not realize that if someone wants to commit such a heinous crime as murder undoubtedly is, it will be difficult to stop him if he has to break some insignificant regulation in the process. To not see or ignore this trivial principle really requires an extreme level of blindness from state propaganda, according to which every problem can be solved by restricting freedom.

title: Referendum on leaving the EU
text:
"If elections could change anything, they would have been banned a long time ago," is a sign spray-painted on a building I pass about once a week. It is quite possible that Czech politicians also go there, because the government rejected the proposal of the Úsvit MPs (not that they were any better, but this time they happened to be right) to organize a referendum on leaving the EU; membership in the EU is said to be one of the Czech Republic's basic starting points in foreign policy, and withdrawal would be in sharp conflict with the interests of the state. Not that I don't consider democracy to be
crap
,
idolatry
a
factory for incompetence
, however, it's funny how even this can be suppressed when it suits the powers that be (which only confirms my words in the linked articles).
The Government Office has issued a statement for its ministers, in which it also points out that it is not entirely wise to hold a referendum on leaving the EU at a time of migration crisis; Well, sure, it's not entirely wise if we're interested in a specific result, but otherwise it's exactly the opposite - considering leaving the European Union makes the most sense precisely when a reason appears; waiting to make a decision until this has passed can be described as pure dementia (or in this case, calculation).
Polls show that if a referendum were held today, citizens would vote to leave the EU; and although it is not advisable to trust statistics that you do not falsify yourself, these seem quite credible to me, because the government itself is so afraid of such a referendum that it quite openly denies its subjects to express their opinion on this matter. Something similar could be expected, but I wouldn't see it so bleakly, because Eurosceptics are more or less on the right track; after all, as Gandhi said, "First they will ignore you; then they will laugh at you; then they will fight you; and in the end you will win."
In my opinion, our membership in the EU (and most likely the EU itself) is reaching its inevitable end; the question is how much longer it will last and how it will end - it would be good to get all four. If the dictates of the EU were to be replaced by a totalitarian government of monsters like Petr Hampl or Martin Konvička, we would not help ourselves much (rather the opposite); on the other hand, if we finally get it to a referendum (although not under the current government, but there will be others) initiated by someone who is not so extremely dangerous at the same time (which could easily be the fools from Úsvit, but also perhaps Svobodní), we can celebrate a partial victory.

title: Home freedom: intervention, sunk!
text:
Another state attack on our freedoms this time comes from a rather unexpected place; the Ministry of the Environment is coming up with a law that allows municipal authorities to inspect households that are drowning in all kinds of unapproved garbage. Inspectors (I ask myself, what kind of "people" can do this job; shame on them) will gain the right to enter private homes, poke around in other people's stoves, take samples of other people's ashes, which will then be analyzed in a laboratory; whoever refuses to let these pigs cross the threshold will be fined up to fifty thousand kroner (and the law does not say anything about the fact that the same control cannot follow with the same penalty).
Of course, the government promises that the checks will not be "bullying" (interestingly, probably no politician in history has ever introduced a law declaring that it would be "bullying"; but hey, somehow we've managed to look around and see one legal shenanigan next to another); of course, everyone is concerned only with our health, the health of our children, the health of our children's children and the health of their children's children. The social democrat Jiří Dienstbier assures us that controls will of course be the last resort after all other attempts at correction have failed; I can see it completely, because it is completely out of the question that it could hypothetically work like, for example, cashiering in the traffic police.
The Minister of the Environment, a member of the party of fools led by the big fool Babiš, Richard Brabec, honors his name and the party with the following statement (I quote): "Our opinion has been confirmed that the inviolability of housing is not unlimited." That's an opinion, sir! If I made a living by robbing houses, I would stop at the Brab family's house at night, whitewash them from the basement to the attic, and leave a message: "Dear Minister, I hereby confirm your opinion that the inviolability of the home is not unlimited." I completely understand that morons like Mr. Brabec hold these views, but I consider the state of society in which the person in question still boasts of such reprehensible views to be very sad.
"And what is the market solution?" As usual, I first emphasize that the free market cannot be predicted; however, if I had to guess, I expect that if someone was bothered by it, they would simply wait for the wind to blow the smoke from the neighbor's property over theirs, capture it, and analyze the smoke (repeated measurements from different locations would hopefully prove contamination). It is also worth noting that if the state did not waste resources, society would be richer and fewer people would have the motivation to burn with harmful materials. And finally, the most important thing - if in a free society someone broke into another's house and it was found that it was wrong, the attacker should compensate the victim; not that something similar couldn't apply even now (if the law isn't "bullying" after all, so what's the point, they certainly won't break into anyone's house), but of course Mr. Brabec doesn't want that, because it smells like the state should be responsible for its actions.

title: Even more social engineering!
text:
The Ministry of the Interior came up with another brilliant law, according to which everyone should have a permanent residence where they actually live; and whoever is caught not having it there will pay a fine of up to fifteen thousand crowns. The official justification for this fiddling for fiddling is the efficiency of public services provided and crisis planning in the event of natural disasters such as floods. According to the drafters of the law, three hundred thousand people live in the Czech Republic whose real residence does not correspond to their permanent residence; the interesting thing is, if they already know it anyway, why bother with such bureaucratic nonsense?
The proxies for the introduction of this law are truly absurd. Improving the quality of public services? Phew! Which of the private companies making money in a market way has access to such information as the state? And what would happen if any of them provided services as bad as the public ones? Well, she simply wouldn't make a living and was forced to quit. The reality is that
without the possibility of economic calculation
public services will always cost a fart no matter how much information the state coerces from its subjects; on the contrary
the free market can provide them better
even without unnecessary fuss.
And crisis planning? Well, years ago I was among the volunteers who helped firefighters evacuate people trapped in houses on the banks of the flooded Radbuza; and I can say that the very last thing anyone was interested in at that time was some unreliable information from unnecessary officials. And if it is a matter of more mass planning (capacity of various shelters and the like), then it must be taken into account that three hundred thousand people are three percent of the population; and are any reserves really planned so closely? After all, even just a normal commute to work will make many times greater differences between where people actually are and where they have permanent residence (for example, the Central Bohemian region becomes substantially depopulated during the day when people go to work in Prague, where there are therefore more of them to return at night).
In reality, this is nothing more than social engineering and other state-buzzing of citizens; the real reason will then sound something like this: "Ordnung muss sein."
In any case, I wonder how the state wants to enforce and control compliance with this law; will officials or uniformed monkeys go from house to house at night and find out if those who are reported to the office are present? Or will some more advanced tampering tools be deployed? In any case, we have a lot to look forward to...

title: Fluctuate the amount of social insurance
text:
The Ministry of Labor came up with a brilliant proposal for social insurance; the more children, the lower the amount one has to pay. The "logic" behind it is said to be that those who raise taxpayers should get a discount, because they also pay a decent amount to the state for insurance over the course of their lives; well... or not, because I can imagine all kinds of socially excluded families, who, among other things, acquire them as an additional "source of income", but not in the sense that they would take care of them in adulthood, but also because of the money that the state will give them for it, regardless of any tax breaks, or there are also people who simply have it on the hook, they don't use contraception much and whatever the devil wants, sometimes something is born.
There is, of course, a public debate about the issue, and it is similarly fruitless, as debates on similar topics typically tend to be in our democratic society; in particular, how many children a person has, how much they will or will not pay taxes, how much money they will pay to the state in total with their children, and the like. Some feel unfairly disadvantaged when the state is taxed for their decision not to have children, while others are themselves harmed because their descendants should pay for their pensions not only for them, but also for other people who have allowed themselves to have no children; the positions of both parties are understandable in a way, but they completely ignore the essence of the problem.
So what is the problem? Well, primarily in the fact that there is any social "insurance" at all; what if the state simply did not interfere and
he left everyone to take care of his own pension
in a way of your own choosing? Someone can save (whether for a mattress, or trust some institution... and of course bear risks that can be reduced, for example, by diversifying investments), someone else will raise productive children who will take care of him in his old age (of course, there are some risks here too, but that's life), someone else will start a prosperous company (the risk here is of course huge), or there will certainly be people who somehow combine the above methods.
That people will then lose their certainties? Yes and no. No one is ever completely certain (everyone can be hit by a car), but anyone who really cares can reduce the level of risk so that it is close to zero; of course it's not free, but it's certainly not even if it's provided by the state (which is probably even more expensive). The problem is that today the state orders everyone to buy (incredibly overpriced) "certainties", so those who want to invest their money differently (and take risks) are simply out of luck. Not to mention all the other disadvantages of the unfairness of this system, which are shown, for example, in discussions about this law - in fact, there is no way to set a "fair" amount of that "insurance" (especially as long as its amount depends proportionally on the income of the person concerned).

title: Compulsory kindergarten
text:
I consider the indoctrination of children, who are obliged to go to school, where the state propaganda of democracy and the establishment is hammered into their heads from an early age, to be one of the biggest pieces of crap by the state; but compulsory school attendance as we know it now is clearly not enough for the government - it came up with an amendment to the Education Act, according to which parents will be forced to send their preschool children to kindergarten for at least one more year.
