The coalition MPs gave the green light to the proposal, now the question is how the situation will develop further; but I'm afraid that this is another one of those laws that, even if they don't pass once or twice, they will eventually be pushed through, and then no one will ever repeal it.
However, it is interesting how the opposition argues against this law; it is said that it is not good for the state to constantly interfere in everything and change the rules of the game, they are unnecessary bureaucratic measures, it is not necessary to order something like that, education belongs to the family, not to the kindergarten, the parents are responsible for the healthy development of the child. Well then, I laugh at that, gentlemen of the opposition; Your words should be set in stone. The question, however, is whether these are truly seriously expressed opinions of those concerned, or whether it is simply that they do not like those who propose the law, so they would take any random argument that they could throw at them as a thank you.
If the opposition politicians really thought that the parents are responsible for the healthy development of the child, that their education belongs to the family and that the state should not constantly interfere in everything, then the question is why we actually have standard compulsory schooling, because their arguments are of course completely applicable against it; I wish they were taken seriously and not just as fluff for politicking. In fact, we have come so far that reasonable ideas seem so absurd to the powerful that when they say them themselves, they don't even think that there might be some truth in them...
An interesting question, by the way, is how much compulsory schooling will expand in the future; of course, it would be best to cancel it completely, but we probably won't see that. On the contrary, it will rather be extended, I just thought until now that the procedure would consist of artificially increasing the number of high school graduates and university students (which is already happening), until their numbers increase in this way to such an extent that the given type of education can be declared compulsory and almost no one will be against it, because such a regulation will in practice change the lives of only a small number of people; but the ways of the state are unfathomable, now they try it from the youngest.

title: How the hell he shot people
text:
Before Christmas 2014, a drunk policeman Pavel Koblížek burst into a disco, where he started waving his city card and demanding free entry for himself and two friends; such an incident beautifully shows how the uniformed monkeys perceive themselves - as superhumans, whom others have to accommodate and entertain them for free, because they are sycophants of the state. However, the gorillas in the club did not give a shit about the fizzle, they took it out in their teeth and bequeathed it to the appropriate limits; however, the person in question did not like it, because the subjects dare to oppose the henchmen of the powerful, so the police aggressive brute entered there again and sprayed it with tear gas.
This understandably pissed off the club's security and they decided to put the scumbag in the booth; so they began to chase him, which culminated in the person in question starting to shoot at them, killing one of them, wounding another, and the third preferred to run away. And this is where the accounts begin to diverge, because while the security claims that the victim simply turned around and started shooting, Fizl maintains that he only fired after the physical attack took place - he is said to have been knocked to the ground, kneed and strangled by the gorillas, as a result of which he feared for his life, so he fired in danger of his life. Well, the fact that the statements diverge is not so surprising.
Fízl, however, got away with the witness; he first testified that the security guard from the disco caught up with Koblížek and beat him up, but when asked directly if he saw it, he answered: "I think so, after all, when they chase someone, they jump on them, don't they?" Convincing, huh? Anyway, what I find far more interesting than the witness statement is the fact that there was no fizzle DNA on the gorillas' hands and no DNA from any of the victims was found on the body of the killer; how is that possible when he allegedly knelt on him and strangled him? Another remarkable fact is that, although the city policeman shot with his right hand someone who was allegedly kneeling on him and strangling him, he hit the person in question from the other side (that is, in the victim's right side, which would correspond to the shooter's left hand).
Here I would be very interested in the motivation of the witness to testify as he did; does he really think he saw what he said he saw? And what about the strange wording about the fact that when someone chases someone, they also jump on them? I understand that it was dark, there was confusion, it was difficult to find your way around, the statements logically diverge. Or was there any influence at the gym in favor of a colleague? Hard to say. However, DNA is DNA and it is difficult to shoot someone in the hip with one hand. Even if that wasn't the case, what about the aspect of a drunken punk who walks into a disco and demands free entry on the basis of some punk card?

title: Schoolboys - immigrant henchmen; or the state?
text:
An interesting thing happened in Germany; the sun-loving teachers of a school "volunteered" their eighth-grade students to clean up after some immigrants and make their beds. Officials from the ministry have the whole event in the "voluntary" column, but the eighth graders themselves say otherwise, and I personally believe them; even if I set aside my policy of never believing what the government tells me (although in this case it's a foreign government), I can't quite imagine an eighth grade class where everyone volunteers to make their beds for immigrants (I can understand that there will be a few, because sitting in a desk all day isn't fun either, but the whole class seems extremely unlikely to me; not to mention that at least one of the girls made participation mandatory).
As expected, Islamophobic people (of course also here in the Czech Republic) can go crazy because of this, they call the whole incident outrageous, and on social networks you can read threats of violence to the principals of their children's schools, if something similar occurs to them; I personally agree with the Islam killers here, the whole situation is completely intolerable and I consider it outrageous that children are modern-day slaves and servants of someone depending on what their teachers (or ministerial officials) feel like doing. Whoever wants to help should help in their free time and at their own expense, organize it themselves, but don't let the schools get involved.
However, I hope that the Islamo-killers will hold this view even if they are not refugees; he problem is far from just that the students served migrants when some multi-culti fool tried to give them some strange message, but in compulsory schooling as such. While democratic politicians talk about freedom with such fervor, the reality of compulsory schooling is that children are locked up somewhere for a significant part of their lives, regardless of what they themselves or their parents think about it. It's perfectly fine to be concerned about solar propaganda, but it's not fine to simply replace it with another one; the only correct solution is not to prescribe to the schools what they should teach and let the parents choose the educational facilities that suit their child.
In principle, there is no difference at all between an institution that compulsorily educates children to love refugees and an institution that compulsorily educates children to love democracy; it's just a matter of what one agrees with and what one's opinion is, however immigrant-hating parents should have exactly the same options as democracy-hating parents (not having their children indoctrinated against their beliefs). Let every parent teach his child what he sees fit; the state should not have the slightest right to interfere in any way and decide what is right and what is wrong for the child.

title: Hell is going through the city!
text:
Prague: The police were filling their own pockets with fines!
Random checks by the police officers in Prague revealed fraudsters who were already falsifying block fines by giving the fined person a block for a litre, they also took it from him, but they made it look like the fine was only for a kilo at the forgery. There they also found a genius who simply swindled a hundred thousand out of the cash register without bothering with any forgery; he just saw the money, so he took what he cared about any consequences - I really wonder what kind of thinker this must have been. And the boss set an example for them: From the owner of a car repair shop, where the city had its cars serviced (including those Hummers bought a few years ago that were vitally necessary and subsequently sold again at a loss), he took five percent for the fact that the person in question won the selection process, which made the uniformed monkey a mega and a quarter.
It's also funny what came out of the PČR, which is investigating, in connection with how the police officers cheated with the ID cards:
They were said to be using penalty slips that did not have an amount pre-printed on them, so it was always necessary to fill them in by hand; it's supposed to work in such a way that the monkey writes the amount in the pad, which the monkey hands over to the person being fined, while she remains with a copy (which she then hands over to the processing plant), where everything is transcribed using a copier that the constable inserts between the pads.
And now the funny part: the police of the Czech Republic cannot reveal how exactly the monkeys committed fraud.
Seriously? How about a detective story? I understand that the genius who pinched the hundred liters without trying to disguise it in any way probably won't figure it out from the description above, but without wanting to overestimate the intelligence of those uniformed demented people, can anyone else still not understand from the given information how to carry out the fraud?
Beroun: Sixteen out of eighteen police officers accused of abusing the powers of an official!
The town hall made it known that although it respects the presumption of innocence, it is also looking for new police officers; while their boss resigned from his post immediately after it broke. Something tells me they must be innocent and their boss is sure of it. Mocipans from the town hall shout that the city cannot function without police officers; from my point of view, it looks more like a fear of not finding out that it would work much better without them, which would make it very difficult to assert that they are actually needed... something like the Hummers and hovercrafts in Prague, which were also absolutely necessary, before it turned out that actually, what a surprise, it is a little overkill for conquering Prague's roads after all.
Otherwise, the cities of Beroun basically turned it into crap - they tolerated wrong parking for selected citizens. I'm absolutely sure that similar - and worse - things happen all over the place; and the advantage is that the smaller the town, the better it gets through, and it is precisely in small towns that have five and a half monkeys in uniform that a similar accusation (especially if proven) can paralyze whole towns.
Don't you happen to know about something?

title: At the eaten shop
text:
Do you also, dear readers, miss the queues for bananas and are downright bored of the damn bourgeois market, where you can buy goods practically at any time, even on holidays? If so, I bring great news: Our noble deputies will save us, because no stranger's blood flows! They prepared an amendment to the law, according to which most stores with an area of more than two hundred square meters must be closed on holidays. I am especially jealous of the ethical genius who, on the basis of certainly wise considerations, established the fairest possible limit of the area of shops that will have to close under the threat of violence.
MPs from the KDU-ČSL informed us that they welcome this proposal as a contribution to a better combination of work and family life. What about the fact that people do not buy, what about the fact that workers who already want to work will not earn, and those who have no family will sit at home on holidays instead of working for extra pay. But why should MPs be interested in what problems they caused to whom with their demented laws? They bear no responsibility, they can do whatever they want, approve any bullshit, no one will ever force them to answer, after all we elected them in democratic elections, so what?
Although some people (probably in vain) protest against this, virtually all arguments on the subject are utilitarian; almost no one will stop to note that the primary and fundamental immorality of this law is not who ever buys, but the threat of violence by the state against anyone who does not submit to this disgusting will. It is also remarkable how extremely far removed this completely nonsensical regulation is from all conceivable arguments for the necessity of the existence of the state: "We need laws so that we don't kill each other here." Well sure; and this one above all! Without it, there would be a complete zombie apocalypse.
Please, let's put an end to these absurdities and bullshit; let's spread awareness and explain to every decent person that by electing such creatures we will eventually get to a state where everything will be regulated by law... not that we are particularly far from it now. If legislative development continues in this way, a generation will come which will invent laws regulating various areas of human life simply for the reason that they are not yet regulated; because it will be completely normal that absolutely everything must be subject to some legal norm, violent coercion will become an integral part of absolutely all aspects of human lives.

title: Reflective vests for pedestrians
text:
The new road law is a piece of crap par excellence; D-FENS already wrote about it in detail in his
article
, which unfortunately describes a harsh reality. However, I would like to deal with one of its parts in a little more detail; if the law passes in its current version, it imposes on pedestrians outside the municipality the obligation to wear reflective elements, for example a vest. Why and how demented the regulation is, he discussed in his text D-FENS, however, I am also afraid that, among other things, with this law we are opening a Pandora's box from which nothing good will come; not only that, once a law is established, it is rarely repealed, but this is the regulation of an entirely new area.
However much motorists have been booed for many years (and it's still getting worse), pedestrians have so far remained relatively untouched by the authorities and their henchmen; and this is the first claw stuck in their freedom. And unfortunately, this is how the totalization of each area begins; first comes an inconspicuous law that is "clearly there only for our safety", and later more and more come, because once something is already regulated, it seems "normal" to everyone that the legislation regulates it more and more. Not infrequently some even use one regulation as an argument for another; for example, the ban on smoking in restaurants is defended by the fact that the owners already have to comply with hygiene regulations anyway, so one more ban will not upset them anymore.
I can very well imagine that when people get used to the mandatory reflective elements for pedestrians outside the municipality after dark, the uniformed monkeys will start to enforce this ban, many will babble at first, but there will be more and more people who will explain to them that the law is the law; the media will begin to blur the accidents of those who did not wear reflective vests, which will create a social demand for someone to "finally clean things up", gradually disappearing the discussion about the meaning of the given law and it will begin to be taken as automatically correct. Then there will be mentions of accidents that could have been prevented if the reflective elements had at least some prescribed size, or the decree will also apply to municipalities.
The next generation will already be born into a world where pedestrians are regulated, of course, so they will start inventing more absurdities; perhaps we will see pedestrian permits (after all, recently someone wrote in Stok about a person who is seriously inventing a points system for pedestrians; and that is just one example), mandatory tests on knowledge of regulations and it is hard to say what else. And if I live to see it and write an article in thirty years about the fact that pedestrians should not be regulated at all, people will tap their foreheads, what kind of crazy anarchist I am, because of course it is completely clear to everyone that there must be some kind of regulation, without it it simply wouldn't work.

title: A teacher in a niqab teaches seventh graders!
text:
Trutnov teacher Zuzana Růžičková took her history class, where she was supposed to teach about Islam, somewhat unconventionally; she came in front of her students wearing a niqab and lent them a chador, hijab and burqa to try on. The experiential lesson was even ended with a Muslim prayer towards Mecca, in which the students were supposed to participate as well. As could be expected, the whole event caused a huge stir, especially on the Internet, where some support the lessons conceived in this way, because students remember the material better, while others sharply criticize the teacher's actions, because they perceive it as part of the Islamization of society; some, on the other hand, condition their approval on the fact that the person in question teaches about other religions in a similar style.
However much the overwhelming majority of commenters - actually I have not seen a single exception - deal with Islam and a specific incident in connection with what Zuzana Růžičková demonstrated, I personally perceive the problem in a completely different way; in my opinion, it is not at all a question of whether similar behavior is okay or not, but rather that there is simply no answer to this question - for some parents this approach to their children is acceptable, for others it is completely unacceptable; and it is impossible to determine who is "right", as the demands of both groups of parents on how their children should or should not be taught are perfectly justified.
So does the problem have a solution? But of course! Laissez-faire, laissez-passer, let us act, let the free people establish schools in which they may teach whatever they think fit, regardless of what the civil servants think; let parents choose at their own discretion which school to send their children to. There is no right answer to the question of how Islam should be taught, nor how students should learn anything else, because everyone is different; and if we strive for uniformity at all costs, we will inevitably commit many fatal mistakes in those dearest to us—our children. Allowing every historian in the Czech Republic to teach about Islam while wearing a niqab is not right; but banning them isn't any better!
Unfortunately, the government doesn't even want to hear about any liberalization of education, because schools are the most effective tool of state propaganda; and whoever thinks I'm exaggerating, let them find the White Paper, the National Education Program and focus on civic competences - there the obligation of every teacher to indoctrinate their students is written in black and white (I also taught at a private gymnasium at one time; and because my conversations with students were directed against state propaganda, I had some problems because of this). I consider state propaganda aimed at young children to be one of the greatest evils in our society; please let's try it
to change
!

title: Even more mandatory liability
text:
The Ministry of Finance is going to hell!
While the owners of all vehicles from the motor vehicle register currently have to pay compulsory insurance (which, among other things, also applies to various museum pieces that have not driven on the road for years), Babiš's ministry proposes that there should be an obligation to pay also for motor machines that drive off public roads; the intention is to force owners of garden tractors, go-karts, mini-karts and the like to pay and massively cash out.
The reason for this whole hurrah action is the befel from the European Union, which wants to force all member countries to accept this stupid law; the impetus for this European madness is the case from Slovenia, where someone managed to run over a man with a small tractor on his own property. And here we see another amazing effect of globalization within the EU: In Slovenia, a peasant runs over a peasant, some lobby of insurance companies is added, the efforts of dobrosers for a perfectly safe world, and lo and behold, a complex law affecting over half a billion people is in the world. Thousands of politicians and officials jump around, long hours of time that could be used meaningfully are wasted, clouds of people are buzzing... and why? In reality, for nothing, after all, no reasonable person can even expect that such a law will change something for the better!
However, the comrades from the GDR made a mistake in something; because they forgot that motorized vehicles include, among other things, wheelchairs powered by an electric motor. Until now, the law on compulsory liability did not apply to them, because on the one hand they were not in the motor vehicle register and on the other hand they did not drive on public roads; well now... the law is the law after all. Can you imagine a city that stops wheelchair users and demands their vehicle documents? Such a thing will probably be stupid for them too, because then they would be smeared by the media; but perhaps there will be some downright conscious monkey in uniform who will be the perfect arm of justice.
And you know what? I might even support such a law; indeed, if it is really introduced in its current form, it will show in all its nakedness the mockery and absurdity of the legislative framework in which we are forced to live. Every law that people choose to disobey en masse is a small step towards the state being eventually ignored as a whole.

title: Straw talk show: no smoking
text:
When I sometimes feel that I haven't heard a good dose of various clichés for a long time, I turn on the popular talk show "Máte slovo", where Michaela Jílková invites all kinds of exotics (after all, I've already had the honor) to talk to conformist politicians or other representatives of the state, who either talk condescendingly to their subjects or bark at each other like little brats; in both cases, incredible things fall out of them, often illustrated by their acquaintances in the audience (as a guest, you can bring some other people with you). And what the hell, I just watched the recording of the discussion about banning smoking in restaurants; as expected it was appalling.
Except for a few reasonable (and desperately lonely) inputs from sane people who rightly pointed out that the focus of the "smoking ban" topic is not so much the smoking as the ban, the vast majority of the time only the harmfulness of cigarettes was addressed; arguments about whether cigarettes are harmful, how much harm they do, how many people die as a result of smoking, how cigarettes actually help, how harmful they are compared to exhaust gases, how smoke spreads (by the way, we learned that just like urine in a swimming pool, because such a fundamental topic could not remain untouched), when it is economically advantageous for the state to let its subjects die, or that smoking is prohibited in the Czech Television studio, but there anyway someone smoked, although there must be rules, and the bombardier until the end turned out to be a certain gentleman in the audience who came up with the fact that science is just lies, cigarettes are good for health, which he proved by the fact that he has smoked all his life and is perfectly healthy, not to mention that last year there was a kind of shot on the news on Nova about the healing effects of cigarettes, for which he earned the condescending pained smile of a social engineer convinced that only she knows best, what is best for everyone, or a certain politician who advised businessmen that the smoking ban will pay off for them, so the state actually provides them with a service... the voice of the people rag!
We were also treated to rhetorical magic on the topic of freedom: "You fight for freedom? But I have the same freedom, and I have the right to go to any restaurant I want and breathe the healthy air there."
However, the following sentence became the most compelling argument: "Those pub owners can't do whatever they want in their business anyway, they have to comply with hygiene standards; and if the state can regulate this, then smoking too."
Here, unfortunately, I have to admit that for those who approve of state interventions to this extent, this argument is fatal, because the smoking ban can of course be seen as another hygiene norm.
I sincerely regretted that there was no one there to explain why the state should not interfere at all; however, I am afraid that people would look at him in the same way as the gentleman who is said to be healthy only because of his lifelong smoking.
The saddest part of the whole thing seems to me how few people care at all about any liberty or private property of the tavern-keeper; that already seems secondary and unimportant, the whole discussion is basically only about whether and how much cigarettes harm, whether smokers pay off economically for the state, and the "right to a non-smoking pub" is already something as self-evident as the fact that in a democracy everyone can decide on the property of others and it is right.

title: Poor cop!
text:
Jiří Vítek, a police unionist (hey, that's my phrasing, dream job) received a letter containing the whining of a uniformed monkey whose job it was to be a watchman in a refugee camp; strangely enough, the subject of whining was not that the person in question can't even look in the mirror because of his job, because he's become such a pig that he's ashamed of it, but the poor thing is said to be humiliating to look after the refugees, who are already rolling in their beds and laughing at him, while he poor thing has to look after them outside in the winter and no one even brought him food to the gymnasium, which, think for yourself, is explained lawlessness - a poor policeman who, when he finds himself somewhere without food, orders a pizza and thereby descends to the level of an ordinary citizen.
Abbreviated whine transcript:
[blah blah]
appalling situation that is happening to the citizens of this country
[blah blah]
refugees arrive and arrive in really very decently equipped premises
[blah blah]
new beds, tables, wardrobes, bedding
[blah blah]
is trying in every possible way to meet even the smallest needs of these migrants
[blah blah]
a police officer will serve 14 hours of guard duty between the fences in 24 hours
[blah blah]
food was not provided, there is no shop or other catering option in the village, at three o'clock in the morning I was woken up by the cold from sleeping on chairs, even though I was dressed
[blah blah]
I have been working for the police for twenty years, I never thought that together with my colleagues, I would ever experience such a humiliation for all of us, when we, as citizens of this country, frozen, exhausted and half-starved with poor facilities, look through the windows at people who have broken the laws of this country, at people who enjoy above-standard care and hospitality
[blah, blah.]
One would almost cry; and more than one has already shed a virtual tear in the comments of the situation on the Internet. It just seems to me that these people are forgetting who is really who and which group is on which side of the fence. All in all, there are illegal immigrants going to Germany all over the territory of the Czech Republic, they mostly don't want to stay there, which is quite mutual, because the majority of the original inhabitants don't want them here either, so an optimist might cheer that there was a beautiful agreement; but the footbridge's fault - the state intervened in the matter, they accidentally catch and close the benga, which creates a paradoxical situation where one group of people who do not want to be in a certain territory, whose inhabitants typically do not want them there either, are detained in this territory by another group of people who whine that the resulting situation humiliates them. I would not hesitate to call it a typical state solution!
I am certainly not a supporter of quotas or mandatory feeding of refugees or any type of "state aid to the needy" (whoever wants to, let him help, but in his own way and for his own sake); on the other hand, I absolutely refuse to detain people anywhere just because they don't have documents and are here illegally. A uniformed monkey, who participates in all this for a share of the protection money called taxes, is a pig to me; and if on top of that she whines, complains about the too good conditions of the prisoners, complains to the unions and feels humiliated (yet she continues to do the job), she is also a cowardly pig.

title: Who can bet and how?
text:
I like to bet a lot, always have been; as a small child I used to bet with my sister, later with my friends (and still do), I love poker, I sometimes bet on the formula and actually almost whenever something difficult to predict appears, I take it as an opportunity to play - not necessarily for money and never for large amounts, but I just enjoy it; I like to win and sometimes I actually lose. However, our rulers feel that this is not right, so they set out to regulate this activity and once again poke their noses into things they have nothing to do with; after all, they know best what is best for us.
Fascinating about the whole thing are two clowns at the moment – Kalousek and Babiš; the two have absolutely nothing to blame, the first-named is an expert in borrowing, then winning over voters by sounding the alarm about the debt, in order to get room to chop more debts, while the second is a master in milking subsidies and forcing his company's products on drivers through state power. When they both realized that they could find enough dirt on the other, they began to dig into each other's pasts and throw the discovered shit at each other like two harrants; the resulting situation would be laughable if it weren't for crying.
Most recently, one buffoon accused another of being prosecuted for not wanting to ban online gambling; jester number two again claimed that it didn't happen, so the production of more fart balls could successfully start again. This time, however, they embellished it a bit more - they bet ten million on which of them was right; personally, I consider Kalouska to be the winner of the bet, however, I assume that the result will be nothing, because both will confidently claim that they won until the whole thing blows up. I have nothing against their actions as such, I would even support it if their income did not come either directly from the state or from a company favored by the state.
But I find it utterly ridiculous that the object of the ten million bet lies in the anti-gambling laws by which these crooks want to restrict other people how and why they gamble; where does the godliness in them come from? I personally consider betting to be fun, that's why I enjoy it, but I wouldn't dream of restricting someone in such an activity; the two agree that the subjects should be regulated in betting, but would they themselves set an example of this belief? Not by chance. Laws are for the plebs after all.

title: On the Power of Propaganda and the Word "Strike Call"
text:
I write very often about indoctrination in public education, which I consider to be the "root of evil", because from a very young age each of us is exposed to brutal government propaganda and incredible brainwashing on the subject of the need for central authority; young children's thinking is distorted and words are given meanings that suit collectivists, while schools try to stigmatize and dismiss individualism. In "civic education" (!) subjects, teachers typically pretend to impartially explain to children individual ways of managing and functioning of society, but in reality it is an advertisement for democracy (and some teachers don't even try to hide it anymore). How are children supposed to make up their own minds when they are told from an early age that democracy is good, while everything else is evil?
We can have long debates about the depth and impact of this indoctrination, although it is probably impossible to measure anything like it; however, I would like to share a personal experience of the importance of who first assigns meaning to a word. Of course I was also indoctrinated in my youth that democracy is good, medical care should be "free", speculators are evil and we must obey the laws regardless of whether they are good or bad; however much I've re-evaluated my views in a completely fundamental way throughout my life, I still don't find it strange to constantly see these terms around me used the way the establishment wants them to be - I don't agree, but it's not strange. Nevertheless, one word escaped my manipulators - "strike trouble"; I was simply completely unaware of its existence for the first twenty-two years or so of my life. I was first introduced to it by Walter Block in his book "Defending the Indefensible", where he described strike-callers in a unequivocally positive way and explained their benefits; since then I haven't heard (or at least didn't register) the word again for years.
Until a few days ago... I was watching some series on the second monitor, although "watched" is a strong word, I was more like playing it as a soundtrack; one of his works was precisely about the strikers, who were depicted in it in a negative sense of the word - and I must say that it was very strange. I've seen speculators portrayed in a negative light in many movies and series, not to mention good cops (or maybe Batman as a whole: a positive hero who constantly initiates violence and violates the property rights of drug dealers, who are only satisfying the needs of their customers, but the comics portray them as evil); do I agree with such a view of the matter? Not in the least. Do I look weird? Not a bit, not distracting at all. I find the depiction of the strikers as wretches stilted and distracting, grabbing my attention more than the plot itself; I think a statist might feel the same way if he saw a series about the evil Batman cracking down on good drug dealers.
Can you imagine what our society would look like if children were not brainwashed by propaganda and delusions? What would happen if concepts like freedom, free market, state, police, solidarity, redistribution, capitalism, socialism and many others were explained to them for the first time without propaganda gibberish? How much better would the world be if children found a story where a positive hero initiates violence against free-trading people really weird? What would a world be like in which almost everyone saw the government as a legalized mafia and despised not only specific politicians, but above all their posts themselves?

title: Soldiers just follow orders...
text:
Mass murderers in the military are often excused as "just following orders", so they can actually kill and not take responsibility for their actions; I, on the other hand, claim that if some people voluntarily join an organization in which they have to obey orders, it is indeed their business, but they cannot then make excuses for it and pretend that someone else is to blame for the negative consequences of their decision, because it was only them who signed up for it. The last time I led a discussion on this topic was regarding the bombed MSF hospital; although most people do not approve of this action of the US military, they do not attribute the blame for it to the pilots, but to their superiors (I am not saying that they are not guilty; only that this does not stop the pilots from being murderers).
Do you think roughly this?
A pilot only obeys orders, he must always do what his superiors tell him, disobeying orders is shot in the army; it is not possible for a soldier to ask his superior for the reasons before carrying out an order, war simply does not work. Moreover, nowadays the pilots can no longer even see what they are actually bombing, they only get coordinates from the commander, at that speed they cannot evaluate what they are actually dropping the bombs on; they have no way to prevent the destruction of an unwanted target if the guide makes a mistake.
Then surely you will agree with this as well, or not?
A suicide bomber just obeys orders, he must always do what his superiors tell him to do, disobeying an order is shot in the terrorist cell; it is not possible for a terrorist to ask his superior for the reasons before carrying out an order, war simply does not work. Moreover, nowadays suicide bombers no longer assemble their bombs themselves, they get them from other terrorists and do not vouch for their reliability; they have no way of preventing the destruction of an unintended target if the bomb maker makes a mistake.
Does any of the above excuse the "pawns" in terrorist cells? If not, why should it excuse the soldiers?
If the "rank and file terrorist" (not just his superiors) is guilty of his atrocities, then the rank and file soldier must also be guilty if he joined the army voluntarily; both have joined a hierarchical organization that does not tolerate disobedience, meaning that either they are both responsible for their actions, or neither. Any normal person will understandably condemn a terrorist, even if he was "just following orders"; unfortunately, many people will not condemn the soldier for the same, because the state has brainwashed them as part of its propaganda by saying that people in the army can kill and it is okay.

title: Internet censorship
text:
The internet is too free, so politicians have been figuring out how best to chain it for years; now they have an excuse - hate speech! The possibilities of their censorship are discussed in Luxembourg by the ministers of justice of the member countries of the European Union; and our Pelican is no exception. They are said to have agreed that the spread of hatred is unacceptable, so now they are just looking for ways to do it best; as always, some freedom is at the bottom of their interests.
Czech European Commissioner Věra Jourová made it known that it is necessary to find that fine line when it is no longer about freedom of expression, but about clear support for hatred; seriously? Does such a line exist? It can be compared to declaring that there is a need to find that fine line when it is no longer a food but a steak; after all, in the same way that steak is food, clearly supporting hatred is of course free expression! Ms. Jourová should realize that freedom of speech is not only about letting reasonable, wise, educated and truthful people express their decently presented opinions, but above all about how we stand up to evil, snarky, stupid or hypocritical liars when they rudely and recklessly present their insults and slander.
"We should deal with lying on the Internet," says Czech Minister of Justice Robert Pelikán. Sure, but how to solve it? Who will judge what is true and what is false? Shall we set up a committee for this? Or will we ban lying and anyone can be prosecuted for every lie? How can this possibly end?
According to Pelikán, false messages on Facebook look very credible; good, but who is preventing you, Mr. Pelikán, from crawling (or letting your sprouts crawl) that Facebook and setting it straight? Probably no one, but why would you waste your time (plus the risk of being ridiculed) when you can forcibly silence those whose opinions you don't like, right?
Censorship is another path to totalitarianism; because as soon as we work towards some more massive censorship of the Internet (we have already worked on it on a small scale), then of course there will be no reason to censor only hate speech, there will also be clouds of other things that someone declares to be harmful, dangerous, incorrect and should be banned altogether. In a few decades, the discussion about whether to censor the Internet will no longer be successful, but it will be "clear" to everyone that yes, the only question will be what exactly... and if the libertarians object to it, all parties will silence them again, saying that we of course need censorship, because without it "it wouldn't work", we just need to "find some reasonable limit".

title: PČR prides itself on buzzing
text:
On weekend evenings, the Police of the Czech Republic distinguished themselves once again - they carried out a large raid against minors with a non-zero blood alcohol level. In practice, of course, this meant, for example, detaining a seventeen-year-old girl just because she had 0.69 per mille in her blood (which is about a glass of wine), while her friend a year older was fined for buying her an alcoholic drink; after the teenagers were taken to the prison, the uniformed brute called their parents, who had to come for them and were forced to pay additional fines to the authorities. In addition to the parents, the bartenders also had to pay, and proceedings were initiated against the businesses.
What was it all for? Well, the uniformed monkeys have been messing around in the media and making a lot of money; The whole event apparently had no other meaning, because how could such a fuss help those children or their parents? That like if they catch them once, they won't do it again? But come on! What late-night drinking teenager would come to some self-reflection from a similar experience and not just use it as a good story to make fun of in front of friends? On the contrary, many people were fined, sniffed and booed completely unnecessarily; how much time did it all take on all sides? But why should the state be interested in the lost time of its subjects?
Aside from the time and money lost, even from a human point of view this action is completely indefensible; the state has set some absurd (and apparently high) age limit by which it judges adulthood, completely ignoring, of course, that people are different and everyone is an adult at different times. Among the boozers there were certainly quite a few individuals who, although they were not yet eighteen, were already capable of taking responsibility for their own actions; kidnapping such people and releasing them only for a ransom from their parents is nothing but endless crap regardless of what the law says about the whole thing, because even that is made up of goons.
So I say to the police of the Czech Republic: "Screw your ass!"
To those who support the action, I say: "Screw your ass!"
To parents who are worried about their children, my message is: "Raise or babysit your children or hire someone to do it; if you want the state to do it, then fuck off!"
No, seriously… mind your own business and leave me alone; I seriously don't want to pay anyone demented uniformed babysitters, which I only do because I'm forced to do so by threat of violence.

title: The law is the law...
text:
Sometimes a man obeys laws more or less by accident, because they just so happen to correspond to his beliefs; I suppose we typically don't kill and rob our neighbors not because it's codified somewhere, but because we think such behavior is wrong. Often one obeys laws simply because the price they would have to pay for breaking them is too high; I expect that we can easily cross a red light on an apparently empty street, but not if there is some uniformed monkey standing against us. But how do we act in the event that state power is not within reach, but the law orders us to do something stupid?
Unfortunately, it is not uncommon for me to come across the opinion that the law is right to obey because it is simply the law; and even if the person in question violates it, for example, in similar moments, he perceives this behavior as wrong and places it in the "should not" category. Paradoxically, however, the vast majority of such thinking individuals have no problem admitting that the government and parliamentary staff are typically crooks; but what is the point of obeying their laws?
Aren't politicians among the last whose opinions should dictate what is right and what is wrong? Imagine you have a moral dilemma; will you go and ask the Minister of the Interior, for example, what he thinks is right? Or if, hypothetically, two hundred MPs issued some kind of statement (not by law, they would just publish it) and they all signed it, would you think that it is right and you should live by it? If not, then what difference does it make if the exact same people make it law?
I fear that despite the paragraphs above that clearly show the pointlessness of laws, as a result of the state propaganda that all citizens are brainwashed from elementary school anyway, most people will still be convinced that obeying laws is simply right because it is right and because they are laws; while breaking them is wrong because it is simply wrong and because they are laws.

title: Salaries of celebrities, salaries of angels
text:
I don't even know how many times I've read or heard a debate on the same topic that was brought up again by two young people; parts of their conversation from the next table could not be overheard - I'll take the liberty of paraphrasing what was bothering them: "How is it possible that top model Kate Moss is making millions while doctors and firefighters, who are far more beneficial to society, are not?"
I'll try to give a short answer: "All the doctors and firemen combined are certainly more beneficial to society than Kate Moss; and together they earn more. While each one of them is quite obviously not that beneficial to society."
How do I know? Well, quite simply: If that were the case, they would make more money than that model on the open market; the truth is that we don't have a direct free market here, because the state distorts it, however, even from what we can see, it can be judged that an ordinary doctor or fireman would not reach Kate Moss's salary even in the free market.
How to determine someone's "usefulness to society"? Most likely, a kind of aggregation of benefits for all members of this society. But how to measure such a thing? A fireman can be extremely useful to those he saves from the flames (and their loved ones), Kate Moss will probably be less useful to them, on the other hand, her appearance will probably make far more people happy than the fireman will ever manage to save. Thus one will do something extremely valuable for a few individuals, while the other will do something probably less valuable, but for clouds of people; how to compare
Since it was a rhetorical question, I'll reveal the solution: Ludwig von Mises proved that you simply can't compare anything like that; the only way to know who is more useful is to have people voluntarily pay them for their services, with whoever earns more being clearly more beneficial. There is no other meaningful measure.
Seeing Kate Moss probably represents far less pleasure for the vast majority of us than being pulled out of flames and saved by a particular firefighter; on the other hand, the first of the listed situations occurs significantly more often. Payments for various services are then the best indicator of our preferences, not reflections on the topic of who benefits how.

title: When ISIS jumps out of a window, must we too?
text:
Lately, I keep coming across Islamophobic arguments in the sense that if "we" are not allowed to do something "at their place", we should also ban "them here", for example:
"In Muslim countries, our women are not allowed to wear bikinis, so we should ban burqas here."
"We are also not allowed to build churches in Muslim countries, so we should ban mosques here."
I do not want to dwell on the fact that this is not entirely true, for there are considerable differences between Muslim countries; however, I would like to point out the absolute stupidity of this argument even if it were true.
If we start from the assumption that Islam is evil, suppresses freedom, human dignity and is basically the worst violent barbarism in the world, then perhaps we can agree that it is not exactly an example suitable for following. How is it possible to hate something or someone and attribute the worst imaginable qualities to it or him, but then use it or him in your argument as an example worth following? It's probably as stupid as labeling Babiš as a reprehensible thief, but then going to steal with the justification that Babiš does it too!
A completely different - but no less stupid - argument then reads: "Even if a Muslim says he doesn't want to kill us, he actually wants to, because Takiya allows him to lie." Erm... not that she doesn't allow it, but is it technically impossible to lie without permission? Have you never met anyone who would lie without explicit permission? The permission to lie has no meaning, for it is implicitly possessed by all men in the world; that is, with the exception of those whose brain damage does not allow them to lie. Moreover, there is another interesting paradox: Taqiya allows Muslims, among other things, to claim that they are not Muslims, ergo anyone can be a Muslim claiming to be not a Muslim; it follows that there is no way to know if a completely arbitrary person is not lying according to Takiya.
What do these two completely different arguments have in common? Well, both are so extremely stupid that they require the user to turn off critical thinking entirely; and unfortunately we can hear them around us quite often, which says something about the state of society. If you meet someone who uses these arguments, it is a clear indicator that the person has switched from rational thinking to instinctive and emotional reasoning, ergo unable to accept a logical argument that contradicts their current beliefs; and if you happen to use such (or similar) arguments yourself, dear readers, I believe that this is a sign for self-questioning.

title: And the pork again...
text:
Seventy-five years ago there was a concentration camp in Lety na Písecko; currently someone runs a piggery there.
The situation suits me personally, because I love pork belly, bacon, sausages and breakfast sandwiches, while I absolutely hate Nazis and concentration camps; however, there are also those among us who are no longer satisfied with the current situation, as they do not find the piggery appropriate and would rather welcome a memorial in its place.
I totally understand that different people have different priorities; however, I find it absolutely disgusting that every time the "pig sty" issue is brought up again (and it happens every few years), all sorts of activists emerge to sign something and try to convince politicians to fix it. Now seventy-three MEPs have signed a similar appeal, not to mention politicians and activists from twenty-two countries.
Why do I find their behavior despicable?
Well, no one prevents them from organizing a collection and buying the pork from the owner; he is permitted to sell, though of course not to give away his possessions.
However, they don't want to give anything of their own, they only know how to sign and forcibly force others to pay for it instead of them - shame!
Anyone can protest and play on emotions; however, sacrificing something to achieve your goals is another matter.
After all, how do you know whether it is better if there is a piggery or a memorial in Lety? How to compare two such extremely different things?
On the one hand it is food, on the other hand it is an ideal. What should take precedence?
There is one perfectly ingenious and perfectly just way of deciding such a thing: Let the people act; what would they rather willingly spend their money on? If for a belly, let there be a piggery in Lety; if for a monument, they can buy the area and start building. It's as simple as that.
If politicians get involved and force people to build something that would not otherwise have been created and that they would not willingly spend their money on, something that is beneficial to society will be exchanged for something that is less beneficial; and there is no other way of finding out what men really think beneficial than to let them act freely.

title: Fair justice and ass
text:
Almost every time, when I declare somewhere that I consider the state judiciary to be supremely unfair and extremely immoral, since even this function of the current state can, in my opinion, be far better performed by free individuals in the free market, I come across - in addition to the classic "that wouldn't work" argument - the argument that we need state courts in order to prevent situations in which one of the litigants is in some way related to the judge...
...perhaps if one of the litigants worked for the same organization as the judge; that would be appalling, wouldn't it?
Well, it wasn't that long ago that the cops needed to give a motorcyclist a bit of a boost, which resulted in an accident that left him injured on the ground, whereupon a uniformed monkey jumped out of the car and started kicking him; under normal circumstances the pigs would of course sweep it under the carpet, but this time they were caught on camera, so in the end sweet benga ended up in court.
Why doesn't anyone suddenly stop to think about the fact that a state court decides a dispute in which a state body is one party?
And the result corresponds to this: The court could not quite acquit this uniformed monkey, since there was indisputable evidence that it kicked the wounded man lying on the ground; and punishment? The wise judge decided that even coming to court was punishment enough for the scumbag, so he is guilty, but he will not be punished.
Actress Lada Bělašková found herself in a similar situation from the other side – after she and a colleague got drunk, they got the idea to remove the Czech flag from the flagpole in front of the Czech Television editorial office; some alert citizen called a benga to them, who allegedly started beating the actor.
So Lada Bélašková kicked one of them in the ass; of course I appreciate the act, although I believe she should have waited for the person to turn around. Anyway, they are now dragging her around the courts, saying that if her actions are proven, she could get up to four years.
What's worse? Chasing a motorcyclist, causing an accident and brutally kicking an injured person lying on the ground, or kicking the ass of someone who isn't hurt and, on top of that, maybe attacked another person?
And if there is no punishment for the first incident, how can anyone even consider punishing the second incident?

title: To help and protect society
text:
The most despicable violent gang in the country - the Police of the Czech Republic - attacked the collectors of technological hemp, which they mistook for marijuana; that in itself isn't all that surprising, because what can we expect from dull, sadistic monkeys in uniforms, right?
However, I found the public reaction interesting; she correctly identified the reckless assailant who physically attacked and brutally beat decent people who were just looking out for their own interests.
The vast majority of people correctly understood what happened:
The owner of the field grew plants on his land and paid other people to harvest them so that he could then sell them to customers who were interested in them and were able and willing to pay for them voluntarily; a gang of armed goons in uniforms took them by storm and brutally beat them up, violating the property rights of both the owner and the collectors.
And what would the description of the same situation look like if the field did not grow technical hemp, but marijuana?
The owner of the field grew plants on his land and paid other people to harvest them so that he could then sell them to customers who were interested in them and were able and willing to pay for them voluntarily; a gang of armed goons in uniforms took them by storm and brutally beat them up, violating the property rights of both the owner and the collectors.
Find ten differences... or at least one. Nothing? Interestingly. I don't see any either.
Does anyone want to argue the social danger and harmfulness of THC? I hope not, because if that were the argument, we'd have to make the same move against alcohol manufacturers.
However, something tells me that the public reaction would be completely different in the latter case, even though there is no rational reason for it.
And this, my dear friends, is an example of the impact of state propaganda, which has been brainwashing us since elementary school.

title: Green brains
text:
A secret survey was conducted among the soldiers of the army of the Czech Republic; his results were broadcast by TV Prima in the main news xD
The green brains are found to be mages; about half would be in favor of some form of final solution to the Roma issue, some participate in "extremist" actions (which I take with a grain of salt, as extremism is now considered to be almost anything), many of them are in foreclosure, they do not know how to manage their own money, more than a quarter encounter corruption in the army, three quarters consider the Islamic State dangerous, but one in eight would be in favor of the death penalty by stoning, cutting hands, flogging, or honor killings in the Czech Republic - of course, if "they" do it, it's barbaric, but our state would certainly handle it well and fairly.
Well, who would be surprised by this state of affairs, you ask? But is it really that unexpected? We have an organization that is widely known that you have to obey orders, suppress your individuality, let yourself be booed, the highest superiors are politicians, and the main purpose of the existence of this strange association is that its members will, if necessary, kill people they don't know at all, in the name of the screwed-up Czech government or some demented patriotism.

Both Babiš and Stropnický want to "solve" the whole situation; and I seriously wonder how they imagine they will change the army, whose very essence consists in suppressing one's own individuality and dull obedience to orders, so that there are not so many magors in it. Will they recruit among pacifists or anarchists? Sure, they probably wouldn't want to exterminate gypsies, and their tendency to harm others would probably be generally lower; and that's why they're going to turn their backs on an army from on high. On the contrary, those who don't poop...

title: Banning Islam in Angola
text:
The President of Angola, José Eduardo dos Santos, has announced a ban on Islam in this West African country, home to less than a hundred thousand Muslims across a population of sixteen million; photos of demolished Angolan mosques can be found on the Internet, and if they are real, according to the date (and various texts I have come across) it seems that this process has been going on for a long time, although the official ban was announced only recently.

It is not so surprising when the majority of radical Islam killers applaud this ban, express enthusiasm and hope that something like this will come in the Czech Republic as well; it's a little (though not really) surprising how many of these fanatics who applaud the destruction of mosques were just a few weeks ago white-hot when some ISIS goons blew up the Temple of Baal-Shamin. I'm afraid that (far from only) this doublethink shows how many people have long since moved from the realm of rational debate deep into the realm of mindless fanaticism, condemning the same idiotic behavior on the one hand while applauding it on the other; the moment someone starts evaluating actions not by themselves, but by who committed them, it is practically impossible to accept any rational arguments.

Please, let's wake up!

title: Basic income
text:
In recent years, the discussion about the basic unconditional income, which the state would pay everyone for nothing, has become more and more relevant; according to many, this system could replace the current social policy, which is riddled with excessive bureaucracy and unnecessarily complicated — instead of a far-reaching solution to who is "entitled" to support (and how much), everyone would simply receive the same.
I suspect that most libertarians will initially react to this proposal in the same way that I did the first time — with strict rejection. However, when I had discussions with basic income advocates on this topic, I had to admit that in the short term it is not nearly as bad as it seems; if we accept redistribution (which is of course monstrous) as a given fact, then in my opinion an even distribution is better than when civil servants start getting involved and making up some conditions — when, to whom, how much. Simply handing out government money to private individuals equally isn't such a stupid idea.
However, a huge problem arises in the long run; basic income will create the next generation completely dependent on the state. Just as it was the case with every field that originally functioned on the basis of market mechanisms, the state subsequently took it over, so that in a few decades (or hundreds) of years everyone acquired the belief that the given field simply could not function without the state, I can reconstruct the same in the case of basic income, which after some time will begin to be considered a necessity, because "without it it would not work and people would kill themselves".
So while the proponents of basic income are right about some things, I fear that ultimately this way of redistribution is extremely destructive in the long run.

title: Triple fines!
text:
Fascist Minister of Transport Dan Ťok, a non-partisan for ANO, basically publicly admitted that the points system does not work; of course he didn't say it in those exact words, but that after ten years of operation it no longer has as strong a preventive effect as it did after its introduction. Based on this statement, perhaps some could conclude that the preventive effect of the point system was observable ten years ago; inu, it really was in a way, because since 2003, when the point system began to be prepared and talked about, the number of road deaths decreased by four to seventeen percent per year, only to increase by fifteen percent immediately after the point system was introduced (with the injured, the trends were the same, just different numbers).
In general, the number of deaths and injuries on Czech roads has been decreasing for a long time since the mid-1990s (with some exceptions; for example, after the introduction of the points system - such an increase in deaths as after its introduction, by the way, last occurred twenty-five years ago), which is probably due to the modernization of the vehicle fleet and the increase in passive and active safety of cars. Only last year there was a deterioration (by the way, the first since the introduction of the point system), ergo it must be used to justify further state terror.
Dan Ťok therefore proposes tripling the amount of fines; he said that he personally would be in favor of even higher fines, but even triple seems acceptable to him. In particular, speeding, using the phone while driving and driving under the influence were mentioned; the last offense is especially absurd given the zero tolerance of alcohol behind the wheel, which we currently have in the Czech Republic - in practice, this means that you drink one beer (there is no question of any intoxication), drive in an hour (actually no impaired driving skills) and lo and behold, a fine of up to sixty thousand crowns. Great huh?
What I find particularly sickening about the government's drivel about transport is how many people go along with it because they feel that the harsher the penalties, the better, only opening their eyes after uniformed monkeys wipe their asses and take away their driver's licenses, or slap huge fines on them for nothing, but even then they often fail to realize that this is a feature of the system, not a failure of it; does anyone know of a way to open the eyes of these individuals?

title: Internet, hotbed of radicals
text:
It is probably no secret that various pro-European think tanks have been receiving massive subsidies from their beloved cash cow for years; I don't want to advertise them here by inserting links, but just google it, they usually brag about receiving European money on their website (which is probably a condition of those grants). By the way, it is very interesting to compare their outputs with those produced by various - not subsidized by public money - libertarian think tanks, which I do not want to write about now; manipulation of our (public) opinion for our money is quite standard for the EU.
The next level became paid professional internet trolls, in which the EU invested two million pounds in 2014; the task of people paid in this way is to go through discussion forums, search for so-called "falsehoods" about the EU (from the point of view of the establishment) and refute them, i.e. trolling in practice. Some of the agents paid in this way allegedly also worked in the Czech Republic; in connection with that, I wonder if I have already had the honor with any of them, because I have no idea how to tell the paid ones from the unpaid ones.
Because the paid trolls have apparently proved their worth, the EU decided to go a little further - the European anti-terrorist coordinator (my goodness, that's my job) Gilles de Kerchove came up with the thesis that the Internet is a "breeding ground for radicals", which he solves by, among other things, sending a "team of experts" to Prague whose task is to "train the government in the fight against radicalization of citizens on the Internet"; and something tells me that the central theme of the training will probably not be that fanaticism does the worst in a free society.
Ideally, the goal of the entire event is for the coordinator to show some activity, the team of experts to absorb some money from the budget and the members of the government to get a good night's sleep during the training, which we will of course pay dearly for all of them; in the worst case, there will be some output from this in similar "necessary measures", which, although they limit freedom, will definitely protect us from the hotbed of radicals. In the context of the current mood in society, it is perhaps in this way that the politicians would be able to defend themselves against a non-negligible part of the population. How do you think the whole situation will turn out? You can share your opinions in the comments.

title: Anarcho-capitalists, let's raise anarcho-capitalists!
text:
My son came home from school upset; when I asked what happened, he explained to me that the teacher tried to explain to them in the course "Fundamentals of Social Sciences" (for me, by the way, it was more aptly called: "Civic Education" - different chest, the same shit) how wonderful an institution the state is, while when he tried to develop a debate about anarcho-capitalism, she dealt with it as a proper bearer of state propaganda: roads - people would kill each other - it is extremism - we don't have time for such discussions.

So anarcho-capitalists, libertarians, let's have children, let's set an example and make them free beings, not slaves to the state! xD

title: Where will I live?
text:
» ...that's why I drove at night without lights,
after six tequilas and five joints in the opposite direction,
and watched the shadows of the trees below the hill illuminated only by the moon
and the outlines of houses in the midnight gloom; so I'm really screwing it up today. «
Who recognizes the passage? I'm not much into Czech music, but Mňága a Ėorp is one of the few exceptions; and it is in this song that Petr Fiala repeatedly asks: "Where will I live?" And when I listened to him while reading some kind of mňága (with a small m) on the IVČRN website, I also asked myself that question.
Pretty much everyone with a hole in their ass has an opinion about what should be done with immigrants; I also have a hole and I think that the solution to the situation is

.
