title: Free Harbor Studio: About Freedom, Science, Faith and Ethics with Štěpán Drábek
text:
Štěpán Drábek offered me wonderful topics for the second interview; and I gladly accepted them! Last time we covered the economy, which I enjoyed a lot; and it was no different when we honed in on questions of ethics. I enjoy debating with Štěpán, especially because of his ability to abstract.
We discussed scattered information in society and its connection with freedom; we also got to the deification of science - and came to the very interesting conclusion that the scientific method is actually faith (as strange as it sounds, it makes sense in that context).

– Štěpán Drábek; economist; analyst at the Institute of Liberal Studies; libertarian; seeker of truth

title: Will Tim walk away from the debate with Urza an anarchist?
text:
At first Tim found anarcho-capitalism to be a trade-off, then he took it seriously, then too seriously, only to stop making sense at some points; he asked me for a debate in which we could discuss these aspects so that he would hopefully (finally) be clear.
We talked about defense against internal and external enemies, recreational nukes, and other favorite anarchist topics (except for children's brothels); of course, we have not forgotten the (not only Austrian) economy, human behavior and interpersonal incomparability of utility.

– Tim; libertarian; perhaps a future anarchist; youtuber; student of political science and philosophy; LGBT activist

title: Freeport Studio: What is (and is not) freedom?
text:
The December livestream will be visited by Teri Paul, who I already consider to be one of the principled supporters of freedom, of whom, unfortunately, she is like saffron; most libertarians only want it when it's convenient, or at least when it's not too expensive or inconvenient.
Teri herself brought the topic "What is (and is not) freedom?" – and I pick it up with joy, because it seems quite essential to me; above all, a dialogue about the limits of freedom, or rather what freedom is no longer, because unfortunately we cannot do with the end of the freedom of one at the beginning of the freedom of the other.

– Teri Paul; libertarian; anarcho-capitalist; idealist; author of the podcast "And who would build roads?"

title: Freeport Studio: Indoctrination by (not only) Masaryk
text:
Ema went out into the streets of Brno, where she asked people three questions: Who was Tomáš Garrigue Masaryk? Do you think he was a good person and a good president? If you think he was, why do you think so?
For the most part, the answers didn't surprise us; nevertheless, interesting phenomena regarding indoctrination in schools can be observed on them - teachers know what we should "correctly" think, but mainly how we should feel. I consider the creation of positive and negative connotations to concepts to be a more powerful weapon than the manipulation of facts and misinformation.

– Emma; creator of Freeport; anarcho-capitalist; libertarian; student Hedgehog without a cage

title: Anarcho-capitalism: How (not) to talk (not only) to the cops?
text:
In the November lecture from the Anarcho-Capitalism cycle, we will deal with how to (not) talk (not only) with the police (but also with other state authorities); you requested this topic as a follow-up to September's #disobedience event, as a result of which this laziness may come in handy - but regardless, this laziness may be more than useful. People often live in the belief that those who do nothing wrong have nothing to fear - but the reality is different; in severely totalitarian regimes, this is not the case, but even in our democracy, this is not the case - or rather, it may be the case most of the time, but you never know when you will find yourself in the wrong place at the wrong time. A person does not have to be a criminal or harm anyone to be occasionally affected by the weight of state power; I think it's good to be prepared. I would also like to talk about the various media causes and shortcuts that people like to jump on; and how many times they can ruin someone's life.
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ll/

During the debate it became clear that I probably have trouble understanding the speech of the philosophers (which was already evident in some of the earlier works); I found his criticism rather shallow, but maybe I just misunderstood something. Please, would you write to me in the comments what you understood?

– Filip Staněk; philosopher; a critic of anarcho-capitalism, and by extension the entire Western civilization

title: Freeport Studio: #disobedience
text:
In the fifty-fourth live stream of the Free Port, we will focus on the #disobedience event; it took place on September 16, was filmed and its recording will be published during October - unfortunately not via YouTube (or even Odysee), as the video violates the terms of the contract.
With that event, I would like to start the next stage of my work; it will be followed by others like it - and who knows what will happen next (I certainly don't). I would like to not only discuss with you what you think about it; I am mainly interested in your ideas for other similar performances. Do you share?

– Emma; creator of Freeport; anarcho-capitalist; libertarian; student Hedgehog without a cage

title: Studio of the Free Port: About the effect of drug illegality on users with Tonda
text:
I met Tonda at the CryptoByte conference in Liberec; I was giving a lecture there about Bitcoin and anarchoagorism, he then came to me and offered me an interview in the Studio with a person under the law addicted to drugs, which I found to be a very interesting topic, so I agreed.
We talked about his experiences in state education and the overall meaning of it (and asked ourselves what the high school diploma is for); then we moved on to drugs and the effects of prohibition on regular (and often minor) users. Finally, we dealt with various anarchist schools and their connection with voluntarism.

– Tonda; anarchist; libertarian; drug user

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Capitalism as a Mirror
text:
From October, the Anarcho-Capitalism cycle shifts again; this time to the emerging libertarian den Liberty Loft. In order to maintain a balance between the topics of personal and economic freedom, I would like to focus on capitalism this time; the latter is the target of criticism by many, often including anarchists, while everyone criticizes him for something different - from excessive hierarchization and centralization to the destruction of the environment to insufficient interest in the soul of the individual. I myself could identify with some points of this criticism, but I would not blame capitalism per se for any of them; because I am convinced that this system only reflects the needs and nature of people in society (both on the side of consumers and producers), while it does not create the problems described above in itself, it only brings them to light. So let's discuss it more closely together!
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ll/

title: Studio Freeport: About (constitutional) democracy with Jan Mošovský
text:
When I watch some of the output of Students for Liberty or the Institute of Liberal Studies, it raises a number of questions in me; I decided to invite Jan Mošovský to discuss them, since he sees (constitutional) democracy as a glass half full, I rather half empty.
I can imagine that some viewers will be quick to reject Honzo's position (perhaps too much), or even turn off the video; however, I personally think that it is definitely worth listening to, but above all for subsequent reflection, however different our approach may be.

– Jan Mošovský; anarcho-objectivist; libertarian; member of Students for Liberty; associate of the Institute of Liberal Studies

title: Basics of anarcho-capitalism, education and other free topics in České Budějovice
text:
Aleš Mikulejský invited me to České Budějovice to give a lecture on the foundations of anarcho-capitalism; and because he tried hard to bring in as many people as possible, he had a very diverse audience of seasoned anarchists and bitcoiners, but also those who had never heard of these topics before.
I enjoyed the lecture (or discussion) a lot, which is why it lasted two and a half hours; perhaps I liked the diversity of the audience, which was challenging at times, but I think that in the end we enriched each other. I am really glad that so many people came, open to new ideas, attitudes, values...

title: Darkry discusses intrinsic motivation, RVP and teaching (not just IT) with Urza
text:
We both enjoyed the last debate with Darkry about indoctrination in education, so we decided to continue; this time our conversation was led by Darkry, who prepared the topic and the questions. I'm not sure how much we followed his outline; but I think we both enjoyed it.
Darkry asked about Ježek, changes in RVP, but also IT teaching, especially media literacy; however, from each topic, sooner or later we always ended up with internal motivation - unfortunately, this is often killed by attempts to stimulate the external one.

– Darkry; beginning teacher; developer; graphic designer; writer; narrator; entertainer; youtuber (@Darkry, @ZOOVymřelin)

title: #disobedience: Why does Urza publicly break the law on camera?
text:
The shortest episode of Freeport Studio is actually just a trailer for another video that I would like to show you, but unfortunately it would be against YouTube's (and Odysee's) terms and conditions to upload it here, as I am breaking the law in it.
At the same time, I also explain why I do it, I talk not only about (dis)obedience, but also about victimless crimes, the right of the stronger (state) and discuss a lot of other related topics; this is a milestone in my work - it will now develop in this direction as well.

Links:
https://www.urza.cz/nep
https://stoky.urza.cz/texty/ne-poslusnosti-proc-urza-verejne-porusuje-zakony-pred-kamerou-3333

title: Freeport Studio: About Bitcoin, deflation and ethics with Štěpán Drábek
text:
Štěpán Drábek is a young economist (he calls himself a future economist), libertarian and bitcoiner; that's probably why Kicom invited him to his channel, where they talked about bitcoinization, the potential bitcoin economy, but also the deflationary economy in general.
I decided to discuss the topics with him again, since Kicom himself admitted that they were too technical for him in economic matters; now we've broken them down in more depth to find out what an economy without central banking actually looks like. Finally, we also dealt with the ethics of freedom.

– Štěpán Drábek; economist; analyst at the Institute of Liberal Studies; libertarian; bitcoiner

title: Cryptoanarchy, anarcho-agorism, anarcho-capitalism for Prague Business Club
text:
Entrepreneurs from the Prague Business Club were interested in a private lecture on cryptocurrencies in connection with the Brno-Bitcoin-Blažek case; fortunately, we only marginally covered it, for which I am sincerely glad, because the world of cryptocurrencies is a fascinating place that completely overshadows any incompetence of politicians.
I was much surprised at how receptive an audience I spoke to; and not only about crypto-anarchy, but also about anarcho-capitalism and anarcho-agorism. Entrepreneurs (and not only on the basis of this lecture) I consider (together with children who have not been processed by school) to be the most open-minded group of people possible.

title: Pre-election speech "Nevolte Urza.cz" (parliamentary elections 2025)
text:
As part of the party's pre-election campaign, "Urza.cz: We don't want your votes; you can't claim freedom. We'll reject every political function; we don't want to dictate to people how they should live. We have a different vision. We're going a different way - you can find it on the website www.urza.cz." until the 2025 parliamentary elections, I took part in several debates and performances.
As usual, it was about the Political spectrum, the presentation of the party in ČT and CRo, and this time also one debate on the radio; you can find a montage of all this in this video. This year we ran only in Prague (not in the other regions), so with a slightly smaller reach, but for (order of magnitude) less money.

title: Freeport Studio: To vote or not to vote? That's what's (not) going on with Mikýř
text:
Mickýř did not want to come to the Studio for a long time, because he is used to a different way of communication, debates do not suit him; all the more I appreciate that he finally accepted my invitation in connection with his call to the people to go vote. I didn't go, Mikýř was just returning from the urn, so he stopped to talk.
We were just talking about whether (not) the (not) election makes sense; and above all we tried to explain (and understand) why - I found that very interesting and productive. Finally, we went to the United States, which led to an unexpected and interesting point of our discussion.

– Micky; youtuber; influencer; entertainer; the author of the invitation to participate in the elections

title: Students for Liberty: Bitcoin (Urza) versus fiat (Mojmír Hampl)
text:
At the launch of the book The Theory of Money and Credit, there were inaccuracies about Bitcoin; therefore, together with Students for Liberty and the Institute of Liberal Studies, we decided to organize a debate on Bitcoin and fiat money, in which Urza and Mojmír Hampl defended these instruments.
We have addressed the various features of Bitcoin, its advantages and disadvantages; we agreed on some things, although the highest degree of difference of opinion prevailed around LN, about whose functionality Mojmír Hampl still has his doubts. We also debated fiat and its sustainability without the state.

– Mojmír Hampl; economist; former vice-governor of the Czech National Bank; chairman of the National Budget Council

title: Is it legitimate to vote from the anarchoagorist's point of view?
text:
Tomáš Kupec contacted me saying that, from the point of view of an anarcho-agorist, it does not seem legitimate to him to vote in democratic elections (that is, he considers such an act to be a violation of the NAP); I do not share this view, even though the election does not make sense to me, but I consider it legitimate.
I enjoyed the debate a lot and although we did not reach a clear agreement and a common conclusion, we learned that we see many things from a similar perspective; in particular, (value) consistency is very important for both of us.

– Tomáš Kupec; anarchoagorist; Taoist; aikido trainer (facebook.com/aikidogympraha, instagram.com/aikidogympraha, aikidogym.cz)

title: Freeport Studio: Parliamentary Elections 2025 with Tim
text:
On the third of October there will be an election; the second one is a livestream, so the topic is offered a bit - or I'm not enough of an anarchoagorist to recognize that it isn't offered (but what do we know, maybe one day I'll completely ignore the rituals of statism even in my work).
Since Emu is not interested in politics (he is further along than I am), I invited Tim, who deals with the elections, to the Studio for a chat, so we will discuss the individual parties and the possibilities of who (not) to vote for; perhaps we will help you find your way around your (non)choice as well.

– Timofey Kozhuchov; libertarian; maybe a little anarcho-capitalist; youtuber; student of political science and philosophy; LGBT activist

title: Anarcho-capitalism: (Dis)obedience
text:
I have been talking about (dis)obedience a lot in the last year; I mention it in many presentations on various topics, because it leads me to it from different sides and it seems really essential to me - so much so that I would like to dedicate a separate lecture to it. And since it is a September lecture, of course the topic of education and the state education system will not be missing in it; these are closely connected with (dis)obedience. I would like to deal with (dis)obedience in different contexts, both in the free market and in the state environment (including legislative or property law boundaries); I also want to focus on the "types" of (dis)obedience - including their consequences. When is (dis)obedience harmful? And to whom? How is it related to fear and therefore inner freedom? How about the outer one? We will not only address these questions at the lecture...
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/grail/

title: Urza with Markéta Šichtařová on Radio Prostor
text:
Markéta Šichtařová invited me to Prostor pro dvo on Radio Prostor; we discussed (not only Austrian) economics, (not only anarcho-individualist) philosophy, the path to anarcho-capitalism in practice, and finally (dis)obedience and anarcho-agorism.

– Markéta Šichtařová; economist; blogger; author of many books

title: Urza in the show Real Life with Jaroslav Grűnwald about Hedgehog without a cage
text:
Jaroslav Grűnwald invited me (for the third time) to his show Real Life, where we were supposed to talk about "alternative" education, but in the end it was actually all about Hedgehog; and not very generally - we only covered a few aspects, but in great depth.

– Jaroslav Grűnwald; shaman; lecturer; therapist

title: Freeport Studio: Ctirad Musil, Moravané, Stačilo!
text:
Before the elections, some politicians are starting to contact me with the wish to debate in the Studio; one of them was Ctirad Musil, chairman of the Moravian party (at that time on the candidate list of the Stačilo movement!), who particularly interested me in the topic of participation or non-participation in elections - I like to think about that.
In addition, we discussed the Moravian program and Stačilo!; when I studied it, it seemed inconsistent to me, which I asked the guest about, however, I see more inconsistencies in his answers rather than explanations - however, judge for yourself, maybe they will make sense to you.

– Ctirad Musil; chairman of the Moravian party; candidate for the Enough!

title: Pre-election interview with the spokesperson of the Czech Crown
text:
Martin Cikán from Koruna Česká contacted me with an interest in filming a pre-election interview; since I have been interested in Koruna Česká for some time, I studied their program (which is not so terrible in some areas) and nodded to it.
The course of the conversation actually surprised me quite a bit; I expected certain inconsistencies (as they arise from the program), but their level and (non)explanation was significantly higher than I could have imagined. On the other hand, probably no politician in the Studio has yet admitted that I also write empty phrases in the program.

– Martin Cikán; spokesperson of the Czech Crown; monarchist; candidate for the Chamber of Deputies

title: Urza and Tim about the state award on Anděl
text:
Tim organizes events where he talks to people on the street; so we organized one of these together - the topic was the price of the state, which I calculated for my lecture, in which I introduced the audience to how much the state would cost us in 2024.
We just informed a number of people, gave them leaflets and they went again; however, to my delight, some started debating – some opposed economically, others philosophically or socially.
You can find the link to the entire recovered calculation here:
urza.cz/public/c.cenastatu.xlsx

– Timofey Kozhuchov; libertarian; maybe a little anarcho-capitalist; youtuber; student of political science and philosophy; LGBT activist

title: Studio of the Free Port: Voluntia is waiting for the first elections with Tomáš Roud
text:
Tomáš Roud founded the political party Voluntia; the first interview with him came out here when he was looking for signatures, which he managed to do in the spring. Now Voluntia is facing its first election, so it is trying to get as many libertarian votes as possible; he won't get mine, but he will get space in the Studio.
We addressed the anarcho-agorist versus political approach to freedom and, in relation to that, the developments in Voluntia, where I illustrated the risks of politics; in fact, certain signs that Svobodní showed years ago are beginning to appear in it...

– Tomáš Roud; volunteer; libertarian; founder of the Voluntia Party; proponent of self-government; businessman; former soldier

title: Urza for BTC Prague 2025
text:
I was pleased to give a talk at the biggest Bitcoin conference in Europe; I was given twenty minutes and chose the topic: To regulate or not to regulate Bitcoin? That is the question.
But I didn't stop at Bitcoin; my speech explained the same approach for quite every area of our lives that states try to regulate. How can we defend ourselves against such attempts? What can we do when politicians use their power to control us? I believe that the approach I present regarding Bitcoin is universally applicable to other aspects of our lives as well.

title: Interview for Students for Liberty at BTC Prague (they probably finished my squealing in post-production xD)
text:
In the summer I spoke at Europe's largest bitcoin conference, BTC Prague; there too I lectured (in English) about (dis)obedience in connection with Bitcoin regulations, which you will of course also be able to listen to on the Freeport Channel (although it is a short presentation, I am very satisfied with it).
After the lecture, I was caught by Students for Liberty for a short interview about Bitcoin (in Czech); even though it was basically just such basic questions, I liked their selection (especially the ones about the controversy) so I decided to publish the video even though I'm slurring in the audio track for some reason (I understand them though) xD

title: Studio Freeport: On the development and (il)legality of turquoise (self)management with Vláďa Dobeš
text:
Vláďa Dobeš and I debated at ASDŠ meetings (not only) about the (il)legality of self-government; in connection with one of the debates, Ježek left the association without a cage, because our way is to live our own way and then solve the laws, while other schools have it the other way around.
One of those schools – Donum Felix – was founded by Vláďa; I find it interesting how different it is from Ježek, although it is also a self-directed "turquoise" organization. However, we did not only deal with schools, but also the impact of self-management on the whole society.

– Vladimír Dobeš; founder of the democratic school Donum Felix; lecturer; former politician and mayor; engineer; turquoise organization expert

title: Urza at the Freeport House on Anarcho-Agorism, July 2025
text:
I dedicated my second talk for the 2025 Freeport House Summer Residence to anarchism, especially anarcho-capitalism and anarchoagorism; we started by explaining terms (some did not know or understand them at first), but in the end we opened a very interesting discussion.
We dealt with politics, elections, Svobodna and Voluntia; and our attitudes towards it all. Towards the end we talked about breaking the law, and I was far from alone in sharing; there are already other people who report to something like this (even on the record). And those who don't want to record, at least after the end of the recorded part...

title: Urza in the House of the Free Port about Hedgehog without a cage, July 2025
text:
My first talk at the Summer Residence at the House of the Free Port 2025 was about the Hedgehog without a cage; a lot of people came to it again, and I think this year, among other things, because I wasn't there alone from Ježek, but also with Jíťa (another adult), Míša (a student) and Filo (a schoolboy), who complemented their views.
There were people in the audience who didn't know much about the operation of Ježek, so quite classic questions were asked first, however, after some time the debate settled on conflict resolution, which I consider a very interesting topic; how to proceed when there are no penalties and everything must be voluntary?

title: Freeport Studio: Learning (and Living) Without a Cage
text:
Freeport's fifty-second live stream is released in September - the first week of school; therefore, our topic will be, as always, (ubiquitous) learning, (formal and informal) education, (state and free market) education and perhaps also the upbringing of children (not only by parents).
We would like to make this livestream a little broader and more interactive - You will ask questions or bring theses to the discussions (at least in general on the above-mentioned topics); we will try to look at them from different (albeit typically anarchist) points of view and work with them.

– Emma; creator of Freeport; anarcho-capitalist; libertarian; student Hedgehog without a cage

title: Studio of the Free Port: About self-management with Richard Veselý
text:
I have known Richard Veselý for many years; this time he addressed me with a topic close to me, namely self-management; he did not come to question it - or the autonomy of children - in any way, as he himself considers them to be a necessary minimum, but he wanted to talk about what could be above this minimum.
Letting children make their own decisions preserves their freedom, but freedom is not everything; what self-managed collectives can look like, what makes them different and what can a teacher or camp leader do - we discussed all this (and much more) in this part of the Free Port Studio.

– Richard Veselý; libertarian; chemist; scientist; lecturer; seeker of truth; youtuber

title: Anarcho-capitalism: Why the state doesn't work and how to fix it?
text:
The state is criticized from all sides – as dysfunctional, inefficient, unjust, authoritarian or blind to the needs of minorities. But what if all these complaints are not just random complaints, but a symptom of a deeper flaw in the way the state works as a process? In this lecture, we will look at specific problems that people of different value frameworks feel: from the alienation of the majority to the failure of the rule of law to the oppression of minorities. For each point, we will focus not only on its symptoms, but above all on where the very mechanism that should solve these problems fails. And we will also propose specific alternatives – small but significant interventions that could correct these defects.
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/grail/

– Teri “The Idealist” Paul; volunteer; defender of freedom; YouTuber

title: Freeport Studio: Children's (Im)rights
text:
Ema came up with a topic that touches her personally; it is about the (im)rights of children in our society. The preparation of this piece was relatively easy for her - she just watched for some time what she needed to do in life, but the state prevents her from doing it on the basis of age discrimination.
I consider it important to constantly remind how the state still denies all rights to children; and even the fact that we have become used to it does not change the injustice that arises from it - people were also used to discrimination based on race or gender for centuries, so it was necessary to point it out.

– Emma; creator of Freeport; anarcho-capitalist; libertarian; student Hedgehog without a cage

title: Urza for anarchy versus Tadeáš Ždárský for not growing on Brno's Scio
text:
I like the students from the Scio school in Brno more and more; as part of our cooperation, they decided to organize a debate between me and Tadeáš Žďárský from Néraťas, as they are now focusing a lot on the topics of capitalism, anti-capitalism, environmentalism and ways of organizing society.
Unfortunately, I was not in the best shape, so I did not have the strength to push the topics I wanted to talk about; as a result, we didn't really get into the economic calculation and discussed topics important to non-growth almost all the time.

– Tadeáš Ždárský; one of the founders of the non-growth team at NaZemi; environmentalist; feminist; anti-capitalist

title: Urza about (crypto) money or (state) army for Kryptoplebs
text: Jan Egan invited me again for a chat; unsurprisingly, for the Kryptoplebs channel, we talked about (not only crypto) money, but we also touched on other topics - we talked about pensions, the war (not only) in Ukraine, the army (not only Ukrainian, Czech, Russian, but in general), Rose Island, and we also talked about "plan B".

title: Urza about tax optimization, self-management and the army with Daniel Holánek
text:
From time to time, Daniel Holánek will do an interview with me; and I always really enjoy talking with him, because I get the feeling that he really thinks deeply about the topics, so I happily nodded to the next call on the three topics (chosen by him).
First, we discussed tax optimization - you can get practical advice from a financial advisor; then we spent some time on Rozičov's fears about self-control; and I consider the conclusion to be the most interesting part, where we talked about the (de)centralized army, while I rather advocated the strength of the centralized one.

– Daniel Holánek; anarcho-capitalist; investor; YouTuber; financial advisor

title: Urza, Kicom and Standa deal with BTC of the Ministry of (In)justice
text:
Standa invited me and Kicom to dissect bitcoins from dark markets for the Ministry of (In)justice; who buys what from the state?

– Jakub Kicom Vejmola; bitcoiner; youtuber; Bitcoin Channel author; cryptocurrency investor
– Standa Hruška (www.standashow.cz); youtuber; streamer; gamer; moderator

title: Freeport Studio: Freeport Holidays 2025
text:
Another season of Freeport ends; during the holidays, our traffic will be a little smaller again, as viewership and readership decrease, but we also need to step back a little from our work (and prepare more). You can look forward to a lot more content (not only) next year; even for a new event on the edge (or rather already beyond the edge) of the law.
I made this video to say goodbye to you; but also in order to bring you closer to what we are doing now, what we are planning, where the Free Port will go, but also as a look back at the last few months and a recommendation of something from our work that, in my opinion, should not fit in.

title: Urza versus about 15 statists
text:
Tim organized a debate in which twenty (or more) statists were supposed to oppose me, but only about fifteen turned up; we brought a number of theses, each with a total of twenty minutes of clear time, the debater was always determined by lot and recalled by the others when they did not find his arguments convincing.
Although I certainly liked the format and it felt good to debate for several hours against always fresh opponents, I probably lacked more space for individual theses (I would have preferred a longer time limit on each topic); among the theses, the most popular (for socialists) seemed to be those related to finance, which I managed to balance.

title: Darkry discusses his video about indoctrination in education with Urza
text:
Darkry made a video about indoctrination in education; he claimed in it that none is taking place there, or if it is, it is an individual action of individual teachers that is not supported in the national education strategy or in the RVP, which I do not agree with.
I asked him if he would be willing to discuss the video with me; to my delight he nodded and to my even greater delight he actually listened. We discussed the 2030+ Strategy and the RVP; in the end we agreed that indoctrination is indeed contained in them.

– Darkry; student of pedagogy; future teacher; developer; graphic designer; writer; narrator; entertainer; youtuber (@Darkry, @ZOOVymřelin)

title: Freeport Studio: About drugs, medicine and prison with a criminal prosecution
text:
Jakub, with many pseudonyms, contacted me saying that he would like to openly share his story in the Studio about (not only) the use of drugs (or medications?) for his severe ADHD and how the state (not only didn't) help him in this, but what sticks he threw at his feet instead.
In my opinion, the interview shows, among other things, how the (state) war on drugs "excludes" people from society and "drives" them into the "underworld", where it is unfortunately quite common to report others to the police and courts out of fear of punishment or simply out of desperation.

– Jakub with many pseudonyms; marijuana user and grower; user of other drugs; prosecuted

title: Urza deals with CzechCloud (not only) (Trump's) tariffs, the army or incest
text:
CzechCloud invited me (again) to his livestream; in our standard time, we agreed well on the geopolitical situation, Trump, customs, Ukraine, incest, but not so much on the Czech army.

– CzechCloud; Czech streamer; youtuber; (political) commentator; former professional player and World Hearthstone Champion

title: Urza with Tim and Roman Joch (not only) about the defense of the state
text:
At the Freeport 2025: Culture Wars Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow Conference, we started an interesting debate with Tim and Roman Joch; Tim then decided to follow her up at The Grail, which I gladly accepted.
We discussed gratitude and victimhood, conservatism and progressivism, but we were most concerned with the defense of the state in time of war; who would defend their homeland and who would not? And what are the motivations for both decisions?

– Timofey Kozhuchov; libertarian; YouTuber; student of political science and philosophy; LGBT activist
– Roman Joch; director of the Civic Institute; publicist; commentator; teacher at CEVRO Institute and VŠE

title: Free Port Studio: About freedom and travel with Vítek from Cestopiss
text:
You wanted Vítek from Vítkov Cestopissa; it was a bit more difficult to find him, but after a few small vicissitudes it was finally successful (I'm not very good at contacting people in general) - I'm very happy that I finally caught him in the Czech Republic and he arrived (and he also brought me kratom from his garden xD).
Before we talked (in general) about freedom - here Vítek also connects it with private property; we also took a bite out of the war on drugs and the stigmatization of drugs, but of course traveling and comparing freedom and lack of freedom in different countries did not remain in the background.

– Vít Vomáčka; traveler; youtuber from the Vítkův Cestopiss channel; libertarian

title: Urza about (dis)obedience and (dis)regulation of (not only) Bitcoin for CryptoByte
text:
The CryptoByte conference was held in Liberec on the exact day I was passing through it from the House of the Free Port, so I was happy to bet on the lecture; the organizers asked me to combine talking about cryptocurrencies with how anarcho-capitalism affects my daily life.
So I talked about how and why everyday anarcho-capitalism made me an anarcho-agorist, what it actually means to me and how it manifests itself; of course, I did not forget the connection with crypto-money, although I perceive it "only" as one of the tools to achieve freedom, although undoubtedly very important.

title: Urza and docent Tomáš Sobek on individual freedom
text:
The student association Lexicon from the Faculty of Law in Brno invited me to a debate with Docent Tomáš Sobek. The person in question is a legend in the faculty – and I quickly understood why; rarely in my life have I met someone who works so brilliantly and quickly with logic.
Two hundred people came to the debate; we started with future obligations (according to most people, the return of borrowed money can be demanded, but not necessarily the promised sex) and we came to argumentation ethics, which Tomáš Sobek described to me in such a way that I finally agreed (although it is a weaker statement than it is commonly used).

– Assoc. JUDr. Tomáš Sobek, Ph.D.; lawyer; college teacher; a logician

title: Freeport Studio: Involuntary Psychiatric Hospitalizations with Jožo Mero
text:
Jozef Mera - the father of one of my students - offered me to film an episode of the Free Port Studio with him on the topic of involuntary hospitalizations in psychiatric hospitals, which unfortunately he experienced quite a few in his life (he was hospitalized six times in total).
We analyzed chronologically Jož's experiences from individual hospitalizations, whether voluntary or involuntary; we dealt with the approach of doctors to patients, which is quite crucial in the case of psychiatric diseases. Unfortunately, as always, we come across the incentives and limits of socialist healthcare...

– Jozef Mera; psychiatric patient; supporter of freedom

title: Urza and Vojtěch Lapuník on anarcho-capitalism and democracy
text:
Sometimes the conversation fails me; and I think this is the case. Even so, after consulting with you, dear viewers and listeners, I decided to publish it; in it we deal with the possible weaknesses of ankap and the utilitarian approach to democracy, which can show its advantages and disadvantages.

– Vojtěch Lapuník; programmer; a democrat

title: Freeport Studio: Streamarathon 2025 (1pm to 5pm)
text:
We've broadcast two streamarathons so far: In 2022, it lasted 13 hours; and in 2024 even 16 hours. How long do you think this year's will last, with the two of us for the first time? You can write comments and call as always; ask any questions to Emma or Urza.
Unlike other regular livestreams, we won't cover any one specific topic, so we can cover anything you want; and, as in the case of previous streamarathons, we can occasionally deviate a little (more) from libertarianism.

– Emma; creator of Freeport; anarcho-capitalist; libertarian; student Hedgehog without a cage

title: Freeport Studio: Streamarathon 2025 (Hour 1 to 12)
text:
We've broadcast two streamarathons so far: In 2022, it lasted 13 hours; and in 2024 even 16 hours. How long do you think this year's will last, with the two of us for the first time? You can write comments and call as always; ask any questions to Emma or Urza.
Unlike other regular livestreams, we won't cover any one specific topic, so we can cover anything you want; and, as in the case of previous streamarathons, we can occasionally deviate a little (more) from libertarianism.

– Emma; creator of Freeport; anarcho-capitalist; libertarian; student Hedgehog without a cage

title: Freeport Studio: On Critical Thinking and War with Peter Ludwig
text:
I have known Peter Ludwig for a long time as a promoter of critical thinking; however, lately I have been receiving contributions from him (mainly about Ukraine) that contradicted my critical thinking - so I decided to invite him to the Studio and discuss it with him.
What I really liked about the interview was Peter's humility, his willingness to learn and openly (publicly) admit that something is not clear to him; such qualities are rather rare in my opinion. We also addressed the warlike state of mind; and how explorers and warriors perceive the world differently.

– Peter Ludwig; promoter of critical thinking; publicist; businessman; supporter of Ukraine

title: Anarchocapitalism: Anarchoagorism
text:
From May, the cycle Anarchocapitalism moves to a new space; I will perform at The Grail. I'm going to talk about anarchoagorism, which is making more and more sense to me; it differs from anarcho-capitalism in that it doesn't recognize political solutions, which resonates with me quite a bit, although I probably wouldn't be as sharp about it. However, I would like to address why I don't think we will change anything by (obediently) voting or changing laws; central planning does not work not only in the economy, but also in efforts to achieve greater freedom, in my opinion. I would like to focus on what we can actually do and what is as effective as possible; because I am convinced that we can make our own free life, which happens to be the best way to a free society.
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/grail/

title: Urza and Lawrence "Larry" Reed on freedom and humanity
text:
Larry captivated me with his talk at LibertyCon; it was undoubtedly the best lecture of the event for me and perhaps one of the best I've ever heard. That's why I was delighted when he accepted my invitation to appear in the Free Haven.
We discussed his concept of human virtues as the foundation of liberty. I described my concept of outer freedom and inner freedom (limited by fear) — an idea Larry resonated with. We concluded by discussing how to practically cultivate these virtues in everyday life.
Biographies I Recommend — by Lawrence W. Reed:
1/ Beneath a Scarlet Sky by Mark Sullivan—the story of World War II Italian resistance figure Pino Lella, who is still living today at 92.
2/ Bonhoeffer: Pastor, Martyr, Prophet, Spy by Eric Metaxas—about Dietrich Bonhoeffer, the Lutheran pastor who became a part of the 1944 plot to kill Adolf Hitler.  
3/ Destiny of the Republic: A Tale of Madness, Medicine and the Murder of a President by Candace Millard—follows the final two years in the lives of James A. Garfield, 20th U.S. President, and his assassin, Charles Guiteau.
4/ Longitude: The Story of a Lone Genius Who Solved the Greatest Scientific Problem of His Time by Dava Sobel—about how the clockmaker John Harrison won the prize for discovering how to determine longitude at sea.
5/ Ronald Reagan: How an Ordinary Man Became an Extraordinary Leader by Dinesh D'Souza—one of the best of many Reagan biographies.
6/ When Character Was King by Peggy Noonan—another great and inspiring Reagan biography.
7/ Bury the Chains: Prophets and Rebels in the Fight to Free an Empire's Slaves by Adam Hochschild—an excellent history of the British anti-slavery campaign, with special focus on the personalities of Thomas Clarkson and Olaudah Equiano.
8/ Amazing Grace by Eric Metaxas—the best biography of anti-slavery parliamentarian William Wilberforce.
9/ The Myth of the Robber Barons by Burton W. Folsom—excellent chapters on American business figures such as Cornelius Vanderbilt, John D. Rockefeller, Charles Schwab and others.
10/ Real Heroes: Inspiring True Stories of Courage, Character and Conviction by Lawrence W. Reed—contains 40 chapters on great men and women of politics, business, humanitarianism, etc.
11/ The Cross and the Switchblade by David Wilkerson—the story of a Pennsylvania preacher who attempts to change lives in inner city New York.
12/ Cicero by Anthony Everitt—the best biography of the ancient Roman statesman and orator.
13/ The Last Jeffersonian: Grover Cleveland and the Path to Restoring the Republic by Ryan S. Walters—about one of America's greatest but forgotten Presidents.
14/ Margaret Thatcher: Everything She Wants by Charles Moore—focuses on the Iron Lady's premiership from the Falklands War on.
15/ Sophie Scholl and the White Rose by Annette Dumbach and Jud Newborn—fascinating story of a brave college student who challenged the Nazi regime.
16/ The Final Race: The Incredible World War II Story of the Olympian Who Inspired Chariots of Fire by Eric T. Eichinger and Eva Marie Everson – about Scottish athlete and missionary Eric Liddell, a man who was about as good as it gets.
17/ A Man of Iron: The Turbulent Life and Improbable Presidency of Grover Cleveland by Troy Senik – America's 22nd and 24th president stood for sound money, free enterprise, low taxes and strong character.
18/ The Child is Father of the Man: C. H. Spurgeon by Tom Nettles – one of several good biographies of the most famous minister of 19th Century England.
19/ The Revolutionary: Samuel Adams by Stacy Schiff—a thorough recounting of the man and his principles that played a huge role in the founding of America.
20/ Red Scarf Girl: A Memoir of the Cultural Revolution by Ji-Li Jiang—a story of the horrors of Mao Zedong's murderous regime from one who experienced the worst of it.
21/ Founding Martyr: The Life and Death of Dr. Joseph Warren, the American Revolution's Lost Hero by Christian Di Spigna—a thrilling walk through the beginnings of the American Revolution and the story of a courageous man who gave his life for it at Bunker Hill.
22/ The Jazz Age President: Warren Harding by Ryan Walters—America's 29th president, often derided as among our worst, deserves far more appreciation than he gets, and Walters explains why.

– Lawrence “Lary” Reed; libertarian; free man; president emeritus of the Foundation for Economic Education (FEE)

title: Studio of the Free Port: Motorists, education and Ježek with Matěj Gregor
text:
Matěj Gregor - the Motorists' expert on education - contacted me to say that he would like to discuss some questions about Hedgehog without a cage; and since I too would like to discuss some questions about the Motorists, I decided to invite him to the Freeport Studio, where we debated (sometimes fiercely).
We started with the overall vision and political program of the Motorists, which mainly consists of streamlining services and modernizing the state; we continued with Matěj's vision of education, which (at least on paper) sounds quite good to me. Finally, Matěj asked about the functioning of Hedgehog without a cage.

– Matej Gregor; expert on the education of the Motorists party itself

title: Anarchy in the context of Parallel Polis Košice
text:
I accepted another invitation to the Košice Parallel Polis; although it's a bit out of hand (1400 km there and back), it makes sense for me to go there and perform, since (I like to drive and) the audience there has a considerable interest in ankap, moreover, I don't meet these libertarians very often otherwise.
I consider this lecture to be one of the best for "advanced" listeners; because the audience was mainly libertarians (often anarcho-capitalists), so there was no need to explain who would build the roads, but we were dealing with anarchy in a broader context, very practically focusing on the individual here and now.

title: Urza on the creation and development of the Liberal constitution
text:
People often invite me to lecture on anarcho-capitalism, (not just self-directed) education, economics and the (free) market; but I have never yet been approached to come and lecture on the Liberal Constitution; until the Ambasáda club did so, where I was happy to visit.
I presented my proposal for the outline of the Liberal constitution, then the comments of the Liberal government to them, the further development of the constitution and the articles of the provisional government (current replacement of the constitution); in this development, I also illustrated the effect on people (including libertarians) of the tempting appeal of power, to which, unfortunately, not many people are immune...

title: Freeport Studio: How the state does not compensate vaccination victims with Natália Bret
text:
Natálie Bret represents a client in court who became paralyzed after a covid vaccine; he should have been compensated by the state, which took responsibility for the side effects of vaccines - supposedly to make it easier for those affected to claim compensation (that's what the politicians claimed at the time).
As an anarchist, I am rarely surprised by the immorality, inefficiency, dysfunctionality or insolence of the state; however, this shocked me. I submit that state courts cannot be impartial in trying an action against a state that pays them; does anyone think otherwise after watching the video?

– Natalia Bret; lawyer; libertarian; attorney for one of the victims of serious side effects of the covid vaccine

title: LibertyCon 2025: Being Right Is Not Enough
text:
I spent a long time thinking about what second topic to present at LibertyCon 2025. In the end, I chose to base it on my older talk Being Right Is Not Enough — which I improved, shortened, and translated into English.
At first glance, it might not seem like a strictly libertarian topic; however, I think it is extremely important for the practical path towards freedom, which I discussed in the talk preceding this one. Our certainty that we are right can actually distance us both from the truth itself and from the ability to share it with others.

title: LibertyCon 2025: Anarcho-agorism
text:
It was a great honor for me to perform at LibertyCon 2025, as its organizers – Students for Liberty – are an initiative I deeply respect; and since this LibertyCon was heavily focused on politics and democracy, I was happy to provide a sort of counterbalance.
I used this opportunity to talk about practical paths to freedom (anarchy); I explained why I don't believe in political ones, but rather base my approach on individual liberty and grassroots strategies, as only bottom-up change can truly transform society. It cannot be centrally planned.

title: Freeport Studio: Relational Anarchy with Ultimate Cuba
text:
Jakub Konečný approached me saying that he would like to speak in the Studio about anarchy (and anarcho-capitalism) in a slightly broader concept; he originally even came up with the idea that "anarcho-capitalism is not enough", which we can agree with, because we certainly need other things in life than just freedom.
We talked about anarchy in all possible types of interpersonal relationships - economic, work, parental, school, friendship, partnership, but also about the relationship of a person to himself; I think it's a very interesting look at anarchy, so hopefully you'll appreciate it too.

– Jakub Konečný; libertarian; member of Students for Liberty; a seeker of knowledge

title: NAP and polycentric law in the Cherubín tea house
text:
One lecture at the Cherubín teahouse eventually became a whole series; I like to go back there because the place has the right tea tree and a great atmosphere (and a Buddha statue with the inscription: "When the god said: "Let there be light," the sound already existed.").
I consider the principle of non-aggression to be one of the basic pillars of anarcho-capitalism; polycentric law is then a practical implementation of free market law. How are they related? Can law have any meaning even without being enforced by force? I answer these - and other - questions in the lecture; I mainly analyze things that are not clear to people on first listen.

title: Urza and Michal Hužva on freedom and self-determination
text:
Michal Hužva wrote in my guest book (https://piste.urza.cz/) several interesting topics related to individual freedom and self-determination; they included deontology and utilitarianism, value rankings, the principle of non-aggression, but also the Hedgehog without a cage and self-management.
As I was intrigued by what he wrote, we set up an online call; and I want to share his recording with you, dear viewers. Our discussion went quite deep, we didn't just skim the surface; I will be very happy if it enriches you as well, which you can - as well as any other observations - share in the comments.

– Michal Hužva; libertarian; explorer of freedom

title: Freeport Studio: Freedom of Speech
text:
In the fiftieth livestream, we return to the roots; for the very first time (then still with Tereza) we streamed precisely about reputation, freedom to gossip and the like. However, since more than five years have passed and this topic is very important, it certainly deserves to be reopened.
We will discuss not only lies, ownership of reputation and good reputation or economic damage caused by slander, but also incitement to violence, murder for hire and we will certainly get to other topics; we will be very happy if you come to chat with us.

– Emma; creator of Freeport; anarcho-capitalist; libertarian; student Hedgehog without a cage

title: Studio of the Freeport: Libor Vondráček and Svobodní on the SPD candidate list
text:
After apologizing for the (unsuccessful) coalition with the Tricolor, the Liberals are going to run with it again; and unfortunately, not only with her, but also together with PRO Jindřich Rajchl, they all appear together on the SPD candidate list, which made me wonder if they would apologize even in the event of a successful candidacy.
I understand that after sixteen years of trying to get into Parliament, Liberals are frustrated by the failures; but really, the way to ensure success is to join parties with a fairly socialist program? How does Libor Vondráček see this and how does he justify his decision?

– Libor Vondráček; chairman of the Free Citizens Party

title: Anarcho-capitalism: How much does the state cost (us)?
text:
The April lecture in the Anarcho-Capitalism series will take place the day after April Fools' Day, which is a good thing, because otherwise you might think I'm joking; I want to calculate how much the state actually costs us. Being a theorist (which many consider a slur, but I certainly am not), you are used to theory from me; this time, however, we will look at the specific practice of the state - we will calculate not only individual taxes (including those called "insurance", fees and the like), but also other costs. We will pay special attention to pensions, as they make up the largest part of the state budget; and we will show how we could live without a pay-as-you-go - Ponzi - pension system. I will also explain why the day of tax freedom according to the Freeport would be even after the Deloitte or Liberal.
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/bbc/bbc70.cenastatu.pdf
Calculation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/bbc/bbc70.cenastatu.xlsx

title: Urza and Tim debate with Gabriela Svárovská and Matěj Pomaháč
text:
Two Green Party chairmen approached Tim with a desire to debate; and I'm very happy that Tim chose me as a debate partner, even though I didn't manage to give him space, which I want to learn.
We discussed human rights, equality between women and men, redistribution and the voluntariness of individual decisions about their lives; our views were mostly fundamentally different.

– Gabriela Svárovská; co-chair of the Green Party; human rights activist; publicist
– Matěj Pomaháč; co-chairman of the Green Party; agricultural consultant
– Timofey Kozhuchov; libertarian; YouTuber; student of political science and philosophy; LGBT activist

title: Studio of the Free Port: About Ross Ulbricht with Lukáš Pazderník
text:
After ten years, Ross Ulbricht was pardoned by Donald Trump; this caused enthusiasm among libertarians, but also controversy - because the accusation of murder-for-hire is probably no longer against him, even though nothing was ever proven against him (it didn't even go to trial).
I've been following Ross Ulbricht's case pretty much since the beginning; and I found out that Lukáš Pazderník does so in much more detail, so I invited him to the Studio of the Free Port, where we talked not only about Ross's arrest and release, but above all about his life.

– Lukáš Pazderník; anarchist; volunteer; philosopher; supporter of the Free Port

title: Urza in Talks of Anarchy: Freedom and Self-Government
text:
Lukáš Pazderník is a long-term supporter (and occasional author and commentator) of the Free Port; I like his way of thinking and I like our discussions - that's why I gladly accepted his proposal for an online conversation about self-management.
This time Lukáš presented his theses, on which he wanted my comments and feedback; I think we ended up agreeing on all points, as my contributions tended to refine or modify his thesis rather than completely contradicting it. Even so, I enjoyed our conversation.

– Lukáš Pazderník; anarchist; volunteer; philosopher; supporter (and occasional author and commentator) of Freeport

title: Urza in the podcast And who would build roads?
text:
I happily accepted an invitation to the "competition" podcast And Who Would Build Roads? We talked about anarcho-capitalism and anarcho-capitalists.

– Teri the Idealist; anarcho-capitalist; author of the podcast And who would build roads?
– Václav Veselý; anarcho-capitalist; podcast author And Who Would Build Roads?

title: Studio of the Free Port: Customs (not only from Trump) with Vlaďa Krupa
text:
You often write about reactions to current events in the Czech Republic or in the world; I don't (targetedly) respond to some, but tariffs are something I feel a strong need to talk about. This is one of the oldest taxes; and despite various political proclamations, it only harms the economy.
Vláďa Kurpa is a counterpart to the economy and geopolitical situation, including (especially) historical contexts; that is why I invited him to talk about this topic together. Of course, we deal mainly with Trump, but far from only him!

– Vladimir Krupa; longtime contributor to Mises.cz; libertarian; analyst of the (current and historical) geopolitical situation

title: About the (non)state company for the Josef Božek Gymnasium in Český Těšín
text:
The students of the Josef Božek Gymnasium in Český Těšín asked me to come and tell them (not only) about anarcho-capitalism; I was very happy to come to see them (and if you also find meaning in it, you can contribute to my trip in the ways mentioned above).
We addressed the state, alternatives to it, but also free self-directed education; we showed each other how everything could be different without knowing or thinking about it. It could be seen that the initially apathetic students were interested in my lecture (although they show much less in the classical school than in the alternative schools); a few of them even came to thank me afterwards.

title: Urza in TradeCZ
text:
Petr Plecháč invited me to his TradeCZ podcast; his questions surprised and pleased me at the same time, because they differed from other similar interviews in some way - I don't actually know if it was dynamic, content or something else.

– Petr Plecháč; author of the TradeCZ podcast; financial market analyst; trader

title: Freeport Studio: About LibertyCon and SfL with Honza Mošovský
text:
LibertyCon is coming soon! do you have tickets If not, you can buy them at https://libertycon.net/; after entering the discount code URZA you will get a 50% discount. Shall we meet there?
If you are hesitating, this video is just for you – in it, we rebuild LibertyCon with Honza Mošovský; and not only that, we are also talking about Students for Liberty, that is, the organization of which Honza is a member and which organizes LibertyCon. Which is not all! We discuss, for example, the situation in Ukraine or politics in the USA and populism there and in Europe; Do you think Fico is an ideologue or a pure pragmatist? We didn't agree.

– Jan Mošovský; anarcho-objectivist; libertarian; member of Students for Liberty

title: Urza is (slowly) turning CzechCloud into a libertarian
text:
CzechCloud invited me (again) to his livestream; we dealt with freedom, the system of social justice, pensions... and above all, I blew CzechCloud's breath away by describing the principle of economic calculation.

– CzechCloud; Czech streamer; youtuber; (political) commentator; former professional player and World Hearthstone Champion

title: Urza with the Quakers on the search for consensus
text:
Vláďa – one of the parents of children from Ježek – approached me with an offer to interview the Quakers about their decision-making process; and I'm really glad that several of them took the time to meet me and explained to me how it works for them (including answers to my questions) - they also described the disadvantages of democratic voting and what is better about finding a consensus of all involved.

– Paul; main contact of Czech Quakers; a longtime member of the Quakers from České Budějovice
– Ondra; the first Czech accepted member of the Quakers
– Andre; a Quaker from the USA with many years of experience in the decision-making process in the Czech Republic and abroad
– Vlaďa; apathetic; new to the quakers (not yet a member)

title: Urza with Jakub Novák (SOCDEM) about self-management for Students for Liberty
text:
Students for Liberty organized a debate on self-management in my beloved Pilsen, to which they invited me as a supporter and Jakub Novák from Social Democracy as an opponent of this concept of education; I was very happy to accept their invitation for the topic and venue of the debate.
Right from the start, we ran into the problem of defining the "general basis of education", which although we want children, we have a problem describing it other than with examples; in the debate we often came to the question of whether the goal of education is the happiness of the individual or the benefit of society.

– Jakub Novák; member of the Young Social Democrats; member of the Social Democracy; budding politician

title: Gabriela and Urza: A debate at the Scio school reunion that turned into a conversation
text: The students of Scio schools invited me to their meeting where we were to discuss alternative methods of teaching; in the end it "degenerated" into a conversation with Gabriela, who accompanied me there. I found it interesting to observe how the approaches of Scio school students (and not only) to freedom differ from each other.

title: Freeport Studio: Anarchism & Capitalism
text:
Anarchism and capitalism are perceived by society as great opposites (in addition, both strongly hated); anarcho-capitalists, thanks to Murray Newton Rothbard, see them as two designations of the same condition—that is, a free society.
Emma and I would like to discuss what anarchism and capitalism mean for us - and for you; what do those terms evoke? We would also like to address separately both anarchism and capitalism (including social impacts); we also want to distinguish anarchy from chaos and capitalism from consumerism.

– Emma; creator of Freeport; anarcho-capitalist; libertarian; student Hedgehog without a cage

title: Free Harbor Studio: About freedom in different countries with Jan Vidim
text:
Jan Vidim sent me an email with his travel experiences; and although travel books are perhaps the most boring reading for me personally, I found that when their central theme is freedom, I enjoy it a lot - so much so that I invited Honza to the Studio of the Free Port.
We compared freedom in the Czech Republic and abroad; then we got to interesting places all over the earth - from no man's land to no-go zones to states in civil wars. Honzo's view of people (or humanity) as such often surfaced in conversation; and I must say that I more than resonated with him.
