title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Spontaneous Order
text:
I want to dedicate the March lecture from the series Anarchocapitalism to a topic I have been dealing with for almost twenty years; that theme is spontaneous order - the creation of rules "from below" without the existence of a central authority or violent coercion. After studying theory for so long, there is nothing better than when one gets the opportunity to verify one's knowledge in practice! In Hedgehog Without a Cage, I understood that schools based on self-directed education are excellent examples of decentralized rule-making; so I started visiting these schools and comparing the experience from Ježek with other similar collectives. In doing so, I came to some unexpected conclusions that really surprised me; and it is in this lecture that I would very much like to share them with you and also discuss them.
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/bbc/

title: Gabriela and Urza with a love of freedom and learning for the UOL Club
text: As part of our series of talks with Gabriela, we visited the entrepreneurial UOL Club; I was interested in how entrepreneurs who had never heard of self-management responded to it - their questions went in a slightly different direction than what we are used to from other discussions. What do you think?

title: Freeport Conference 2025 Panel Discussion: Culture Wars Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow
text:
We ended the Freeport 2025: Culture Wars yesterday, today and tomorrow conference with a panel discussion in which Urza, Tim Kožuchov, Roman Joch, Teri Idealistka Paul and Pavel Ševčík took part; Ema took on the role of moderator.

The complete program of the conference can be found here:
https://konference.urza.cz/2025/img/program.1024x1448.png

title: Pavel Ševčík: Culture war in Hollywood and its victims (KSP25: Culture wars yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
The sixth speaker of the "Free Harbor 2025 Conference: Culture Wars Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow" was Pavel Ševčík with his lecture "The Culture War in Hollywood and its Victims".

How does the culture war manifest itself in Hollywood production? Who is actually at war with whom? And is it really a battle between progressivism and conservatism, or something else? We will find the answer to these questions and show ourselves who paid the most for the culture war.

Pavel Ševčík is a programmer and crypto-anarchist. He has a long-term interest in technological, political and cultural issues and their influence on contemporary society.

title: Teri Paul: State vs Identity, How the State Harms Trans People (KSP25: Culture Wars Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow)
text:
The fifth speaker of the "2025 Freeport Conference: Culture Wars Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow" was Teri Paul with her talk "State vs. Identity: How the State Harms Trans People."

Trans people face many obstacles in expressing their identity, and the state is often not a helper, but rather a source of problems. Society may seem open, but state laws and regulations often lag behind. At the lecture, we will show concrete examples of how the state restricts the freedom of trans people - from official administration to access to medical care.

Teri "The Idealist" Paul is a volunteer and freedom advocate. She creates videos on the YouTube channel "idealistka" and is the co-founder of the podcast "And who would build roads?".

title: Vláďa Krupa: History of the Culture Wars (KSP25: Culture Wars Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow)
text:
The fourth speaker of the "Free Harbor Conference 2025: Culture Wars Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow" was Vláďa Krupa with his lecture "History of Culture Wars".

Political agitation since the mass expansion of suffrage takes place not only through direct methods such as election campaigns or advertising spots, but also through indirect influences that have a long-term and often subtle impact on public opinion. These indirect methods are, for example, novels, songs, plays, films and other forms of mass-consumed culture. These cultural influences often shape the political opinions of people who shy away from direct political messages. An example of the influence of these cultural methods is the process that took place in Great Britain in the 19th century. There, a combination of literary influences and the programs of the Fabian Society succeeded in transforming the ethos of classical liberalism into evolutionary socialism. Key figures of this change were, for example, John Stuart Mill, Bernard Shaw, Sidney Webb or authors such as Carlyle, Ruskin and Kingsley. This process of transformation of public opinion from the perception of state power as an inhibiting factor of progress to the perception of the state as a guarantee of freedom and an engine of progress was achieved to a large extent precisely through the non-violent path of cultural influences.

Vladimír Krupa is the co-founder of the Czech Mises Institute, an organization focused on spreading the ideas of the Austrian school of economics and individual freedom. As a prominent translator and author of articles, he has been devoted to the topics of economic history and monetary history for a long time, which enables him to look at the culture wars from a unique economic and historical angle.

title: Urza: Culture Wars or Freedom? (KSP25: Culture Wars Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow)
text:
The third speaker of the "2025 Freeport Conference: Culture Wars Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow" was Urza with his lecture "Culture Wars or Freedom?".

Conservatives feel that progressive "woke" propaganda is taking away their freedom (often through the state); progressives, on the other hand, are convinced that their freedom is limited precisely by conservatives (often through state intervention). And so culture wars arise... But which of the above statements is true? Unfortunately, both; and when two fight, the third laughs. Who is the third one? The state, of course... What about it? I'm afraid the only workable solution is to stop fighting, however tempting it may be to involve the state in the conflict; for the state is a bad servant, but a bad master. I find it infinitely naive to think that the culture war can be "won" with the help of state power without serious consequences for both sides; thus only authoritarians can win, while freethinkers will be defeated.

Urza is an anarcho-capitalist author and teacher at the self-governing Hedgehog Without a Cage school; wrote over a thousand libertarian texts on the web and in print media and the first Czech book on anarcho-capitalism. For fifteen years, he not only reads, thinks and writes about freedom, education, the free market and the role of the state in society, but also lectures, discusses, debates and makes videos. Together with his student Emma from the Hedgehog without a cage, he forms the Free Harbor; he heads the Czech and Slovak Institute of Ludwig von Mises, of which he is a co-founder; belongs to the board of the Freedom of Learning association and cooperates with many libertarian initiatives. You can find more about him on the Urza.cz website.

title: Timofej Kožuchov: We are not afraid of progressivism (KSP25: Culture wars yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
The second speaker of the "2025 Freeport Conference: Culture Wars Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow" was Tim Kožuchov with his lecture "Let's not be afraid of progressivism".

Most people associate the word progress with a positive emotion. But why is this not the case when we talk about progressivism as a political ideology? During the lecture, we will talk about the history and meaning of this term. We will look at a frequent dispute in libertarian circles about whether a free society must also be a progressive society. Progressivism does not have to be about imposing new values, but about opening space for dialogue and respect for diversity.

The lecture will be given by Timofej Kožuchov. Tim was born in Russia, has Czech citizenship. He studied political science, economics and philosophy in London. On his channel Debatní deník, he comments on social issues and debates with people he disagrees with. In 2022, then a staunch socialist, he first debated with Urza about ankap and freedom. After reading many books and listening to many lectures, Tim is now a libertarian.

title: Freeport Studio: The direction of Freeport
text:
We all evolve and grow over time; I myself perceive that as I change, my work changes with me, which many of you have registered. Some respond positively to the change and appreciate more kindness or openness; others do not like it and miss confrontational debates.
However, it is not just a way of conducting debates; The free port already consists of quite a lot of projects and formats, but we will be happy for any other ideas. Anything is open to discussion; that doesn't mean we'll accept every idea, but we'll definitely listen to them.

– Emma; creator of Freeport; anarcho-capitalist; libertarian; student Hedgehog without a cage

title: R. Joch: Conservatism is freedom, progressivism is the opposite (KSP25: Culture wars yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
The first speaker of the "Free Harbor Conference 2025: Culture wars yesterday, today and tomorrow" was Roman Joch with his lecture "Why conservatism is for freedom and why progressivism is against it".

Conservatism wants the state to defend society, but not to interfere with its spontaneous, free development; progressivism wants the state to intervene and "improve" it, prohibiting and commanding people to do various things. Conservatism is for private property, progressivism not so much, or even against. Conservatism perceives man as a unique individual, an original; progressivism through the prism of gender, racial, sexual, cis- or trans-gender identity and intersectionality. Conservatism wants to protect (conserve) Western Civilization, the cradle of freedom; progressivism considers it uniquely evil and wants to "deconstruct" it and replace it with a new, "better" post-civilization.

Roman Joch (1971) is a columnist and university teacher. He studied general medicine at Charles University in Prague. He is the chairman of the Civic Institute. In the years 2010-12, he was an advisor to the Prime Minister of the Czech Republic for human rights and foreign policy, and in the years 2020-23, he was the director of the Institute for Work and Family Research in Bratislava, Slovakia. He is a teacher at the University of Economics and CEVRO University, where he also works as a Senior Fellow of its Center for Transatlantic Relations (PCTR). He is the author of several books and studies on political philosophy and politics, a contributor to the Czech and Slovak media. Among his books are "Rebellion Against the 20th Century Revolution," about American post-war conservatism, and "No, Mr. Prime Minister!" on the experience of the advisor to the Prime Minister.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: The "Failure" of the Market
text:
The February lecture from the cycle Anarchocapitalism will be devoted to so-called market "failures"; or perhaps it would not be appropriate to write "market" failure - indeed, on the basis of them, suboptimal allocation of resources can occur (i.e. outside the Pareto optimum), but I do not consider this so much a property of the market, but rather a property of the world. In my opinion, this is one of the most obvious (unfortunately sanctified by the academic sphere) economic mistakes; however, it is unfortunately so widespread that almost every time I mention it, there is a proponent of it. So I decided to devote a whole lecture to him; I'd love for you to come - especially if you believe in market failure - and argue with me and challenge my arguments.
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/bbc/

title: Studio of the Free Port: About the Prague school Drak with Katka Čápová
text:
Katka Čápová - with other co-founders - founded the (self-managed) Drak school a year ago; however, the owner of the (approved) building backed out on the day the contract was signed, with the result that Drak also lost its state registered school status, so the Drakians founded a community school.
However, they were not discouraged by the failures and are trying to start again from the next school year - in another building in Zdibe; however, for this they need money, volunteers and children, which is the reason why Katka performs in the Studio. Maybe this is the opportunity for you!

– Katka Čápová; co-founder of Drak School; supporter of self-directed education; anarcho-capitalist

title: Conversation about cryptocurrencies for the entrepreneurial UOL Club
text:
Entrepreneurial UOL Club held a conference on money; as part of that they invited me to talk about cryptocurrencies; the entire conference had only short twenty-minute presentations, which is not an ideal format for me, but I was happy to accept anyway, because I like this topic very much.
The interview with me was conducted by the founder of the club, Jana Jáčová; luckily, we didn't cover any investments or how much bitcoin will cost, but we did cover its decentralized freedom-related features or possible government regulations that are still tightening up.

– Jana Jáčová; founder of the UOL Club

title: Freeport Studio: About (anti)drug policy with Jindřich Vobořil
text:
I have been following Jindřich Vobořil for a long time; I agree with some of his performances, with some I don't, but above all they seem quite diverse (opinionally), which is something I wanted to ask him for a long time - and that's why I invited him to the Studio, among other things.
We talked about drugs, repression, prevention and harm reduction; Jindřich Vobořil takes a rather pragmatic approach to the whole issue, based on numbers and hard data. His pragmatic approach, however, brings to a large extent similar starting points as an ideological leaning towards freedom.

– Jindřich Vobořil; (former) National Anti-Drug Coordinator; founder and chief director of the Podané ruce Association

title: Getting to know cryptocurrencies at the Scio school in Prague
text: Students from Prague's Scio school wanted to learn something about cryptocurrencies; I was delighted when they approached me to introduce them.

title: Studio Freeport: About freedom (and not only) speech with Gabriela Sedláčková
text:
Gabriela Sedláčková and I have been following each other - and respect each other - for quite a few years now; and although we talked about the conversation a long time ago, the time has come for it (and I think that today our conversation looked a lot different than it would have looked, say, two years ago).
First, we addressed freedom of speech and my perception of the Society for the Defense of Freedom of Expression, which Gabriela more or less confirmed to him; then we honed in on national conservatism and finally on education and child rearing.

– Gabriela Sedláčková; manager at the Society for the Defense of Free Speech; owner of Bar Behind the Curtain; Christian; supporter of nationally conservative positions

title: EU fines Intel
text:
In 2009, the EU fined Intel $1.1 billion for "conditional rebates" and "naked restrictions" (payments to those who do not buy from competitors); Intel sued the EU and won in 2022 because the EU's "conditional rebates" failed to prove a specific impact on competition (and the fine did not specify which part was for "conditional rebates" and which part was for "naked restrictions"). In 2023, the EU demonstrated the effects of "naked restrictions", for which it fined Intel $386 million; but Intel sued the EU for lost interest on the wrongful fine, which had risen to $536 over those 15 years. The entire court case therefore cost taxpayers $150 million - if we do not count the expenses for the European Union authorities, which messed up the decision and subsequently dealt with it for many years.

That story deserves (in addition to our money) Hitler's commentary with subtitles, don't you think?

title: Freeport Studio: Culture Wars with Karolína K.
text:
A pre-conference livestream is often associated with it; and it will be no different in February. The Culture Wars conference will be preceded by a livestream on the same topic. However, I am not inviting any of the speakers to the Studio in order not to reveal the content of the conference.
February's guest will be my friend Karolína Kváš; on the one hand, we haven't filmed together for a long time, but above all, the topic of culture wars is close to her, she is interested in them, she doesn't have a very specific attitude towards it, and her mind is always open. Come create with us!

– Karolína Kváš (https://karolinakvas.cz/); tarot rebel; authoress; traveler; anthropologist; blogger; creator; coach

title: Free Port Studio: Fifty Shades of Anarchy with Štěpán Sukdol
text:
Štěpán Sukdol refers to himself as an anarchist; when asked to elaborate, he does not hesitate to describe himself as an anarcho-syndicalist but also a voluntarist, which to libertarians may seem an unlikely or odd combination to say the least.
Our conversation about anarchism actually quite surprised me; although I expected a lot of friction, we found more and more agreement wrapped up in just different terminology. Although we probably have slightly different ideas about the world, as voluntarists we tolerate each other; and thus we agree on non-violence.

– Štěpán Sukdol; anarchist; volunteer; anarcho-syndicalist; agorist

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Punishments
text:
The December lecture from the cycle Anarchocapitalism will be devoted to punishments and the concept of punishment in general; and it will (at least for me) be challenging for many reasons. First of all, I will try to separate my personal views from anarcho-capitalism as such as much as possible, which will be needed here, but I am afraid that it will still be the same for many people. Next, I will come up with a criticism of something, to which I will not present a functional alternative; nevertheless, I consider this criticism so fundamental that I want to present it anyway. In addition, the issue of punishments is one area in which my opinion has shifted significantly in recent years, for example since the publication of the book Anarcho-kapitalismus or the lectures in Paralelní Polis; that's why I'll be happy for any feedback!
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/bbc/

title: Freeport Studio: Fifty Shades of NAP with Ori
text:
Ori made a very nice impression on me when we met in Tim's Debate Club, where we debated together as a team; even our subsequent conversation in the Studio made a lot of sense to me, so I did not hesitate to invite her again when she wrote to me about (interesting) topics she would like to discuss.
Although initially there were a lot of them, in the end we more or less revolved around the NAP most of the time; sometimes it felt a bit like the "favorite" questions from the Forum, but it definitely made more and more complete sense to me (not that I don't enjoy the questions on the Forum). Towards the end, we also reached self-management (and not only in connection with the NAP).

– Ori; member of the debate club

title: Getting to know ankap at the Scio school in Brno
text:
The students of the Brno Scio school have been dealing with alternative social arrangements for the past month; so far, they are most interested in ankap and non-growth. They originally wanted to hold a debate of the representative of the ankap against the representative of the spawn; it ended up falling apart because we couldn't find a date, so they invited us one after the other.
The format was a talk; and with good questions from the audience (many focused on ecology). In the end, it turned out that I only convinced one of the students directly about the ankap; on the other hand, during the discussion, several of them dropped their sympathy for infertility, which surprised me, since we did not deal with it much.

title: Freeport Studio: About economics and Bitcoin with Lenka Zlámalová
text:
I know Lenka Zlámalová from her appearances in the Czech media, where she is often the voice of (libertarian) reason; has a negative attitude towards regulations, but above all warns against the ever-increasing dependence of citizens on the state. However, she recently filmed an interview where she questioned the importance of cryptocurrencies.
First, we addressed the economy and market laws for small and large companies, big tech and the connection between corporations and states; then we got to crypto-currencies – or rather Bitcoin – and their real importance for the economy, which I hope I managed to convince Lenka Zlámalová in the end.

– Lenka Zlámalová; economist; journalist; publicist

title: Urza at the 2024 Autism Conference
text: At the fifth Autism Conference, we were originally supposed to have a discussion with Gabriela and introduce Ježek; in the end it didn't work out, so I just performed on my own and we also dealt with my Asperger's.

title: Free Harbor Studio: About Ježek and freedom with Honza
text:
Honza is a friend of mine who has been studying at Ježek without a cage for about half a year longer than I have been working there; at the same time, he deals with libertarian ideas, which he was led to by Free Harbor, which I was surprised to find out only recently, and I was actually very pleased.
We resolved the differences between the Hedgehog without a cage and the gymnasium from which Honza came to us; the whole conversation thus touched on freedom, but also on defiance (not only) of authority, but also of orders in general. We also talked about self-development, but also anarcho-capitalism, libertarianism and Bitcoin.

– John; student from Hedgehog without a cage; libertarian; anarcho-capitalist; bitcoiner

title: Urza about ankap in hackerspace Base48
text:
I like hackerspaces; that's why I was pleased by the invitation from Brno's Base48 to come and tell them something about the basics of anarcho-capitalism (even for people who have never heard of it - although most have). I really enjoyed lecturing between 3D printers, milling machines, CNC machines and all sorts of other hardware.
First, I described the ankap for about a quarter of an hour, then I answered questions from the audience; we mostly focused on the hegemony of power, the potential monopolization of security agencies and structures, but there were also many other topics from ecology to socialism to economics - yesterday, today and tomorrow.

title: Freeport Studio: About Pirates and Freedom with Ivan Bartoš
text:
Ivan Bartoš was the chairman of the Czech Pirate Party practically throughout its existence; now he is a pirate MP. Since I have been criticizing the Pirates for a long time, I decided to discuss it directly with Ivan Bartoš personally in the Studio; I'm glad he accepted my invitation.
We talked about the vision of his political career and the meaning of the founding of the Pirates; we discussed freedom - we probably perceive it diametrically differently. Of course, we did not forget the digitization of the state administration, which is important to me!

– Ivan Bartoš; one of the founders and former chairman of the Czech Pirate Party; Member of Parliament; former Deputy Prime Minister for Digitization

title: Urza in KryptoSpace
text:
Petr Lukáč did an interview with me years ago for Hospodářské noviny - one of his first ever about cryptocurrencies; now he's reached out to me to chat about crypto again on his KryptoSpace podcast.

– Petr Lukáč; longtime business journalist; crypto podcaster; former editor of Hospodářské noviny

title: Free Harbor Studio: About business and freedom with Jirka Fabián
text:
In the past, Jirka Fabián invited me a few times to his podcast or to the company TopMonks for a discussion about anarcho-capitalism, which was nice - because these are interesting projects; a few years later, I also decided to invite him to the Freeport Studio.
We talked about his business, startups and companies (almost) without hierarchy; we also dealt with libertarianism, minarchism and anarchism, but eventually we also honed in on Taoism. We also touched on the possible re-establishment of – a little different – Parallel Polis.

– Jiří Fabián; libertarian; anarchist; Taoist; startup wizard; founder of JetMinds and TopMonks

title: Urza with Kryštof Chajda about utility and NAP in Debatní Deník
text:
Kryštof Chajda listened to my presentation with Tomáš Guth Jarkovský, where he was interested in the part in which we debated the measurability and interpersonal incomparability of utility; invited me to a discussion in Debatní Deník, where he decided to oppose my theses, which I gladly accepted.
We covered the utility in the first part of the show; most of the time we dealt with the NAP, the definition of which Kryštof first called cyclical, which he took back after a while. Later we got to the (evolutionary and utilitarian) origins of the NAP; but also to why I actually consider it a natural right.

– Kryštof Chajda; member of Tim's Debate Club

title: Freeport Studio: Christmas Talk 2024
text:
In the Christmas video, you usually heard some kind or nice message, or something that I thought was important, while in the New Year's video, Teresa and I always took stock of the past year from the perspective of the Harbor and beyond; this year, however, this will be a little different.
Emma and I decided to merge the videos into one Christmas video; in addition to our Christmas messages, we also summarize events in the Freeport, but also in the Czech Republic and a little bit abroad, even if only from my subjective (and at the same time) libertarian point of view.

– Emma; creator of Freeport; anarcho-capitalist; libertarian; student Hedgehog without a cage

title: Urza for the Club of Young Political Scientists at VŠE
text: The club of young political scientists from VŠE approached me with a request to record a podcast with me; we discussed ankap and mainly discussed education, polycentric law and other topics.

title: Freeport studio: Not only about politics with Jakub Horák
text:
I know Jakub Horák from his Eccentric Club, of which I was a member for some time, and in addition I lectured and gave talks there a few times; I decided to invite him to the Freeport Studio and discuss (not only) political marketing with him.
Unsurprisingly, the conversation turned to the Pirates, as Jakub Horák helped them enter high politics; I was interested in how he evaluates his decision with distance and what he actually thinks about the Pirates. We also dealt with democracy or digitization of state administration; at the end of the interview, Jakub asked about ankap.

– Jakub Horák; political marketer; founder of the Eccentric Club; writer, producer, satirist

title: Urza in the program Real life with Jaroslav Grűnwald about the "system" and education
text:
Jaroslav Grűnwald invited me (for the second time) to his show Real Life, where we talked about the "system" (and the "anti-system") and education; we also got to the elections, the current political scene, specifically the Pirate Party and the various dangers associated with it.

– Jaroslav Grűnwald; shaman; lecturer; therapist

title: Urza and political scientist Jan Charvát (far from only) about anarchy
text:
Jan Charvát is a political scientist, and I was impressed by the fact that (in my opinion) he does his job really well - he describes, analyzes, looks for connections, but at the same time does not judge and does not bring his personal evaluations and beliefs into the research, which he obviously likes to talk about.
I originally invited him to discuss anarchism, which eventually happened; however, we started with a thorough historical description of the political spectrum from the Great French Revolution to the present with a lot of (at least for me) interesting detours.

– Jan Charvát; political scientist; an expert on political extremism; teacher at the Institute of Political Studies FSV UK

title: Freeport Studio: Privatization with Dušan Tříska
text:
The interview with Dušan Tříska was very important for me personally, mainly for reasons that the audience probably didn't even notice; however, the response was so incredibly positive that it exceeded my (already very high) expectations.
So I decided to invite Dušan Tříska to the livestream as well; partly because I forgot to ask him one important question, but also so that you could ask too. I hope you will take advantage of this and come create our show with me!

– Dušan Tříska; the father of Voucher Privatization; economist (in both socialism and capitalism); mathematician; physicist; lawyer; scientist; academician; economic libertarian

title: Free Port Studio: "A child has the right to die," says Martina from Erazim
text:
Martina from Erazim caught my attention at the Association of Free and Democratic Schools when she talked about her approach to self-management - hers and her children's. Since then, we have met several times in Ježek or Erazim, which led to my invitation to the Studio.
Martina lives self-management quite radically; when her three-year-old daughter was in danger, she did not take her to the hospital until she had her consent. In her own words, this experience taught her that a child has the right to die; these words alone make this one of my rawest conversations about self-management.

– Martina; a person who lives self-directed education; teacher in Erazim, Opava

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: The People's Creative Economy
text:
In November, we will focus on the economy in the cycle Anarchocapitalism; this time the people's creative economy. Some argue that economic science is intuitive; others do not find it intuitive, or even perceive it as counterintuitive. I think that although they all have some part of the truth, I would like to deal mainly with those parts of economics that work differently than one would expect without a deeper study; because from these arise all sorts of false assumptions, on the basis of which we can, for example, during democratic elections, vote for politicians who directly harm our interests, although we can believe that the opposite is the case. I will also try to explain where these economic fallacies come from; because I believe that they arise completely naturally and inevitably.
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/bbc/

title: The Free Port Studio: On Objectivism with Ondřej Starek
text:
Ondřej Stárek responded to an interview about Objectivism with Jiří Kinkor; he wrote a text clarifying some of Mr. Kinkor's theses in a way that I could understand. Based on our subsequent conversation, I decided to invite him to the Studio; I think that his explanation of objectivism could be closer to you as well.
We devoted ourselves to objectivist morality and a bit of political philosophy; but we also dealt with the basic axioms and principles of objectivism, including the derivation of other consequences and implications. This conversation probably brought me the closest to Objectivism; I don't agree with everything, but at least I understand something.
– Ondřej Starek; objectivist

title: Freedom in the Cherubín teahouse
text:
One lecture at the Cherubín teahouse eventually became a whole series; I like to go back there because the place has the right tea tree and a great atmosphere (and a Buddha statue with the inscription: "When the god said: "Let there be light," the sound already existed.").
I have been dealing with freedom basically all my life; and even though in recent years I have been mainly dealing with inner freedom, I don't want to stay only with it, although I also touched on it in the lecture. Above all, however, I devoted myself to exchanging freedom for security, which Benjamin Franklin had already talked about; it has a lot of interesting implications, but above all the reasons why people do it in the first place...

title: Freeport Studio: On Freedom and Hierarchy with Ori
text:
I met Ori in Tim's debate club where we were on the debating team together; after the debate ended, she had some interesting questions for me, which interested me so much that I invited her to the Studio, which Ori accepted (probably also because she watches the Freeport Channel for a long time).
First we defined freedom; Ori came up with a definition that expanded mine, though not in a very practical direction for me. Most of the time we dealt with the effects of (mainly voluntary) hierarchies; but also their weakening. We wanted to make it to the NAP as well, but in the end we left it for the next time; a number of other topics also arose.

– Ori; member of the debate club

title: Urza with CzechCloud about the free market
text:
CzechCloud got into debates about anarcho-capitalism in livestreams; and so you invited me - we talked about the principles, functions and consequences of the free market and the (Austrian) economy.

– CzechCloud; Czech streamer; youtuber; (political) commentator; former professional player and World Hearthstone Champion

title: I am not the state!
text: "We are the state because we make the state," an opponent told me in one debate; I felt the need to explain to him that I am definitely not the state. Although my explanation was more than a minute long, I shortened it a bit to fit this video format; I tried to at least keep the most important things.

title: Freeport Studio: Self-Management with Gabriela
text:
For the fourth November in a row, Gabriela Ježková - the founder and director of the Ježek school without a cage in Brno - is a guest of the Livestream of the Free Port; in those four years, we have come a long way together, a non-negligible part of which is precisely self-management.
Self-management is our big theme that we talk about often; but every time we focus on him as part of talking about something else - for example, the Hedgehog without a cage. This time we decided to explain what self-management is and dedicate a separate livestream to it.

– Gabriela Ježková; founder, owner and director of the Ježek bez klece free school in Brno; anarchist; libertarian; a teacher

title: Freeport Studio: Right to Life
text:
With Emma, we consider self-ownership to be one of the fundamental pillars of freedom and libertarian ideas in general; that's why we decided to dedicate an entire section of the Free Port Studio to it, in which we analyze its consequences and practical effects on our freedom.
We dealt with suicides and respect for the decisions of people who choose to end their lives; we talked about assisted suicide and euthanasia, which some countries allow (the Czech Republic does not, although it circumvents the ban); finally we discussed abortions and surrogacy.

– Emma; creator of Freeport; anarcho-capitalist; libertarian; student Hedgehog without a cage

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Protecting Minorities
text:
In October, Tim Kožuchov will give a lecture as part of the cycle Anarchocapitalism; he has been dedicated to minority rights for a long time. We often hear that liberal democracy is there to protect minorities. But does it happen in practice? In which cases does the state harm and in which cases does it protect minorities? The lecture is mainly focused on various marginalized groups - i.e. Roma, homosexuals, transgender people and the like. We will also talk about the experiences of specific members of minorities with the state.
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/bbc/

– Timofey Kozhuchov; libertarian; YouTuber; student of political science and philosophy; LGBT activist

title: Freeport Studio: Farmer Jiří Syrovátka: "I'm better off without subsidies."
text:
It was a nice coincidence that you asked for an interview about agriculture and at the same time Jiří Syrovátka contacted me, because he wanted to correct something that was said in the Studio regarding subsidies; Jiří Syrovátka is a competitive farmer who refuses subsidies.
Together we dealt with various (not only) European agricultural subsidies and their effects; although I'm used to many things, I have to admit that a lot of information from the interview surprised me, because the inefficiency of subsidies exceeded even my wildest (anarchist) expectations.

– Jiří Syrovátka; peasant; farmer; orchardist; businessman; co-owner of Chrámce Castle Gardens; practical libertarian; subsidy opponent

title: Basics of ankap for the Parallel Polis Left
text:
The performance at Paralelná Polis Košice, where I first presented anarcho-capitalism and then Gabriela and I talked about self-management and Hedgehog without a cage, also attracted the attention of Paralelná Polis Left, which invited us for the same purpose; and we gladly accepted their invitation.
Everyone in the audience was familiar with anarcho-capitalism (at least to some extent), so we moved on from the basics quite quickly; after the classic questions (there were also recreational nuclear weapons), perhaps the most interesting part came to me about the political (un)enforceability of anarcho-capitalism, where several new arguments were voiced.

title: About logic, argumentation, evidence and the scientific method with Tim
text:
Tim approached me for a consultation on his (in-progress) book on debating and argumentation; although it may not be directly related to ankap or libertarianism, it is definitely at least indirectly related in my opinion, which is why I am publishing the interview here.
The beginning of the debate was a bit academic, and it took us a while to understand each other; but as time gradually passed, I think we came to more and more interesting questions and topics. There were also – important for me – observations regarding science, the scientific method, evidence and experimental verification.

– Timofey Kozhuchov; creator of the Debate Journal; active libertarian; a seeker of knowledge

title: Freeport Studio: Equal pay for equal work!?
text:
"Equal pay for equal work!" Lately we have been hearing this slogan from trade unionists and socialists of various stripes; they are celebrating a victory - the courts of all instances (including the Constitutional Court) ruled in favor of the Olomouc driver who sued his employer because his Prague colleague (quite logically) received more money.
Unfortunately, these court decisions - as well as the law from which they are based - are a manifestation of absolutely desperate economic illiteracy; and public debate on the subject is usually not much better. So I would like to address not only this nonsense, but also the potential consequences of enforcing this law.

title: Urza in The best podcast (not only) about freedom of speech
text:
Maestro Kubelík invited me to the next Best podcast, where I had the honor to debate with Martin Rota and Dan Vávra.

– Martin Rota; youtuber; creator of the Science Hammer, Explorers and Totally Retarded channels
– Daniel Vávra; game developer; influencer; youtuber; conservative; former libertarian

title: Urza in Live TV about the limits of a child's freedom
text:
Leri and Vlasta Švec invited me to their show on Live TV, where we talked about the limits of a child's freedom; although the debate took place in a spirit of almost complete agreement, we went into great depth describing how we perceive self-governance.

– leri Veleslav Švec; therapist; member of Conscious Life; healer

title: Studio Freeport: About the political party Voluntia with Tomáš Roud
text:
Tomáš Roud is currently founding the libertarian voluntarist political party Voluntia; in addition, he is a supporter of self-government (a parent of one of our students in Ježek) and an entrepreneur, while in the past, among other things, he served in the army.
We start the interview with Tomáš's introduction; then we get to Svobodny, of which Tomáš was a member for about a year; and finally we deal with Voluntia, its foundation, plans for the future, various moral dilemmas, but also possible risks that can threaten (almost every ideological political party).

– Tomáš Roud; volunteer; libertarian; founder of the Voluntia Party; proponent of self-government; businessman; former soldier

title: About freedom in ZŠ SVOBODY
text:
ZŠ SVOBODY invited me and Gabriela to talk about freedom; Unfortunately, Gabriela could not participate due to health reasons, so unfortunately only I spoke about freedom, which in my opinion is a shame, because I consider Gabriela's perception of freedom to be one of the purest.
At the beginning I defined external freedom, then I slowly got to internal freedom, which is significantly intertwined with self-development; from that we quite naturally came to self-directed education. The lecture beautifully shows how these topics are connected; I think I am able to present this connection better and better.

title: Bizarre interview for the Czech Party of Asocials
text:
The Czech Party of Asocials asked me for an interview in front of the House of Representatives; they say it will be serious and funny. When I wrote to them that I wasn't funny, they said they didn't mind, let me leave it to them; so I left it up to them, judge the result for yourself.
Several students came, I enjoyed talking with them; they somehow edited the video - maybe jokingly, I don't see much in it. I publish it for you to judge for yourselves; at least that interview is quite different from the others. I'd love it if you let me know what you think about it in the comments; I don't know what to think myself.

– Karel Hrubián; Chairman of the Czech Party of Asocials

title: Free Harbor Studio: About freedom and learning about the world with Anička Honzíková
text:
Anička has been working for the Free Port as a volunteer for years and is constantly listening to our work; in the process, he not only learns, but also always gives me valuable feedback or interesting observations. She recently told me something that I felt was a shame not to film with her.
We talked about how our emotions (and which) affect logical thinking and prevent us from knowing the world; we discussed how to recognize them in ourselves and what to do with them. Paradoxically, the sharper our mind is, the more effectively it can work not only for us, but also against us.

– Anna Honzíková; Freeport volunteer; libertarian; anarcho-capitalist

title: Urza with Tomáš Guth Jarkovský about self-ownership in Debatní Deník
text:
Tomáš Guth Jarkovský is a Pirate who was willing to debate with me about self-ownership, which made me very happy, because people usually don't want to talk much about such abstract topics; I hereby thank Tim for organizing our debate in the Debate Journal.
Self-ownership was the focus of most of the conversation; in the end, we came to the point that we differ mainly in that Tomáš, unlike me, elevates some rights of the state above the rights of the individual to own his body. However, we also opened up freedom of speech; and at the very end also the (im)measurability of benefit.

– Tomáš Guth Jarkovský; pro-European politician; a member of the Pirate Party; math physicist

title: Not just about free will with Matthias
text:
Matthias came to me with the idea of filming a somewhat unusual interview that is not primarily about anarcho-capitalism; but ultimately yes, because in it we talk about personal responsibility and different paths to freedom and happiness in life.
Do we have free will? If so, what would that mean? If this were not the case, what would be the consequences? Would it change anything for anarcho-capitalism or the Austrian school of economics? How would Human Action be rewritten if we didn't have free will? And to what extent are we masters of our lives?

– Matthias; author Stok Freeport; libertarian; volunteer

title: Freeport Studio: Debunking the Myths of Capitalism
text:
With the arrival of Emma, the economic topics you have been talking about lately will probably start to open up more in the Freeport; and one of the examples of this phenomenon will be the October livestream, where we want to disprove widespread myths about capitalism (and that there are some).
We will prepare some in advance and come with them; however, we firmly believe (and as we know you, it is probably a justified belief) that many myths to be disproved will come from you. Do you think we will refute successfully? Come create our show with us! You can write and call; we look forward to it!

– Emma; creator of Freeport; anarcho-capitalist; libertarian; student Hedgehog without a cage

title: Studio Freeport: About freedom and democracy with Václav Láska
text:
Václav Láska is a senator, lawyer and chairman of the Club for Liberal Democracy and the Senator 21 movement; a former police investigator, chairman of the board of Transparency International and a civic activist. As he enjoys debating, he came to my Studio.
In a busy conversation, we discussed the differences between the work of a politician and a civil activist, we dealt with human rights and freedoms, mobilization in Ukraine, the state of Czech society, legality, legitimacy, misinformation and the differences between freedom and democracy.

– Václav Láska; senator; lawyer; former police officer; former chairman of Transparency International's board of directors

title: Anarcho-capitalism: Adultism (and other prejudices) and freedom
text:
In September, in the Anarchocapitalism cycle, we will, as always, focus on the education of (not only) children; this time we will look at the connection between adultism and other prejudices with individualism and freedom. Children are the most oppressed group in our current society, whose rights are systematically (and institutionally) still massively trampled upon; they do not have direct representation in decision-making processes, as their parents act for them - just as in the past men acted for "their" wives or masters for "their" slaves or subjects. Although this parable does not fit us emotionally, its logical analysis can teach us to "reframe" social paradigms and look at the world without them; swallow Morphe's metaphorical red pill and develop a sensitivity to unfreedom...
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/bbc/

title: Urza with Adam Trunečka about the state in Debatní Deník
text:
Adam Trunečka is Tim's friend whom Tim supported in the European elections - despite certain differences of opinion; and perhaps also thanks to them, Tim decided to organize a me vs. Adam debate in the Debate Journal, where he himself took on the role of moderator, a role that, in my opinion, fits him perfectly.
We addressed the role of the state in society, thus its legitimacy; we also got to monopolies, dominant players and state interventions "against" them. Although we wanted to discuss the Green Deal as well, in the end we ran out of time; as it is, we rarely manage more than one topic in discussions with Tim.

– Adam Trunecka; politician; member of STAN

title: Freeport Studio: On Anarcho-Capitalism and Respect with Teri Paul
text:
Teri Paul is an active libertarian and promoter of freedom; although she has her own podcast, I decided to invite her to my studio to talk about freedom, as the love for her unites us both, which was a good basis for a nice conversation.
We talked about her journey to ankap, what role school and other influences played in it; we also got to the motivations for its creation. Above all, however, she showed very clearly why for her anarcho-capitalism mainly means respect, empathy and concern for other people.

– Teri Paul; libertarian; anarcho-capitalist; idealist; author of the podcast "And who would build roads?"

title: Urza with debate coach Milan about the protection of minorities in Next Zone
text:
The first discussion with the debate coach Milan was a lot of fun for both of us; So Tim decided to organize another one - and this time he rented the Next Zone space in the Smíchovské Secondary Technical School for it, where a lot of spectators and listeners could come.
Our second debate was on the protection of minorities; will it be more meaningful under anarcho-capitalism, or under the baton of the state? We came to many interesting conclusions; and in addition, in addition to the classic, commonly mentioned minorities, we dealt with an atypical one, but in my opinion the most oppressed.

– Milan; debate coach; opponents of child labor; utilitarian; supporters of state intervention and regulation; social engineer

title: Urza with Pavlo Hlávka about media (non)dependence
text:
I appeared in the program Interactions in action by Pavel Hlávka; in addition to clarifying views on freedom, we also talked with the audience mainly about the (un)enviousness of the media.

– Pavel Hlávka; initiator of radio Svobodný vášač CZ; coordinator of the integration project of free and independent radio studios of the Free Broadcaster

title: Freeport Studio: State Against the Poor
text:
Ema "checks out" quite quickly in Freeport; and I'm happy to perceive and experience it in every video - her reactions in front of the camera are more and more natural and relaxed (even if the "real" Ema reacts even more promptly outside the conclusion, which you can look forward to).
This time she came up with an important and interesting economic topic for me - how the state harms the poor, on whose (declarative) protection it constantly builds its PR; as part of thorough preparation, she came up with a lot of examples, which we then organized into larger units.

– Emma; creator of Freeport; anarcho-capitalist; libertarian; student Hedgehog without a cage

title: Urza on Access to Secular Power for Christian Congregations
text:
To my considerable surprise, I received an invitation to give a lecture to young Christians at a camp about the approach of (not only) Christians to worldly power (specifically the state); although it was quite difficult for me, I accepted the invitation because I had not spent time in the company of Christians and talked with them for a long time.
At the beginning of the lecture, I explain my approach to faith and the Bible, which is quite a personal topic for me, so it was not easy for me to talk about it publicly; however, I think it was an important introduction to the next part of the lecture on the anarchist approach to the state in accordance with the Bible and God's laws.

title: About money for an unnamed gymnasium in Brno
text:
I accepted an invitation to give a lecture (not only) about money for a gymnasium in Brno, whose management did not want me to directly name the school when publishing the record; the lecture was interesting because many students disagreed and objected to discuss the topics for many days afterwards.
I began by explaining to me the most important – and notoriously neglected – function of money; the debate then turned to child labor, which we lingered on for quite a long time to finally get to free education, the concept of which was hard to imagine for the students of this gymnasium.

title: Freeport Studio: On Socialism and Privatization with Dušan Tříska
text:
To my great joy, the invitation to the Studio was accepted by the mathematician, physicist, lawyer and, above all, economist Dušan Tříska - the "father of Coupon Privatization", who tried to make central planning more efficient under socialism; while he painfully learned that it was not possible.
We talked about central planning and Dušan Tříska's work at the Academy of Sciences under the previous regime; unsurprisingly, we devoted most of our time to the privatization of Coupons; we also dealt with the wild nineties or Dušan Tříska's collaboration with STB.

– Dušan Tříska; the father of Voucher Privatization; economist (in both socialism and capitalism); mathematician; physicist; lawyer; scientist; academician; economic libertarian

title: Urza in the House of the Freeport on self-governance, July 2024
text:
My second talk at Worldschooling 2024 in the House of the Free Port was about self-management and the Hedgehog without a cage; a (smaller) part of it was devoted to self-management in general, but in the end we got more and more directly to the practical questions of how it goes in Ježek without a cage.
He opened the entire debate with a very interesting question about "partial self-management" - that is, schools that are not (yet) self-managed, but may (maybe) become so in time; and how to act in them if one does not agree with the management of children? The other interviewers were more directly interested in Hedgehog without a cage, how we approach children or what our rules are.

title: Urza at the Freeport House on Freedom, July 2024
text:
My first talk at Worldschooling 2024 in the House of the Free Port was about freedom, especially inner freedom; this time we weren't so much dealing with anarcho-capitalism - and not at all in the sense of who would build the roads - but rather freedom in our hearts and minds.
We discussed conformity to a (quite arbitrary state) regime and how internal freedom is related to risk aversion, what it is good for, what it gives us and what it takes away; in connection with this, we also dealt with our (physical and especially psychological) resistance, breaking points, game theory and different types of (inter)human interactions.

title: Free Harbor Studio: We (learn) (un)freely
text:
In September, we're doing our first live broadcast with Emma; however, this does not change the fact that, as always, the (September) theme will be learning, education, schooling and state indoctrination of children, as we consider these areas to be the key to (im)freedom in our society.
Since this is Emin's first livestream, we understand and expect that you will probably have a lot of questions about her and about her, even outside the topic of education; don't hesitate to put them to her, create our live broadcast with us and take another step towards a free society.

– Emma; creator of Freeport; anarcho-capitalist; libertarian; student Hedgehog without a cage

title: Freeport Studio: About education with Stanislav Štech
text:
Stanislav Štech has devoted his whole life to pedagogy, learning, education and education, where at one time he held the highest post - Minister of Education in Sobotko's government; despite this, he talks about state propaganda in education a bit like me, only he considers the phenomenon to be positive.
I invited him to the Studio of the Free Port to debate about (un)free education, compulsory school attendance or the different approach to children in traditional schools compared to self-directed education (for example in Ježek bez klece).

– Stanislav Štech; professor of educational psychology at the Charles University; former Minister of Education; chairman of the Czech section of UNESCO

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Inner Freedom
text:
I want to dedicate the June lecture from the cycle Anarchocapitalism (again) to inner freedom; same as in June last year. At that time, I opened the topic by saying that I can't even define inner freedom, but by talking about it, I would like to get to some usable definition; and I promised to share the knowledge gained. Year after year, I think I'm coming up with a working definition; not only you contributed to its discovery, but also life in Ježek without a cage. In addition to the definition itself, I would also like to address the meaning of inner freedom, which, in my opinion, is underestimated by most libertarians and anarcho-capitalists; I would very much like to hear your opinions again (especially those that disagree), thanks to which I can move forward in my understanding of (not only this) topic.
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/bbc/

title: Interview about education with Nella Hegyi
text:
Nella Hegyi from ODS asked me for a short interview on the topic of education, which she wants to use as part of her graduation thesis; the questions were more mainstream, but even so I decided to share them - and my answers - with you in the form of a video.

– Nella Hegyi; high school graduate; member of the ODS program team for finance

title: Urza at AnkapFest (background noises)
text:
Lukáš Nestrojil invited me to AnkapFest; so far it is a small event, but in the coming years the organizer expects more people, which I wish from the bottom of my heart - I am happy when people do whatever they can and can do for freedom. We'll see how the AnkapFests continue.
At the beginning of the interview, Lukáš presented the concept of his festival and space; then we got to ecology and free market environmental protection. Towards the end we talked about people's access to truth, knowledge, science and research; I think that's really important.

– Lukáš Nestrojil; organization of ankap fest; anarcho-capitalist

title: Urza with Pavlo Hlávka about communism, culture and the European elections
text:
I appeared in the program Interactions in action by Pavel Hlávka; we started with the previous regime, continued with freedom (of speech) in theaters and ended with the European elections.

– Pavel Hlávka; initiator of radio Svobodný vášač CZ; coordinator of the integration project of free and independent radio studios of the Free Broadcaster

title: 4D for the separation of the police from the state!
text:
Four reasons for separating the police from the state!
Like any monopoly maintained by force, the state police provide expensive and poor quality services. 
In practice, the salaries and rewards of police officers do not reflect the degree of their benefit to society or their success in solving cases and the like. There is no financial incentive to help and protect.
The police can be misused against citizens at any time by state power; it wouldn't be the first time or the last time.
Free market law leads to more effective assistance and protection of the population. You can learn more about this in the Freeport Channel in the Polycentric Law Enforcement Lectures.

title: Freeport Studio: Encryption, the EU and the digitization of state administration
text:
The EU - like any totalitarian power - would like to control all aspects of its citizens' lives, ideally down to the smallest detail; and one of the ways to do this is to deprive us of privacy, for example in the form of the possibility of encrypted communication - of course under the noble pretext of fighting against the spread of child pornography.
How do "our" Czech politicians protect us against this? Not at all; Věra Jourová from ANO applauds it (with a bleeding heart), the current government is washing its hands. Instead, however, they are pouring the digitization of state administration on us; unfortunately, few people are aware of its dangerousness in all its consequences, that's why I spoke about it again.

title: Urza with Pavlo Hlávka about the European elections and education
text:
I appeared in the program Interactions in action by Pavel Hlávka; we started with the European elections and my candidacy, continued with education and ended (again) with ankap.

– Pavel Hlávka; initiator of radio Svobodný vášač CZ; coordinator of the integration project of free and independent radio studios of the Free Broadcaster

title: 4D for the separation of the judiciary from the state!
text:
Four reasons for separating the judiciary from the state!
Like any monopoly maintained by force, the state judiciary provides expensive and poor quality services.
Just as other professions compete in the free market, so can judges. Where there is a demand for justice and dispute resolution, there is also a supply. 
The impartiality of state judges is only illusory. The state pays them and appoints them to positions, so at least they cannot be impartial in disputes with the state. Moreover, instead of finding justice, judges only interpret the intentions of the state to organize social relations.
Only a decentralized judiciary allows each dispute to be judged by someone who does not belong to either party; more information can be found, for example, in the recordings of lectures on polycentric law; you can listen to them here - on the Freeport Channel.

title: Urza with Pavel Hlávka about ankap and money
text:
I appeared in the program Interactions in action by Pavel Hlávka; we talked not only about anarcho-capitalism, but also about the financial system in the past and present.

– Pavel Hlávka; initiator of radio Svobodný vášač CZ; coordinator of the integration project of free and independent radio studios of the Free Broadcaster

title: Capitalism versus socialism in the debating club
text:
Tim leads the Debate Club, in which he organizes regular debates; he invited me as a supporter of capitalism and Václav Soukup as a supporter of socialism to one of them to defend the economic systems that are close to us and that we consider suitable and effective for society.
This discussion was followed by academic (competitive) debates in which I was given the opportunity to defend socialism; I found that interesting, although I don't really like their overall format (I like interactive debates with the possibility to respond rather than short punchy speeches).

– Václav Soukup; director of the Association of Debating Clubs; socialist; statist

title: Free Port Studio: Vláďa Krupa translated Mises' Theory of Money and Credit
text:
Vláďa Krupa translated Ludwig von Mises' Tory of Money and Credit; it is one of his early works, in which he does not yet approach praxeology as comprehensively as, for example, in Human Action, which may facilitate the understanding of his development.
In the video, Vláďa analyzed one chapter of the book after another; we interspersed their content by reading excerpts and various observations on the author's life or - not only - the Austrian economy. Please write in the comments how you like this format.

– Vladimir Krupa; longtime contributor to Mises.cz; libertarian; fellow of the Liberal Institute; translator of libertarian books

title: Ankap as global respect in the Cherubín tea house
text:
One lecture at the Cherubín teahouse eventually became a whole series; I like to go back there because the place has the right tea tree and a great atmosphere (and a Buddha statue with the inscription: "When the god said: "Let there be light," the sound already existed.").
Lately, I've been exploring the view of anarcho-capitalism through "global respect," that is, respect for people whose existence we don't even know exists; and along with freedom and responsibility - two sides of the same imaginary coin - I began to perceive (following the example of Gabriela and other founders of free schools) respect as the third side of the imaginary triangle.

title: Urza about ankap for students of the Hotel School and Business Academy in Havířov
text:
Students of the Hotel School and Business Academy in Havířov approached me with a request to give a lecture at their school; here we tried to come to an agreement with the management, which turned out to be quite complicated, so after several attempts we decided to meet outside the school in our free time.
We talked about the foundations of anarcho-capitalism, discussed the principle of non-aggression (for people and animals), property rights, self-directed education, Czech education and many other topics - including psychedelics and self-development; I really liked the relaxed (extracurricular) atmosphere and the fact that there was no one who didn't want to be there.

title: Freeport Studio: Does the state own us?
text:
Sometimes you send me interesting texts and videos; and I just came across bans on energy drinks for minors, a ban on HHC or other drugs, and a rejected request for euthanasia. Seemingly quite unrelated topics; however, I see one common denominator in them - the will of the state and the effort to own us.
Self-ownership is one of the cornerstones of libertarianism and anarcho-capitalism; we primarily own ourselves – our body – and subsequently the fruits of our labor. But is it really so? Who ultimately decides what we can and cannot do with our bodies? Unfortunately, the answer won't surprise anyone much; but why?

title: Urza with Ondra Matouš about anarcho-capitalism and Ježko
text:
Ondra Matouš invited me to his podcast; it turned out to be a very pleasant (four-hour xD) chat. We spent the first half talking about ankap; the second one we analyzed Ježek, we even (unplanned) started the admission interview with the parent on a whim.

– Ondřej Matouš; podcaster; libertarian; father

title: Gabriela and Urza: Age is just a number or friendship in JbK
text: In addition to classic talks, we also organize talks on specific topics; on this one we talked about mixed-age friendships: We are both friends with children and believe that friendships between children and adults are no different from any other, even if many supporters of self-management disagree with us.

title: Freeport Studio: War in Ukraine
text:
You may have noticed that I speak minimally about the war in Ukraine; no video on this topic has been released yet - and I hoped it would stay that way. But with regard to your reactions to some of my statements, I finally decided to film what I think about this conflict and its effects on us.
In the video, he also tries to explain why I formulate some of my statements about this conflict, how I formulate them; I hope (although I don't really believe it) that I will be able to convey my thoughts in such a way that even in today's polarized society they will be understood without being automatically put into a box.

title: Pre-election performance "Nevolte Urza.cz" (European elections 2024)
text:
As part of the party's pre-election campaign, "Urza.cz: We don't want your votes; you can't claim freedom. We'll reject every political function; we don't want to dictate to people how they should live. We have a different vision. We're going a different way - you can find it on the website www.urza.cz." until the 2024 European elections, I took part in several debates and performances.
ČT24 presented me as a candidate in the news, and I appeared twice in their Political Spectrum; CRo invited me to the program where they presented the top female candidates; in the end I also spoke with Xaver at XTV (however, they did not allow me to publish the entire interview). You can find a montage of all this in this video.

title: Pre-election clips "Don't vote Urza.cz" (European elections 2024)
text: As part of the party's pre-election campaign, "Urza.cz: We don't want your votes; you can't claim freedom. We'll reject every political function; we don't want to dictate to people how they should live. We have a different vision. We're going a different way - you can find it on the website www.urza.cz." we created these clips for the 2024 European elections, which were broadcast, among others, by Czech Television and Czech Radio; if it also makes sense to you to use the pre-election frenzy to spread libertarian ideas, please support us!

title: Freeport Studio: On Objectivism with Jiří Kinkor
text:
After the last debate with Jiří Kinkor, where we were pressed for time, the person in question accepted (with certain conditions) an invitation to my Studio; here we could debate for as long as we wanted, which ended up being over three hours.
We started with political philosophy, a debate about no versus minimal state, the principle of non-aggression or violence; finally, we moved freely to the philosophy of objectivism as such, its basic starting points, and again addressed (not only) arbitrary statements.

– Jiří Kinkor (www.aynrand.cz); leading Czech representative of Objectivism; philosopher; economist; financial analyst; author of "The Market and the State" and "Hayek's Road to Slavery"

title: Freeport Studio: Streamarathon 2024 (1pm to 4pm)
text:
It's been two years since the last streamarathon; and I got the urge to have it again! But I have more contact with the body, so I think I will fall off sooner than two years ago, but let's be surprised. What is streamarathon all about? At 19:00 the broadcast will begin; and it will last until you or I fall away.
We have no predetermined topic, we will talk about what you write in the chat, or what you call with; ankap topics will have priority (at least initially), but I wouldn't limit myself to them, because there are a lot of interesting detours that we can take on our journey of knowledge. I'm looking forward to it!!

title: Gabriela and Urza with a love of freedom and learning in Cologne's Bitclub
text: As part of our series of talks with Gabriela, we performed at Bitclub in Cologne; this time the audience was not primarily made up of those interested in self-directed education (although there were also some), but mainly bitcoin enthusiasts. We discussed several interesting topics, some new; for example drugs in Ježek.

title: Ankap and crypto in Cologne's Bitclub
text:
When I accepted the invitation to the Bitclub in Cologne, I couldn't wait with great curiosity to see what crypto space I would actually visit; then the reality exceeded all my expectations - I immediately fell in love with the space full of nice free-spirited people and its great atmosphere.
I didn't have my performance very precisely prepared in advance, which was useful; together with the listeners, we conceived it as a discussion with a short introduction about ankap and a long block of interesting questions, which showed that they were being asked by people who have been thinking about freedom for some time now and at the same time living it.

title: Freeport Studio: Streamarathon 2024 (Hour 1 to 12)
text:
It's been two years since the last streamarathon; and I got the urge to have it again! But I have more contact with the body, so I think I will fall off sooner than two years ago, but let's be surprised. What is streamarathon all about? At 19:00 the broadcast will begin; and it will last until you or I fall away.
We have no predetermined topic, we will talk about what you write in the chat, or what you call with; ankap topics will have priority (at least initially), but I wouldn't limit myself to them, because there are a lot of interesting detours that we can take on our journey of knowledge. I'm looking forward to it!!

title: Freeport Studio: Social Networks (and Elections)
text:
Ema brought her first theme to the Freeport Studio; and this topic is social networks - how they affect us, how they change society, but above all how they can influence elections, which is probably the most important subtopic for me.
We discussed the influence of social networks on our lives in great detail; we also touched on anonymity on the Internet as such. I enjoyed our conversation very much; I especially like how Ema is getting more and more relaxed in front of the cameras and acting more and more naturally. What do you think about it?

– Emma; creator of Freeport; anarcho-capitalist; libertarian; student Hedgehog without a cage

title: About the prices of living with Matthias
text:
Matthias has been kind of pushing me to do a video on house prices lately; I didn't really want to do that, which I repeatedly answered. However, he came up with the idea of doing the video with me; which I was happy to agree with - you can take this as a guide.
We talked about why housing is so expensive (and what it even means to be expensive); but in addition, we dealt with how the public media actually present it, which in this case is not the least bit objective or unbiased, which I think is perhaps more interesting than the price of housing itself.

– Matthias; author Stok Freeport; libertarian; volunteer

title: Freeport Studio: Who is Ema?
text:
Last week you heard (at least for me) some sad news - Teresa left Freeport; this week you can find out who is taking her place. Ema is my student in the Hedgehog without a cage; and we decided to create together.
At first, Ema was a little nervous, but that changed quite quickly. You can get to know some of her views in the video; and as it happens, I tried to give the most space to those who differ from me - I like to surround myself with people who are able to oppose me.

– Emma; creator of Freeport; anarcho-capitalist; libertarian; student Hedgehog without a cage

title: Students for Liberty: Petr Bláha for the state versus Urza for anarchy
text:
Students for Liberty organized a debate on the state and anarchy in the Děčín Municipal Library; my opponent defending the state was Petr Bláha, head of the political science department at the Jan Evangelista Purkyně University in Ústí nad Labem.
I was honestly hoping for a more grounded opponent in the forum; Mr. Bláha left me a lot of space in the debate, which "degenerated" into a form similar to when I answer questions after a lecture. On the other hand, I think that we still commented on quite interesting questions from the audience (and the moderator).

– Petr Bláha; Head of the Department of Political Science at Jan Evangelista Purkyně University in Ústí nad Labem

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: The Bitcoinization
text:
Josef Tětek will give a lecture in May; his topic will be – unsurprisingly – Bitcoin, as he has been intensively devoted to it for many years. Although there are many Czech promoters of this cryptocurrency, Pep's anarchist view of the (Austrian) economist stands out among them; it does not deal too much with the technological (undoubtedly also fascinating) side of Bitcoin (and certainly not with the development of the price on the stock exchange), but it describes very well its (economic) consequences for our entire society. A great deal of understanding of the past (and present) of this digital money also lends a lot of weight to Pep's predictions of the future; you can use this when asking questions. Pep's trips to Africa are also interesting, where he observes with his own eyes - and also contributes to - the bitcoinization there.
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/bbc/

– Pepa Tétek (stackuj.cz); bitcoiner; anarcho-capitalist; podcaster; publicist; economist; co-founder of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Liberal Institute; author of Enemies of the State and Bitcoin: Separating Money from the State

title: About the culture war with Michal Janda
text:
Michal Janda is a member of Svobodné, who creates a program, the trailers of which he puts in the Forum of Svobodné přístad; sometimes I agree with him, sometimes I don't, however, one of the posts caught my attention so much that we arranged a debate about the culture war.
Michal Janda is concerned about (potential) progressivist totality; I am trying to explain why I consider the criticism of progressivism itself (as opposed to the criticism of state enforcement of any ideology) to be very counterproductive to the preservation of freedom.

– Michal Janda; gay politician; member of the Free Citizens Party; author of the program Office for presenting left-wing stories on "Prava Strana"

title: Freeport Studio: Tereza is leaving Freeport
text:
Unfortunately, Tereza is leaving Freeport; we filmed a farewell video for you (at least for some time), where she explains her reasons for leaving, but we also look back together at the good moments of our cooperation.
We're also looking at the possible future, both together, and you'll also learn a little about Teresa's surrogates - there are two of them, although you'll probably only see one in the videos, but we won't get more details until next week.

title: Urza in The Best Education Podcast (Part Two)
text:
Maestro Kubelík invited me to the Best podcast about Czech education; together with me, the shadow minister of education Jana Berkovcová for the ANO movement and the journalist and teacher Michal Semín, who, in contrast to me, defended "traditional" education accepted the invitation. title: Studio of the Free Port: About the Tricolor with Zuzana Majerová
text:
Zuzana Majerová is the president of the Trikolora party; and it was her program (not only before the European elections) that we discussed - we gradually analyzed all three basic pillars on which this program stands.
One can easily identify with some from a libertarian point of view - for example, the free market, which, however, does not recognize the Tricolor to some extent (for example, by supporting Czech companies); in other points I see even greater contradictions, which I tried to formulate in the interview. You can take a look, judge for yourself and write us a comment.

– Zuzana Majerová; President of the Tricolor; former Member of Parliament; former member of the ODS

text:
The pirates have the show Férovka; to my surprise, Minister Lipavský and Mikuláš Ferjenčík invited me and Dan Steigerwald to it (originally Tim was supposed to go with me, but in the end he was sick).

– Jan Lipavský; foreign minister; member of the Czech Pirate Party; former Member of Parliament
