title: Gabriela and Urza with the love of freedom and learning In the common field
text: As part of our series of talks with Gabriela, we performed in Ostrava at the Ve commenesme poli festival; originally it was supposed to be a lecture, but in the end quite a few people came, so we chose a standard talk format for a fairly knowledgeable audience who wanted to work with their fears.

title: Freeport Studio: On progressivism and totalitarianism with Václav Szőcs
text:
Václav Szőcs is a libertarian and long-term supporter of the Free Port; at the same time, he is a critic of the ideology of progressivism, which he considers a potential threat, since totalitarianism can be built on it, which I agree with him on.
However, we do not agree on how to proceed in such a case and what to actually defend against; I believe progressivism is only a proxy threat - statism is the real one. In the video, I try to explain why the fight against progressivism as such, on the contrary, increases the threat of totalitarianism.

– Václav Szőcs; libertarian; anarcho-capitalist; supporter of the Free Port; opponent of progressivism

title: Gabriela and Urza with a love of freedom and learning in Parallel Polis Košice
text: As part of our cycle of talks with Gabriela, we performed in Košice's Paralelná Polis; our conversation (with Gabriel's introduction, as they don't know Ježek very well in Slovakia) loosely followed on from my lecture on ankapa, which preceded the conversation (the recording was also published on the Free Port Channel).

title: Basics of ankap for Parallel Polis Košice
text:
Gabriela and I accepted an invitation to Košice's Paralelná Polis, where, in addition to the great atmosphere, they were also interested in a lecture on the basics of anarcho-capitalism and then a joint discussion about the Hedgehog without a cage; here is the first recording, the discussion will follow in a separate video.
I tried to both introduce anarcho-capitalism to the few ignorant people in the audience, but also to go in depth with those who already knew; I thought that both were quite successful. The talk also reached polycentric law, from which we got to the legitimacy of its enforcement and the statism carefully cultivated in state education.

title: Studio of the Free Port: Euro elections with Martin Pánek
text:
In May, Martin Pánek, director of the Liberal Institute, will come to the Freeport Studio for a live stream; and our topic will be the upcoming elections to the European Parliament, as our guest has been dealing with the issue of the European Union for a long time.
We probably won't focus our topics purely on the election, quite possibly we'll get to other related libertarian questions or answers; we will be happy if you decide to co-create our show with us in the chat or call to talk to the guest directly.

– Martin Panek; director of the Liberal Institute; libertarian; economist; former MEP assistant

title: Studio Freeport: About freedom of speech in the media with Marko Přibil
text:
Marek Přibil is a writer and journalist who you probably know from the recordings on which he and Andrej Babiš discussed what would and would not be written about, or when; came to the Studio to talk about the state of freedom of speech in (mainly) Czech media, but we also talked about abroad.
At the very beginning of the interview, I opened up about the recording case with him, as I did not want to leave this topic unaddressed; then we got to people's fear of expressing themselves, which, in my opinion, does not necessarily mean a restriction of freedom of speech. Towards the end, we also dealt with the freedom to gossip.

– Marek Přibil; journalist; the writer

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: The Road to Ancap in Practice
text:
The April lecture from the cycle Anarchocapitalism will be about different (non)paths to (non)freedom; both on an individual and societal level. We will talk not only about what steps in my opinion lead to freedom (and here I develop a lot over the years, I reevaluate my views - perhaps as a result of a deeper understanding of freedom), but also about which paths do not lead to freedom, or may even cause the opposite of the intended result (here I am fairly constant over time, although I notice certain - rather minor - changes of opinion in this as well). Moreover, it is possible to aim at two seemingly different goals - freedom for oneself as an individual and freedom for society; here the first makes more and more sense to me, but I also perceive an increasing "overlap" of both approaches.
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/bbc/

title: Nations of Sanity: Land ownership
text:
Matthew Sands invited me to a series of discussions for his project Nations of Sanity; in this fourth episode we were discussing land ownership versus the land dominion principle.
It was quite a theoretical debate again; we both obviously like such kind of discussion! I hope you will enjoy it despite my not so fluent English.

– Matthew Sands; volunteer; founder of Nations of Sanity project

title: Freeport Studio: Haiti on Fire! Failure of anarchy?
text:
In recent weeks, you have written extensively about my commentary on the current situation in Port-au-Prince, Haiti; many of you - anarchists - are disturbed by what is happening there in the - partially - stateless society. Also, you ask for advice on making a logical argument about Haiti towards statists…
In my opinion, why can't Haiti - and not just Haiti - be used as an example of anarchy not working because it is inherently violent? And from my side, this is certainly not an argument of the type: "This was not true socialism or communism," which we often hear from socialists regarding the Soviet Union and its form.

title: On the importance of individualism for freedom with Matthias
text:
Matthias has recently been concerned with individualism and its effect on freedom (and by extension the transition to a stateless free anarcho-capitalist society); since he writes interesting texts about it, I was pleased when he asked for space in the video to present his thoughts.
Our debate was conducted in a very friendly spirit, we agreed on almost everything, however, I certainly consider it beneficial; Matthias emphasizes a little different things on his path to freedom than I do, which I am really happy about, because the more paths we take, the more likely we will reach the goal.

– Matthias; author Stok Freeport; libertarian; volunteer

title: Urza with the organizer of Ankapfest
text:

title: Urza with Jiří Kinkor about philosophy (and) objectivism
text:
Jiří Kinkor is a leading Czech representative of Ayn Rand's philosophy of objectivism; and since one of the implications of this philosophy is freedom, I want to bring it closer to the viewers of the Freeport Channel.
The debate was quite theoretical, which is to be expected from a discussion of philosophy; but the more I debate objectivists, the less consistent their ideas seem to me - but maybe I'm just misunderstanding them, judge for yourself. We addressed aesthetics, arbitrariness, and concepts.

– Jiří Kinkor (www.aynrand.cz); leading Czech representative of Objectivism; philosopher; economist; financial analyst; author of "The Market and the State" and "Hayek's Road to Slavery"

Joel entered the Hedgehog Without a Cage gymnasium at the same time as me; she as a student, me as a teacher, but we don't play it much at Ježek. title: Anarcho-Capitalism: License and Permit
text:
The March lecture from the Anarcho-Capitalism series will be about state licenses and authorizations to do things that we have a natural right to do; nevertheless, the state fit the role of someone who should allow us to do what it has no business doing - even in cases where we do not harm anyone and do not violate anyone's freedom or property. To carry out many activities, we need licenses of various types - whether it is teaching, social work, driving a motor vehicle, treating or burying people, food production, banking services, auctions, tourism or simply "just" a certificate of medical fitness for any profession (including office). What are the effects of all these legislative interventions on the economy? We will show this with practical examples and in theory...
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/bbc/

title: Jan Romportl: How AI has penetrated us through ChatGPT (KSP24: Technology yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
The sixth speaker of the "Freeport Conference 2024: Technology yesterday, today and tomorrow" was Jan Romportl with his lecture "How AI has burned into us through ChatGPT".

The ChatGPT system, which was presented to the public by OpenAI at the end of November 2022, achieved several major results. For example: (1) planet-wide ChatGPT fetishism; (2) the emergence of an incredible number of new "AI experts" whining about language models and whose jobs those models will take away; (3) popular influencers, who until recently unboxed, tested and commented on new iPhones and filmed themselves doing so on YouTube, are now unboxing new AI products in the same style and spreading consumer awareness about them to the lay public; (4) alerting an unexpectedly large number of people that there really might be some kind of AI; (5) the strained argumentative gymnastics of AI opponents who rely on the notion that ChatGPT is just a "statistical parrot" that, unlike a human, does not "truly" understand the text; (6) OpenAI suggests that they are indeed starting to approach Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), and that we should finally start paying attention. So... So how are we really doing now? What piece is still missing between big language models and AGI? Why is A(G)I one of humanity's main hopes and at the same time a fundamental existential risk? You can look forward to all this in the lecture.

Jan Romportl, founder and former CEO of Dataclair.ai, is now an independent AI consultant and runs his own startup that focuses on solving the problems of today's online world with AI. A PhD holder in Artificial Intelligence and Philosophy, he has over 12 years of university research and teaching in the areas of Artificial Intelligence and Human Machine Interaction. His experience also includes a leading position in the Department of Human-Machine Interaction at the University of West Bohemia in Pilsen and cooperation with the Center for Theoretical Studies of Charles University and the Association for Effective Altruism.

title: Jan Skalický: Fraud on the Internet and the digital trail (KSP24: Technology yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
The fifth speaker of the "Free Port Conference 2024: Technology yesterday, today and tomorrow" was Honza Skalický with his lecture "Fraud on the Internet and the digital footprint".

The lecture will deal with the phenomenon of fraud on the Internet, make a brief classification of them and focus on a common type of fraudulent purchase of goods. It analyzes the digital trail they can leave and how it can be used to prosecute fraudsters. The presented situations will be illustrated by examples from practice, and at the end we will also think about the role of the state in the problem being addressed.

Ing. Jan Skalický studied computer technology at the Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Czech Technical University. He currently works as a head of SW development and a lecturer of programming courses. In addition to positions as a specialist in the development of microcomputer systems, he also worked at the Temelín nuclear power plant. He is a supporter of the Austrian school of economics, classical liberalism and decentralized systems, which include Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies. He is the co-author of two books on the subject.

title: O.T.: Cross-section of systemic technology risks (KSP24: Technology yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
The fourth speaker of the "Freeport Conference 2024: Technology yesterday, today and tomorrow" was O.T. with his lecture "A cross-section of the systemic risks of technology".

As powerful as technology can be, it can also (just as powerfully) rob us of our freedom. As?

O.T. uses analytical methods to examine individual aspects of various systems, from function requirements to design and architecture to implementation, and finds real risks in them, their causes, how they can combine and how the consequences of risks cascade.

title: Urza: Fear Against Freedom (KSP24: Technology Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow)
text:
The third speaker of the "2024 Freeport Conference: Technology Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow" was Urza with his talk "Fear Against Freedom".

Human history is full of fascinating inventions and innovations that have often changed people's lives and society beyond recognition; of course, most such changes did not come without massive fears about the future - human progress is fringed by fear of the unknown. The older generations have been cursing the younger since time immemorial; many people in virtually every historical epoch feel that the real or metaphorical end of the world is approaching. Nevertheless, we always manage in the end; and not only that, as a company we are constantly developing and improving in the long term. However, fear is immutable; the rulers have long since understood that it can be used to rule and control the masses, so they like to feed it. How can one approach this? Is there anything we can do? And if so, what exactly?

Urza is an anarcho-capitalist author; wrote over a thousand libertarian texts on the web and in print media and the first Czech book on anarcho-capitalism. For fifteen years, he not only reads, thinks and writes about freedom, ethics, education, the free market, the economy and the role of the state in society, but also lectures, makes videos and is invited to various programs and panel discussions. Co-creates Freeport; teaches at the free school Ježek without a cage and has been actively cooperating with many libertarian initiatives for a long time.

title: Jan Hubík: Cryptoanarchy (KSP24: Technology yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
The first speaker of the "Free Port Conference 2024: Technology yesterday, today and tomorrow" was Jan Hubík with his lecture "Cryptoanarchy".

Cryptoanarchies are primarily practical tools for achieving digital freedom.

Honza has a formal education in several fields from physics to finance and started his working life as a data scientist in astrophysics. But he always liked technology and everything related to computers, which led him to Bitcoin in 2013, and since then he has been interested in it from many perspectives - mining, investment, use in life and business, and the impact on society. Since 2015, he has been involved in Parallel Polis and its Institute of Kryptoanarchy, from where he left for Alza in 2019, where he started the Fraud & Risk department. In 2021, he was lured from Alza by Xapo Bank, where until the end of 2023, in the position of Anti Financial Crime SME, he debugged transaction monitoring systems.

title: Studio of the Free Port: About growth with Ondřej Kolínský
text:
Ondřej Kolínský is an active supporter of non-growth willing to debate with libertarians; Students for Liberty were already convinced of this. I invited him to the Studio to present what non-growth consists of; subsequently we argued about it in an unmoderated discussion.
I have to admit that I was actually surprised to what extent not growing (or rather the version of it presented by Ondřej Kolínský) resonates with ankap; I expected (even according to their website) something far more distant, although ideals are one thing, their real implementation is another.

title: Anarcho-capitalism: Freedom, (not only) children and technology
text:
The February lecture from the Anarchocapitalism series will be about technology in (not only) children's hands and the freedom related to it; Recently, the topic of children and technology, or their restriction and regulation, resonates more and more often in society - it is no coincidence that this is the most frequent question asked at the discussions that Gabriela and I organize. However, after long debates, I came to the conclusion that technology in the hands of children is more of a proxy problem for the (dis)trust with which we approach them, which has direct effects on their (dis)freedom; while the degree of freedom that society allows its children then logically affects how much freedom those people will be willing to leave to others when they grow up - because what we learn in our youth often follows us throughout our lives.

title: Freeport Studio: How much did my paragliding accident cost (You)?
text:
In the public debate (and in the Freeport Study by some opponents) it is heard that health care is prohibitively expensive, so that the "normal person" cannot afford even a routine operation if it were not for the state; this belief spreads throughout society and becomes a universally accepted norm.
I have tried to debunk this myth several times in different ways, but maybe an example from practice (and my own life) will help. How much did my paragliding accident cost the public health insurance system? How much did it cost me? How much did it cost you, the taxpayers? Personally, I was definitely surprised by the amount; my guesses were way off.

title: Urza with debate coach Milan about child labor in Debatní Deník
text:

Instead of the original three topics, only child labor was dealt with in the discussion for three hours; on the one hand, you can hear Urza's deontological view and defense of freedom, while his opponent is pushing a utilitarian approach and trying to manage human lives to minimize suffering.

– Milan; debate coach; opponents of child labor; utilitarian; supporters of state intervention and regulation; social engineer

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: The Opportunity Cost
text: The December lecture from the Anarcho-Capitalism series will be about opportunity costs - an absolutely essential economic topic; although it is actually very trivial, it has extremely far-reaching consequences for the whole society. It is certainly not difficult to explain this topic - no more than one sentence; and hopefully no one will contradict him. Nevertheless, the opportunity cost theory has many implications that are certainly not easy to see; and the vast majority of people don't do that in everyday life, which makes them easily manipulated by politicians. It would be far more difficult for them if we were all constantly aware of the simple truth that every action has its price, at least in the form of everything we could have done instead of what we actually do; this is true in life, in education, in relationships, in the economy... in short, everywhere!

title: 4D for free market legislation!
text:
Four reasons for free market legislation!
The Department of State Analysis of the Institute of State and Law of the Academy of Sciences found that in 2010 there were about 1.6 million legal norms in the Czech Republic, and in the long term they are increasing by 55 thousand per year. So today we probably have over two million valid orders, prohibitions, regulations and legislative orders.
Although ignorance of the law is no excuse, there is no one who knows all the laws. Lawyers are also represented by colleagues if they are conducting a dispute outside their field of law. Officials often do not even know the few laws under which they are supposed to work.
Because of the state, we live in a legislative jungle; we have become accustomed to solving all problems with laws that politicians churn out like on a treadmill. The state thus controls our lives more and more, which is a sure way to totalitarianism.
Free market law does not allow anyone to spout laws so easily, as it arises from below and is not centralized. You can learn more on the Freeport Channel in the lectures on polycentric law.

title: 4D: Why not trust the government!
text:
Four reasons not to trust the government!
We recognize the propaganda of historical or foreign regimes easily because we are not used to it. In contrast, we tend to ignore the propaganda that we are exposed to all the time.
Propaganda does not belong only to totalitarian dictatorships; all governments – even democratic ones – have a need to shape their citizens in a certain direction.
From an early age, we were all continuously indoctrinated in schools with theses about the necessity of the state, the correctness of democracy or the dysfunctionality of anarchy; the result is the inability of most people to think critically about these topics.
Schools are not the only vehicle for spreading propaganda; the media - especially the public ones - or the ubiquitous signs announcing what the EU has financed, as well as a number of so-called fact-checkers, in addition to information, push us emotions and the "right" view.

text: As part of our series of talks with Gabriela, we performed at Bystrouška Primary School near Pavlova; in the discussion, we also opened up topics that we had not dealt with so far. title: Basics of ankap for business UOL Club
text:
I accepted an invitation to the entrepreneurial UOL Club to introduce its members to the basics of anarcho-capitalism; for many of them it was a completely new concept that they had not encountered before - which always promises interesting moments. I have a more than good feeling about the reactions of the audience (especially after the lecture).
Most of the listeners were quite open to new ideas, so we effectively got to the principles themselves and only minimally got stuck on the details; in addition, we have even taken a bite of self-directed education. After the lecture, I was also sought out by opinion opponents, with whom we found common ground.

title: Studio of the Free Port: About the Hedgehog without a cage with Janina
text:
Janina has been going to Ježek without a cage for several years; she is my student and at the same time a person whom I like very much - we learn a lot from each other and experience many interesting life situations together. The hedgehog left for a while to try going to a standard school; then she came back.
I was so interested in her experience that I asked her if she would take a trip to Prague with me and talk about it on camera; I think it illustrates very well the differences between learning something intrinsically motivated because we want to, and being forced to, which is woefully inefficient.

– Janina; a student from Ježek bez klece

title: Free Harbor Studio: How do Gabriela and I perceive freedom?
text:
I assume that perhaps all regular followers of Freeport know Gabriela from The Hedgehog without a Cage; for the last two years we have been creating together in Ježek, at meetings, in Přístav and in our personal life, which really pleases and fulfills me.
This time the main topic will not be Hedgehogs; we will solve how we perceive freedom. Many (and not only) libertarians disagree with our methods of publicly admitting to breaking the law, for example; we'd like to talk about what makes us do it.

– Gabriela Ježková; founder, owner and director of the Ježek bez klece free school in Brno; anarchist; libertarian; a teacher

title: Freeport Studio: On Freedom of Speech with Dan Steigerwald
text:
Dan Steigerwald is one of the unmissable figures of the Czech libertarian scene; his glosses have long inspired me to various reflections. I enjoy talking to him; I like how deeply he understands the implications of market mechanisms on society.
This time I invited him to discuss freedom of speech - because he wrote a status where, from my point of view, he advocates its suppression for the sake of a safe society; he himself probably wouldn't have described it that way, so there was something to debate about.

– Daniel Steigerwald; absolute anarchist; anarcho-capitalist; thinker; eccentric; showman; programmer; Independent software Gardener

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Decentralization
text: The October lecture from the cycle Anarchocapitalism will be about decentralization; this, in my opinion, is very closely related to freedom - after all, it is not for nothing that I describe anarcho-capitalism in four equivalent ways for me: (a) mutual voluntariness, (b) complete demonopolization, (c) absolute decentralization and (d) the principle of subsidiarity and the right to self-determination brought to fruition. Although decentralization tends to be better accepted by people than anarcho-capitalism, it nevertheless raises a number of concerns; these mainly revolve around the impossibility (or considerable complexity) of controlling decentralized systems (compared to centralized systems). What about when "undesirable" enclaves, such as racism, sexism, religious fundamentalism or sectarianism, begin to emerge in a decentralized society? You can learn that - and much more - at the lecture.

title: Freeport Studio: On Capitalism and Mises with Lukáš Pazderník
text:
Lukáš Pazderník is a long-time supporter of the Free Port, who some time ago went through a transformation - from a "capitalist" to an "anarchist", although he remained and still remains a voluntarist the whole time; besides, he is a philosopher, so he thinks a lot about the above concepts.
That's why our conversation was more like meditation than some kind of wild discussion shootout; not necessarily because we agree on everything, but rather because Lukáš's goal was not to convince anyone, but rather to show new perspectives on the world.

– Lukáš Pazderník; anarchist; volunteer; philosopher; supporter of the Free Port

title: Urza's webinar for Joyful World
text: The Slovak community school Radostný svet asked me for a webinar on children's obedience (not only) in schools, which I was happy to oblige; we dealt with all sorts of issues, for example freedom versus the safety of children in kindergarten, which in my opinion is a very good parallel for many issues in our "adult" world.

title: Freeport Studio: Impacts of paying taxes and receiving subsidies
text:
You have heard countless times on the Freeport Channel why I consider taxes to be immoral and ethically comparable to mafia protection money; I have also talked a lot about how subsidies distort the market and distort information about the scarcity of goods distributed decentralized by society through the market mechanism of prices.
At the request of one of our supporters - Ondřej Vlko Krumpolc - I worked on a topic that is very interesting to me, which is related to the above, but has practically not been discussed so far: What are the specific practical effects of paying and not paying or reducing taxes? And what about receiving and not receiving subsidies?

title: Zrzka and Matfyzák on the inefficiency of state education
text:
In addition to the Free Port, I also have the Zrzka and Matfyzák channels:
https://www.youtube.com/zrzkaamatfyzak
We organized the first joint event, as the topic of education concerns both projects.

– Redhead; youtuber from the Zrzka and Matfyzák channel; a girl who likes to be interested in what goes on in people's heads
– Matfyzák (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board; a teacher at the independent school Hedgehog without a cage

title: Mises Academy 2023: Anarcho-Capitalism with Teresa
text: Tereza spoke at the Liberal Institute's Mises Academy; introduced young libertarians to the basics of anarcho-capitalism. She took Urza's slideshow and supplemented it with her own interpretation, which differed from Urza's in places, which is highly desirable; let libertarian ideas spread to as many people as possible in as many different forms as possible, because then they will reach their destination more easily.

title: Freeport Studio: Are Anarcho-Capitalists Asocial?
text:
In October we will livestream again with Teresa after some time; our topic is the question of whether anarcho-capitalists are anti-social. We'd love for you to join us and create content with us; you can write to us or call the Studio.
We will deal with the internal setup of anarcho-capitalists; this is inherently very subjective - just as our observation is fundamentally influenced by the social bubble. Not only for this reason, we will be happy if you share your experience with us.

title: Freeport Studio: On the War on Drugs with General Frydrych
text:
General Jakub Frydrych is the director of the police National Anti-Drug Headquarters; he is therefore a leading representative of the Czech state's war against drugs. Because I believe in peaceful dialogue with everyone, I decided to invite him to the Studio; the general, to my delight - probably for similar reasons - accepted the invitation.
I find the interview an interesting clash of two different worlds; while I am based on individualism and ethics independent of laws, General Frydrych derives his view of what is right and wrong precisely from the valid laws of the Czech Republic.

– General Jakub Frydrych; director of the police National Anti-Drug Headquarters

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: False Advertising for Education
text:
In September, Markéta Čermáková will lecture on anarcho-capitalism; he will talk about the fact that the state guarantees children the right to education by imposing it on them as an obligation. The state promises to take into account the educational needs of the individual, mutual respect and tolerance, tolerance of opinions, solidarity and dignity of all participants in education. Among other things, it imposes on educators the obligation to create a positive and safe climate in the school environment and to support its development through their approach to education and training. Does that sound good to you? To Marquette (apart from that duty) yes. Does this sound like a description of most mainstream schools? Unfortunately not. We will look at the ways in which legislation and school practice most often differ. And also to the main thing - why education, as it is set up, does not take into account the real needs of children, and how else (and why) children can be educated happily and effectively.

title: Gabriela and Urza with a love of freedom and learning in Ústí nad Labem
text: As part of our cycle of talks with Gabriela, we performed in Ústí nad Labem; the audience was rather atypical - many of the listeners did not know Ježek or self-directed education. So the debates were different than usual; which was beneficial for me, because we probably changed the horizons of several people.

title: Freeport Studio: Let's Create!
text:
After the conversation with the Tomš brothers about founding a political party, a number of you spoke up and advised them not to found a party; for many it was a cringe, mostly about the "bad name" they would allegedly give to libertarian ideas. I don't see it that way; I would like them to implement their idea - although I am not a fan of the political path myself.
I explain my position (concerning not only the Tomš brothers) in this very video; at the same time, I call on all libertarians to create, to support the creation of others, or at least not to destroy it.
Link to the article mentioned in the video:
https://www.urza.cz/public/l.harsh.truths.pdf

title: Students & Politics: Interview with Urza
text:
I prefer to appeal to young people with the ideas of anarcho-capitalism; this is also why I accepted the invitation to interview in the Students & Politics project. A personal meeting did not work out for us; at least online.

– Viktor Mašek from the Studenti & Politika project (https://youtube.com/@studentiapolitika; https://studentiapolitika.cz/)

title: Gabriela and Urza with a love of freedom and learning in Prague's Eccentric Club
text: As part of our series of talks with Gabriela, we performed at the Eccentric Club; it was exceptionally open to the public. We addressed how schools prepare children for the labor market; and whether that should even be their purpose. We talked about the will to overcome ourselves and do things we don't enjoy.

title: Freeport Studio: Ankap with Kat
text:
Kato is one of the most famous Czech rappers and lyricists of the hip hop scene; his work came to me already in my childhood, when he created as a member of the group Chaozz (then called himself Deph). He later founded his own project Prago Union; he has been working there for over twenty years.
A while ago we had a conversation in the Studio about drugs; in the process, I learned that Kato is quite open to new ideas, moreover, he had already heard about ankap before, or rather read (and lost) my book, which I dedicated to him again. And you came to talk about ankapa again...

– Adam Kato Svatoš; rapper; DJ; lyricist; supporter of complete decriminalization of all drugs

title: On the founding of the Libertarian Party
text:
The Tomš brothers asked me to consult with them on the proposal to establish a libertarian party; and although the political path is not mine, I will gladly support those who embark on it to freedom, even if I do not see the point in it myself.
I see a lot of mistakes in the presented project, on the other hand, I'm really glad that they are working on it; I believe the best way to learn something is to just do it.

– the Tomš brothers; libertarians; active students; those interested in founding a libertarian party

title: Eating with Urza at the House of the Free Port about self-directed education in Hedgehog without a cage, August 2023
text:
At Worldschooling 2023 in the House of the Free Port, Jíťa and I decided to introduce the participants to the Hedgehog without a cage; the entire discussion was carried out in a friendly spirit, as the listeners are mostly close to self-directed education.
We talked about normal functioning in Ježek, resolving conflicts, creating rules, but we also talked about concerns about whether children will be able to cope with high school or university after they leave Ježek; we also talked a little about other similar schools.

– Jíťa; a teacher at the independent school Jezek without a cage; anarcho-capitalist; longtime volunteer of the Free Port

title: Urza at the Freeport House on Freedom, August 2023
text:
My first talk at Worldschooling 2023 in the House of the Free Port was about the freedom of the individual and the whole society; we actually talked about anarcho-capitalism again, but probably a little differently than our regular followers are probably used to from similar discussions.
We were primarily concerned with the connections between (external) freedom in society and (internal) mental, spiritual and perhaps even spiritual settings of the individuals who make up such a society. Indeed, external and internal freedom greatly influence each other; free individuals make a free society which makes free individuals.

title: About ankap with Gabriela for ZŠ Heureka
text:
This time, Gabriela also took on the lecture - or rather the discussion - about ankap for Heureka Primary School; I'm very happy for that, because I'm not used to lecturing to such a young audience.
We discussed the classic topics - who would provide health care, education, the military or diplomacy; we devoted most of our time to polycentric law – this time we discussed ethics rather than practical functioning.

title: Freeport Studio: Schooling with Sára Kvasničková
text:
Sára Kvasničková is a recent high school graduate and my friend is dedicated to self-directed education and work with children; he helps at the stays of the House of the Free Port and occasionally also at the Prague EduCorn. I want to create a livestream with someone without much distance from state education.
I would like to talk to her about her personal experiences with state education, especially from the pre-matriculation period; we will then compare them with a non-authoritative environment in schools focused on self-directed education.

– Sára Kvasničková; recent graduate; promoter of self-directed education; co-worker of Prague EduCorn; volunteer

title: Studio Freeport: Children, technology, fear and (un)freedom
text:
Technology is currently a hot topic (not only) in circles around (not only) self-directed learning; games today are designed to make children dependent on themselves, against which they need protection - at least that's what more and more people think, now even a number of the more free-spirited ones.
I, on the other hand, believe that children (like everyone else) can best protect themselves; that is, they can't find a way to deal with the dangers in their lives that we "shield" them from, which won't last forever anyway - a clash with reality is always inevitable. And how does it all relate to fear, the state and politicians?

title: Anarcho-capitalism: Freedom external, internal and in Ježek
text: I am dedicating the June lecture from the Anarchocapitalism cycle to my life's theme - namely freedom; I see its study and the subsequent sharing of acquired knowledge as my mission. I've actually been researching external freedom since childhood, and I think I've known it to some extent and consistently described it; I cannot say that about inner freedom, even though I have been very intensely interested in it for the last few years. Ježek bez klece (a school as free as the Czech legislation allows for anarchists), where I've been teaching since September (but I've been spending time there for more than a year), has pushed me incredibly far in the last year in learning about freedom. I probably have more questions than answers about inner freedom, so I will be very happy if you come and share your knowledge; a very effective form of learning for me is dialogue and inspiration from other people - that's why I welcome any feedback.

title: Urza in Tim's eight-hour livestream (about everything)
text:
Tim invited me to the Debate Journal livestream (both D's are capitalized in this title); we dealt with ankap as always, but then it also slipped into drugs, sex, nonsense and other topics as always. This time there was also an auction!

– Timofey Kozhuchov; creator of the Debate Journal; active libertarian; a seeker of knowledge

title: Gabriela and Urza with love for freedom and learning in Polná (sound with echo)
text: As part of our cycle of talks with Gabriela, we performed in Polná; the audience included both people familiar with self-directed education and those who were unfamiliar with it. We debated about everything; I consider the most interesting topic to be the fears through which we perceive the world and pass them on to our children.

title: Urza in an interview for Creative Society
text: I accepted an interview invitation for the Creative Society; my goal was to introduce anarcho-capitalism to viewers and listeners. We talked about the economic side of things, inequalities between people and the creation of wealth; we discussed regulation and why a free market organization of society is better than a centralized one.

title: Urza on UTXO.23
text:
Although I have been focusing more on education than crypto for some time now, I am happy to receive the second invitation to UTXO; I gladly accepted it, although my speech was nowhere near as technical as most speakers'. Hopefully I will be at this conference in 2024 as well.
First, I explained the function of money and economic calculation, as in my opinion these are very neglected topics, the consequences of which are not monitored by anyone from the crypto community; at the end of the lecture, I tried to break down the regulation of cryptocurrencies, which some bitcoiners have recently been calling for.

title: Tereza in the debate for Legalize It
text:
Tereza participated in the final debate at the Legalize It conference organized by Students for Liberty; her opponent was general Jakub Frydrych and the topic was, of course, drugs.

– Jakub Frydrych; director of the National Anti-Drug Headquarters

title: 4D: Why the state should not restrict freedom of speech!
text:
Four reasons why the state should not restrict freedom of speech!
All communication platform rules should be determined by their owners; including any restrictions. State intervention in any direction contradicts property rights.
If we ban the public presentation of some opinions, they will not disappear from society anyway; on the contrary, it will be much more difficult to oppose them than if we let them be heard.
I believe in finding the truth through dialogue. If we suppress criticism of a position, we limit the possibility of its constant review and possible reevaluation.
Words have great power to do much harm; however, they have exactly the same power in defense against such damage. Let us fight against word with word, against sword with sword.

title: 4D: Why the state does not have to build roads!
text:
Four reasons why the state does not need to build roads!
People want to be transported; and where there is demand, there is also supply in the free market.
The state has no additional resources available to it beyond those it collects from taxpayers. To give an idea: No company in the Czech Republic has such profits as the state earns from motorists after accounting for all costs. 
Notoriously known corruption - connected precisely with the construction of the road network - is, in principle, only possible where someone makes decisions about other people's finances - just like the state about taxpayers' money.
The private investor is motivated to manage and operate roads to the satisfaction of their users; not according to current – often ideological – political demand.

title: Gabriela and Urza with a love of freedom and learning in Pilsen
text: As part of our series of talks with Gabriela, we performed in my beloved Pilsen; a lot of people came. In addition to classic topics, we dealt with the establishment of new registered and community schools focused on self-directed education; there was talk of local specifics in the way people think.

title: Urza in KryptoVlaď's livestream on UTXO.23
text:
After my performance at UTXO.23, I was caught by KryptoVláďa to do a live interview in the studio there; as expected, it was a very pleasant performance, because I always had a nice chat with Vláda - this time more generally about freedom than just about crypto.

– KryptoVlaďa; crypto anarchist; youtuber

title: Jíťa and Urza at the Liberecká Sudbury school about creating rules
text:
Decentralized order has fascinated me for over fifteen years; I am constantly learning about it and thinking about it on a theoretical level, however, there are schools where rules are formed in this way in practice, which is different from the general social order, but it helps in understanding it.
I decided to go around these schools and learn there; Jíťa also visited the Liberec Sudbury school with me. We compared their – domcratic – rule-making system with our – consensual – system in Ježek. Here too we come to the fact that the method of codification of the rules matters.

– Jitka Nyklová; a teacher at the Ježek free school without a cage

title: Gabriela and Urza with a love of freedom and learning in Prague's Communication Space
text: As part of our series of talks with Gabriela, we performed in Prague's Communication Space. We dealt with respecting children, forcing them to do anything they don't want to do, and protecting them from a dangerous world; we also talked about interpersonal relationships and setting rules in Ježek.

title: Urza in the program Laws of Wealth with Tomáš Lukavac
text: Tomáš Lukavec invited me to his program Laws of Wealth, where I briefly introduced anarcho-capitalism to those who do not know it; we talked, among other things, about the law and its enforcement, and unsurprisingly, free education was also mentioned. I enjoyed the interview; towards the end I also answered free questions from the audience.

title: Freeport Studio: Holidays 2023 and the direction of Freeport
text:
I have a lot of questions and comments about the functioning of the Free Port; since many of them are repeated, I decided to answer them in this video. In addition, we switch to vacation mode in a moment, so the video also serves as a farewell (if only for a few months, during which we can also meet in person at the House of the Free Port).
I invite you to our various events (even here in the summer); and I am also talking about the overall direction of the Freeport in the future. We will continue to focus on anarcho-capitalism and education; I also explain why such a large percentage of our port content is (and will be) about education.

title: Gabriela, Urza, Jotka, Amálka, Verča and Emily with love for freedom and learning in Brno
text:
As part of our series of talks with Gabriela, we performed (again) in Brno. This time our students - Jotka, Amálka, Verča and Emily - participated with us; unfortunately almost no spectators came. The conversation was – with regard to the children – rather chaotic, although very pleasant for me; on the other hand, you can recognize the authentic expression of some of our pupils on it.

– Jotka; pupil of Ježek school without a cage
– Amalka; pupil of Ježek school without a cage
– Veronica; pupil of Ježek school without a cage
– Emily; pupil of Ježek school without a cage

title: The road to anarcho-capitalism in the Cherubín tea house
text:
One lecture at the Cherubín teahouse eventually became a whole series; I like to go back there because the place has the right tea tree and a great atmosphere (and a Buddha statue with the inscription: "When the god said: "Let there be light," the sound already existed.").
This time I devoted myself to the road to anarcho-capitalism; because I often talk about the goal state, but rarely about how to get there. This is an important topic; and not only for ways to live through anarcho-capitalism (rather metaphorically), but also to warn against ways that, in my opinion, will definitely not work, because in principle they cannot.

title: About money for ZŠ Běchovice
text:
I consider lectures and discussions for children to be one of the most important parts of my work; therefore, I was very happy to accept an invitation to the Prague – Běchovice Primary School, where I was asked to explain the function of money to the students. It was also working with a younger audience than I'm used to.
I feel absolutely great about the conversation; I think it was one of the most successful. It was a joy to watch the students think about the topic; many of them certainly went more under the surface, many of them changed their opinions right during the discussion. I hope you enjoy listening at least half as much as I enjoy the discussion.

title: Urza in the first episode of the Best Podcast
text:
Maestro Kubelík invited me to the first episode of the Best Podcast, in which my favorite debate opponents Dan Vávra and Filip Turk also appeared; we talked (for a long time) about everything possible, especially freedom of speech.

– Jakub Zeman; Czech Samurai; Japanologist; writer; translator
– Daniel Vávra; game developer; graphic designer; photographer; influencer; youtuber; conservative; former libertarian
– Filip Turek; political commentator; Formula 3 racer; car collector

title: Studio of the Free Port: External and internal freedom in Ježek
text:
For the first time in the history of the Freeport, we are broadcasting a Thursday livestream with the name and topic of Wednesday's lecture; my main intention (lecture and livestream) is to move myself and my own perception of freedom. I firmly believe that you, dear viewers and listeners, will help me in this; and that you will enjoy the process.
We will start with external freedom (NAP and property rights), then move to internal; I also want to share some of what I learned in Ježek. I will be very happy if you send me your thoughts, experiences, observations - in short, I will appreciate any feedback; especially criticism, it moves me the most.

title: Freeport Studio: Guns and Children with Tim Kožuchov
text:
Tim Kožuchov—formerly a socialist, now a libertarian—asked me for help in arguing for gun deregulation and compulsory schooling; and to make it more interesting (for me) and more useful (for Tim), we limited ourselves to utilitarian arguments.
As always I enjoyed working with Tim as he asked great questions; I like his thirst for knowledge and open mind. We've tackled a lot from a state gun registry to mass shootings (not just in schools) to mandatory reading, writing, and math classes.

– Timofey Kozhuchov; libertarian; YouTuber; student of political science and philosophy; LGBT activist

title: Anarcho-capitalism: Ankap is a fairy tale!(?)
text: The May lecture from the series Anarchocapitalism will be devoted to the popular (dis)argument against ankap; namely, that it is a nonsensical fairy tale that does not hold up in the real world. Whether it is a comparison with communism as a "nice theory", the homo economicus model, the demand for a "new anarcho-capitalist man" and a change in human nature, or the idea that evolution shows the dysfunctionality of an establishment that has not historically prevailed, it seems to me that many - although certainly not all - efforts to refute (or perhaps overthrow) anarcho-capitalism are burdened by ignorance of the topic. I would like to elaborate on some of them; as part of this, I also intend to outline realistically functional (albeit slow) paths to freedom (and eventually a stateless society). I will be very happy for your questions, polemics and this time more than ever for comments and suggestions.

title: Lecture for the secondary film school in Zlín
text:
The students of the secondary film school in Zlín invited me to lecture them about anarcho-capitalism; I gladly accepted. And I enjoyed it a lot; the atmosphere there absorbed me - it seemed to me that the audience and I really understood each other - I would say that I am still learning and improving, which fulfills me.
First, at the request of the audience, I briefly described anarcho-capitalism; then I answered their questions for a while - you could see that they were thinking about the answers. Then – unsurprisingly – we got to the Hedgehog without a cage; freedom in education is, in my opinion, the key to freedom in society.

title: Free Port Studio: About children's autonomy with Pavel Fornůsk
text:
Pavel Fornůsek came to one of the discussions that Gabriela and I organized; he had good questions about the matter, he started a good discussion. Later, he contacted me by email with the wish to discuss the topic further; so I invited him to the Studio so that other people could benefit from our conversation.
We discussed the creation of rules in children's collectives; we focused on how best to set the rules so that, on the one hand, everyone's property rights are respected and, on the other hand, mutually equal partner relationships with children are not disturbed.

– Pavel Fornůsek; scout leader; supporter of self-directed education

title: Gabriela and Urza with a love of freedom and learning in Klatovy
text: As part of our cycle of talks with Gabriela, we performed in Klatovy; an interesting audience was waiting for us there too. From the obligatory technologies we got to the deeper themes hidden behind them; namely fears, mistrust of children and themselves. How deep does the rabbit hole go?

title: Interview for the Slovak Trend magazine
text: When Gabriela and I visited Bratislava, they approached me with a request for an interview from Trend magazine; we talked about freedom, anarcho-capitalism, the state, self-government and a lot of other topics with a pro-libertarian editor. We compared the situation in the Czech Republic and Slovakia; freedom is worse there...

title: Freeport Studio: Ethics and Conservatism with Alexander Kraft
text:
One of the advantages of lecturing and lecturing in schools is that sometimes there are students who are interested enough in the topic to work on it in some way; Alexandr Kraft is one such student who solves the society in which he lives. He is an anarcho-capitalist and a conservative at the same time.
We discussed several ethical topics with him: the legitimacy of abortion, marriage for all and transgender people, especially children. I found the debate quite civilized, respectful and calm; at the same time rewarding because we have chosen topics on which we disagree.

– Alexander Kraft; anarcho-capitalist; conservative; student

title: Gabriela and Urza with a love of freedom and learning in Ostrava
text: As part of our series of talks with Gabriela, we performed in Ostrava!!! I found the conversation very pleasant; and even though a lot of questions about self-directed education are repeated to a certain extent, I am actually constantly gaining more knowledge through them - and I hope that you are with me.

title: Urza in Investocka
text: Libor Flössler invited me to his show Investocka; from the moment I arrived, I felt comfortable in their studio, which was reflected throughout the interview. It was one of those that just flowed and entertained me regardless of the cameras; originally I was in a hurry and wanted to leave after an hour, which didn't work out - and I'm glad for that.

title: Studio Freeport: About the company with Tomáš Hajzler
text:
Tomáš Hajzler has quite a wide scope in his activities; so we also have quite a lot of intersection - free education, self-governance, society, free market and many other topics. In some we agree, in others partially, in others not at all.
This struck me as a good starting point for the debate; and I would say that I was not wrong. It was one of the most peaceful debates with a man from the opposite end of the (at least economic) spectrum; however, that didn't make her (at least from my point of view) any less interesting.

– Tomáš Hajzler (www.peoplecomm.cz, www.tomashajzler.com); anti-capitalist; publicist; localization promoter

title: Gabriela and Urza with a love for freedom and learning in Bratislava
text: As part of our series of talks with Gabriela, we visited Slovakia; Students for Liberty invited us to Bratislava. Although the degree of freedom in Slovakia is significantly lower than in the Czech Republic, it is never too late to change; I'm really happy for all the libertarians who are trying to defend freedom.

title: About anarcho-capitalism in the Eccentric Club for the second time
text: It was with great pleasure that I accepted another invitation to lecture at the Eccentric Club; after the presentation of ankap, a very interesting debate broke out.

title: Freeport Studio: Drugs with Kat
text:
Kato is one of the most famous Czech rappers and lyricists of the hip hop scene; his work came to me already in my childhood, when he created as a member of the group Chaozz (then called himself Deph). He later founded his own project Prago Union; he has been working there for over twenty years.
I heard him on Drunk Zone some time ago where he stated that the only way is to legalize all drugs; and I couldn't do it, I had to invite him to the Studio - both because of the drugs and because I wanted to get to know a person whose work I had been listening to since my early childhood.

– Adam Kato Svatoš; rapper; DJ; lyricist; supporter of complete decriminalization of all drugs

title: Debate with the deputy director of the Smíchovská Secondary Technical School and a representative of the Municipal Council of Prague 20
text:
The students of the Smíchovské secondary technical school and gymnasium invited me to a debate on anarcho-capitalism with Petr Růžička, deputy director of the SSPŠ and representative of the Municipal Council of Prague 20; we also opened self-directed education.

– Petr Růžička; deputy director and teacher at SSPŠ; representative of the Municipal Council of Prague 20 – Horní Počernice

title: Freeport Studio: Disinformation
text:
Fighting misinformation (even boys with misinformation) is a hot topic in society lately; however, it has many pitfalls and unintended consequences. And not only in the hands of the state (although of course there primarily); even purely private initiatives to combat disinformation can do more harm than good—not to mention their ever-present tendency to grow with the state.
So come and debate with us - in writing and by phone - and thus create the next part of our program; we look forward to it!

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: The State Against the Poor
text: The April lecture from the Anarchocapitalism cycle will be devoted to how the state harms the poor; and this despite the fact that as part of his propaganda he constantly convinces everyone of the opposite. Many people believe that in a world without the state, it would be the poor today who would be the ones to suffer; however, in my opinion, this is a big illusion created by the state in order to create fear and thereby justify its existence. Even if the state is redistributing to help some of the poor - which is very easy to see - there are plenty of other (really strong) state influences that clearly harm the poor - which is much harder to see. Let's focus on them and look - like Frédéric Bastiat - at what (at least at first glance) is not visible.

title: Gabriela and Urza with love for freedom and learning at the University of the Third Age at BUT in Brno
text: I really enjoyed the lecture on money for the University of the Third Age at BUT; and the listeners apparently too, so we arranged a continuation about education. Gabriela undertook this with me; unlike the other discussions, this time we started with a lecture (on self-directed education and Ježek).

title: Gabriela and Urza with their love of freedom and learning at the Pod Čarou Theatre
text: As part of our series of talks with Gabriela, we performed at the Pod čarou Theater in Písek; the audience was quite diverse and the debate interesting. We opened the – rather emotional – topic of parents' involvement in the school and the teaching process; we explained why we try to keep our parents away from Ježek.

title: Free Harbor Studio: About Anarchy with Štěpán Sakala
text:
Štěpán Sakala impressed me on social networks with his knowledge of anarchism and its individual schools; especially the collectivist ones. After a long and unsuccessful attempt to get him to the Studio, I happened to meet him as part of a performance at his school; we both agree on the importance and importance of peace dialogue.
In the debate, we mainly discussed collectivist anarchist trends, especially anarchocommunism, anarchosyndicalism and anarchomutualism; we also got to anarcho-primitism, anarcho-pacifism and other schools.

– Štepán Sakala; anarchist; student of the Smíchovské secondary technical school

title: Gabriela, Urza and Štěpánka with a love of freedom and learning in Otrokovice
text:
As part of our series of talks with Gabriela, we spoke at the scout center in Otrokovice. Our beloved colleague Štěpánka also participated; and we mercilessly dragged her into the story (even if she didn't expect it). Attendance was high this time; and the questions focused mainly on the details of the operation of the Hedgehog without a cage.

– Štěpánka Červenková; a teacher at Ježek school without a cage

title: Liquid Zulu: Argumentation Ethics
text:
Liquid Zulu is a propagator of Hoppe's argumentation ethics which I don't find valid even if I believe in non-aggression principle and self-ownership. I hope you enjoy our discussion on this topic.

– Liquid Zulu; anarcho-capitalist

title: Freeport Studio: Economic calculation at the (Czech) Post Office
text:
The cancellation of Czech Post branches and the dismissal of employees of the same state-owned enterprise arouses a lot of passion among people; these lead to a public debate: On the one hand, there is no money, on the other hand, postal unionists are fighting for "quality of service" (and more or less mean the preservation of jobs).
What is basically everyone forgetting? On the problem of the impossibility of economic calculation in central planning; and the current situation of this notoriously desperately inefficient state enterprise shows us in full nakedness. What is the "correct" density of the Czech Post branch network? No politician or official simply knows that; and he can't even know.

title: Rules in Ježek and Donum Felix
text:
When they called me from Donum Felix to come talk to them about the Austrian School of Economics, it made me very happy; I immediately arranged to see if I could spend the whole day with them, to which they agreed - and for me it was a very pleasant, beneficial day, full of discoveries and great experiences.
After the discussion about the Austrian economy, we also organized a debate about the rules in Ježek and Donum Felix; although they are similar, seemingly small differences cause big differences in consequences. This debate has changed my perception of decentralized systems, polycentric law and spontaneous order.

title: Austrian School of Economics in Donum Felix
text:
When they called me from Donum Felix to come talk to them about the Austrian School of Economics, it made me very happy; I immediately arranged to see if I could spend the whole day with them, to which they agreed - and for me it was a very pleasant, beneficial day, full of discoveries and great experiences.
During the discussion about the Austrian economy, we introduced its founder and Ludwig von Mises as well as Friedrich August von Hayek; including their main contributions to the economy - we then dealt with these in more depth. In the end, we left the economy and dealt with anarchy (anarcho-capitalism) versus the state.

title: Freeport Studio: Box Politicians
text:
My stance on the presidential election angered a lot of people—often libertarians—as expected; and although it was often unpleasant, in one case even painful, I decided to transform it into something good - a lecture on martial law (mind) and a video about charismatic politicians.
The problem with politicians who seem presentable and polished is that they get away with a lot of things; and worse, they add seriousness to their authorities, thereby encouraging statism in the people - the most dangerous religion of today (and perhaps of the past). I am not telling anyone how to vote; just take it as food for thought.

title: Gabriela and Urza with a love of freedom and learning in Erazim in Opava
text: As part of our cycle of talks with Gabriela, we performed at Erazim in Opava; many people came, mostly at least somewhat familiar with the concept of self-directed education. This was matched by the spirit of the debate, where less usual topics were also addressed; for example, for the first time, there was no mention of technology.

title: Freeport Studio: Politics with Tomáš Pajonek
text:
Tomáš Pajonk is one of the libertarians who took a political path in the past; he was vice-chairman and chairman of the Party of Free Citizens and a representative of the Zlín Region. Although I do not believe that politics leads to freedom, I have always respected Tomáš.
In this livestream, we will discuss not only his work in Svobodny, but also (libertarian) politics in practice; we will also get to his work in the council. We will of course be happy for your questions; and you can also call us.

– Tomáš Pajonk; libertarian; former chairman and vice-chairman of the Free Citizens Party; former representative of the Zlín region; businessman

title: Freeport Studio: Atlas Rebellion with David Jirsa
text:
David Jirsa is the author of the Na potítku channel, where he reviews various literary works in individual videos; I was brought to him by his review of the novel Atlas Rebellion by Ayn Rand, which surprisingly (for a libertarian) I actually quite relate to.
On the other hand, from David Jirsa, there are various views on libertarians, the state, regulation and the free market, which I take issue with; we honed - in addition to literature - in a lot of different areas from anarcho-capitalist movements in the world to the meaningfulness of state regulations to education and training.

– David Jirsa; author of the Na poítku channel; literary critic; teacher

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Martial Law (Think)
text: The March lecture from the Anarcho-Capitalism cycle will be about the "war mentality"; about a vision of the world in which all people belong either to the "us" category (that is, the good, righteous, decent and kind-hearted ones with pure intentions and striving for a good world), or to the "them" category (that is, the bad, vile, bad and evil sons with dark intentions and an effort to do harm). This view of the world is "activated" in people from time to time - usually during an impending perceived or real danger - and state institutions have learned to control it very well over the thousands of years of existence and use it to their advantage; whether during real wars, the coronavirus, the climate crisis, the regulation of everything possible and impossible, or presidential elections.

title: Freeport Studio: Economic calculation in child psychiatry
text:
For some time now, reports of the catastrophic situation in child psychiatry have been leaking to the media; some industry insiders even talk about the fact that the industry has already collapsed. In one discussion I heard several suggestions for improvement; one of them caught my attention more than the others.
I think that the problem of the impossibility of economic calculation in central planning can be well demonstrated on the desperate situation in child psychiatry; and using a concrete example to show that partial central planning (for example in the health sector) suffers from similar ailments as the whole centrally planned economy - it differs only in the extent of the problems caused.

title: Panel Discussion Freeport Conference 2023: Drugs and Weapons Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow
text:
We ended the Free Port 2023: Drugs and Weapons Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow conference with a panel discussion in which Martin Duřt, Urza and Jakub Engelmajer took part; Tereza Urzová took on the role of moderator.

The complete program of the conference can be found here:
https://konference.urza.cz/2023/img/program.1024x1448.png

title: Ondra Plachý: Workshop, Air guns without a firearms license (KSP23: Drugs and weapons yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
Not all attendees of the "2023 Freeport Conference: Drugs and Guns Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow" need a lunch break; and it was for them that Ondřej Plachý prepared his workshop "Air weapons without a firearms license".

In today's age of various state restrictions, at the moment there is a unique opportunity for every individual to equip himself with an air gun, which he could not own until about a year ago without having to own a firearms license and register the weapon. These highly accurate and at the same time relatively powerful weapons can be perfectly used for sporting purposes, but in extreme cases also for survival or self-defense.

Ondřej Plachý is the founder and chief developer of Altaros Air Solutions, which manufactures PCP air rifles and their accessories. On a professional level, he has been dealing with airguns for 15 years, and during that time he became the author of several Czech and foreign patents. He holds the world record for the longest target hit with an air rifle at a distance of 1280m. He also developed unique technologies for the production of lead bullets for air rifles, which are produced using the machining method on specially modified CNC lathes. He set the world record with a PCP air rifle of his own design and the already mentioned CNC turned lead bullets.

title: Dominik Stroukal: A game of cat and mouse and unicorns (KSP23: Drugs and weapons yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
The sixth speaker of the "Free Port Conference 2023: Drugs and Weapons Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow" was Dominik Stroukal with his lecture "The Game of Cat and Mouse and Unicorns".

The Dark Web is not a static place, but an ever-evolving ecosystem where (among other things) drugs can be purchased. Actions against dark markets provoke reactions. There is a fundamental difference between drugs and weapons. Why? Can we predict where the online drug and gun trade will go?

M.Sc. Ing. Dominik Stroukal, Ph.D. lectures at the Metropolitan University of Prague. He is the author of several books, including the latest Dark Web: Sex, Drugs and Bitcoin, is a member of the National Economic Council of the Government (NERV) and an economic advisor to SatoshiLabs. You can hear him regularly on the Ve váta podcast.

title: Jakub Engelmajer: Freedom, security and an armed citizen (KSP23: Drugs and weapons yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
The fifth speaker of the "Free Harbor Conference 2023: Drugs and weapons yesterday, today and tomorrow" was Jakub Engelmajer with his lecture "Freedom, security and an armed citizen".

An individual's firearms and access to them are linked to personal freedom, personal responsibility and societal freedom. Why be an armed citizen, what it actually means to be armed and what real effects it has on individual gun owners and society as a whole - you will hear all this at his lecture.

Jakub is a graduate of Political Science and European Studies from UPOL, a long-time holder of a firearms license, and since 2016, as an examination commissioner for weapons and ammunition appointed by the MVČR, he has been examining applicants for a firearms license at professional competency tests. Since the establishment of the association at the end of 2021, vice-chairman of the Association of Examination Commissioners for Weapons and Ammunition in the Czech Republic. Since 2019, he has been a member of the board of LEX z.s. Association for the Protection of the Rights of Gun Owners and coordinator of LEX East Bohemia. He holds a firearms license for instruction or training in shooting and is an instructor of the B-rdy Combat Shooting team. He acts as a referee for LOS and IDPA shooting competitions. As part of his activities, he lectures, organizes shooting training, cooperates in creating and commenting on new weapons legislation, and gaining allies and partners to support the right of citizens of the Czech Republic to own, hold and carry a firearm.

title: Martin Duřt: Are psychedelics a revolution in psychotherapy? (KSP23: Drugs and guns yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
The fourth speaker of the "2023 Freeport Conference: Drugs and Weapons Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow" was Martin Duřt with his lecture "Are psychedelics a revolution in psychotherapy?".

Nowadays, we are experiencing a psychedelic revolution, a renewal of scientific research into this unique class of substances after many decades when research in this direction was not possible for political reasons. New studies show the great potential of psychedelics to help treat a number of mental disorders. Although this represents new hope for people suffering from otherwise difficult-to-solve problems, question marks remain and it is important not to fall into the romantic notion of psychedelics as panaceas for all ills.

Martin Duřt is a researcher in the phenomenology of psychoactive substances, co-founder of the harm reduction platform Czeched Substance, member of the Czech Psychedelic Society and author of the utheraptor.art blog. In his work, he focuses on revealing the influence of drugs on human consciousness and reducing their risks. When he's not doing science, he creates art using artificial intelligence and writes.

title: Urza: Time of Prohibitions (KSP23: Drugs and Guns Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow)
text:
The third speaker of the "2023 Freeport Conference: Drugs and Guns Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow" was Urza with his talk "Time of Prohibitions".

What happens when we ban something? Regardless of the reasons or the meaningfulness of such a ban, most people have a need to believe that the ban in question is meaningful; without knowing anything about the given issue, they can retroactively "invent" why this or that was forbidden and what would "certainly happen" if it was not forbidden. There's just one catch - very often it's simply not true; however, this does not prevent states from exploiting this ignorance (and fear) in enforcing bans. Drugs and guns used to be common "everyday" items a hundred years ago; until quite recently they were stigmatized and banned - yet it seems that only without them can our civilization function. It's interesting that a lot of people who have learned the futility of drug or gun bans are vehemently pushing for the regulation of the other... Why?

Urza is an anarcho-capitalist author; wrote over a thousand libertarian texts on the web and in print media and the first Czech book on anarcho-capitalism. For fifteen years, he not only reads, thinks and writes about freedom, ethics, education, the free market, the economy and the role of the state in society, but also lectures, makes videos and is invited to various programs and panel discussions. Together with his wife Teresa, he forms the Free Harbor; teaches at the independent school Hedgehog without a cage; he heads the Czech and Slovak Institute of Ludwig von Mises, of which he is a co-founder; he belongs to the board of the Freedom of Learning association and has been actively cooperating with many libertarian initiatives for a long time. You can find more about him on the Urza.cz website.

title: OC: Interesting Weapons, Pernicious Laws (KSP23: Drugs and Guns Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow)
text:
The second speaker of the "2023 Freeport Conference: Drugs and Guns Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow" was OC with his talk "Interesting Weapons, Pernicious Laws".

At several historical moments, we will show how firearms have developed from ancient history to the present; in addition to the interesting technical aspects, we will take a closer look at the changes in society's approach to personal weapons, personal freedom and personal responsibility, as well as the consequences to which this inexorably leads.

OC has been dealing with guns for many years; he is a collector of them as well as an active shooter. He published a number of articles, devoted to the technique and history of weapons; in addition, he is the author of many professional publications in the field of IT.

title: Freeport Studio: Bans
text:
As some of you may have noticed, the conference on drugs and guns was actually a conference on prohibitions and regulations manifesting in (among other things) the war on drugs and gun control policy; unfortunately, the effort of all governments to control people through prohibitions and regulations is ubiquitous - which is why it is important to describe, expose and talk about it.
So come and debate with us - in writing and by phone - and thus create the next part of our program; we look forward to it!

title: Tereza Urzová: The Unintended Effects of Prohibition (KSP23: Drugs and Weapons Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow)
text:
The first speaker of the "Free Port Conference 2023: Drugs and Weapons Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow" was Tereza Urzová with her lecture "Unintended Consequences of Prohibition".

I stand for the legalization of all psychoactive substances, starting with legal nicotine today, ending with heroin. Does that sound crazy to you? Yes, I once felt that way too. Gradually, however, I came to the conclusion that other legislation made no sense to me, both from a medical point of view and from an economic, moral and human point of view.

Tereza Urzová is a doctor, co-founder of the Free Port association cooperating with several libertarian associations. The topic of the prohibition of psychoactive substances is a favorite topic for her, in which the issues of medicine, economics and personal freedom meet.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: A Brief History of Psychoactive Substances
text: We all grew up in a society that treats drugs as a phenomenon of the modern age, for which it is a scarecrow, and as responsible individuals we should fight against it by all means. From history, we may vaguely remember the hippie movement or the development of meth-cooking plants in socialist Czechoslovakia, but otherwise we consider the use of addictive substances by the lay public to be relevant especially for the present. Meanwhile, at the end of the nineteenth century, any citizen could buy marijuana, hashish tincture, cocaine, morphine, heroin, and sometimes even exotic psychedelics at a pharmacy. Drugs can also be medicine and have long been viewed as such. How is it possible that after more than a hundred years we have reached a situation where a medicinal plant that anyone can grow for their own treatment in the garden is threatened with prison?

title: Urza in StandaShow (for the third time): Presidential elections
text:
The video with me was filmed by Standa at StandaShow (https://www.standashow.cz/) and is published here on the Free Port Channel with Standa's explicit consent (he sent me the video himself so that I could publish it here at an agreed time interval), for which I owe him my thanks.
Standa Hruška invited me to his StandaShow for the third time; and I always enjoy debating with him. This time we dealt with the presidential elections, their effects, we discussed the individual candidates and the meaningfulness of the election as such; we also got to the differences between an "ideological" and a "pragmatic" view of things.
Although our opinions differ on many things, I think we have been able to have a meaningful dialogue about them; I consider something like this to be the basis of mutual understanding - and not only between the two of us, but hopefully we will also make our positions comprehensible to the listeners and viewers.

– Standa Hruška (www.standashow.cz); youtuber; streamer; gamer; moderator

title: He is not an anarchist like an anarchist in the Cherubín tea house
text:
One lecture at the Cherubín teahouse eventually became a whole series; I like to go back there because the place has the right tea tree and a great atmosphere (and a Buddha statue with the inscription: "When the god said: "Let there be light," the sound already existed.").
This time I focused on different anarchist schools, since anarcho-capitalism is not the only anarchist trend; in addition to individualist and market anarchists, there are also collectivist and socialist ones - after all, there are a majority of them (especially historically). I have tried to outline their different approaches; and if possible do not strawman.

title: Democracy for the J.K. Tyl Gymnasium in Hradec Králové
text:
The initiative of the students of the J.K. Tyl Gymnasium in Hradec To invite me to the meeting was supported by the teachers, who simply did it without consulting the management; to my surprise, they were excited about the lecture, they invited me to the next class, and according to the reactions, it seems that we will continue to work together.
This recording is from the sophomores' Social Studies Foundations class, where their teacher invited me after she heard my talk I had given to the third and fourth graders earlier. Sophomores and I talked about democracy and its limits; I am glad for the willingness of the teacher in question to let pluralist opinions be heard.

text:
The initiative of the students of the J.K.
