title: Gabriela and Urza with a love of freedom and learning in Prague's EduCorn
text: As part of our series of talks with Gabriela, we performed at EduCorn in Prague. In addition to the usual topics, we also reached children with so-called special educational (or other) needs; and, as always, computer games and limiting technology to small children were also discussed.

title: Urza versus Marek Prchal at VŠE
text:
Marek Prchal invited me to his lecture at the University of Economics, where we debated anarcho-capitalism and the state; although our conversation was probably a bit disorganized or without a coherent structure from my point of view, I believe that there were interesting moments in it.

– Marek Prchal; political marketer; Andrej Babiš's marketing advisor

title: Studio of the Free Port: Arms with Jakub Smetánka
text:
Jakub Smetánka is vice president and member of the board of LEX, z.s.; this association strives to preserve the right of every ordinary citizen to possess a weapon for the purposes of self-defense, sport, hunting, for the exercise of a profession or employment, or for collecting purposes.
In the Freeport, we would like the state not to interfere with this right at all; in our opinion, people should be able to arm themselves at their own discretion. Together with Jakub Smetánka, we would like to present weapons as "ordinary" objects (without stigmatization).

– Jakub Smetánka; shooter; vice president and member of the board of directors of LEX, z.s.; businessman

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Regulatory Principles
text: The December lecture from the Anarchocapitalism cycle will be devoted to the regulatory principles of anarchocapitalism; despite popular belief among people who have heard little of anarcho-capitalism, anarchy does not mean the absence of rules, but only the absence of (forced and involuntary) rulers. However, people need - and therefore demand - rules for their daily lives, therefore they create them also on a voluntary basis; however, unlike central planners, the free market has the ability to flexibly create, change, and cancel these rules according to the momentary needs of its participants. In the lecture, we will focus on the most common principles on which market regulations work; and we will discuss them together.

title: About the 2023 presidential election with Karolína K.
text:
Karolína invited me (again) to her podcast Chatting without education; we dealt with the current topic - the presidential election. Does it even make sense to go to them? If so, who to vote for? And why?

– Karolína Kváš (http://karolinadobrovska.cz/); tarot rebel; authoress; traveler; anthropologist; blogger; coach

title: Freeport Studio: Ankap and self-management
text:
Ever since I've been teaching at Ježek without a cage and organizing a number of projects with Gabriela - especially talks - you often ask what will happen to the Free Port, or why we are so concerned with education; and it's no wonder, because we also devote ourselves intensively to it in Sewers of the Free Port, at KSP22 and not only there.
I have always considered education to be the most important aspect of the path to a free society; and the more experience I have with freedom, anarcho-capitalism and self-directed education, the more strongly I am convinced of this. In the video I explain why, in my opinion, self-directed education is essential for ankap and a free society.

title: Christmas talks in the dark in Ježek without a cage
text: As part of our cycle of talks with Gabriela, we of course performed in Ježek; it was a rather unconventional discussion - for two reasons. First, we and the audience were blindfolded; and secondly, mainly teachers and students from Ježko, or their parents, participated.

title: About money at the University of the Third Age at BUT in Brno
text:
With great joy and curiosity, I accepted the offer to give a lecture on money at the University of the Third Age at BUT in Brno; I like to do new things - or old things differently - and I haven't spoken to a similar target group yet. I had perhaps no expectations; but a lot of enthusiasm and curiosity about what will happen.
In the end, I was more than pleasantly surprised by this audience: I have probably never experienced a greater acceptance of anarcho-capitalist ideas among a (foreign) audience (i.e. not a libertarian one); I perceived from the listeners an understanding not only of capitalism, but even a certain sympathy for anarchy.

title: Lecture for the EDUCAnet Prague gymnasium
text:
A few years ago I taught at the EDUCAnet gymnasium in Kladno; that's why I accepted the invitation to give a lecture at the Prague branch of EDUCAnet. We discussed the stateless society, the free market and democracy, which were quite controversial topics for the listeners; thus it generated a good discussion.
Towards the end, we got to self-directed education in the Hedgehog without a cage; unsurprisingly, high school students accepted these theses far better than anarcho-capitalism. I am really happy for the invitation and the opportunity to present my thoughts on EDUCAnet; whether they meet with consent or not.

title: Urza on Tim's 2023 presidential election livestream
text:
Tim invited me to the Debate Journal livestream (both D's are capitalized in this title); we discussed the candidates for the 2023 presidential election, but we also got to other topics such as faith or anarcho-capitalism versus minarchism.

– Timofey Kozhuchov; creator of the Debate Journal; newly libertarian

title: Gabriela and Urza with a love of freedom and learning in Ostrožská Nová Ves
text: As part of our series of talks with Gabriela, we performed in Ostrožská Nová Ves; the questions this time went in a slightly different direction than usual. We focused far more on running the school, creating rules or resolving disputes than on technology or other pitfalls of a self-directed life.

title: Freeport Studio: Happy New Year and Happy New Year (2023)
text:
The year 2023 is here; and with it our summary of the year 2022. Both from the perspective of the Free Port and our other activities, as well as global events. The free port is doing well, but overall 2022 was a rough year for many people in the Czech Republic and in the world.
We hope that 2023 will bring changes for the better; perhaps ending the war or taming inflation. But even if not, we wish you to be well and handle everything that life throws at you; and if possible they enjoyed it.

title: Urza in the program Real life with Jaroslav Grűnwald
text:
Jaroslav Grűnwald invited me to his show Real Life, where we talked about freedom and anarcho-capitalism. The whole program is – just like its author – tuned to a bit of the esoteric, which I certainly didn't mind at all, rather the opposite; I like to penetrate into other worlds.

– Jaroslav Grűnwald; shaman; lecturer; therapist

title: Gabriela and Urza with their love of freedom and learning in Pardubice (movements in the background)
text:
As part of our series of talks with Gabriela, we performed in Pardubice at the invitation of the Indigo free school; we talked a lot about life in Ježek, the safety of children and (not) restricting their freedom in order to reduce the risk of their potential accidents or injuries.
We apologize for the poor sound quality (we do not want to pass microphones between participants for greater flow of conversation); thanks for your understanding.

title: Freeport Studio: Christmas Thanks (2022)
text:
I love Christmas; to the Christian in me, they remind me of the birth of the Lord Jesus; the capitalist in me rejoices in their material aspect; and as an anarchist I celebrate them with my loved ones in my own way regardless of social expectations. I'm very good at it, so I look forward to them every year; and this year is no different.
At the same time, I feel endless gratitude not only for my absolutely blessed life; I am infinitely grateful to the supporters and supporters of Freeport, libertarians, anarcho-capitalists and other anarchists who discover, know, live and spread freedom. In this way, I want to thank you all from the bottom of my heart.

title: Freeport Studio: Emperors of Dreams (Book)
text:
You occasionally ask me for book reviews; unfortunately I'm not the right person for that because (aside from fiction) anything I read blends in with everything else I've read in the past, so I'm unable to distinguish what was in which book. For example, the entire Austrian economy is (more or less) "one book" in my head.
However, I consider The Emperor of Dreams an important book – not only – because of the upcoming conference; it discusses the history of drugs and between the lines it can be beautifully read that in the past they were things of "daily" need, until their stigmatization came as a result of prohibitions, the aim of which, however, was not to protect people's health.

title: Urza at Dynamic Education
text: Vojtěch Kozelka invited me for an interview on the program Dynamic Education; although at first I was a little hesitant to accept his invitation considering the focus of the show (male self-development, dating, etc.), I ended up really enjoying the debate - we mainly covered ankap, but then also self-development.

title: Gabriela and Urza with a love of freedom and learning in Sklenářka
text: As part of our series of talks with Gabriela, we performed at Villa Sklenářka; it was a private conversation in the middle of the woods, but the topics were interesting. The main one was - as it probably won't surprise anyone - technology. I also consider the resolution of "conflicts" between the rights of children and adults to be very interesting.

title: About the market failure with Tim Kožuchov
text:
Tim sent me a video criticizing Mises' idea of the impossibility of economic calculation in socialism and pointing to market failure; to my surprise, the impossibility of economic calculation was correctly described in the video, which I found interesting, since most of its critics do not understand it.
Together we decided to comment on the video and explain why we think Mises was right and central control is always less efficient than the free market in allocating resources; finally, we comment on the so-called "market failures".

– Timofey Kozhuchov; libertarian and (perhaps also) anarcho-capitalist; YouTuber; student of political science and philosophy; LGBT activist

title: Studio of the Free Port: Technology of (un)freedom with Jan Skalicky
text:
Honza Skalický is my long-time friend, with whom I like to discuss society, science and technology; and because you liked the video with him in the Studio that we made a few months ago, we decided to broadcast another livestream.
We will focus on topics close to us, which are freedom, technology and their various connections; you can ask us anything you want, we will be happy to help you orientate yourself in the basics of the safe use of various technologies.

– Honza Skalicky; anarcho-capitalist; libertarian; technologist; software architect; author of the book Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies of the future

title: Freeport Studio: State Like Big Brother
text:
The tax office suspected that the controlled entity had falsified the driving record; therefore, he requested the police for records from static cameras on the roads. Although these are supposed to be used against terrorists, possibly to search for stolen vehicles, the Supreme Court approved their use.
It is said that any material that was not obtained in violation of the law may be used for the investigation; this means, among other things, that data obtained by the state for some purpose can be used in practically any way. So it is essentially irrelevant for what purpose the state claims the security forces are collecting the data; they can use them against you at will.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Psychedelics
text:
The November lecture from the Anarchocapitalism series will be devoted to the topic of psychedelics and psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy, the current legislative status of these substances and the resulting paradoxes that this topic brings to light. The current position of psychedelics in society hits the barriers not only of the existing system, but also the need for a societal discussion and support of decades of mystified and stigmatized field. If we are able to shine a light into all the dark corners that the psychedelic theme and its unstoppable renaissance and the need for systemic change bring, we could also lay the foundations for fundamental changes in other areas of our lives.

– Eva Césarová; co-founder of ČEPS and the Sarava Foundation; the creative force of the PSYRES Foundation for Psychedelic Research; the media voice of scientists researching psychedelics at the National Institute of Mental Health

title: Studio of the Free Port: About freedom of speech (and LGBT) with Petr Hájek
text:
Petr Hájek is a journalist and former press spokesman for former president Václav Klaus; he became famous for his controversial views on a number of issues. In the Free Harbor Studio, we talked about freedom of speech and LGBT issues; I find the discussion stimulating.
In the first half, we mostly agreed with each other in the dialogue about the restriction of freedom of speech by the state; however, in the second half, our opinions differed and there was a confrontation regarding the freedom of speech of corporations, or possibly powerful people promoting LGBT.

– Petr Hájek; journalist; former press spokesman of former president Václav Klaus; editor-in-chief of the periodical Protiproud

title: Gabriela and Urza with a love of freedom and learning at the Liberec Sudbury school
text: As part of our series of talks with Gabriela, we spoke at the Liberec Sudbury School; the audience also responded to this – it had its own experience with self-directed education. So we dealt with various finer nuances rather than the basics; although popular concerns about technology have also occurred.

title: Freeport Studio: About intellectual property with Vojta Moravec
text:
Vojta Moravec is a libertarian who has been following the Free Port for a long time. Some time ago he wrote me his reservations about the legal implementation of intellectual property in accordance with the NAP; I found them so interesting that I decided to invite him to the Studio and record an interview with him.
In the first part of the debate, we mainly discussed branding, brand protection, logos and consumer deception, while in the second part we jumped into patents. At the end - as a bonus - we discussed ownership as such, especially the concept of homesteading.

– Vojta Moravec; libertarian; follower of Freeport

title: Gabriela and Urza with the love of freedom and learning in Rychnov nad Kněžnou (worse sound and children's activity)
text:
As part of our cycle of talks with Gabriela, we performed in Rychnov nad Kněžnou; from the beginning you asked very interesting questions about self-directed education. We discussed everything from technology and computer games to drugs and safety to preparing children for graduation or wasting food.
We apologize for the low-quality sound (we don't want to pass microphones between participants for greater flow of conversation) and the interference of children in the recording (we weren't prepared for that - hopefully we'll solve it better next time); thanks for your understanding.

title: Studio of the Free Port: #freepepo Alexander Rackovic
text:
Alexander Račkovič is the founder of the #freepepo initiative for ending the war on drugs and freeing cannabis prisoners in Slovakia, where the legislative situation is significantly worse than in the Czech Republic - for a few grams of weed, you can go to prison for twenty years unconditionally.
What I also found interesting in the debate was a certain ambivalence of the guests' attitudes, when on the one hand they clearly see the crimes of the state and for the sake of power, while on the other hand the state defends itself to a certain extent; nevertheless, I consider his activity to be very beneficial.

– Alexander Rackovic; founder of the #freepepo initiative; activist for the end of the war on drugs and the rights of cannabis prisoners

title: Urza versus Petr Hampl about the economy in the program Badatelé z sstatte
text:
František Feer Balej invited me for the third time to his show Badatelé z statte; this time also with the debate opponent, who was Petr Hampl. We debated the economy, the free market and central planning.

– Petr Hampl; ("right-wing") sociologist and socialist; white heterosexual male; anti-immigration activist

title: The principle of non-aggression in the Cherubín tea house
text:
One lecture at the Cherubín teahouse eventually became a whole series; I like to go back there because the place has the right tea tree and a great atmosphere (and a Buddha statue with the inscription: "When the god said: "Let there be light," the sound already existed.").
We discussed the principle of non-aggression, which the anarcho-capitalists favor so much, which is why, despite the high interactivity of the entire discussion, we managed not to get bogged down in questions such as whether this or that absurd thing is against the NAP; instead we got to psychological violence, which is real but not covered by the NAP, so we explained why it is.

title: Free Port Studio: Hedgehog without a cage with Gabriela Ježková
text:
Since September, I joined Hedgehog without a cage as a determinist; I see that place as an island of greater freedom in the otherwise unfree sea of education. And freedom is far from everything I go to Ježek for; there is also a lot of love in that place.
With Ježková, the founder, owner, director and my current boss, Gabriela, we start various projects - for example, discussions or a suburban camp - and we agree on the perception of anarcho-capitalism and free education; that's why I'm inviting her to the livestream again after a year.

– Gabriela Ježková; founder, owner and director of the Ježek bez klece free school in Brno; anarchist; libertarian; a teacher

title: Freeport Studio: About the Army and the Police with Charon
text:
Ondřej Charon Charvát contacted me as an ex-soldier, ex-policeman and ex-batcher saying that he would like to debate centralized versus decentralized army and police; because he himself holds the opinion that these components should be centralized.
From my point of view, it was a very interesting debate, because Charon, despite his background in the forces, is a minarchist; apart from the function of common defense, he therefore agrees with me on the uselessness and inefficiency of the state. In addition to the discussion on the topic, we also got to interesting things from life in the prison service.

– Ondřej Charvát; former soldier; ex-cop; former bachelor; a minarchist

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Bad Money Inflation
text: The October lecture from the Anarchocapitalism cycle will be devoted to the causes of current inflation; however, it will not be a detailed economic analysis, but rather general principles that inevitably lead to inflation. The media is less concerned with the causes of inflation rather than more; and when they do, they mostly stick to analyzing particulars, or even finding culprits, while completely ignoring the bigger picture, according to which the current situation is basically an inevitable consequence of the way our banking – and entire monetary – system is set up. This lecture aims to introduce the audience to the principles on which today's (fiat) money works, to show how it causes inflation, and to outline a better solution; however politically impenetrable for now.

title: Free Port Studio: About (free) education with Robert Čapek
text:
Robert "Lazy teacher" Čapek wrote a very critical text in response to the publication of my statuses about the admission process in Ježek bez klece in EDUzín magazine; and as both his followers and mine desired our conversation face to face, I decided to invite him to the Studio.
We discussed respect for pupils and students, dirty words on school grounds, the illusory versus real freedom of children in Ježek without a cage and many other interesting topics; and since our views differ significantly, this has resulted in an interesting debate - at least from my point of view.

– Robert Čapek; teacher; school psychologist; textbook author; author of the concept "Lazy Teacher"

title: Martin Tomša and Urza on politics (and) education
text:
Martin Tomša told me that he would like to conduct a dialogue on the record and tell something to the listeners; even though he is only fifteen, I appreciate his activity and desire to get into things. I enjoyed talking to him, so I will comply with his wishes and publish it; I hope you enjoy listening.

– Martin Tomša; minarchist; active student

title: Freeport Studio: About Anarcho-Capitalism with Tim Kožuchov
text:
Not even half a year ago, you could listen to my almost four-hour interview with the socialist Tim Kožuchov in the Studio; while today you can listen to my completely different almost four-hour interview with libertarian (and now possibly anarcho-capitalist) Tim Kozuchov.
We each brought two topics; we then devoted ourselves very thoroughly to them. For me it was socialism in banking and the ecology of Bitcoin; for Tim, argumentative capital and polycentric law.

– Timofey Kozhuchov; (newly) libertarian and (after the video maybe also) anarcho-capitalist; YouTuber; student of political science and philosophy; LGBT activist

title: 4D: Why the state and politicians always lose in the fight against corruption!
text:
Four reasons why states and politicians always lose in the fight against corruption!
Space for corruption arises wherever someone makes decisions about other people's money. And deciding on foreign money is the very essence of the state.
Unfortunately, every control authority that should fight and combat corruption is also corruptible in principle. There is no reason why he shouldn't be; nor a way to ensure it.
In principle, incorruptible are those who manage their own – not other people's – money and property; bribing them then means nothing more than making a deal with them.
The only truly effective way to fight corruption is to eliminate public budgets and leave the money in the hands of those who earned it.

title: Urza in the program Researchers from the essence: Value, history and connections
text: František Feer Balej invited me for the second time to his show Badatelé z statte; we addressed value in economics, moved on to history, and ended with a debate about the perception of connections between events around us. I didn't enjoy this interview as much as the last one, which unfortunately showed in places; hopefully the next one will be better.

title: Freeport Studio: Election 2022
text:
Although municipal and senate elections are perceived by citizens - and actually politicians - as less important, we decided to record a livestream about them; and not only that, we even run for Nevolte Urza.cz in them, however - at least for now - only in Prague, in order to find out the benefits and costs for deciding whether and how to participate in similar elections next time.
In addition to the debate about the election results, we can also talk about democracy in general; it depends on what you ask!

title: Studio of the Free Port: About the anarchic period with Standa Hruška
text:
A number of you wrote to me that Standa Hruška from StandaShow has his "anarcho period", which you wanted to hear more about; so I took on the role of moderator - which is normally reserved for Stand - and decided to interview him in a friendly way, which I enjoyed a lot.
We dealt with Stand's view of the state and its redundancy or necessity; we also got to why Standa doesn't call himself an anarchist, although he's certainly not a fan of the state and definitely believes in the free market more than central planners. Towards the end of the interview, we got to his show and his work as a presenter.

– Standa Hruška; youtuber; streamer; author of StandaShow; a native of Bruntál

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: The Rights of Children
text: For several years now, every September lecture from the Anarchocapitalism series has been about education or children. However, we have not yet covered children's rights in anarcho-capitalism, as there is (surprisingly) not much demand for this topic; however, the time has slowly matured, so we will talk about children in a stateless society. Does self-ownership apply to them? Who has the authority to make decisions for them on issues they do not (yet) understand? Who will - as weaker individuals - protect them? What if someone abuses children? Can something be done about it even without the state? Can a child enter into contracts? And what if she decides to leave her parents and go her own way? What will a society look like without banning child labor? If you are interested in the answers to these and other questions, come and listen to the lecture; and possibly ask about anything yourself.

title: Freeport studio: Over 400 km/h on the highway and subjective preference
text:
Radim Passer entered the Guinness Book of Records by driving over 400 km/h on a German autobahn in his Bugatti; in fact, he did it twice, with Bugatti congratulating him for it in 2015 and disavowing it in 2022. Why? What has changed?
How do people's reactions to this event relate to reactions to the anti-smoking law, drug and gun bans, or perhaps the obligation to handcuff yourself behind the wheel or not drink in canoes? I believe that they are all heavily influenced by the degree of understanding of others' subjective preferences; and I am convinced that if they were not, we would live in a better society.

title: About money at the Soběsta(te)čnosti festival
text:
With joy, I accepted another invitation to the annual festival of Soběsta(te)čnosti organized by the Sklenářky community; I really liked the whole event again, in addition, I added a sacred grove to interesting places for lectures - such as a church or a teepee.
Following the conference, the theme this year was money and its functions; unfortunately, this option proved to be quite unattractive to the local community, resulting in a record low number of participants. Nevertheless, I hope that the recording can enrich other people over the Internet.

title: Freeport Studio: Ankap versus the state from the perspective of the working class
text:
Kateřina Zettelová is an assembly worker who explicitly classifies herself as working class; yet her worldview better describes anarcho-capitalism than socialism. The state and politicians cannot stand; and not just the current ruling party. Why is that so? Of course, this is a minority phenomenon, but is it really surprising?
Lately I hear in the public space that the "modern left" no longer defends the interests of the worker, but of the urban intellectual; this interview helped me better understand why this is so. Not to mention a lot of other things related to state indoctrination.

– Kateřina Zettelová; assembly worker

title: Consultation of seminarian Vojtěch Velebný
text:
Vojtěch Velebný writes a seminar paper on various forms of anarchism; as part of that, he asked me for a consultation, which I gladly agreed to, as I want to support the creation of such works. In return, I asked for permission to record and publish our conversation, which he graciously agreed to. If any of you are a student who is writing a thesis on a libertarian or anarchist topic, would benefit from a consultation and would not mind appearing on the Freeport Channel, please do not hesitate to contact me; I'd love to chat with you.

– Vojtěch Velebný; author of a seminar paper on anarchism

title: Free port studio: About inflation with Jíťa
text:
Although I try to explain everything as simply and clearly as possible, it still happens that you respond that I speak too professionally or complicated; and I probably can't do it better myself. It turned out to be a good solution to invite someone who is interested in the issue, even if they don't know much about it, and talk to them.
Jíťa is a long-term volunteer working for the Free Port and was interested in the causes of the current double-digit inflation, as well as the outlook for the future; perhaps the conversation will be beneficial for other ignorant economics enthusiasts (probably it will not bring anything to the advanced).

– Jíťa; anarcho-capitalist; longtime volunteer of the Free Port

title: Democracy in the Cherubín Tea House
text:
One lecture at the Cherubín teahouse eventually became a whole series; we like to go back there because the place has a great atmosphere (and a Buddha statue with the inscription: "When the god said: "Let there be light," the sound already existed.").
This time we talked about democracy; today it is taken as a good - essentially by definition. However, we discussed not only how it is perceived by people, but also the practical consequences and effects of its operation on our society.

title: Studio Freeport: Free education with Michal Kandler
text:
As in every September, this year we will also focus on free education in the Studio and in the series of lectures; and the guest in the livestream will be Michal Kandler, the long-time administrator of the House of the Free Port (formerly the Svobodom), about whom we will also talk.
Michal and I have been working together for many years on projects whose goal is to increase individual freedom in education, research and promotion of self-directed education or unschooling and the separation of education from the state; so it will not only be about the House of the Free Port.

– Michal Kandler; administrator of the House of the Free Port (former Freedom House); member of the Freedom of Learning board; libertarian

title: Studio Freeport: About central banking with Mojmír Hample
text:
Mojmír Hampl accepted the invitation to the Freeport Stud after speaking at the Freeport Conference 2022: Money yesterday, today and tomorrow; our topic was, of course, central banking.
While Mojmír Hampl considers fractional banking and elastic money to be "the second best system, the first best not being known" and therefore an inevitable "necessary evil", I view contemporary banking as a means of robbing all holders of contemporary money; it laid a good foundation for an interesting debate.

– Mojmír Hampl; member of the National Budget Council; former member of the board of the CNB; economist; co-founder of INEV

title: Anarcho-capitalism: Being right is not enough!
text: Although I usually lecture on things I think I know something about, in June I would like to speak on a topic in which I myself have great reserves, which I have been trying to replenish for years; I want to focus on the ways and possibilities of communication about libertarian topics (and maybe not only about them). It is one thing to have the truth—of which we can never be certain—and quite another to convey it to others; being right is often not enough. I will talk about humility - which I myself have a lot to learn - and respect for the opinions of others - which is especially difficult for me if I find their thesis inconsistent. As time goes on, these topics have become more and more important to me; I'll be happy if you come pick them up with me.

title: Urza at Freeport House, July 2022
text: The first stay at the House of the Free Port certainly could not miss a discussion about ankap, freedom, free market and stateless society; as part of the questions, we discussed various interesting topics, including recreational atomic weapons. On our stays, you will also find a lot of interesting programs that are not recorded.

title: Urza at Free Haven's House, July 2022
text: There were families from foreign countries at the Summer Stay of the Free Haven's House; so I made my anarcho-capitalism talk in English. We were talking about freedom in general or about a transformation to the stateless society.

title: Urza with Dan Vávra on VoxTV
text:
I accepted the second invitation to VoxTV, where Dan Vávra wanted to discuss with me the same thing as Filip Turk last time; and I enjoyed it again. Thanks to VoxTV for allowing me to post the video on the Freeport Channel.

– Daniel Vávra; game developer; graphic designer; photographer; influencer; youtuber; conservative; former libertarian

title: Nations of Sanity: NAP and its implementation
text:
Matthew Sands invited me to a series of discussions for his project Nations of Sanity; in this third episode we were talking about the practical implementation of the non-aggression principle into our society.
It was quite a theoretical debate again; we both obviously like such kind of discussion! However, we were also talking about the history (and possible future) this time. I hope you will enjoy it despite my not so fluent English.

– Matthew Sands; volunteer; founder of Nations of Sanity project

title: Filip Versteeg and Urza on political ideologies, human rights and ankap
text:
Filip Versteeg asked me to debate political ideologies from a philosophical point of view. Although the first 45 minutes or so were a bit long from my point of view, an interesting discussion developed afterwards.

– Filip Versteeg (you can contact him on Facebook or Instagram); student of philosophy, sociology and political theories

title: 4D: Why is housing so expensive!
text:
Four reasons why housing is so expensive!
Construction is such an extremely over-regulated industry that only entities large enough to dedicate enough people to just deal with the red tape can operate in it. This limits competition and raises prices.
Due to state regulations, construction procedures are extremely long, which increases costs. It is not built when the owner needs it, but when officials and politicians allow it. The offer then hardly responds to the demand.
The state's monetary policy consists in the permanent devaluation of the currency. Because of the state, money thus lost the ability to store value in the long term; people then store this in real estate, among other things, which increases their prices.
In addition to Czech regulations, European ones also affect us; of these, especially green policy requirements (for example, energy labels and the like) increase the price of housing.

title: Urza on Tim's livestream about everything
text:
Tim invited me to the Debate Journal livestream (both D's are capitalized in this title); I was looking forward to it because I really enjoy debating with him, although many of my followers don't (sorry about that). This time we opened up other topics besides ankap.

– Timofey Kozhuchov; creator of the Debate Journal; "left libertarian"

title: Urza about the economy and economics with Daniel Holánek
text:
Daniel Holánek invited me to his show; we discussed economics and economics, business cycles (and their explanation from the point of view of the Austrian school of economics), inflation, cryptocurrencies, investments and many other topics. I enjoyed the conversation; so I hope you enjoy it too.

– Daniel Holánek; anarcho-capitalist; investor; YouTuber; financial advisor

title: Urza in the program Badatelé z statte: Náhled na svět
text: František Feer Balej invited me to his program Badatelé z statte; the interview with him was interesting for me, although unfortunately we missed some of the announced ankap topics, so it seems that we will continue next time. This time we tackled freedom, ankap, faith, science and compared "Western" and "Eastern" medicine.

title: 4D for the separation of healthcare from the state!
text:
Four reasons for the separation of healthcare from the state!
State socialist health care is killing people as a result of misallocation of resources; overworked, tired medical professionals or long waiting times for CT, MRI and other examinations can mean the difference between life and death.
Fees for true market health insurance would be based not on salary but on actual risks; people would thus be financially motivated to lead a healthy lifestyle.
During a pandemic, health insurance companies would be motivated to set up anti-epidemic measures for their policyholders as efficiently as possible, because every sick person costs them money; not like politicians who bear no material responsibility for their decisions.
The state prevents doctors and patients from having mutually voluntary relationships; some then get angry at others without realizing that the real problem is in the legislation and the setting of the entire system.

title: Urza on UTXO.22
text:
I gladly accepted the invitation to the UTXO.22 conference, which - as the name suggests - was devoted to cryptocurrencies; however, my lecture was not as technical as others; I decided to talk about the free money market and what we actually need it for.
I dealt with cyclical economic crises and explained how they arise; I also outlined a solution - what could be done to get rid of them once and for all. Although it is a feasible solution, unfortunately there is no political will for it yet.

title: 4D: Why the state poses a big risk to our privacy!
text:
Four reasons why the state poses a great risk to our privacy!
Personal data protection has finally become a societal issue; people began to rightly ask what data private companies collect about them and what they do with it. Unfortunately, the state is completely neglected in similar considerations.
At the same time, we do not even have to give our data to private companies; on the other hand, the state assigns us a birth number at birth and then collects sensitive data about us without consent, from health documentation to records of economic activities.
We have to report a lot of sensitive data to the state under the threat of sanctions. We can only minimally influence the way the state will deal with them - and who will be able to abuse them.
If there is a change of political regime, all state data will remain; therefore, we give them not only to the current government, but also to all future ones. The Jews in Nazi Germany also acknowledged their origin to a government other than the one that exterminated them en masse.

title: Anarcho-capitalism with Adriana: Healthcare
text:
The Slovak lawyer invited me as a regular guest to her program "A nice day with JUDr. Adriana Krajníková" on Slobodné váchteča.
In the third part, we talked about health care - we discussed free market health insurance and an alternative to the current central management.

– Adriana Krajníková (https://zalobyvocistatu.sk/); Slovak lawyer; author of the book Genocide of the Slovak Nation 2020; civil activist

title: 4D: Why not resign yourself to responsibility for your life!
text:
Four reasons not to resign from responsibility for your life!
Freedom and responsibility are two sides of the same coin; a free man bears the consequences of his decisions, from which he constantly learns.
A state that seeks to babysit its citizens absolves them of responsibility for their lives; those concerned then lose not only their freedom of choice, but also the opportunity to learn from mistakes and the ability to make fundamental decisions.
In a society where the state has created a lot of irresponsible people, there is a growing demand for more state intervention; as a result of these, even more irresponsible people are born, who call for even stricter regulations and so on and on.
If people get used to making decisions for themselves and facing various risks, sooner or later the state will end up in the hands of someone who will abuse it against them.

title: Free Harbor Studio: About Freedom and Cryptoanarchy with Honza Hubík
text:
To my great joy, Jan Hubík - one of the formerly very active libertarians in the Czech Republic - accepted the invitation to the Studio; thanks to him and his involvement in Paralelní Polis, among other things, my lecture series Anarchocapitalism was created, not to mention a lot of other activities.
We talked about what freedom means to us, we discussed democracy, capitalism and of course crypto-anarchy as a practical implementation of anarcho-capitalism in the real world; I really enjoyed the interview, so hopefully you will too.

– Jan Hubík; crypto-anarchist; anarcho-capitalist; volunteer; data scientist; physicist; former head of the Cryptoanarchy Institute

title: Urza with Filip Turk on VoxTV
text:
I gladly accepted the invitation to VoxTV, where in the end Filip Turek spoke with me instead of Daniel Vávra; and I enjoyed it a lot, probably even more than in the Studio. Thanks to VoxTV for allowing me to post the video on the Freeport Channel.

– Filip Turek; political commentator; Formula 3 racer; car collector

title: Free Harbor Studio: About the war in Ukraine with Jan Dobrovský
text:
Jan Dobrovský accepted my invitation to the Freeport Studio for the second time; and I'm really happy for that not only because I respect him as a person, but also because I find debates with him very pleasant and I enjoy them a lot, because he sees the world significantly differently than I do and at the same time I have the ability to explain his point of view logically.
We addressed the war in Ukraine and the individual versus collectivist view of general mobilization; we talked about propaganda in CT and other media and the influence of propaganda as such; and finally we discussed the blocking of "pro-Russian" websites by CZ.NIC in cooperation with the government.

– Jan Dobrovský; journalist; dissident; businessman; billionaire

title: Philosophy Spring 2022: Free Haven`s House
text:
What is the Free Haven's House – previously SvobodUm – about?
It is a center for self-directed and community education.
It is a community for families that commute or live here regularly.

title: Freeport Conference 2022 Panel Discussion: Money Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow
text:
We ended the Freeport 2022: Money yesterday, today and tomorrow conference with a panel discussion in which Palo Lupták, Mojmír Hampl, Urza and Pepa Tětek took part; Tereza Urzová took on the role of moderator.

title: Honza Pobořil: Workshop - Introduction to Bitcoin (KSP22: Money yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
Not all attendees of the "2022 Freeport Conference: Money Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow" need a lunch break; and Honza Pobořil prepared his workshop "Introduction to Bitcoin" just for you.

Honza Pobořil is a freelance developer, consultant and Bitcoin specialist; is a co-creator of the berubitcoin.cz project.

title: Marianna Sádecká and Palo Lupták: Money of Latin America (KSP22: Money yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
Sorry for the audio quality; we did our best, but we didn't record the two lectures as well as we wanted.
The conference "Free Port Conference 2022: Money yesterday, today and tomorrow" was closed by Marianna Sádecká and Palo Lupták with their lecture "Money of Latin America".

What useful items can be made from Venezuelan bolivars? Why never use cash in Uruguay? Conversely, why never use payment cards in Argentina? Is Bitcoin or Western Union better for sending money? What crypto wallets to use in El Salvador? What is a Panamanian Balboa? In which Latin American countries can you pay with euros?

Marianna Sádecká plays with life in several fields - in the economic field, where the most free paths are offered to her, and also in the artistic field with theater and music. She studied political economy and media, but always added an interest in new technologies. He considers cryptocurrencies and encryption tools to be a powerful tool for protecting human privacy. She took part in Demobite – a festival of computer art, founded Slovak Students for Liberty, considering it important to increase economic literacy. She likes to take a broad view of life and experiment - in music, food and travel. He loves Berlin, Belgrade, Brno, Bratislava and Latin America.

Pavol Luptak is a crypto-anarchist and volunteerist who is dedicated to technological and social hacking. He started his career as a computer hacker with many prestigious IT security certifications. In 2007, he founded the IT security company Nethemba focused on penetration tests and ethical hacking, a few years later he co-founded Hacktrophy. He is responsible for a number of projects in the field of public safety (eg hacking of the most used Mifare Classic cards, hacking of public SMS tickets for transport/parking, e-Kasa hack). As a hacker enthusiast, he co-founded the Progressbar hackerspace in Bratislava and Paralelní Polis in Prague and Bratislava. In addition to technology, Pavol also loves contemporary art. He became a member of the well-known Czech contemporary art group Ztohoven, which is responsible for many hacktivist projects of contemporary "media sculpture", and together with his friend founded the digital art company Satori. With the development of Parallel Polis, Pavol decided to achieve his vision - a complete opt-out from the system. Thanks to globality and flexibility, he decided to give up permanent residence, switched from bank accounts to cryptocurrencies, started using global healthcare and became a global citizen.

title: Mojmír Hampl: Elastic money (KSP22: Money yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
Sorry for the audio quality; we did our best, but we didn't record the two lectures as well as we wanted.
The fifth speaker of the "Free Harbor Conference 2022: Money yesterday, today and tomorrow" was Mojmír Hampl with his lecture "Elastic money - the essence of the current monetary system".

It is surprising that we all use the monetary system on a daily basis, but often even the most educated people have only a vague or even zero idea of its nature and functioning. In the lecture, we will focus on how the current elastic money system is different from fixed money systems and explain how and where money is created and destroyed.

Mojmír Hampl is a Czech economist, banker and columnist with degrees from the University of Economics in Prague and the University of Surrey in Great Britain. He devoted most of his professional life to date to the Czech National Bank (ČNB), where he joined as an analyst after defending his diploma thesis with the then Vice-Governor of the CNB, Pavel Kysilka.
After a four-year break, when he worked as an economist at Česká spořitelna and later as a member of the management of the Czech Consolidation Agency, he returned to the CNB in 2006 when he was appointed to its banking board. Between 2008 and 2018, he held the position of Deputy Governor of the CNB. Throughout his life, he repeatedly returns to the topic of money, currencies and central banks in his works. This is also why he is known for his very sharp views on the subject of the euro and also European integration. He has published more than three hundred popular and professional articles in various areas of his broad interest - from macroeconomics, through economic history to contributions on the topic of cryptocurrencies. He lectured in many places around the world, especially on monetary policy and central banking.

title: Pepa Tétek: Bitcoin - money that sets people free (KSP22: Money yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
The fourth speaker of the "Free Harbor Conference 2022: Money yesterday, today and tomorrow" was Pepa Tětek with her lecture "Bitcoin: money that liberates".

While in the West Bitcoin is often seen as a portfolio diversification, in poor countries it is rapidly becoming a tool of liberation. How do people from countries like Cuba, South Africa, or Lebanon feel about Bitcoin? And why do people without financial privilege often click on bitcoin right after the first introduction?

Josef Tětek is an economist with a long-term interest in the nature of money and bitcoin. He is the brand ambassador of the Trezor hardware wallet and the creator of the Stackuj.cz Podcast. Josef is the author of the books Enemies of the State, Friends of Freedom and Bitcoin: Separation of Money from the State. You can find him on Twitter as SatsJoseph.

title: Urza: The Internet of Ancient Times (KSP22: Money Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow)
text:
The third speaker of the "2022 Freeport Conference: Money Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow" was Urza with his lecture "The Internet of Ancient Times".

I sometimes refer to money in my lectures as the "Ancient Internet"; it is a wonderful means of communication between people, which in addition to information also conveys motivation. In my opinion, this is one of the most important inventions of mankind; it allows us to efficiently allocate resources and send important signals to people whose existence we have no idea, but with whom we can still cooperate and coordinate our wealth-creating efforts through a system of prices. This way of communication is going great until states start disrupting it when they want to "aid and protect" their citizens; most people - politicians included - do not know or understand this invaluable function of money, so they will not even see the consequences of its (partial) paralysis.

Urza is the author of the first Czech book on anarcho-capitalism and more than a thousand libertarian texts on the web and in print media. He not only reads, thinks and writes about freedom, ethics, education, the market, the economy and the role of the state in society for more than ten years, but also lectures (for example, as part of the series Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis and in (de)Central, but also in schools and at many conferences), makes videos and accepts invitations to various programs or panel discussions where he defends the freedom of the individual.
Together with his wife Teresa, he forms the Free Harbor; heads the Czech and Slovak Institute of Ludwig von Mises, which he founded together with other anarcho-capitalists; creates the Freeport Studio, the Freeport Sewers, the Freeport Channel and the Urza.cz website; belongs to the board of the Freedom of Learning association; he actively cooperates with libertarian movements promoting personal and economic freedom and writes articles for various websites dealing with the functioning of society.

title: L. Kovanda: BTC as a revolutionary stop in the evolution of fiat money (KSP22: Money yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
The second speaker of the "Free Harbor Conference 2022: Money yesterday, today and tomorrow" was Lukáš Kovanda with his lecture "Bitcoin as a revolutionary stop in the dangerous evolution of fiat money".

The history of money is somewhat the history of its gradual disconnection from real goods, and ultimately, unfortunately, from reality as well. The original ethos of Bitcoin was precisely to try to reverse the secession of money into a reality. Did it work?

Lukáš Kovanda, Ph.D., is a Czech economist and author of economic literature. He serves as the Chief Economist of Trinity Bank. He is a member of the Government's National Economic Council, which is now focusing mainly on the fight against the economic consequences of the spread of the COVID-19 disease. He is also active as a socio-economic analyst at the United Nations (UN). He analyzes and comments on macroeconomic topics, investments and new phenomena such as the shared economy, cryptocurrencies or fintech. It follows the development of the (geo)political and economic situation in the world and in the Czech Republic.
He lectures at the Faculty of Economics at the University of Economics in Prague. He is a member of the scientific board of the Czech Banking Association. He published two collections of interviews (not only) with Nobel Prize laureates for economics. He is the author of the behavioral-economic books Why air is free and virginity is expensive and Why women can't buy attractiveness, and men can, which were also published in Slovakia. Together with Evžen Korec, they published the book Buying an apartment under a magnifying glass or How to successfully choose, finance and buy an apartment.

title: Petr Bartoň: The golden system had no change, or the History of Money (KSP22: Money yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
The first speaker of the "Free Harbor Conference 2022: Money yesterday, today and tomorrow" was Petr Bartoň with his lecture "The golden system did not have change. It did not just boil over with kindness. It was especially hard on the poor: Freedom was cut down by a robot.".

Czechs and Czechs can be proud and proud. They gave the world the dollar (the last currency pegged to gold), the first competitive single European currency (both Rome and the EU imposed their own currencies), and the word robot. All the more we should keep in mind that serfdom and robots were the result of the lack of small change in the Middle Ages. All that glitters is not gold.

Petr Bartoň is the chief economist of the Natland investment group. He studied economics at the universities of Cambridge and Chicago and is a member of a number of international groups dealing with solving current economic issues.

title: Freeport Studio: Fainting Streamarathon!
text:

This time it will be different! I will be livestreaming entirely by myself, i.e. only on one camera, which means that there will be no need for non-stop directing. We will chat as long as someone communicates or until I pass out from exhaustion.
You can come up with any topic not only in the chat, but there will also be a much larger space for callers (if I somehow manage to get Skype working without overhead). How many hours do you think we will do?

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Foreign Policy
text: The May lecture will be about foreign policy in a potential anarcho-capitalist society. If there is no state in a certain territory, who will have the mandate to act "on its behalf" with possible neighboring states? Will it be possible to conclude something like international agreements? Before we start looking for an answer to these questions, it is crucial to realize how a stateless society can arise in a territory; we will, of course, deal with this at the lecture - and not only from the point of view of possibly foreign policy, but also because it is a topic that is interesting in itself. If you have any questions about the above, please come, as always you will be given the opportunity to discuss.

title: Freeport Studio: Scientific Consensus
text:
Science is often underestimated and ignored; other times fetishized and dogmatized. I don't think either approach is reasonable; both can do a lot of damage, especially if political interests start to interfere with science, which unfortunately happens to some extent in today's state-run society.
In this video I attempt to explain what scientific consensus is (and especially what it is not); unfortunately, it is often used by non-scientists precisely to dogmatize science. Many people believe that the scientific consensus gives us "basic certainty"; however, such a thing is far from the truth.

text:

However, something else occurred to me while watching the races - although we probably all understand how big the difference is between doing something out of fear and doing the same thing with enthusiasm, not everyone projects the consequences of this consideration into deciding whether to entrust something to the state or the market.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Questions and Answers

title: 4D: Why make recycling decisions on a free market basis!
text:
Four reasons why to make free market decisions about recycling!
It makes sense to recycle precisely when the resources needed for recycling are less scarce than the resources needed to obtain new raw materials and process old waste.
The rarity of goods on the free market is reflected in their prices. The variant that consumes less rare goods is thus also cheaper. Recycling is therefore more gentle in an undistorted free market precisely when it pays off economically.
Otherwise, recycling is nothing more than a waste of human or natural resources. Depending on the technology used, recycling may consume too much energy, etc.
Artificial state support for recycling leads to a distortion of the market, as a result of which it can be worthwhile to recycle even where it means waste instead of frugality.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Freedom (of Speech)
text: The February lecture from the Anarchocapitalism series will be devoted to freedom of expression; and not only her. In the debates about freedom of speech, especially recently, the differences in what different people imagine by the very term "freedom" have become apparent; while for some of us (mainly libertarians) it mainly means the absence of oppression and aggression, others (mainly socialists) imagine the possibilities they have in the world under this term. These views can be understood as "logical" and "emotional" perceptions of freedom; and although I see both feelings and logic as important tools for learning about the world, logic, unlike feelings, is consistent. However, even many anarcho-capitalists get carried away with their emotions in the free speech debate; because it's human.

title: Freeport Studio: Russia, Ukraine, ANCAP and foreign policy
text:
The situation on the Russian-Ukrainian border is not exactly rosy; Russia – like the Soviet Union before – likes to launch its invasions under the guise of military exercises. But is this the case? Hard to judge.
In connection with this, we also want to discuss the "foreign policy" of a potential anarcho-capitalist territory. How can an anarchist country conclude international agreements with neighboring states? And how can he negotiate?

title: 4D for Free International Trade!
text:
Four reasons for free international trade!
When goods cannot cross the border, soldiers will. It is not so easy for governments to make an enemy out of someone you know and who is beneficial to you. 
Division of labor means prosperity. Artificial efforts at national self-sufficiency create barriers to trade, thereby limiting the division of labor; both at the level of the individual and at the level of entire states.
While tariffs may help domestic producers, they harm all consumers as they artificially make goods more expensive. If tariffs were really beneficial, there would be no reason to levy them only between states; we could easily introduce them between cities as well.
Import quotas reduce supply, thus raising prices similar to tariffs. Competition is desirable in the market, and any restriction of it harms customers. This applies to competition from abroad just as much as to domestic competition.

title: Freeport Studio: I would write for communist and Nazi newspapers!
text:

I face ongoing criticism for both; and it would be easier for me to stop—among other things considering some of the Freeport supporters who support me.
In this video I try to explain why this makes sense to me; and why I believe that it also applies much more generally - namely, if everyone tried to conduct an (honest) dialogue, especially with those who are farthest from them in terms of people, ideas, opinions and morals, perhaps we could (as a whole society) move further - towards greater understanding and harmony.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism with Adriana: An Introduction
text:

title: Freeport Studio: Infinite Coronavirus
text:
It has been two years since the coronavirus was with us; nevertheless, it surprises governments and states again and again, so we can watch their parody of crisis management from the front row. Even if we see all that is wrong, there is little we can do about it, because we do not live in a free society, but in a society ruled by someone.
However, the state power's approach to the coronavirus is nothing new or unusual; the corona crisis only shows us a little faster - but very vividly - how the state works in practice in everything else as well.

title: Freeport Studio: Freedom, extremism and totalitarian regimes
text:
No opinion should be excluded from public debate; by excluding him, we will not get rid of the people who support him - they will always be here, only no one will talk to them, so no one will be able to convince them of anything. If no one talks to a racist, he will remain a racist.
At first glance, too much freedom of speech may seem to lead to totalitarianism; but totalitarian regimes are created precisely by suppressing freedom of speech. It is often argued that too much freedom of speech in the Weimar Republic resulted in the rise of the Nazis to power; but the opposite is true - the Weimar Republic suppressed free speech, and that's why, among other things, the Nazis came to power there.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: The New Deal
text:
The December lecture from the Anarcho-Capitalism cycle will be about the New Deal; not about the Green Deal, which the EU is trying to impose on us, but about the original New Deal, which the EU was unfortunately inspired by. President Franklin Delano Roosevelt came up with this in the early 1930s as a solution to the Great Depression; it was a state socialist solution to the problems caused by the states - consisting, of course, of prohibitions, mandates, interventionism and state spending (although Roosevelt won the election thanks to, among other things, his promise to cut government spending and calling his opponent the biggest spendthrift in history).

– Vlaďa Krupa; longtime author of the Ludwig von Mises Institute

title: Freeport Studio: It makes sense to have a dialogue!
text:
I have been saying for many years that dialogue makes sense; that we should debate with absolutely anyone, because no one should be excluded from public discussion regardless of how abhorrent or unacceptable their views are. Silencing someone doesn't make their opinion go away; and neither does the person in question.
I recently gained very valuable experience from a real long debate with people that most of society would prefer to completely exclude from public debate. Their views were quite shocking even to me; on the other hand, I was quite surprised by their willingness to change them - it was significantly greater than I expected. All in all, it was a very interesting few days, so I would like to share my knowledge with you.

title: Welcome to Freeport
text:
Welcome to the Freeport Channel!
The Free Port is an anarcho-capitalist institution founded by the Urz couple for the purpose of spreading libertarian ideas, raising general awareness of the principle of non-aggression, anarcho-capitalism, economics and a free market stateless society, education and public enlightenment.
We are open to debate with anyone; our goal is not to get everyone to agree, but above all to discuss and think. We don't want a revolution, we don't force anyone to do anything by force (even political). We explain to people that the less state, laws, regulations and collectivism, the healthier society; and although many do not want to give up the state, we are happy for anyone who is willing to reduce it even a little.
So try to give anarcho-capitalist ideas a chance; you can possibly reject them at any time.

title: 4D: Why Central Planning Doesn't Work!
text:
Four Reasons Why Central Planning Doesn't Work!
We live in a world of limited resources, where the fulfillment of one wish means that the wish of another cannot be fulfilled. And since no one knows the needs of others better than themselves, each central planner wastes public resources to implement less needed projects at the expense of more needed ones.
The information needed to produce anything is naturally decentralized in society due to the division of labor. The central planner has only limited and distorted access to them; therefore it is woefully inefficient.
In the free market, millions of entrepreneurs are simultaneously trying to do things as best they can by many different methods; the best will naturally take over and expand, the rest will disappear along with failing businesses. In central planning, there is no room for testing so many different approaches and solutions at the same time.
People working for themselves have incomparably more motivation to do good work than those in a socialist economy where "he who does not rob the state robs the family".

We also discuss the material versus spiritual essence of Christmas, as well as the material versus spiritual essence of (many) anarcho-capitalists; capitalism is often confused with consumerism, but they are not synonyms, which many people do not realize at all.

title: 4D for separating money from the state!
text:
Four reasons for separating money from the state!
Money is one of the most amazing inventions of mankind; prices are used to transmit information about the rarity of goods between sellers and buyers around the world. Any artificial intervention in this system distorts information and sends false signals to all market participants, causing a waste of resources.
Interventions by central banks in the economy cause business cycles. Before the existence of central banking, economic crises used to have specific causes - for example, natural disasters, lack of crops and the like; due to interventions by central banks in interest rates, crises occur even without external causes.
Artificial inflation causes injustice because it takes away the value of savings, which is shared between banks and people with access to cheap credit. It makes it impossible to save money effectively and forces even those who do not want to undertake the investment risk.
If the state has power over money, it can at any time decide to devalue everyone's savings for its own benefit; this is how governments typically finance, for example, arming for wars, paying off excessive debts or other large expenditures.

title: 4D: Why take care of yourself and not try to manage others!
text:
Four reasons to take care of yourself and not try to control others!
People are different. Everyone finds pleasure and benefit in something different; everyone is bothered by something different and is afraid of something else. There is no one person who knows what the "right" rules are for everyone.
State-wide solutions may help someone, but always at a price that everyone will pay in the end; they are therefore always implemented at someone's expense. Instead of cooperation, people then focus on the state setting the rules that suit them the most.
Even the people to whom the state provided services that cost it more money than what they paid to the state in question did not have to earn from it. They lost the opportunity to spend their money first and foremost on what they need most. The same applies to European subsidies to member states.
The only way to find out if a service is really worth it to someone is to leave them with their money and the freedom to choose whether to buy it with that money, or make a different decision.

title: 4D: Why the state helps the rich at the expense of the poor!
text:
Four reasons why the state helps the rich at the expense of the poor!
Big companies can influence politicians and thus legislation. State regulations then effectively eliminate competition from smaller companies that do not have the means to meet often unnecessary standards and legal norms. 
Even a law adopted in good faith without corruption will rather be prepared with regard to processes in large companies, which are known to politicians and officials. In addition, corporations have entire departments of lawyers, accountants, and other personnel who can deal with regulations; in a small company, everyone is dedicated to the business itself.
Labor market regulations – such as the minimum wage – harm the least qualified, who then become unemployable, as the value of their work may not exceed the state-enforced minimum cost of their employment. Such people go into the gray area and live on social benefits. 
All state requirements for the minimum quality of services or goods make it impossible to sell products that are low-quality but extremely cheap. This makes life easier for the rich who wouldn't buy them anyway; however, the state deprives the poor of the opportunity to satisfy their needs at least somehow.

text:

As a result of compulsory schooling, all parents must send their children to schools; even if they don't agree with state education.
Unschooling is illegal in the Czech Republic; however, fortunately, there are principals who have decided to allow students as much freedom as possible within their schools, even though this is a big problem with regard to the current legislation. One such director is Gabriela Ježková, whose Ježek school without a cage is an oasis of freedom in our education system.

– Gabriela Ježková; founder and director of the Ježek bez klece free school in Brno; libertarian; a teacher

title: Urza: Freedom to learn (KSP21: How to encourage children to love learning)
text:
The sixth speaker of the "Freeport Conference 2021: How to encourage children's love of learning..." with the subtitle "...because the love of learning is innate in everyone" was Urza with his lecture "Freedom of Learning".

Self-directed education (unschooling) is not legal in the Czech Republic; and there is a reason for it. Why does the state hold and refuse to let go of the monopoly on violence? I am convinced that it is related to his propaganda, which children are massively indoctrinated with in schools. What are the consequences?

Urza is an anarcho-capitalist author; wrote about a thousand libertarian texts on the web and in print media and the first Czech book on anarcho-capitalism. For more than ten years, he not only reads, thinks and writes about freedom, ethics, the free market, the economy and the role of the state in society, but also lectures, makes videos and is invited to various programs and panel discussions. Together with his wife Teresa, he forms the Free Harbor; he heads the Czech and Slovak Institute of Ludwig von Mises, of which he is a co-founder; belongs to the board of the Freedom of Learning association and actively cooperates with many libertarian initiatives. You can find more about him on the Urza.cz website.

title: Zuzana Candigliota: School – institution of unfreedom and obedience (KSP21: How to support children in the love of learning)
text:
The fifth speaker of the "2021 Freeport Conference: How to support children in the love of learning..." with the subtitle "...because the love of learning is innate in everyone" was Zuzana Candigliota with her lecture "School - an institution of unfreedom, obedience and conformity".

The unfortunate goal of education is degraded by the state to attendance at state institutions, which are characterized by lack of freedom, forcing obedience and conformity. The contribution will focus on specific examples and cases concerning the rights of children and parents in education, for example: Does a child lose the right to personal contact with a parent by entering school? Can the school ban children from using cell phones and making recordings? Where is the line between a teacher's strict approach and humiliating and bullying a child? How can children and parents defend themselves?

As a lawyer, even in her private life, Zuzana promotes the freedom and responsibility of each individual for himself and his family, less state interference in human lives and respect for the individuality of each individual. She also works in the Human Rights League as an independent lawyer. It focuses on the legal defense of individuals, especially children, parents and patients, against interventions by institutions and the state, currently especially against unreasonable measures in connection with covid. She founded the advisory Facebook group Rights of children and parents in contact with healthcare, education and the state.

title: Crow mother: Can children be raised to be free in the Czech Republic? (KSP21: How to encourage children to love learning)

Is it possible in the Czech Republic to raise children to real freedom so that they can manage their lives by themselves? Veronika decided to give it a try. Her three children do not go to school and she tries to give them maximum freedom in their education. Together, they spend five months of the year traveling abroad and learning by simply living.

I've always been the "weird one" in a lot of things. Unlike my 15-year-old self, I am no longer ashamed of it. I have more children than hands. Their names are Gréta, Marián and Janek. The children, not the hands. When the children sleep, I write the Ravenclaw Mother blog. And since all three are good sleepers after mom, I wrote 13 more books for adults and children at night. I love the forest, warm feet and my man Honza, who is waiting for me in heaven. I am terrified of residential tours, attempts to pigeonhole and immeasurable people with closed heads.

title: Gabriela Ježková: Meeting in Ježek without a cage (KSP21: How to support children in their love of learning)
text:
The third speaker of the "Freeport Conference 2021: How to support children in the love of learning..." with the subtitle "...because the love of learning is innate to everyone" was Gabriela Ježková with her lecture "Meeting in Ježkov without a cage".

In the talk about Ježek without a cage, you will learn how things work there, what the basic principles are, how they feel about their freedom, what they (don't) want, what they (can't) do, what they (don't) need. Sufficient space will be devoted to questions. Gabriela is looking forward to a joint discussion with you!

Gabriela was born in Brno, where she graduated from grammar school and then became a teacher for the second level, which she followed by studying special education. From a young age, she tutored younger children, visited families and was saddened by what they were going through in connection with education. During her studies, she started teaching at a primary school in Brno, where she experienced what it's like to stand in a classroom in front of people just a few years younger and try to instill in them what someone else thinks is necessary. Everything gradually fell into place for her, and after the birth of two children, she decided to found her own school. He talks about Hedgehog without a cage as a school as free as our current school legislation allows. She would like to see fundamental changes one day that will allow absolutely everyone to live a truly free life.

In addition, it promotes information in the field of children's and parents' rights in education (FB group Solving problems at school, complaints about teachers and schools) and has participated in the development of the SvobodaUčení.cz initiative since 2012. He is also collaborating on the filming of the feature-length documentary Free Children. She loves freedom, Pippi Longstocking, traveling and ice cream.

title: Jana Nováčková: Arguments for internally directed education (KSP21: How to support children in the love of learning)
text:
The first speaker of the "2021 Freeport Conference: How to support children in the love of learning..." with the subtitle "...because the love of learning is innate in everyone" was PhDr. Jana Nováčková, CSc. with his lecture "Psychological Arguments for Internally Directed Education".

Satisfying basic and developmental needs is a prerequisite for the healthy development of children. However, the method of satisfaction is very diverse and individualized, so externally managed education essentially has no chance of satisfying the needs of most children. On the contrary, education that is managed by the children themselves not only satisfies their needs, but also fulfills the requirement of meaningfulness, without which it is impossible to maintain internal motivation.

Jana Nováčková is a psychologist and columnist with years of experience in counseling and psychological research. She is the co-author of the concept Respect and be respected and the book and courses of the same name. Author of the publication Myths in education. Since 1994, he has been engaged in teaching and lecturing. Dozens of her articles or performances are available at www.respektovani.com in the Articles section. He belongs to the critics of contemporary education.
