title: 4D for the separation of education from the state!
text:
Four reasons for separating education from the state!
Education is monopolized by the state. He also decides on the conditions for the establishment and operation of private schools. Educating children in a way not approved by the Ministry is not legal even if it is the world's long-term successful learning methods. Parents with a different view on education are threatened with having their children taken away and imprisoned.
Like any monopoly, the state also provides expensive and low-quality services in education. Tabled teacher salaries discourage the able and attract the less able. The education provided by the state does not reflect the real needs of children - many important things are missing and a lot of unnecessary things remain. 
Even before reading, writing and arithmetic, a child learns to obey the authority assigned to him at school. It is difficult for him to start establishing equal relationships when he spends the entire educational process in a subordinate role. The logical consequence is a society full of conforming individuals always ready to submit to dictates and pressure from the outside.
Centralized education is used by states to indoctrinate young children. Each generation learns from a young age about the advantages of the regime it lives in and the disadvantages of other regimes. This effectively prevents critical thinking and constructive debate about the social order.

title: Studio of the Free Port: About freedom of speech with Libor Vondráček
text:
The chairman of Svobodné Libor Vondráček expressed interest in the debate in the Studio; and since he offered me one of my favorite topics - freedom of speech (on) social network(s) - I was happy to invite him. This issue is, in my opinion, very fundamental; a lot of people look at it from a purely utilitarian point of view, which I try to balance.
I agree with the guest that the current state of freedom on social media is very disappointing; on the other hand, I am convinced that the solution to the situation is not further regulation, but deregulation and the free market. I will be happy if you also write your opinions in the comments.

– Libor Vondráček; Chairman of the Free Citizens Party; conservative libertarian; lawyer

title: Studio of the Free Port: Free learning from the ICU
text:
Due to Urza's injury, it was not possible to broadcast the live stream with Gabriela Ježková; we will definitely move it to another time. Today was a makeshift livestream straight from the intensive care unit; in addition to Urz's injury, we discussed the future of the Free Port, but above all free education.
The overall quality was a bit lower due to the lack of reasonable recording equipment, but also Urza's reduced mental capacity; so it was more about just answering questions from the audience. I hope that it will still be a pleasant listen for you. Thank you all for being with us even in difficult times; we, on the other hand, will try to come back in full force as soon as possible (and even now we are not paralyzed; we keep going).

title: Studio of the Free Port: About social policy with Jana Maláčová
text:
The invitation to the Studio was accepted by the Minister of Labor and Social Affairs, Jana Maláčová. Although I fundamentally disagree with her politics as an anarcho-capitalist, I respect her personally for her principles and ideals from which she does not back down; this, in my opinion, sets her apart from most other politicians.
I invited her to the Studio, among other things, because I believe in peaceful dialogue; I think we should try to really listen and really understand people on the opposite side of the spectrum. Perhaps it was a step in the right direction; and maybe we will continue.

– Jana Maláčová; Minister of Labor and Social Affairs; idealist; vice-president of the ČSSD; a proud social democrat

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: The State Foundation School
text:
The first lecture in the new school year will traditionally be about education, i.e. the formal state-monopolized education system and its potential alternatives. For what reason must education be under the control of the state? Why can't we educate ourselves without the supervision of officials and the permission of the ministry? Couldn't education be mutually voluntary? Or must they be mandatory? And wouldn't compulsory education be better than compulsory schooling? How freely can we learn under the current legislation? What is still possible and what is already over the edge?
You can listen to and discuss all this not only with Urza, but also with Gabriela Ježková. This native of Brno has been dedicated to children and education basically her whole life; a few years ago, she founded the now legendary school Ježek bez klece - one of the freest elementary schools in the Czech Republic.

– Gabriela Ježková; the founder of the Hedgehog without a cage school; education expert; anarcho-capitalist

title: Freeport Studio: About the EU and the Green Deal with Hynk Fajmon
text:
Hynek Fajmon reached out through his assistant and expressed interest in an interview at the Freeport Studio; I was happy to invite him, because it is our mission to conduct a dialogue (including with politicians).
We discussed the functioning of the EU as a whole and its individual bodies; we analyzed the chances of an individual or a member state to change something in its course. Finally we got to the Green Deal and Fit for 55, which were passed quietly and with virtually no media attention; now member states must implement them. What about that?

– Hynek Fajmon; politician; founding member of ODS; former Member of Parliament; former MEP; former mayor of Lysá nad Labem; representative in Lysá nad Labem

title: A spiritual debate about freedom at the self-reliance festival
text:
I gladly accepted the invitation to the Soběsta(te)čnosti festival organized by the Sklenářky community; and I must say that I really liked it there.
This is a recording from the circle of elders, in which we discussed the inner and outer freedom of the individual as well as society and other "higher" entities. I warn viewers in advance that this is not a classic debate, as you are used to from the Freeport Channel - this one is much more spiritual and esoteric. So don't expect a battle of logical arguments; it was much more a matter of feeling, which was the declared goal from the very beginning. Personally, such a format has greatly enriched me, because I try to be more in touch with my emotions, which such a "circle" definitely helps. I will be happy if you write in the comments what you think about it, or if and how this video enriched you. Personally, I would probably look down on a similar conversation before; but I am glad for myself that it is no longer the case today. What do you think?

title: Freedom of learning at the festival of self-reliance
text:
I gladly accepted the invitation to the Soběsta(te)čnosti festival organized by the Sklenářky community; and I must say that I really liked it there. I also had the opportunity to give a lecture in a teepee for the first time, so I could reminisce about my scouting years!
The theme of this lecture was freedom of learning; we talked about alternative models of education, about unschooling, free and democratic schools. In a fairly intimate environment, we were also able to share our experiences from the school desks and the traumas we brought with us from there; the audience really pleased me with their openness, even though many of the stories were really sad.

title: Anarchy or Monopoly? Not only in education... - in Pilsen
text:
Another long-delayed lecture was finally realized in Pilsen in the premises of a (partially former) railway station; and I'm really enjoying being able to talk to people live again - I actually didn't realize how much I missed it; so on the one hand, I hope that you will enjoy the screens as much as I did, but most importantly that you will come to one of the next ones in person.
I talked about unschooling and other alternative educational models, which are unfortunately illegal in the Czech Republic, as the state holds a monopoly on education. And unfortunately not only in education, from which I subsequently moved on to other areas of our lives, in which the state also usurps a monopoly position.

title: Urza in the Napravo show
text:
Štepán Strnad (ODS) invited me to his podcast Napravo; I came with a good amount of curiosity, which turned into joy during the show that I did. We dealt with anarcho-capitalism, politics, political parties (including nevolte.urza.cz) and elections as such (in connection with which I have to admit that I have absolutely no idea who and if to vote; not that it wasn't desperate at other times, but now it's probably even worse). I really enjoyed the dialogue with Štěpán; so I hope that you will also have fun with him - and that you might learn something new.

– Štepán Strnad; creator of the Napravo podcast; member of the ODS

title: Freeport Studio: About Bitcoin with Radovan Vávra
text:
At your numerous requests, we invited Radovan Vávra to the Studio for the second time, because the first time the recording equipment failed in the middle of the interview; and I must say it was worth it. The guest in question is definitely quite interesting and I enjoyed the debate with him again.
This time we picked up where we left off last time; so we talked about Bitcoin. And we stayed with this theme more or less the whole time, although we made interesting detours to the state, capitalism, the environment or energy. Radovan Vávra is a pure practitioner, which is very rewarding for me – a theoretician.

– Radovan Vávra; capitalist; economist; banker; former head of Komerční banka; investor; good person (in own words)

title: Freeport Studio: Tornado and State Aid
text:
A tornado raged in Moravia, which no one expected; it caused considerable damage, destroying over a thousand houses, of which about a tenth was essentially completely destroyed. What about that? People all over the Czech Republic are naturally in solidarity and send a lot of money to the disabled; which is totally cool.
And how did the state react to the tornado? Of course, politicians have to flash, so they also send money; not of course, but money from other people's pockets. However, this is not the only problem. They come up with rather strange keys according to which they want to divide the finances among the disabled. I decided to make a video explaining what and why I think about it; I would be happy for comments where you tell me what you think in return.

title: Freeport Studio: About (crypto)anarchy with Pal Lupták
text:
My favorite Palo Lupták finally visited the Czech Republic and the Freeport Studio after the COVID postponement; and I enjoyed talking to him very much, because I always considered him and I still consider him a very capable, intelligent and, above all, free-spirited person.
We discussed his digital nomad lifestyle; and how such a thing is combined with anarchy. Understandably, we dealt with cryptocurrencies for a significant part of the debate. Pal's view of the state was quite noticeable from the whole conversation; that's why we ended the conversation with a topic close to both of us - namely anarchy.

– Palo Lupták; ethical hacker; digital nomad; crypto anarchist; volunteer; anarcho-capitalist; businessman

title: About freedom of speech in the Cherubín teahouse
text:
This time we talked about freedom of speech with several guests in the Cherubín teahouse. What is freedom of speech anyway? Can it be said that we have freedom of speech here? And if so, to what extent? Can "absolute freedom of speech" work? And what does that even mean?
We also got to the subject of free speech on social networks. Is it okay for Facebook, Twitter or YouTube to ban their users or delete their comments? Where does something like this lead? Can "bad" thoughts be eradicated from society?

title: Students for Liberty: Teresa on the coronavirus
text:
Liberty Webinars is a series of webinars by Students for Liberty CZ and Slovak Students For Liberty, which they organize at a time when face-to-face events are not possible.
Almost exactly a year ago, Tereza Urzová and I talked about the experiences of doctors in the fight against the first wave of the epidemic and the government measures that were supposed to help them in this effort, and they were not always successful. Moreover, even after a year since the end of the first wave of lockdowns, this effort is still ongoing.
Was the state better prepared to help doctors and hospitals during subsequent waves than at the beginning of the crisis? How do doctors see it after the first wave sprint turned into a longer distance run? And in a year's time, we will still have the Corona virus from inside the hospital vol. 3? Come and ask Tereza Urzová these and other questions.

title: 4D: Why save for (your entire) retirement!
text:
Four reasons to save for (your entire) retirement!
The continuous pension system is a plane - a pyramid scheme. Although the state forces us to contribute huge amounts of money to the system, what we get back from it is in the stars. The plane only works when new participants continue to enter the system and pay off the older ones.
Although politicians see that the pension system is collapsing, and even talk about it lately, they have no reason to do anything about it. They are elected for four years, so they have no reason to take unpopular measures to solve a problem, the consequences of which will be felt when they themselves are secured in political retirement.
The state is a lousy landlord; spends and gets more and more in debt. No one asks if they will go into debt anymore; we only deal with how much. A deficit in "mere" tens of billions is considered a success. Do you really believe that such an institution will take care of you in your old age better than you yourself?
We have no guarantees. When the money runs out, politicians will simply blame the incompetence of previous politicians. Pensions don't just have to be ridiculously small; the retirement limit can also be moved arbitrarily. Therefore, do not rely on the state and try to secure the entire pension yourself.

title: Freeport Studio: On Capitalism with Radovan Vávra
text:
Capitalist Radovan Vávra visited this part of the Free Port Studio. We talked about privatization in the nineties and its consequences. We also dealt with monetary policy, the Austrian theory of economic cycles and possible alternatives to the current unbridled increase in the money supply.
We ended up talking about Bitcoin, but unfortunately there was a technical glitch that caused us to lose half of the recording (and for perhaps the first time we forgot to turn on backup recording). However, the guest is willing to come again if interested, so write in the comments!

– Radovan Vávra; capitalist; economist; banker; former head of Komerční banka; investor; good person (in own words)

title: 4D: Why the state should not protect us!
text:
Four reasons why the state should not protect us!
Whenever the state protects us from any danger, it assumes part of the responsibility for our life. In that area, we have less freedom, which politicians take away from us through laws. The more "protected" we are, the less we make decisions about our lives.
The less we make decisions about our lives and the more the state protects us, the less we are able to take care of ourselves. Instead of ourselves, we rely on laws, politicians, government and government assistance. We are trying to solve a new problem with a new claim on the state. We are becoming dependent on the state.
The more people depend on the state, the more likely we will pass this dependence on to our children and future generations. Instead of self-confident and responsible individuals, society will be made up of people who are "entitled" to state aid.
If society is made up of people who "entitle" to state aid, it will cause a spiral of constant state growth. We will be "protected" even where we don't need or want it. Under the guise of protecting us, politicians will abuse their power and impose their ideas on how we should live.

title: Freeport Studio: Thank you (and not only) for your signatures
text:
A month and a half ago, we asked for a thousand signatures on a petition to found a political party "Urza.cz: We don't want your votes; you can't claim freedom. We will refuse every political function; we don't want to dictate to people how they should live. We have a different vision. We are going a different way - you can find it on the website www.urza.cz."; and today we have 1332!
Thank you! You are really amazing; it is only thanks to you that we can create to the extent that we create. You have never turned your back on us; every project of ours had your great support, which we greatly appreciate.

title: Freeport Studio: Market, State and Science
text:
Many people believe that without government subsidies there would be no progress, as no one would fund (especially basic) research; this assumption most likely stems from the fact that currently the state actually funds research - and unfortunately, people have a hard time imagining alternative ways of solving things.
But the incentives to fund (especially basic) research are currently reduced by the fact that states take everyone's money by force and actually allocate part of it to science. However, if that cash flow dried up, the incentives would change; and quite possibly the whole situation with them. Come talk to us about it!

title: Freeport Studio: About politics with Kovy
text:
Kovy came to the Freeport Studio; contrary to my expectations, he knew not only the ankap, but even the Freeport! The interview with him was extremely interesting and rewarding; he surprised me with his thoughtfulness, but above all with his humility. I hope you enjoy it too!
We discussed freedom, democracy, the political situation in the Czech Republic and in the world, freedom of speech on the Internet in connection with the cancel culture in the West, and the attempts of some governments to dictate to large technology companies what expressions they may and may not tolerate in their space; in the end, we also dealt with the European Union and its future.

– Karel Kovy Kovář; well-known Czech YouTuber; political commentator; writer; influencer; comedian

title: 4D: Why not forget the opportunity cost!
text:
Four reasons to remember opportunity cost!
We live in a world of limited resources. So anything we do carries with it what is called an opportunity cost—that is, whatever we gave up in favor of what we did. It cost us at least time, but often something extra.
If we go to the movies instead of the gym, we sacrifice the opportunity to improve our fitness for the opportunity to watch a movie. And in exactly the same way, even nobler goals - for example, protecting the environment - are always realized at the expense of something - for example, treating the sick.
Every law, every regulation, every regulation, every investment, simply any state intervention has a price – not only money paid in taxes, but also unproduced goods, unprovided services, unrealized projects, jobs that will not be created, our time and the possibility of choice.
Opportunity costs must always be taken into account, i.e. when evaluating any state agenda - new or existing. The benefit of people spending their own money according to their preferences cannot be replaced by any state agenda.

title: Urza in StandaShow (second time)
text:
The video with me was filmed by Standa at StandaShow (https://www.standashow.cz/) and is published here on the Free Port Channel with Standa's explicit consent (he sent me the video himself so that I could publish it here at an agreed time interval), for which I owe him my thanks.
Standa Hruška invited me for the second time to his StandaShow; except for the emerging political party "Urza.cz: We don't want your votes; you can't fight for freedom.
We will reject every political office; we don't want to tell people how to live. We have a different vision. We follow a different path - you can find it on the website www.urza.cz." we also dealt with a lot of other topics - and this time not only ankap.
We talked about my faith and my overall worldview; at least for me, it was a very pleasant and interesting conversation, which ended up lasting almost five hours. I hope that you will enjoy listening to it at least partly as much as I (and perhaps Standa) enjoy his work.

– Standa Hruška (www.standashow.cz); youtuber; streamer; gamer; moderator

title: 4D: Why we need market prices!
text:
Four Reasons Why We Need Market Prices!
Prices are a brilliant and irreplaceable tool to convey information. If something is in short supply, the price rises, which informs and motivates all market participants. The one who directs resources to the production of scarce goods or invents a substitute for them will earn. In the event of a surplus, the price falls again and resources are shifted elsewhere.
Prices also determine consumer behavior. Higher prices motivate consumers to save on scarce goods, or to replace them with something else - cheaper and therefore less rare. This saves not only human labor but also natural resources.
We influence the money in the market what we are really interested in. This leads to a better allocation of resources than when the state decides based on the will of the voters. Through elections, everyone tries to assert their abstract preferences at the expense of others, and thus projects are created that people would not spend their own money on.
In a truly free and free market undistorted by the state, those who can best satisfy the needs of the people who willingly pay for it will become the richest. Not those who are fine with politicians and officials making decisions about other people's money.

title: Free Port Studio: About healthcare in the USA with Vladimír Krupa
text:
My old libertarian colleague - Vladimír Krupa, accepted the invitation to the Free Port Studio on your long-requested topic. Vláďa is the author of many articles on the Mises.cz server; and in recent years has been closely following the political situation in the USA (not only in the healthcare sector).
Although he initially refused the invitation on this topic, after the broadcast of the episode with Roman Šmucler, he suggested his participation himself, which I accepted with pleasure. In contrast to the previous talk from doctoral practice, this time we looked at the whole matter through the eyes of an (Austrian) economist. I find both of these views very interesting!

– Vladimir Krupa; longtime contributor to Mises.cz; libertarian; constant monitor of the situation in the USA

title: 4D: Why subsidies are harmful!
text:
Four reasons why subsidies are harmful!
To subsidize projects that will not support themselves because we do not want to pay them voluntarily, the state or the EU must take money from us. Then we can't spend it on the things we really need. The tax for the survival of subsidized projects is that other projects disappear or do not arise at all.
The endowments are as effective as a blood transfusion from the left hand to the right, with some of the blood used for administration. The consequence is the withering of the organism - the economy. In the Czech Republic alone, there are tens of thousands of people who create no value because they deal with subsidies.
Subsidies cause corruption. A bribe is cheaper than convincing customers with quality and price. The number of companies that depend on subsidies and will do anything for the ruling elites is growing. Corruption can only be eradicated by abolishing public funds and leaving the money to the people.
Subsidies harm small and medium-sized enterprises because they do not have the necessary administrative capacity. In addition, the administration diverts subsidized companies from improving and making products cheaper - it is easier to get a subsidy than to increase efficiency.

title: Freeport Studio: A Year with Corona
text:
The corona crisis has been with us for more than a year; despite the dissatisfaction of some viewers, we decided not to devote all our attention to it, as we want to map the failure of the state in all sectors and areas, not only from the point of view of not being able to cope with the fight against the pandemic, as that is quite obvious anyway.
This time, however, we decided to record a livestream on this topic, as we certainly do not want to avoid it. We will be very happy if you write us your observations and impressions; and you will make us even more happy if you decide to call us in the Studio on Skype and create the show directly with us.

title: Freeport Studio: Keynesians, ABCT and Monetarism
text: Another in a series of economic videos discusses Keynesianism and monetarism; of course, as always from the point of view of the Austrian school of economics. Keynesianism was the economic mainstream in the middle half of the twentieth century; why it was so, what is its essence, why the Austrian economic school failed and how Keynesianism was "dethroned" by monetarism, you will learn in this video. You wrote about the given topics yourself in the comments; you can take an example from this and do it again, I'll be happy to make an economical next video on request. To seasoned Austrians, I apologize for certain simplifications.

title: 4D: Why Democracy Is Not As Good As They Tell You!
text:
Four Reasons Why Democracy Is Not As Good As They Tell You!
Even a democratic majority can be wrong. In addition, he decides on things that everyone can decide in his own way. We don't need a one-size-fits-all solution. You make the best decisions about your affairs and money yourself, because you know your needs better than others.
Under the communists, the leading role of the Communist Party was enshrined in the constitution, today we have compulsory democracy. However, democracy without questioning and without restrictions can easily become totalitarianism, i.e. a system affecting all areas of people's lives. There are more and more things that we would like differently than they are democratically decided.
Democracy breaks up society because it turns people into rivals. If we could live our own lives, we wouldn't have to mind people with different values. However, when they can impose their views on us through elections, they are dangerous for us. Instead of tolerance and cooperation, we compete for a share of the collected money; about what we can and can't do.
We are not prospering as we could because of democracy. For more and more people, using the neighbor's state for part of their earnings is more attractive than working as hard as they do.  Therefore, there are more and more "entitled" ones, while those who create values are decreasing.

title: Freeport Studio: About life and unschooling with Jaroslav Dušek
text:
The well-known Czech actor Jaroslav Dušek visited the Free Port Studio; and our conversation was quite atypical for the Studio. The central topic was education, but we also talked a lot about life as such and our view of it; finally we got to unschooling, which we believe is closely related to a happy life.
Our dialogue was very "ezo" and not as closely related to anarcho-capitalism as is usually the case; however, I personally enjoyed it a lot, because I like to get to know new perspectives on the world. Jarda is a very inspiring and inspiring personality for me. I hope that you too will take away material for thinking from the interview.

– Jaroslav Dušek; actor; thinker; builder; fan of unschooling

title: Freeport Studio: We don't want votes; we need signatures!
text:
If you would like to give us your signature, you can do so here:
https://nevolte.urza.cz/
We do not believe that freedom can be fought for; that's why we don't want your votes. However, we need your signature on the petition to establish a political party.
Why do we start a political party if we don't want to be elected and refuse any political office? Because we want to run for office and, as part of that, open a public debate. For us, the elections represent an opportunity to get our ideas to the people - on the one hand, a link to the Urza.cz page on the ballot paper in each mailbox, but also the opportunity to participate in some pre-election debates and explain in them why we do not want to join politics.
Since the state is forcing elections on us, on the basis of which rulers we do not want (none of them), we would like to use them non-violently to spread freedom.
At the same time, we pledge to refuse any political office that we might hope to win in an election (which is extremely unlikely anyway, since we are not vying for anyone's votes).

title: Freeport Studio: Independent Justice? Not for M. Kunce and others...
text:
How does the state treat small entrepreneurs? Total liquidation; which probably won't surprise any of the regular followers of this Channel. But what happens when such an entrepreneur uses the services of the largely monopolistic Czech Post, which flagrantly violates its own contracts, harms customers and refuses to resolve complaints?
You can go to court - formally independent; in practice, unfortunately, the state (or its company) is both a judge and a party to the same dispute. How can justice be sought in such an environment? Similar to quality service at Monopoly; so not at all.

– Martin Kunc; small business owner; toy seller; "customer" of the state "independent" judiciary and Czech Post

title: Freeport Studio: Logic of Argument
text:
Although I thought that a video about argumentation and logic in discussions does not belong on this Channel (or rather Studio), many viewers convinced me otherwise for so long that I agreed with them and filmed it. And my big thanks to them, because I actually enjoyed it a lot.
I hope it will be fun for you too; and that it will bring you something interesting. I didn't want to take the video as a list of argumentative fouls or similar things that the Internet is full of. I have tried to summarize what I consider important and what makes me a good debater in my opinion. It's more about setting yourself up (and your approach to knowing the world) than a technique to be good at arguing with others.

title: The Free Port Studio: About healthcare in the USA with Roman Šmucler
text:
For many months - or years - many of you have been clamoring for a video about American health care; So I tried hard to find a guest to talk about this topic, which was not easy...
... until finally Roman Šmucler accepted the invitation, whose medical family (or part of it) does business in the USA. During the interview, I learned a lot of new and interesting information, many of which surprised me. So how does healthcare work in the US? Will you die on the street if you can't pay for medical care? The answers to these and many other questions are waiting for you in the video!

– Roman Šmucler; president of the Czech Stomatological Chamber; critic of socialist healthcare; businessman; dentist

title: Studio Freeport: About the economy with Lukáš Kovanda
text:
A few years ago, Lukáš Kovanda invited me to his show as the author of the book Anarchocapitalism; this time I invited him to the Freeport Studio, which he accepted to my delight.
We had an extremely interesting conversation about economics as a science, its essence, popularization and (mis)understanding by the general public. We also got to the corona crisis by government regulation (and failure); we also discussed Bitcoin; and finally we (civilized) bit the age-old dispute "anarcho-capitalism versus minarchism".

– Lukáš Kovanda; one of the most famous Czech economists; writer; analyst; organizer of the Economic Olympiad; college teacher; journalist; popularizer of Bitcoin

title: Freeport Studio: Self-sufficiency
text:
Self-sufficiency has many aspects; and to some extent it is related to protectionism, which Frédéric Bastiat already wrote about more than one hundred and fifty years ago. Nowadays, it is again becoming a very topical topic, as Czech politicians (in considerable numbers) are trying to enforce laws on food self-sufficiency.
However, food self-sufficiency is not the only one; protection of jobs and competition from abroad is increasingly used in today's globalized world as an argument for self-sufficiency (or at least protection of the market) in many areas.

title: Freeport studio: About patriotism and the corona crisis with Daniel Landa
text:
Daniel Landa accepted the invitation to the Freeport Studio. We talked about the corona crisis and government measures, which is a big topic for him lately; for me, on the contrary, the big topic is patriotism, which Daniel Landa is able to talk about in a way that doesn't discourage me (in which he is probably the only one so far).
Although the conversation was more general, absolutely non-confrontational and we talked more about feelings than logical arguments, it was very pleasant for me and I am really glad for it; I hope you enjoy it at least partially as much as I did. I consider Daniel Landa to be a very inspiring person.

– Daniel Landa; patriot; the bard; singer; composer; fighter; competitor; man of spirit

title: Freeport Studio: Crypto Vs. fiat currencies and reality vs. the illusion of safety
text:
Does it make sense to store value in Bitcoin? How can we be sure that we will not lose our savings? Nowhere at all; we never have such certainty, because it simply does not exist. While cryptocurrencies are the money of the future, they serve as better stores of value than fiat currencies; however, no one can guarantee that it will not crash unexpectedly.
However, who can guarantee such a thing with fiat? Also no one; however, it is surprising how certain a number of people consider them to be. At the same time, the lifespan of an average fiat currency does not even exceed the productive life of an individual; it's just hard to save for retirement in them. So where does the unfounded confidence come from? Well, where there is a lack of data, there is room for state propaganda.

title: Freeport Studio: Census
text: Before long we will have another census here; everyone will be obliged to report (other sensitive) data and personal data to the state, otherwise they will be fined. Although more and more people now understand the need to protect their privacy and handle their data safely, this understanding is unfortunately limited to private companies, not the state. People very often exclude states from their (critical) thinking and caution and do not accept the risks associated with them; at the same time, we are in greater danger from the state than from private companies.

title: Urza and Libor Vondráček on free market healthcare
text:
The Party of Free Citizens, through its chairman Libor Vondráček, invited me to his program Svobodný Beran. We discussed free market healthcare; we devoted ourselves to the current corona crisis, the government's (in)ability to face it meaningfully, and discussed how entities in the free market without state regulations would deal with it.
Towards the end, we switched roles a bit when I asked Libor about the connection between Svobodny and the Tricolor, which is probably why I won't vote for them for the first time.

– Libor Vondráček; chairman of the Free Citizens Party

title: Freeport Studio: About the European Union with Martin Pánek
text:
The director of the Liberal Institute, Martin Pánek, finally accepted the invitation to the Freeport Studio. We talked about the EU and its internal mechanisms, as the person in question knows them very well, as he worked in the European Parliament for over five years.
You will learn how European legislation is created, how much (or little) MEPs can actually interfere with it, but also how many laws have not been passed by the European Parliament, which is quite a surprising finding. In addition, we also talked about the future of (the Czech Republic in) the EU (including Czexit); and in order not only to criticize, we also focused on the positive aspects of the EU.

– Martin Panek; director of the Liberal Institute; libertarian; economist; former MEP assistant

title: Studio of the Free Port: About society and the state with Jiří Pokorný
text:
Anthropology student Jiří Pokorný criticizes anarcho-capitalism on his YouTube channel; and showed interest in debating with me in the Studio, to which I nodded mainly because one of our most generous supporters, Vojtěch Venclík, wanted it.
A guest asked me to post this bibliography:
Structural obstacles, central power: Lewellen – Political anthropology
Actorship of homeless people in public space: Vašát – Between resistance and adaptation: Everyday practice of the class of the poorest  
The concept of habitus: Yours - Basic concepts of Pierre Bourdieu
Industrial revolution from the perspective of power inequalities: Wolf – People without history
Roma: Šotola – Ethnography of social mobility: Ethnicity, barriers, dominance 
The Limits of Relativism: Fay - Contemporary Philosophy of the Social Sciences 
Discourse and Normative Power: Foucault – The Archeology of Knowledge

– Jiří Pokorný; student of anthropology; critic of anarcho-capitalism

title: Freeport Studio: Solving the Corona Crisis
text: It is clear to everyone that the government has completely failed and continues to fail in dealing with the corona crisis. In the video I try to answer the question why this is so; and I also explain why it basically couldn't have turned out any other way. In addition, I deal with the solution of setting up crisis measures, which could be (at least to some extent) functional in today's state-monopolized world.

title: Freeport Studio: Censorship
text:
We have been dealing with the topic of freedom of speech and censorship on social networks quite often lately; not only for Trump's banned account on Twitter and the ever-shrinking space of what opinions can and cannot be expressed on social networks (not to mention the vague rules), but above all for the foolish efforts of some "right-wingers" to solve the situation at the heart of state regulation, which unfortunately is, as always, a road to hell.
In the stream, we also want to address freedom of speech in general from the perspective of anarcho-capitalism and property rights; its correct understanding is slightly counterintuitive for many people. We would love for you to participate as well; you can call us on Skype or write to us.

title: Freeport Studio: Facebook versus Australia with Karolína K.
text:
I invited Karolína K., who is (literally) locked up in Australia, where she can't get out (you'll learn why in the video), so we filmed a virtual Studio for the first time; however, I tried to get as close to a live debate as possible xD
Our topic was (primarily) Facebook's decision to exclude Australian news sites from its content after the Australian government ordered it to pay those sites to share their articles; but as is usual with Karolína, we also touched on a lot of other topics.

– Karolína Kváš (https://karolinakvas.cz/); tarot rebel; authoress; traveler; anthropologist; blogger; creator

title: Freeport Studio: About (crypto) money with Josef Tětek
text:
Josef Tětek, my old colleague from the Ludwig von Mises Institute, accepted the invitation to the Freeport Studio. Pepa has been dedicated to economics for years, and in recent years to cryptocurrencies and decentralization; he is the author of two books and many texts, and he contributed significantly to the spread of the ideas of Austrian economics and libertarianism in the Czech Republic.
In the interview, we discussed the economy in general, especially money, its function and history; we gradually got to crypto-currencies (crypto-money), especially Bitcoin.

– Josef Tětek (stackuj.cz); co-founder of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Liberal Institute; author of Enemies of the State and Bitcoin: Separating Money from the State; analyst at TopMonks

title: Free Port Studio: About the Zeitgeist and the market with Ján Greguš
text:
A year and a half ago we made a video about The Venus Project; over time, we faced repeated (and apparently justified) criticism that we talked about the project without inviting any of its supporters to the Studio (at that time we were still shooting in two without guests). So I wrote to the Czech Zeitgeist Movement to see if they would be interested in participating in the debate; after some time they sent their representative.
We discussed the resource-based economy, which, according to the Zeitgeist Movement, should replace capitalism and the market allocation of resources through prices. Is such a thing even feasible? And if so, how? What do we need for this?

– Ján Greguš; member of the Zeitgeist Movement; ecological farmer

title: Students for Liberty: Urza and Martin Pánek on freedom of speech (not only n) and social networks
text:
Liberty Webinars is a series of webinars by Students for Liberty CZ and Slovak Students For Liberty, which they organize at a time when face-to-face events are not possible. This time, Martin Pánek and Urza debated on the topic of freedom of expression and social networks. 
The topic of the panel is freedom of speech in the context of recent events involving the suspension of a considerable number of often significantly politically exposed accounts on various social networks, and the so-called deplatforming of some public officials, such as former US President Donald Trump.

Is it an interference with freedom of speech, as many of those banned have claimed? Are social networks and platforms for the sharing of ideological content more than just a private enterprise, and therefore need to be legislated as part of the public power to limit how they regulate their content? What is freedom of speech anyway, and what are its limits?
To support Students for Liberty, you can do so here:

LTC address: LiHRyTsJaJH7GKTMVGZxAXGb3aFxWE6JHu
PayPal: sponsor@studentsforlibertycz.cz

– Martin Panek; director of the Liberal Institute; libertarian; economist

title: Free Port Studio: Dalibor Žák - Who would build roads?
text:
Independent motoring journalist Dalibor Žák was inspired by my interview with D-FENS; he wrote to me and expressed interest in debating the fundamental question of life, the universe and everything in general at the Freeport Studio: "Who would build roads?" Alternatively, more radical: "Who would salt the roads?"
In addition to the question itself, we focused on the meaningfulness of state traffic regulations and the creation of potential road rules in a stateless society where there would be no central authority. We also got to the general state traffic buzz, cycling, car traffic competitions and many other interesting topics.

– Dalibor Žák (www.garaz.cz); independent motoring journalist

title: Freeport Studio: Anonymous on internal and external security
text:
Another guest spoke about the invitation to the Freeport Studio, who wished to speak anonymously with regard to his work with the Czech Republic's armed forces; we discussed internal and external security in a stateless anarchist decentralized society. I think we've touched on some fairly crucial points during the debate, which I hope could broaden the horizons of some viewers and listeners; I hope that you will listen to the debate and that you will like it despite the repeated digressions from the topic, which could seem somewhat fragmented. I consider the lectures from Polis on Weapons, Law Enforcement and the Army to be a prerequisite for a full understanding of this interview.

– an anonymous ex-cop and soldier

title: Free Harbor Studio: About pedophilia with a pedophile
text:
Pedophiles are probably one of the most stigmatized groups in our society; there are a lot of myths and untruths about them - people often confuse pedophiles with sexual predators. In reality, however, they make up only a fraction of sexual assaulters with child victims. So who typically actually molests children? People's anger towards these attackers is completely understandable, but most likely directed in a completely wrong direction.
Wondering why this video belongs on the Freeport Channel? Among other things, because the motto of Ludwig von Mises was: "Tu ne cede malis sed contra audentior ito," which translates to: "Do not retreat from evil, but fight against it even more courageously."

– pedophile Matouš; supporter of the Czechoslovak pedophile community ČEPEK

title: Freeport Studio: Ownership
text:
Property is an absolutely key and fundamental concept for anarcho-capitalism; and not only for anarcho-capitalism, it is one of the absolutely key pillars of any civilized society. Although perhaps the whole of human history is littered with many attempts to organize a society without private property, none of them has ever been successful; we have come to a maximum of various restrictions on the property rights of individuals, which has always logically inevitably been reflected in their personal freedom.
During the livestream, we will try to explain clearly why ownership is important not only for anarcho-capitalism, but also for humanity as a whole. We will also answer your questions, we would like to make this stream more interactive than usual; as always, you can write and call us - and this time we will try to give you more space.

title: Free Harbor Studio: On Freedom and Censorship with František Fuka
text:
František Fuka came to the Free Port Studio at the instigation of many viewers. We discussed freedom of speech, censorship, social networks and their policy of deleting posts and blocking users. We also got a petition for uncensored Facebook and Twitter.
What struck me about František was that, although he was completely ignorant of anarcho-capitalism and only marginally familiar with libertarianism, we agreed on practically everything; also because Mr. Fuka is a supporter of decentralization, I think he could give ankap a chance - at least he got the book from me, he wants to read it and he says he'll let me know, so I'm quite tense.

– František Fuka; publicist; music composer; programmer; film reviewer; translator

title: The reporter invited Urza to the podcast
text:
If you buy the January Reporter, you will find the essay "Democracy can be a totalitarianism"; I consider this text to be perhaps the best of those I have written for a wider public.
I am honored that Reporter approached me to contribute to the cycle "What is the biggest problem of our time" - starting in September, they are giving space in each issue to a personality to write an essay on this topic.
The December Reporter published an article by constitutional judge Kateřina Šimáčková, who called for a strong welfare state; so the editors were looking for someone who would create a counterweight to it, which became my January text.
And now I was invited to record a podcast in which we discussed anarcho-capitalism as such, especially its most complex topics such as polycentric law or security, but not only that.
Finally, I would like to add that the serious reputation that Reportér magazine has is truly more than deserved. I have hardly seen such a correct and professional approach from journalists. Tomáš Poláček and the entire editorial team have my great respect.

title: Studio of the Free Port: On a dialogue with Jan Dobrovský
text:
Jan Dobrovský accepted the invitation to the Freeport Studio; we dealt with dialogue in society, the media, social networks and, in general, the human ability and inability to argue, distinguish feelings from facts, belief from reality, or arguments from shouts on social networks. We addressed the influence of the Internet on society, we talked about the advantages and weaknesses of democracy, about the state and its necessity or necessity. I really enjoyed the interview, Mr. Dobrovský was a great opponent, because in my opinion he is very educated, smart, quick and prompt; I hope you enjoy listening to the video as much as I enjoyed making it.

– Jan Dobrovský; journalist; dissident; businessman; billionaire

title: About democracy with Karolína K.
text:
Karolína Kváš invited me for the second time to her program with the great name - Chatting without education; and she made me very happy! Our theme this time also fits perfectly into the Freeport Channel; we were talking about democracy, its deification and uncritical acceptance by the majority society (including the two of us in the past and a little now). The interview was extremely rewarding for me; so I firmly hope that it will enrich you too.

– Karolína Kváš (http://karolinadobrovska.cz/); tarot rebel; authoress; traveler; anthropologist; blogger; coach
  Book: https://bit.ly/KupKamineky
  Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/karolinakvas
  Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/karolina_kvas/

title: Studio Freeport: "SHARE BEFORE THEY DELETE IT" or Social Networks and Censorship
text:
Twitter deleted Donald Trump's account, Facebook deleted Bratříček's account (including Ron Paul's), and Daniel Vávra will probably go before the Free Port; however, this is certainly not the way to silence those people; and even if it were, it wouldn't bring anything good, because censored opinions don't just disappear from society, which only polarizes itself even more.
What about that? The first idea of many is to petition for legislation to ban these practices; and I'm afraid this solution is the road to hell. Not only is this a (not very obvious at first glance) restriction of freedom of expression; moreover, it will ultimately give the tech giants far more power and hurt their potential competition.

title: Freeport Studio: Coronatotality
text: The coronavirus is a huge topic that shakes the whole society; and government regulations are being labeled as totalitarian by more and more people, even the Freeport is criticized from time to time for not paying enough attention to them. However, in this short video, I ask myself how different these measures are compared to the whole package of state legislation that politicians have been suffocating us with for a long time; and I'm afraid they're not that different from him.

title: The Studio of the Free Port: About state capture and ecology with Michaela Pixová
text:
Michaela Pixová, coordinator of the Climate Coalition, accepted the invitation to the Studio. We discussed many different topics: home births, different perspectives on them, health insurance and state funding of midwives; capture of the state by corporations, ideologies or political parties; the ecological threats of our future and their potential solutions; we also dealt with democracy as such, its limits, potential improvements and problems. I consider the debate to be very interesting considering the difference in thinking of both debaters.

– Michaela Pixová; coordinator of the Climate Coalition; critical social geographer; activist; columnist; college teacher; translator

title: Studio of the Free Port: About psychedelics and CZEPS with Eva Césarová
text:
Psychoactive substances are still quite taboo in our society; over time, their public perception is improving as awareness of them spreads, but it is still very slow. Eva Césarová, co-founder of the Czech Psychedelic Society, accepted the invitation to the Freeport Studio in connection with drugs. This time, the interview with her was not conducted by Urza, but by Tereza, who is close to the issue and knows the person in question. They discussed the activities of CZEPS and the National Institute of Mental Health; they were devoted to the tabooing of drugs and their possible decriminalization or legalization. They also researched the use of psychedelics in psychiatric medicine. Drugs other than psychedelics were also discussed; and also on the general awareness of the population - not only lay people, but also doctors.

– Eva Césarová; co-founder of CZEPS; media representative of psychedelic research at NÚDZ; part of PSYRES creative team; Addictology student

title: Freeport Studio: Christmas and year-round thanks; and people are not stupid!
text:
This video is a thank you to all our supporters and people who create with us or help us with creation in various ways. At the same time, we ask everyone who perhaps only partially agrees with us or our work makes sense to them for any reason to join and also support it.
However, because we didn't want to make a thank-you video, we decided to add one topic that is more loosely related to anarcho-capitalism, but which we think is essential - a lot of people think that most others are jerks; while we believe that this may not be quite true; and we'll explain why!

title: Freeport Studio: What is Anarcho-Capitalism?
text: What exactly is anarcho-capitalism? The longer I try to present it to individuals and to an increasingly wider public, the more I recognize that it is not very difficult to describe it in a few hours; the more interesting challenge is to summarize the main idea in half an hour, which I just tried. For seasoned libertarians, it will not be anything new in terms of information, although I believe that even you can take something away from the way of presentation; for others, it is one of the theoretical videos, the purpose of which is to put the individual topics that we discuss with interesting guests into some kind of coherent framework. Why am I actually an anarcho-capitalist? What does this mean for me? What way of thinking leads to this?

title: On benefit and redistribution from the point of view of evolution with Jiří Sáblík
text:
A lot of you ask me all kinds of questions by email, which unfortunately I don't have time to answer anymore, so I choose the more interesting ones; and if I find one particularly interesting, I will offer the writer an online debate so that others can benefit from that question.
Jiří Sáblík responded to the debate with Petr Firefanatic Hála, tried to contradict the interpersonal incomparability of utility and defend redistribution with reference to some evolutionary imperatives that we have in ourselves as human beings. Since I really like evolutionary arguments, I decided to discuss them with the person in question. I wish you a pleasant listening.

– Jiří Sáblík; follower of Freeport

title: Freeport Studio: Traffic Police FAQ (D-FENS)
text:
I've been reading D-FENS's weblog since I was fifteen; it was one of the first places I published, where I learned to write, debate, and think critically. I owe a lot to D-FENS; and I have great respect for his work. Countless times he stood against the will of the state for those who could not help themselves.
Due to the great success of the previous video, we decided to make a second one where we answer questions from listeners and viewers; at the same time, this D-FENS is the first guest we have invited to the Studio twice. We'd love for you to pass this FAQ around!

title: About marginal utility with Petr Hála
text:
One of the regular listeners – Petr Firefanatic Hála – disagreed with my concept of marginal utility theory on one of the streams; he did what I hope others of you will follow: He debated me on the record on the subject; and it gave rise to an interesting debate about the economy, which can hopefully bring something to others as well. We discussed the value of one thousand crowns for billionaires and for the homeless. Can we increase "aggregate utility" by giving a billionaire's thousand to a homeless person? I will be happy for your comments and opinions in the comments; and if you are interested in discussing any topic with me in this way, please contact me, I am certainly open to it.

– Petr Firefanatic Hall; anarcho-capitalist; supporter of the Free Port; math physicist; programmer

title: Freeport Studio: Healthcare
text:
Although many people already understand why socialism and central planning in general do not work, there is a belief in society that certain industries must be centrally planned by the state because "it cannot be done otherwise"; and healthcare is unfortunately one of them. People are afraid that under capitalist health care, "the poor would die in the streets", which they are trying to fix with socialist health care; in that, unfortunately, people die as a result of misallocation of resources, but it's not seen as much because no one says to anyone, "We're not providing care." But it happens in practice, or the care provided is completely inadequate; as a result, of course, a lot of people die, although it is impossible to measure exactly how many there are, but sometimes specific cases can be pointed to.
As a doctor, Tereza has first-hand access to that system; in this livestream you can ask her anything you can think of on the topic. You can also call our Studio via Skype!

title: Studio Freeport: Drugs, freedom, Řeporyje and Pavel Novotný
text:
The controversial Pavel Novotný visited the Studio of the Free Port; however, we had a surprisingly matter-of-fact conversation, in which there was not so much talking off-topic and off-topic. We covered freedom of speech on and off social media; we dealt with drugs, their use, regulation and prohibition; the talk also came to the city district of Prague-Řeporyje and many other topics. Pavel Novotný is definitely his own, he expresses himself violently and vulgarly, but he was far more open to libertarian ideas than I expected; although of course he properly criticized these as well.

– Pavel Novotný; mayor of the Prague-Řeporyje district; member of the ODS; controversial politician; journalist; professional poker player

title: Platform for a minimal state: Jiří Štecura debates with Urza
text:
Jiří Štecura - a representative of the Platform for the Minimum State - invited me to a debate on basic income and other interesting things; I was very happy to accept. The format ended up being more like an interview than an unmoderated debate, so I was given plenty of room to express myself rather than face off against an opponent, which surprised me; I expected a rather different course, but on the other hand, I think I managed to describe my position on basic income quite comprehensively.

– Jiří Štecura; representative of the Platform for a Minimum State

title: Studio of the Free Port: About the State with Vlastimil Tlusty
text:
The interview with the politician and former finance minister Vlastimil Tlustý took place in a surprisingly friendly spirit; most of the time we discussed the functioning of the state, its expansiveness and parasitism on its own citizens. We also touched on the concept of personal freedom, the stability of covered and uncovered currencies, cryptocurrencies and the anarcho-capitalist world view. Strangely enough, as an anarchist and a politician, we agreed rather than diverged; the only major clash of opinion occurred on the topic of unconditional basic income.

– Vlastimil Tlustý; politician; former Minister of Finance of the Czech Republic; former Member of Parliament; a former member of the ODS and its subsequent sharp critic

title: Studio of the Free Port: About the State from Anarchy with Prokop Hapala
text:
One fine day, physicist Prokop Hapala wrote me a long email criticizing anarcho-capitalism; and since I don't have time to respond to such private messages, because I get just too many of them, I invite the authors of the more interesting ones to a personal debate on camera, which they usually refuse. However, Prokop accepted Hapala; what do you think about such a format? I certainly enjoyed the discussion, what are your opinions, dear viewers? Would you like more such clashes of opinion? I will be glad if you write your opinion in the comments; and of course not only to this format, but also to the debate itself.

– Prokop Hapala; statist; critic of anarcho-capitalism

title: Freeport Studio: Socialism Failed; and the coronavirus won't solve it
text: The corona crisis is ongoing; and we can see many of its manifestations - lack of personnel, lack of protective equipment, lack of capacity... Which of the things we know have manifested themselves in exactly this way in the past? Practically anything in socialist/communist central planning; and therefore I cannot, with the best of my will, attribute the exact same manifestations of problems in our socialist healthcare system to coincidence. The free market is simply efficient in allocating resources; central planning is not. Everything that the theories of the Austrian school of economics tell us is confirmed by the practice of our lives; will we finally start listening to the Austrian economists, or will we close our eyes to them like previous generations?

title: Academic Association of Political Science Students in Pilsen: Anarchocapitalism
text:
The Academic Association of Political Science Students in Pilsen from ZČU organized a discussion on anarcho-capitalism. The format of the debate was rather unusual: Anarcho-capitalism was presented by Urza, whose opponent was PhDr. Ondřej Stulík Ph.D., who, however, did not take the opposite position in the discussion, but acted as an independent commentator and questioner; he supplemented Urza's theses with views from other parts of the political and social science spectrum. As a result, the debate was calm, cultured and in-depth.

– PhDr. Ondřej Stulík Ph.D.; political scientist (specializing in the history of political theories and the relationship between political theories and ideologies from the perspective of sociological hermeneutics); teacher at the Department of Political Science and International Relations at the Faculty of Arts of ZCU

title: About the transition to anarchy, NAP and faith with Jan Kučera
text:
For his birthday, friends bought Jan Kučer - a long-time follower of Free Port - an interview with Urza so that he could answer his questions. Because we found their dialogue interesting, we decided to publish it (with the person's consent) so that other listeners could benefit from it.
In addition to the debate about the transition from the state to anarchy, the principle of non-aggression (and its validity for animals and children), the topic was also Urza's faith in God, so the last part is a conversation of a slightly more personal nature.

– Jan Kučera; follower of Freeport

title: Freeport Studio: About Cryptocurrencies with Slush
text:
Few people know that the Czech Republic is one of the "cryptocurrency superpowers"; and no one has more credit for this than Marek Slush Palatinus, the founder of the first Bitcoin mining pool (SlushPool) in the world and at the same time the creator of the Trezor hardware wallet. And because Slush is both an anarcho-capitalist and the biggest supporter of Freeport, he accepted the invitation to the Studio, although he normally does not perform in public, which I greatly appreciate. We will focus on his story, through which you will learn a lot of interesting things about cryptocurrencies.

– Marek Slush Palatinus; founder of the world's first bitcoin mining pool; hardware wallet creator Trezor; a legend in the cryptocurrency world; anarcho-capitalist

title: Freeport Studio: About negative rights with Petr Hála
text:
One of our regular listeners and supporters – Petr Firefanatic Hála – came to the Studio to contradict my interpretation of negative rights. The debate had two parts; we talked about intellectual property and freedom of speech, especially on social networks. From the point of view of intellectual property, the opponent comes up with a consistent definition of property rights including intangible goods; I criticize this definition. Regarding social networks, he has a significantly different view of implicit contracts, which we extend in the discussion far beyond the framework of social networks towards other services.

– Petr Firefanatic Hall; anarcho-capitalist; supporter of the Free Port; math physicist; programmer

title: Urza at KryptoVládi
text:
KryptoVláďa invited me to his livestream; although I didn't know him before, I liked his channel name so I accepted. In the end, we had a nice chat (unsurprisingly, especially about crypto). At the same time, I apologize for the quality of the sound and the recording, but neither was under my direction this time.

– KryptoVlaďa; crypto anarchist; youtuber

title: Studio Svobodné přístavu: About socialist health care with Vít Samek
text:
Vít Samek is a rescue worker, formerly a socialist, now an anarcho-capitalist; unlike most healthcare workers, they see the solution in the free market, real health insurance (not taxes) and mutual volunteerism in the provision of medical care. He explains how socialist healthcare leads to endless waste on all fronts; he himself witnessed the inefficient allocation of resources within the rapid rescue service as part of his work. Because he spoke publicly about that inefficiency, he displeased his bosses; he therefore left his job, but did not stop talking about the conditions there. And finally we talked about drugs.

– Vít Samek; anarcho-capitalist; paramedic; blogger; the writer

title: Freeport Studio: Railroad Crossings, Security and the State
text: The police have adopted a strategy of honking at level crossings, where they look for a driver to cross the crossing after the shutters are up, but before the red warning lights go out; at some crossings, the barriers go up a little before the red light stops. Whenever I criticize this police practice, someone comes up who starts to stand up for them and defend them by saying that the barriers can go down again right after they are raised, because the red light doesn't have to stop shining at all, if another train goes by for a while. Why do I consider this argument fundamentally wrong, even though I agree that something like this can happen? You will learn this and other connections in the video!

title: Freeport Studio: About the coronavirus and healthcare with Roman Šmucler
text:
The President of the Czech Stomatological Chamber, Roman Šmucler, has recently been seen a lot in connection with criticism of the coronavirus measures; are these measures really excessive? And should it continue to be under the control of the state? How will such government measures affect the personal freedom and responsibility of individuals? In addition to answers to (not only) these questions, in the interview you will also learn about (other) problems of socialist health care; not only do tabular salaries level the salaries of medical staff, but worse doctors are even better rated and vice versa!

– Roman Šmucler; president of the Czech Stomatological Chamber; critic of socialist healthcare; businessman; dentist

title: Studio Freeport: About visa corruption with former ambassador Damjan Prelovšek
text:
The former Slovenian ambassador in Prague collects evidence of corruption at the Czech embassy in Morocco; in his opinion, there is shopping with visas. He submitted the recordings to the Police of the Czech Republic; she thanked him, but apparently she has been out of action for many months. Damjan Prelovšek does not give up and hopes that if he makes the case public, he will perhaps make the police act. Although we know nothing about the case, and as anarchists we are certainly not law enforcement, we decided to give him space; on the one hand, because he seems to believe in his stuff, he played us the recordings (according to which it really seems that visas are being traded), but above all, to show people in practice those features of the state that we constantly describe on a theoretical level.

– Damjan Prelovšek; former Slovenian ambassador in Prague; art historian; photographer; fighter against corruption at the Czech embassy in Morocco

title: Freeport Studio: About raising exotic animals with Matthias
text:
One of the best authors of Stok Svobodné přístanov and Mises.cz accepted my invitation to the Studio of Svobodné přístanov, where we analyze his big topic - the breeding of exotic animals and state restrictions on breeders. We address the main arguments for and against legislative regulation of (not only exotic) animal breeding; we also touch on veganism, fur farms and their bans, animal rights and a popular anarcho-capitalist topic, i.e. the extension of the NAP (principle of non-aggression) to animals. During the entire conversation, Matthias' desire for freedom radiated very pleasantly to me.

– Matthias; long-time author of Mises.cz and Stok Svobodné přístavu; anarcho-capitalist; former breeder of exotic animals

title: Freeport Studio: Monopoly
text:
Although most people imagine something under the term "monopoly" - and even suspect that it is something harmful; however, few distinguish between a true monopoly and a dominant market player, but what's worse - the biggest, most harmful, most violent and most widespread monopoly is completely neglected and ignored. Yes, this is a state that can afford everything that no one else could afford. How is that? Well, by consistently abusing its monopoly position in education, it constantly indoctrinates everyone with its propaganda from the earliest age; people are then willing to view the state in a completely different way than all other subjects.
Through the analysis of the monopoly position of the state, the attitudes of anarcho-capitalists can also be clearly described. Contrary to popular belief, they do not want a world without the services that states provide; in fact, they only seek to de-monopolize the state and enable competition.

title: Studio Freeport: About totalitarianism and espionage with Richard Vokoun
text:
Upon numerous audience requests, I invited Richard Vokoun, one of the best speakers of the "2020 Freeport Conference: Totality Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow..." to the Freeport Studio; the person in question has devoted practically his entire life to the study of totalitarian regimes, widespread surveillance and security.
In the debate, we partially recapitulated his contribution to the conference, as I consider it very fundamental; in addition, we got to another part of his lecture, for which there was no longer room at the conference - its topic was spying carried out not by states, but by shady companies. And since Richard Vokoun is a very good debater, by the end of this two-and-a-half-hour debate (unlike other similar ones), I was quite tired, so you can observe a decrease in my argumentative abilities and alertness.

– Richard Vokoun; pseudonymous author of many texts on totalitarian regimes, surveillance and security

title: About responsibility in the Cherubín tea house
text: Another discussion that we held with Terezka in the Cherubín teahouse was about responsibility; we consider this to be an integral part of freedom. We talked about what responsibility means to us personally, but also how state interventions affect the level of responsibility of individuals in society; we also got to the death cycle of democracy and the explanation of why democracy inherently tends towards socialism - it is a property of that system. We also looked for better alternatives and solutions.

title: Free Harbor Studio: Regional and Senate Elections 2020
text: Since recently you have often asked us who to vote for in regional and senate elections, or who to vote for in general, we decided to make a video on this topic. There we analyze the current political scene (mostly parliamentary - a little bit non-parliamentary - parties) from a libertarian point of view; we even address the question of whether it makes sense for anarchists to vote. But definitely don't take our opinions as dogma; we don't even agree with each other on many things, so we expect that many libertarians will have even more completely different views.

title: Free Harbor Studio: About intellectual property with Dominik Hrubý
text:
Intellectual property represents one of many areas of friction between statists and libertarians; however, the truth is that while most people defend intellectual property, its detractors can be found in both camps. Even among the greats of the Austrian school of economics, we have its supporters from the past (Ludwig von Mises, Murray Newton Rothbard), although nowadays more of them take the opposite position (Norman Stephan Kinsella, Walter Block, Jeffrey Tucker). When I lecture on intellectual property, I usually oppose the proponents of centric law; however, today Dominik Hrubý - a supporter of decentralized society - defended intellectual property against my arguments.

– Dominik Hrubý; member of the Free Citizens Party; intellectual property advocate; law and journalism graduate

title: Freeport Studio: On Human Rights with Zuzana Candigliota
text:
The invitation to the Free Port Studio was accepted by attorney Zuzana Candigliota, a great supporter of people's personal freedoms; I have been following and admiring her work for a long time. We talked about her cases, the dispute with the bar association, city police officers, about education and education from the point of view of ethics and law, but mainly about the rights of patients, mandatory vaccinations and home births. Finally, we addressed polycentric law and first certainty in an anarcho-capitalist stateless society.

– Zuzana Candigliota; lawyer; member of the League of Human Rights; blogger; activist; freedom fighter

title: Urza with Bratříček on freedom of speech
text:
After almost a year, we met YouTuber Bratříček again; last year we had a debate about anarcho-capitalism in general (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RT-BYX_VmP8&list=PLmwDL0lIJTxBIIAJ8m7j32KYTqP09n-xL), this year we focused mainly on freedom of speech and "censorship" carried out by large internet corporations. The debate loosely follows on from my discussion with Daniel Vávra (Bratříček holds very similar views). What do you think? And what will next year bring us?

– Little brother; youtuber; businessman

title: Freeport Studio: "We don't talk to the cops." (D-FENS)
text:
I've been reading D-FENS's weblog since I was fifteen; it was one of the first places I published, where I learned to write, debate, and think critically. I owe a lot to D-FENS; and I have great respect for his work. Countless times he stood against the will of the state for those who could not help themselves.
In this video, we discuss how to proceed when a road patrol stops us in a car. How not to lose your driver's license? How not to be unnecessarily bullied? How to deal with the authorities? How do I get my rights? You will learn this and much more from probably the most professional person in the Czech Republic.
