title: Freeport Studio: On the Transition to Anarchy with Dan Steigerwald
text:
I've been looking forward to interviewing Daniel Steigerwald for a long time; and he really didn't disappoint me - so I hope you won't either. We talked about Dan's idea about the possibility of a transition from the state to anarcho-capitalism, which he has been working on for years; I, on the other hand, talk about him at a minimum, so I'm glad for this addition. During the interview, a lot of interesting thoughts about anarcho-capitalism itself came up. Towards the end, we also lightly touched on the topic of cryptocurrencies, which Dan has also been working on for many years; his idiosyncratic bitcoin maximalism is quite well known in libertarian circles.

– Daniel Steigerwald; anarcho-capitalist; thinker; eccentric; showman; programmer; Independent software Gardener

title: Studio of the Free Port: About Foreclosures/Distraints and the Pirate Party with František Navrkal
text:
For the first time, a member of the Parliament of the Czech Republic expressed interest in participating in the Free Port Studio; and because we believe in dialogue, an anarchist and a politician sat at the same table. In the first hour, we discussed the topic brought up by the guest - the role of the state in debt collection; in his opinion, the state is needed to achieve justice in debt enforcement/foreclosures. For the second hour we talked about my objections to the Pirate Party; in my opinion, they do not defend our freedom, but rather its restriction by the state. In the third hour, we discussed more general questions about centralized and decentralized society.

– František Navrkal; member of the Chamber of Deputies of the Czech Republic; a member of the Pirate Party; data analyst

title: Free port studio: About education with Zdeňka Šíp Staňková
text:
Zdeňka Šíp Staňková is a well-known media face of the Freedom of Learning initiative, of which I am also a member, as I consider free education to be perhaps the most important prerequisite for a free society. And what does free education actually mean? Above all, mutual voluntariness; which is in sharp contradiction not only to compulsory schooling, but also to the whole concept of state socialist education. Zdenka and I will discuss its far-reaching consequences - and the opposite, i.e. self-directed education - while answering your questions; so come!
Štěpán Kunc made an anarcho-capitalist pipe with my name on it; if he auctions it for more than 3,000 crowns, he will send a contribution to the Free Port. You can participate in the auction here:
https://www.facebook.com/dymkykunc/posts/2753474958308700

– Zdeňka Šíp Staňková; member of the Freedom of Learning board; founder of the initiative Children are people too

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Bitcoin's Anonymity and Its Risks
text:
The next lecture from the Anarcho-Capitalism cycle will again be about cryptocurrencies: Bitcoin is not anonymous, despite erroneous assumptions. And in order for it to be good money, it also lacks one essential feature – fungibility or exchangeability. How legitimate is the effort of analytics firms to track bitcoin flows? Is anonymity even achievable in Bitcoin? And if so, what are the risks of applying anonymization tools in a time of growing financial dictatorship? Let's look at these questions together from a more social than technical point of view.
We thank Pavlov Ovesný from HOME | postudia (www.postudio.cz) for fixing the damaged sound!

– Pavel Ševčík; bitcoin maximalist; programmer; contributor to Bitcoin open-source projects; anarcho-capitalist

title: Coronarchy for TopMonks
text:
I've been following TopMonks with its "flat" organizational structure for some time now; with the founder Jiří Fabian, we recorded the CZPodcast two years ago (you can also find it on the Freeport Channel). So I gladly accepted the invitation to a discussion about the coronavirus, measures against it and the impact of the corona crisis on the whole society.
I called the talk Coronary, and together with the listeners, we discuss the responses of states to the pandemic, debate how a stateless society would deal with it, compare the differences and discuss other related topics.
Sorry for the noise in the audio track, we were sitting in a shisha establishment; unfortunately, their pulling is louder in the recording than it was on the spot.

title: Freeport studio: Koruna, euro, cash and deanonymization of data
text:
The first phase of the corona crisis ends; in connection with this, I would like to point out three topics that are more related than it might seem at first glance:
– Koruna versus euro: Are foods expensive because we don't pay in euros, but in koruna? Does the crisis show the unviability of the crown? And how are the actions of the CNB in recent years related to this?
– Cash ban: What would a cash ban do? Is the loss of transactional anonymity an acceptable price for transparency? And can you imagine negative interest rates?
– Deanonymization of data: Is anonymized data really anonymized? What is the difference between anonymized and masked data? What does the deanonymization process mean and why is it dangerous?

title: Studio of the Free Port: Maxík, Oliver, the state and the price of life
text: What if someone had a child dying in anarcho-capitalism that would require 50 million to save, which they didn't have? What then? How would the market deal with this!? Well, the state probably wouldn't ask for another 5 million in protection money (called VAT) from the money that people voluntarily collected. And what if someone was dying in capitalist healthcare because there was no money to treat them? Well, in that case at least he would know and maybe have a chance to try to do something about it; it happens all the time in socialist healthcare, it's just not talked about and no one calls the cases that way. And what is the price of human life? Can something like this be converted into money at all? Don't anarcho-capitalists do something like that? Well... SÚKL definitely does.

title: About life and self-development with Karolína K.
text:
I accepted an invitation to the program Chat without education with the tarot rebel Karolína Kváš; and since I was intrigued by her approach to life before the filming began, in the end our conversation did not revolve around anarcho-capitalism, but we discussed other things that I really enjoy. This is my first public appearance where I did not talk about libertarian issues, but about myself. Originally, I didn't even plan to (and actually it was never my intention to discuss such things publicly), but thanks to Karolína, I changed my mind (and plans).

– Karolína Kváš (http://karolinadobrovska.cz/); tarot rebel; authoress; traveler; anthropologist; blogger; coach
  Book: https://bit.ly/KupKamineky
  Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/karolinakvas
  Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/karolina_kvas/

title: Freeport Studio: Freedom (speech)
text: From the debate on freedom of expression with Dan Vávra, a whole lot of interesting observations and different views on the matter emerged for me; and based on what I've read from the numerous comments, I believe that the very nature of free speech needs to be explained, as there is a lot of confusion on the subject. I start with a few basic starting points, on which I will probably agree with the vast majority of listeners; I then use pure logic to draw conclusions from them, with which few people agree. what is it Let's talk about it; I will be very happy if you write a logical and substantive criticism in the comments - not only of my conclusions, but above all of the starting points and the procedure, because the conclusions themselves are only their logical consequence.

title: Freeport Studio: On Legitimacy and Law with Roman Joch
text:
At your request, we invited Roman Joch to the Freeport Studio; and in retrospect I think it's a great idea, I find the debate extremely interesting. We started with totalitarian regimes and ideologies, we talked about threats to our current freedom. A little unexpectedly, we came to children's rights and corporal punishment. Then we focused on conservatism as a political ideology. And finally we got to anarcho-capitalism; we discussed (natural) law and legitimacy; we very interestingly discussed the advantages and disadvantages of polycentric law compared to centric law.

– Roman Joch; director of the Civic Institute; publicist; commentator; teacher at CEVRO Institute and VŠE

title: Peace with drugs in the Cherubín teahouse
text: Another discussion that we organized with Terezka in the Cherubín teahouse was about drugs. In the first part, we discussed drugs as such, informed about them and tried to do some destigmatization, the aim of which was to act against the generally widespread myths; we compared illegal drugs with legal or medicinal ones. The theme of the second part was the war on drugs; we talked about its history, the present, but above all the consequences of various attempts at drug prohibition, which have had the same results for decades.

title: Free Harbor Studio: About freedom of speech with Dan Vávra
text:
Well-known Czech game developer Daniel Vávra made a video about freedom of speech some time ago; in it he criticized the censorship taking place on social networks. Since I responded to his speech on the Freeport Channel, we agreed on a debate where we will discuss the topic in person; and this is her record. We will be happy if you write your opinions and observations in the comments. Should the right to free enterprise of Facebook and other companies give way to people being able to present their opinions and not be ostracized for them? Among other things, you will also learn why Dan no longer calls himself a libertarian, although he once was.

– Daniel Vávra; game developer; graphic designer; photographer; influencer; youtuber; conservative; former libertarian

title: Studio Freeport: About the libertarian movement with Professor Šima
text:
The Czech libertarian movement is one of the strongest in the world; and although most viewers of this channel know its current active personalities, not everyone knows the "previous generation" that laid the foundations of this movement. One of the most important giants of the Czech libertarian scene is Professor Josef Šíma. I debated with him not only about the past, but also about the present and the future; and we didn't just stay with Czech realities, we also looked abroad. The video may be of value to libertarians rather than the ignorant.

– prof. Josef Šima; rector of CEVRO Institute; one of the "ancestors" of the Czech libertarian movement; promoter of anarcho-capitalism

title: Studio Freeport: On defiance of the state with Michael Poplar
text:
Contest for the book Atlas Rebellion by Ayn Rand: Whoever sends the highest amount to the Freeport account within a week with the caption "Atlas Rebellion" will receive this book from our guest.
Michael Poplar is an investor and entrepreneur turned libertarian by the state; we analyzed the differences in the functioning of states in individual countries, the behavior of citizens with the police, defiance of the state in the past and present; and finally we got to exploring the ways in which we would like to (non-violently and peacefully) get rid of the state.

– Michael Poplar; libertarian; minarchist; enemy of the state

title: Tereza on the coronavirus for the SfL webinar
text: Terezka accepted an invitation to the Students for Liberty webinar, where she spoke about the coronavirus, which she gave an "inside" view (from the healthcare system); of course, it didn't just stay with the coronavirus itself, but also discussed other topics related to it and related to freedom and state measures and the so-called "crisis management" - or rather the parody of it that the government performed.

title: Freeport Studio: On Marxism with Mirek Honcović
text:
The invitation to the Freeport Studio was accepted by a member of the Marxist International; we discussed (historical) materialism, ethical versus materialist arguments against the state, capitalism, socialism, the free market, central planning, class and classless society, class struggle, exploitation, subjective and labor theories of value, and our very different view of economics.
I find the debate very interesting; especially its very end, when we addressed economic topics.

– Mirko Honcović; Marxist; anti-capitalist; proletarian; member of the International Marxist Tendency; editor of Konfrontace magazine

title: Studio Freeport: Why do socialists not understand us?
text: There are a number of barriers and pitfalls in communication with socialists and generally everyone from the opposite side of the opinion spectrum; however, many of them are more communicative in nature than fundamental. How we perceive the world is, of course, based on who we are as people; and the way we think and communicate is based on the kind of people we are. So it is not surprising that an individualist will understand the words of another individualist better than the words of a collectivist; even if both were trying to communicate exactly the same content. Let's try together to understand our differences and weaken the communication barriers a little!

title: Studio Freeport: 85% food self-sufficiency of the Czech Republic
text:
Food Self-Sufficiency Bill Coming; he is applauded by the SPD, ANO and Petr Hampl, which in itself says a lot about him. Frédéric Bastiat explained why this is nonsense more than 150 years ago; but socialists don't make the same mistake (just) twice - rather ten, twenty times... to be sure.
Although food self-sufficiency is perceived by the general public as something positive, we will try to explain why it is a (not only economic) disaster.

title: Freeport Studio: Credit and interest
text: Usury (giving credit with interest) is a big topic that has stirred up strong emotions and passions for hundreds of years; the Catholic Church already took various (rather negative) attitudes towards it in the Middle Ages, as a result of which usury was often prohibited. A wide variety of economists have tried to explain and describe the phenomenon of interest; the Austrian economic school, specifically Eugen von Böhm-Bawerk, shed light on it (as usual). His findings are quite timeless, so they can be used even today as an answer to the call of some socialists for a legislative cap on interest rates. I also touch on the subject of repayment and non-repayment of interest in fractional banking; here, strangely enough, I will stand up against one invalid argument of factional banking.

title: Freeport Studio: Patients versus Doctors and Medical Mysteries
text: The dispute between patients and doctors has been "raging" in society for a long time; while patients complain about reluctance (or even rudeness) on the part of medical staff, lack of freedom, impossibility to decide on their own treatment, poor information about their options (information asymmetry), doctors tend to be poorly paid, overworked and unnecessarily overworked. Unfortunately, there are disputes in society about whether doctors are victims of patients or vice versa; however, we are convinced that both patients and doctors are victims of the state socialist healthcare system, which we discuss in detail in the video. Finally, we also address the issue of medical secrecy, its breakability and the overall danger of keeping medical records.

title: Freeport Studio: State of Emergency and Responsibility
text: May 17 was the last day of the state of emergency declared by the government; does this mean that since May 18 there is security in the Czech Republic and nothing threatens us? Probably not; on the other hand, many people act and think very similarly, even if they would never say it directly. For the state assumed responsibility for the people; therefore, they have no reason to take care of themselves when someone else does it for them. Unfortunately, this is not only related to the coronavirus, but we can encounter it in practically all industries; for the state is constantly trying to manage the risks in all of our lives, making us more and more dependent. What about that?

title: Freeport Studio: Identity cards, identity and privacy
text: There is a widespread belief among the general public that ID cards are needed; it simply wouldn't be possible without them. But why exactly? There aren't many good reasons; actually there is none. However, we decided to go even further; not only are IDs not needed; there is even no need for the state to collect citizens' personal data at all (such as medical records, economic activities, and the like); and what's more - it would be ideal if the state didn't even have any overview of its "own" citizens. Such databases do more harm than good.

title: Studio Freeport: Compulsory state matriculation in mathematics
text: A mandatory state matriculation exam in mathematics will probably not be possible in the end; that is, if someone doesn't change it again, because political will is about as constant as a weathervane on a roof in the wind. Along with this, the amendment to the Education Act brings further changes. What kind? Good or bad? What about the compulsory high school diploma in mathematics - do we need it? And would it be fair not to introduce it when we already have a compulsory high school diploma in Czech and a foreign language? I will answer these and other questions in this part of the Seduced Harbor Study; and I will add a few more thoughts - for example, how the difficulty of enforcing the compulsory high school diploma in mathematics is related to the collectivization of society.

title: Freeport Studio: Behavioral Economics, the Mainstream and the Austrians
text: Behavioral economics comes with an interesting critique of the concept of homo economicus and the concept of bounded rationality; it also disrupts some of the models used by mainstream economics by showing the "irrational" behavior of people. At first glance, it seems to be the antithesis of the Austrian economy (and many people perceive it as such); however, I personally think that these two economic schools have more in common than it might seem at first glance (although their starting points and conclusions are undoubtedly different). At the end, we will also recall how the Austrians perceive rationality; and why it is not a completely happy definition from my point of view.

title: Freeport Studio: Poverty
text: Different people mean different things to poverty; above all, however, it changes over time, as society grows incredibly rich. Today's poor man has many times more options than yesterday's rich man. And although we are constantly creating new and new wealth, sometimes something happens that complicates the economic growth of humanity; recently, for example, the coronavirus pandemic. What will be the consequences? Come and talk about it live with us and at the same time create the next part of our show.

title: Freeport Studio: State Aid in Crisis and the Generality of Arguments
text:
The crisis caused by the coronavirus and government measures has caused many to call for a state solution, or at least help; surprisingly, not all libertarians are opposed. So we decided to discuss several variants of state interventions; strangely enough, we didn't condemn all of them xD
In the second half of the video, we discussed the universality of argumentation; or rather its absence - and the resulting very "popular" argumentative fallacy, which I demonstrated on the examples of the prohibition of incest, the decriminalization of drugs, the voluntary nature of vaccination or the obligation to fasten seat belts in the car - simply on the "tastes" themselves.

title: About ownership with Zdenek Gardelka
text:
The debate at the Freeport Forum on the extension of the NAP to animals resulted in a very interesting Skype discussion; Zdeněk Gardelka had comments and criticisms about my understanding of property rights and the principle of non-aggression, which I did not want to address in writing, so we decided to create a more interesting format. As I find this topic interesting and essential, I decided to publish the debate. I will be happy for your comments and opinions in the comments; and if you are interested in discussing any topic with me in this way, please contact me, I am certainly open to it.

– Zdeněk Gardelka; a long-time member of the Czech anarcho-capitalist community

title: Freeport Studio: Unconditional Basic Income
text: Socialists have been dreaming of a basic income for many years; but only when the coronavirus gave them at least some political will to enforce it. Fortunately, this will happen more likely in Spain (unfortunately for the Spanish), not in the Czech Republic; Czech politicians will hopefully keep their common sense at least in this area for now. In the video, we explain why basic income does not work not only from the point of view of economics and mathematics, but above all, what would be its harmful effects on society even if it were to work by some miracle. Sure, in theory, a basic unconditional income could reduce red tape and simplify the benefits system; but at what cost?

title: Freeport Studio: Market Failure
text: The four types of market failures (imperfect competition, information asymmetry, public goods and externalities) are taught in every possible economic school, constantly repeated and taken more or less as a given; unfortunately, they are not discussed much anymore, and in addition, many people do not even think about them much, they simply learn them for the test and continue to take them as fact. I certainly do not want to contradict what economists are so fond of proving, namely that market allocation is not Pareto-optimal; however, I would like to discuss what it even means and what consequences can be derived from it (and especially point out what consequences cannot be derived from it, although unfortunately this often happens). And does it even make sense to call something like this a market failure?

title: Free Harbor Studio: About education, schooling and self-determination of children
text: The school year was interrupted due to the coronavirus; what will be the consequences? Will he go to observe them at all? Graduations will most likely be; but what if they weren't? What if everyone who gets it got a high school diploma? Would anything change in the world? We are not only talking about this in the next part of the Freeport Studio; we also analyze children's freedom, upbringing, responsibility for their lives, friendships and the possibility to make decisions about their education throughout their lives, not only in adulthood. We also touch on independent schools and address the difference between unschooling (self-directed education) and home education.

title: Free Harbor Studio: Freedom of Speech, Censorship, Elves and Dan Vávra
text: Daniel Vávra made an interesting video about freedom of speech (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OQ1eBSZvFSo); and since you sent it to me massively and asked for opinions, I decided to respond in the form of a video of my own. I've tried to frame it so that it makes sense even if you choose not to look at what I'm responding to. I deal with the issue of communication platforms operated by large corporations and their censorship, which is (at least partially) pushed by states. I try to distinguish between personal preferences regarding free expression and look for a line between subjective beliefs on how to set rules and (not) imposing them on others; it is no less important to distinguish between a (state-enforced) monopoly and a (more or less market-based) dominant player (with existing competition; even if it is significantly weaker at the given moment).

title: Freeport Studio: Vaccination
text: Vaccination of the population has been a big topic in recent years; Anti-vax and pro-vaccination disputes are the order of the day. In connection with the corona virus infection, the debates are still escalating. Does vaccination make sense? What about mandatory vaccinations? The usefulness of vaccination itself does not yet imply the necessity or justification of mandatory vaccination. Who would ensure vaccination in a free stateless decentralized society? Would it be possible to somehow motivate people to get vaccinated? What would happen to those who would refuse vaccination anyway?

title: Freeport Studio: VPN
text:
Network security is an increasingly important topic in the age of sophistication of the Internet; and recently VPNs have come into vogue. That in itself is great because people want to be anonymous and protect their digital freedom. Unfortunately, however, they often use technologies that they have no idea how they work; it can backfire on them. And since I've been getting a lot of questions about VPN lately, I decided to make a video; maybe I will help someone from unwanted exposure of their sensitive data and personal data. At the end of the video, I discuss some general principles of network security.
0:00 Introduction
2:15 What is a VPN?
7:17 Using a VPN for anonymity
9:04 Shortcomings
12:41 Defense against surveillance
18:56 Necessity of at least elementary knowledge of the issue
21:31 Encryption
26:23 Other security risks of otherwise secure communication
30:37 Conclusion

title: Freeport Studio: Deflation Scarecrow, ABCT, interest and fiat money
text:
In a previous video on money creation and artificial inflation, I mentioned that a deflationary economy does not actually suffer from the ills that are widely attributed to it; and since a lot of listeners were asking about it, I made a second video explaining it in detail. I also describe the causes of business cycles from the perspective of the Austrian school of economics; I focus on the connection between the amount of savings, interest rates and the willingness of entrepreneurs to expand their business. But what happens if we artificially lower interest rates? And what are the other implications of central banking and fiat money - other than those mentioned in the previous video?
The video that I follow up with this talk can be found here:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w2Fk-4O5Fjw&list=PLmwDL0lIJTxC9KltdmCmJFA3v49C8XBpN

title: Freeport Studio: Totalitarian Regimes
text: We opened the topic of totalitarianism in the Free Port with a conference, continued it with written texts and would like to conclude them in a live broadcast; so come and create a live broadcast with us with your comments and questions! Just like at the conference, here too we will be happy for every "mainstream" viewer who has perhaps never heard of libertarianism or ancap; if you know any that you think might be interested, please bring them along!

title: Studio Freeport: Are we facing hyperinflation? Let's dump the crown (koruna)!
text:
The media was flashed with unsalted unsalted news that the government is amending the law so that the CNB can buy government bonds. Although minimal space has been devoted to this topic, it is probably the most dangerous thing that the current government has demonstrated during the crisis; quite possibly without most of its representatives realizing it. And since the general public doesn't know much about it, we decided to explain from the ground up what the problem is; we will start with the history of money, we will also deal with fractional banking, we will also get to the harmfulness of artificial inflation, the threat of apocalyptic hyperinflation, and we will end with the connection with the actions of the government and the CNB.
You can find a counter-argument to the postponing consumption claim (as well as a description of the emergence of business cycles) here:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cb_WfSiNE6c&list=PLmwDL0lIJTxC9KltdmCmJFA3v49C8XBpN

title: Tereza in StandaShow
text:
YouTuber Standa invited Terezka to his talk show; they talked about the coronavirus. They discussed the topic from different sides; both from the point of view of the doctor and also from the perspective of the anarcho-capitalist. Among other things, there will be an answer to a very often asked question today: "How would a stateless society deal with a pandemic?" So give it a listen and leave a comment to let us know your feedback!
A recording of the entire show can be found here: https://www.patreon.com/posts/34951065.

title: Freeport Studio: Nothing is as permanent as temporary government measures
text:
The coronavirus is not only dangerous as a disease, but also as a social phenomenon; and few governments miss an opportunity to use the population's fear to their advantage - for the gradual introduction of totality. Our government has already begun; and I have no illusions that she would just let herself be stopped. Babiš will be the "savior of the people" and everyone will have to keep their mouths shut.
For example, have you noticed the amendment to the law on military intelligence, which gives the secret services the ability to monitor all network communication on the Czech Internet? Or did it fit in with the news about the coronavirus?

title: Freeport Studio: Coronavirus
text:
Since many of you requested the topic of the coronavirus, we made a video about it; and since it has many social, human rights, moral and economic aspects, we have been thorough and discussed them from different angles. We deal with individual state procedures, central planning and decentralized solutions.
Now that you can't go out and spend more time on computers, we decided to talk; it ends up being two and a half hours. We hope you enjoy listening; and please leave us comments with feedback, we will be glad. Thank you!

title: Freeport Studio: Parliamentary Immunity and Restraining Orders
text:
Why do deputies and senators have immunity? What is this institute for? At first glance, the reason sounds quite reasonable; but upon closer examination it is a complete mockery.
How are restraining orders related to parliamentary immunity? Not directly; but there is a certain parallel between these two exceptions to the (bad) law. Preservation orders are actually parliamentary immunity "in reverse".

title: Cryptocurrencies (with a hint of ankap) for the František Křižík High School in Pilsen
text: The management of the František Křižík High School in Pilsen asked me if I would give a lecture on cryptocurrencies for several classes. I gladly accepted the invitation; and he easily projected ankap into his speech, even though I didn't say the word. Since it also interested the teachers, maybe they will invite me again purely on this topic. And I will definitely like to visit my beloved Pilsen again!

title: Freeport Studio: Discrimination
text: Discrimination is automatically seen as bad in our society; but must it always be so without exception? And where it is bad, does the state really have to intervene to "save" the situation? In what way would the market discriminate in a stateless society? We will look for answers to these and many other questions with you during the livestream of the Studio of the Free Port. So don't hesitate to create another part together with us!

title: Freeport Studio: Anarchocommunism
text:
Another anarcho-communist accepted my invitation to the Freeport Studio. We had a very interesting debate, which I consider an important part of my effort to conduct a dialogue with anarchists from other anarchist schools, which is not so easy, as anarcho-communists typically refuse to discuss with anarcho-capitalists (at least in the Czech Republic). Although you may not agree with the lessons in the debate and it may seem pointless to you, I am convinced that it pays to listen to the end and try to understand as much as possible of what the person in question is saying; whatever you think about it, knowing is always better than not knowing.

– anonymous anarcho-communist

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Bitcoin and Other Cryptocurrencies
text:
One planned lecture at the (de)Centrála club became a regular cycle (every first Wednesday of the month) due to great interest; the latter to some extent follows the cycle Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis, although the format changes a little. text:
We ended the Free Port 2020: Totality yesterday, today and tomorrow conference with a panel discussion, which was attended by Richard Vokoun, Palo Lupták, Adam Růžička, Jan Zugar and Urza; although these are five supporters of freedom, it is interesting to observe the differences in their perception of the risks threatening our society and the approach to solving existing problems.

title: Palo Lupták: Opt-out of the system (KSP20: Totality yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
The last speaker of the "Free Harbor Conference 2020: Totality yesterday, today and tomorrow" was Palo Lupták with his lecture "Opt-out from the system: How to achieve economic and personal freedom by using globality and flexibility".

1. Choose a suitable country for your permanent residency.
2. Choose a suitable country as the headquarters for your company.
3. Remove centers of interest in your home country.
4. Cancel your bank account.
5. Transfer your finances to cryptocurrencies, prefer truly anonymous ones, support cryptocurrency friendly services.
6. Choose international health insurance.
7. Choose your international mobile operator.
8. Support the sharing economy.
9. Help your friends opt-out of the system.

Palo Lupták is a crypto-anarchist and volunteer focused on technology and hacking society. He is the founder of hacking companies in the field of IT security (Nethemba, Hacktrophy) and contemporary art (Satori). He co-founded the Bratislava and Prague hackerspaces (Progressbar and Paralelni Polis).

title: Freeport Studio: On Capitalism with Dominik Stroukal
text:
Another guest of the Free Port Studio was Dominik Stroukal; we talked quite broadly about a whole range of topics, but basically revolved around capitalism from different angles. But we also discussed the political scene, crypto-currencies and speculated a little about the future. Although we look at things quite similarly, there have been a few topics where we have slightly different opinions. I will be glad if you contribute your bit to the mill in the comments.

– Dominik Stroukal; anarcho-capitalist; Chief Economist of the Roklen Group; lecturer at the CEVRO Institute; author of Bitcoin, Economic Bubbles, and Dark Web: Sex, Drugs, and Bitcoin

title: Adam Růžička: Social tyranny (KSP20: Totality yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
Adam Růžička's lecture for the "Free Harbor Conference 2020: Totality yesterday, today and tomorrow" was entitled "Creeping social tyranny and the importance of freedom of speech".

Under the term tyranny, we usually imagine the violent dictate of a powerful individual or group that oppresses the rest. However, thinkers have long pointed out that tyranny can also manifest itself on a social level, in ways that are harder to define, but all the more insidious, because they are not clearly visible, but often have a comparable influence on the lives of individuals as despotic governments. This threat to free societies was described by John Stuart Mill in his famous essay On Freedom, and Václav Havel also touched on it in The Power of the Powerless when he spoke of social "self-totality". The lecture will present the basic theses of the issue of social freedom and connect them with recent psychological research in the context of the current challenges of democratic societies (e.g. social media, opinion bubbles, the phenomenon of divided societies, etc.).

After studying psychology at Masaryk University, Adam Růžička, MSc. MRes. at University College London, where he worked for several years as a researcher in the field of cognitive neuroscience and researched the brain with a focus on human speech. He currently works as the director of the H21 Institute in Prague, which focuses on collective decision-making, electoral systems, civic participation and the issue of a divided society.

title: Jan Zugar: North Korea (KSP20: Totality Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow)
text:
The next speaker at the "Freeport Conference 2020: Totality yesterday, today and tomorrow" was Jan Zugar with his lecture "North Korea - a country much more open than we perceive it".

There is perhaps no country more emotionally closed to the outside world than the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. In 1950-53, a war took place here, during which the country was divided into southern and northern parts due to the efforts of the north, which sought, with the support of China and the Soviet Union, to unite the entire country under the red flag. This failed thanks to the intervention of UN troops, and so after a three-year conflict, Korea was divided into these two parts by the 38th parallel. While South Korea is a developing country that is moving in the same direction as comparable eastern states, North Korea is closed, an information embargo is imposed on the media of the surrounding countries, access to the Internet, which is also internal only to the DPRK, is almost impossible and the harsh dictatorship of the Communist Party and the Kim clan rules here. It is very rare to get to this country as part of diplomatic trips or a study stay, which Jan Zugar was able to do.

Jan Zugar is a graduate of BUT in Brno, a member of the Young Christian Democrats and an opponent of communism.

title: Lidija Zavoralová: The illusion of freedom (KSP20: Totality yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
Another incredibly engaging speaker at the "2020 Freeport Conference: Totality yesterday, today and tomorrow" was Lidija Zavoralová with her lecture "The illusion of freedom as a greater evil versus totality".

How do we even know what and when totality is and where totality begins? Lidija Zavoralová's story begins at the age of thirteen, when she fought for the overthrow of the Serbian socialist regime under Milošević's rule. She personally printed leaflets and called on the whole school to go and demonstrate with the students. Subsequently, at the age of 19, she discovered that she was trapped, everything about freedom was different than she had imagined, but despite this skepticism, after a year of studying in America, she started working for the secret services, supplying them with information and once again thinking that she was fighting for the democracy of her country. In the lecture, she will also talk about what specific tasks she received as part of this personal mission.

Lidija Zavoralová is a freedom-hacker, business consultant and writer of children's books.

title: Richard Vokoun: Dictatorship vs. totality (KSP20: Totality yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
The special guest of the "Free Harbor Conference 2020: Totality yesterday, today and tomorrow" was the speaker, Richard Vokoun, with the lecture "Dictatorship versus totality, surveillance - and where is freedom?".

Any historian will tell you how historical totalities worked. But how to recognize future totalitarian ideologies and how to survive them? What is the fundamental difference between totalitarianism and dictatorship? Can totality arise only through the state, or are there real "grassroots" totalities from secret groups of fanatics?
In the study of totalitarianism, he gradually went from the historical to the systemic, political, sociological and psychological point of view, and the result is a synthesis of universally applicable principles of functioning of totalitarianism.

Richard Vokoun has been studying totalitarian regimes and the ideologies behind them for 15 years. His profession is analyzing technical systems and predicting their risks and failures, but he also uses these skills to comment on laws. He sees "under the hood" of spying and surveillance systems at work. He also has interdisciplinary knowledge of security studies, the history and functioning of secret services and repressive bodies, Christian and Islamic theology.

title: Urza: The Different Faces of Evil (KSP20: Totality Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow)
text:
The second speaker of the "2020 Freeport Conference: Totality Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow" was Urza with his lecture "The Different Faces of Evil or Recognize Totality".

Although everyone can probably agree that they don't want to live in totalitarianism, for some reason totalitarian regimes are an inherent part of our history; and not only long past, but also quite recent, in short, they keep coming again and again. How is this possible, you ask, when almost everyone rejects totalitarianism? Well, few people offer it to people directly; totalitarian regimes typically come under the guise of promises of safety, prosperity, well-being, and often even freedom. Unfortunately, history shows that most people do not recognize totalitarianism until it is too late. And because Urza does not want (perhaps not only) to repeat this history, during this lecture he will try to teach you to recognize the arrival of totalitarian regimes while there is still time.

Urza is an anarcho-capitalist author; wrote about a thousand libertarian texts on the web and in print media and the first Czech book on anarcho-capitalism. For more than ten years, he not only reads, thinks and writes about freedom, ethics, the free market, the economy and the role of the state in society, but also lectures, makes videos and is invited to various programs and panel discussions. Together with his wife Teresa, he forms the Free Harbor; he heads the Czech and Slovak Institute of Ludwig von Mises, of which he is a co-founder; belongs to the board of the Freedom of Learning association and actively cooperates with many libertarian initiatives. You can find more about him on the Urza.cz website.

Download presentation:
https://prednasky.urza.cz/konferenze/2020.konftot.pdf

title: Roman Joch: Totalitarianism (KSP20: Totality yesterday, today and tomorrow)
text:
The first speaker of the "Freeport Conference 2020: Totality yesterday, today and tomorrow" was MUDr. Roman Joch with his lecture "Totalitarianism as the most radical form of revolution of the 20th century".

His lecture will focus on the philosophical assumptions of totalitarianism: statism, relativism and utopianism. It will reflect on whether and what type of totalitarianism is a substitute religion.

Roman Joch is the director of the Civic Institute, publicist and commentator, teaches at the CEVRO Institute University of Applied Sciences and the University of Economics. He is the author of several books, including "Rebellion against the 20th Century Revolution" and "No, Mr. Prime Minister!".

title: Freeport Studio: Cryptocurrencies
text: Cryptocurrencies are quite broad and an absolutely essential topic from the point of view of economic freedom, which was very "in" a while ago and everyone was talking about it; now there is a little less talk about him in the media space, which is the best reason for us to do a livestream about him. You can get involved, ask us questions, discuss with us, disagree... so come!
