title: Debate with socialist Pavle Šanda about freedom
text:
I accepted an invitation to the František Palacký High School in Neratovice for a debate with the socialist Pavlo Šanda; we talked about the concept of freedom (entitled versus non-entitled), state intervention, large corporations, monopolies and other interesting topics.
I enjoyed the debate very much; while subjectively I consider perhaps its second half to be more interesting. After all, make up your own mind; and don't forget to write it in the comments!

– Pavel Šanda; socialist; a leftist blogger; opponents of conspiracy theories and common sense (outside the area of small agricultural production)

title: Freeport Studio: Shared Drug Record
text:
The shared medication record comes into force, in which the state will automatically manage the highly sensitive data of all those who do not perform the not-so-easy opt-out without explicit permission.
How to do it? And why at all? Are there any risks if you give your data to the state? What are the cons, but also the pros? You can learn all this and much more in this video.
The promised link to SUKL (there you can log in as a verified citizen and cancel the shared drug record):
https://patient.erecept.sukl.cz

title: Debate for puppets in the DISK theater
text:
The DISK Theater organizes a cycle of discussions "Debates for Puppets". This is footage from the first pilot test piece; the entire format is a constant work in progress, so future debates may look different.
The point of the discussion was that each participant was represented by a puppet as an avatar and did not know the identity of the others. I've been through a lot of debates; it's part of my job. This one was probably the most different from all the others; it was a nice change. I liked the idea at first glance, but only during the discussion did I fully appreciate it - one can focus much better on the topic itself and is not distracted by anything.
After the first part, from which the recording comes, there was a second one - with exposed faces; Unfortunately, the theater did not provide me with her recording. Anyway, I was surprised that a number of people in the audience recognized me (the best comment was: "I hope everyone knows an anarcho-capitalist when they hear one." - something that certainly wouldn't have been heard a few years ago); and the puppet debate probably served its purpose also in the sense that one of the listeners told me that for the first time she really listened to me without pre-judging me based on who I was (and she said what I was saying made sense to her).

title: Studio of the Free Port: About the Ankap with the Ravenclaw Mother
text:
Veronika Hurdová, known under the pseudonym Krkavčí matka (http://www.krkavcimatka.cz/), accepted the invitation to the Freeport Studio; the topic was her perception of anarcho-capitalism and libertarianism, but we also honed in on other topics, especially education.
The debate was quite unusual compared to what you are used to from the Studio; less exact and much connected with the outlook on life. I think it's good to look at things from a different perspective from time to time. Write your opinions in the comments.

– Veronika Hurdová a.k.a. Raven Mother; authoress; blogger (http://www.krkavcimatka.cz/); traveler; anarcho-capitalist; a pacifist

title: Lecture for the private school PrimMat in Frýdek-Místek (Second half)
text: I gladly accepted the invitation of the private business high school PrimMat in Frýdek-Místek for two talks (this is a recording of the second one). For the first time in a long time, I came among students where no one knew ankap; despite this, interesting opinions about the functions of the state were voiced right away. I consider this discussion to be the more successful of the two for PrimMat.

title: Freeport Studio: The Emergence of Wealth and Inequality
text:
We've also heard the audience clamor for shorter videos that you can share as part of an argument that even socialists or people who don't want to watch a two-hour debate will watch.
We made a video about how wealth is actually created in society; and we show why the emergence of inequality is an inevitable and inherent part of that process. Feel free to leave your thoughts on the topic and format in the comments!

title: Lecture for the private school PrimMat in Frýdek-Místek (I. half)
text:
I gladly accepted the invitation of the private business high school PrimMat in Frýdek-Místek for two talks (this is the recording of the first of them); and for the first time in a long time I came among students where no one knew ankap.
The first three-quarters of an hour was a bit too confrontational for my taste and I didn't quite enjoy it; however, I think it was better after the break. Please write your opinions in the comments.

title: Freeport studio: On objectivism with Jan Mošovský
text:
I consider objectivism to be a very interesting philosophical trend. Although this is one path to libertarian ideas, there is a certain jealousy between anarcho-capitalists and objectivists; I believe that these are far more personal than principled disputes, which is a shame.
So I decided to invite the anarcho-objectivist (which is a very rare combination) Jan Mošovský to the Studio; maybe he will be able to convey objectivism to (especially anarchist) viewers in a strange way.

– Jan Mošovský; anarcho-objectivist; member of Students for Liberty

title: Ankap in the Church of the Holy Family in ČB (damaged sound especially in the first half)
text:
For the first time in my life I had the honor of giving a lecture in a church; moreover, it was a lecture for a grammar school, and a lot of students came there voluntarily in their free time. In my opinion, the result is certainly interesting.
Unfortunately, the video has damaged sound (especially in the first half). Originally I didn't even want to record it, but a lot of listeners asked me to. If you find the recording unlistenable from the beginning, try clicking halfway (it's a little better there).

title: Freedom of learning in the Cherubín teahouse
text: After the last lecture on anarcho-capitalism, we accepted a second invitation to the Cherubín teahouse, this time with Terezka; our topic was freedom of learning, alternative models of education, state monopoly in education and other related topics. We talked about self-directed education and children's desire to learn, which nothing can take away from them as reliably as a classical school.

title: Freeport Studio: Good Reputation, Slander, Lies and Freedom of Speech (Audio from 16:26)
text:
The first quarter hour of the stream has corrupted audio; however, if we cut it, YouTube will also delete livechat. Therefore, please start watching at 16:26; thank you!
We addressed freedom of speech quite recently in connection with Nazi salutes; but the topic is very broad and we have completely missed one essential part of it: the protection of good reputation, the spread of lies and slander and the harming of the innocent in their personal and economic lives.
We will cover these and other aspects of the issue you write about in this live broadcast!

title: Free Port Studio: About economic calculation with Martin Rota
text:
My favorite YouTuber Martin Rota - a well-known skeptic with critical thinking - accepted the invitation to the Freeport Studio. We debated about economic calculation and a lot of other topics, for example the climate crisis.
Martin is a very good debater, that's why I had a relaxed debate with him, I didn't have to be careful not to corner him, because he can defend his positions himself, which is a relief; that's why the unusual three hours flew by like nothing.

– Martin Rota; youtuber; creator of the Science Hammer, Explorers and Totally Retarded channels

title: Freeport Studio: Guns and Hospital Shooting
text:
In the Ostrava hospital, a man armed with an illegal weapon shot six people and injured two others; he finally ran away. The police caught up with him within a few hours, after which the person in question shot himself.
How would it turn out if someone else was armed in that waiting room? Gun bans make it impossible for those who respect them to defend themselves against people who ignore them. What are the advantages and disadvantages of an armed society?
Link with resources and lots of information:
https://www.gunfacts.info/

title: Symposion 2019 at the Jan Kepler Gymnasium
text: From an early age, each person consciously and unconsciously creates various bonds of various kinds with the environment; it is impossible to prevent something like that, it would probably not even be desirable. In general, we believe that everyone should have the freedom to make decisions about the ties in their life over time. Few people like organizations or sects that try to create strong emotional bonds in young children to be devoted to them before they are capable of effective critical thinking. However, those who themselves have been indoctrinated in this way typically do not find anything objectionable in such behavior; on the contrary, he himself often tends in good faith to do the same to other generations.

title: Studio of the Free Port: Digitization of state administration
text:
Digitization of state administration is a modern trending topic; the state has data about its citizens, but it keeps it in disconnected databases, sometimes even in paper files, and many officials could be replaced by web forms.
Doesn't that sound great? Yes, it certainly has its advantages. But what happens when this data begins to be massively machine-processed with the help of artificial intelligence? The results can be... interesting, surprising, but also disturbing.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: Questions and Answers
text: In today's episode, I answered questions from (not only) listeners; we got to children's rights, child labor, polycentric law and recreational nukes xD

title: Freeport Studio: Not an anarchist like an anarchist
text:
I have been trying to initiate a dialogue with collectivist anarchists for a long time; for years this effort was in vain. Finally, however, one with great willingness to debate contacted me! I find the debate surprisingly constructive and logical; moreover, it led to a match, which was something I had long (secretly) hoped for.
In addition, you can look forward to another (and perhaps bigger) debate with collectivist anarchists in the near future; you'll find out the details in time, I'm trying not to shout it yet xD

– anonymous collectivist anarchist

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: The Science
text:
One planned lecture at the (de)Centrála club became a regular cycle (every first Wednesday of the month) due to great interest; the latter to some extent follows the cycle Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis, although the format changes a little. I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.
At the lecture, we will talk about science and research in a free market environment. How and by whom could science be funded? Would basic research develop somehow, or only applied? Who would finance it if there were no state coercion? Would huge projects like Apollo and space research in general have a chance? What about people who only care about their current well-being but don't think ahead and don't care about progress?

title: Studio of the Free Port: About the labor market with Saša Uhlová
text:
Another extremely interesting guest of the Freeport Studio is the left-wing journalist Saša Uhlová. I find the conversation with her extremely beneficial and interesting; I'm grateful that we could talk and listen to each other in peace.
I think I learned a lot about the motivations and thinking of socialists and statists; a lot of things make better sense to me now. I recommend to all libertarians, try to watch the video with as much effort as possible to understand the opposing side.

– Saša Uhlová; leftist journalist; editor of A2alarm

title: Technology of freedom and unfreedom
text: Do new technologies threaten our freedom, or can they be used to preserve our freedom? This is a powerful tool; the question is who will have it in their hands. Centralized technologies can be a totalitarian tool; on the other hand, the decentralized ones on the way to freedom.

title: Freeport Studio: The Industrial Revolution and Automation
text:
The Industrial Revolution is often referred to as a period of savage capitalism in which people worked in bleak conditions, often at a very young age; that's kind of true, but not entirely true - it was thanks to the industrial revolution that child labor came to an end.
Another topic we address is automation and the phenomenon of machines taking people's jobs. This is a phenomenon that takes place not tens, not hundreds, but even thousands of years. Nevertheless, our society continues to grow rich and prosperous. How is that possible?

title: Freedom of learning in Moravia, October 2019
text:
Freedom of Learning – this time in the form of Michal Kandler and Urza – organized a stay in Moravia; we were hosted by Tomáš Pajonk, for which we owe him a big thank you! In the lecture, Urza presents the basic values and principles on which the Freedom of Learning stands; Michal then introduces the listeners to the individual projects on which we as SU are working. We will be happy if you also participate in the Freedom of Learning events; we will be glad if you support us too!

– Michal Kandler, member of the Freedom of Learning board

title: Freeport Studio: Nazi salutes and freedom of speech
text:
Doing a Nazi salute on a school trip to a concentration camp doesn't pay; in Poland it is punishable by up to three years in prison. Most people would probably agree that this is a pretty stupid idea; but where is the limit of free speech?
Property rights in a free market free society give relatively clear answers to this and other questions; nevertheless, certain ambiguities may arise in specific cases, which we discuss in the Free Port Studio.

title: Tereza and Urza in Svobodom, October 2019
text: I very much enjoy lecturing and debating at the Freedom of Learning stays in Svobodom; this time we organized a discussion about anarcho-capitalism with Terezka, who also came for part of the stay. We had quite an interesting discussion, this time quite calm and without major emotions. Although quite a few people came in the beginning, more people joined over time.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Biotechnology and Ethics
text:
One planned lecture at the (de)Centrála club became a regular cycle (every first Wednesday of the month) due to great interest; the latter to some extent follows the cycle Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis, although the format changes a little. I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.
Tereza will give a lecture today; the topic will be biotechnology and related ethical questions and the answers given to them by both the free market and regulators. CRISPR, biohacking, embedding technology into the human body, genetic modification... where are the boundaries? Technologically further than most people think; but what about the moral ones? How tempting is the evolution of the perfect soldier?

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: A Recap
text: In this piece, we recapitulated what anarcho-capitalism actually is, and we also talked about other anarchist schools; the broadcast of the program was interrupted for several months, but now it is coming back.

title: The Free Port Studio: On minarchism with Roman Kříž
text:
In the seventeenth episode of Freeport Studios, we finally had our first guest; he was minarchist Roman Kříž, founder of the Libertarian Institute and member of the Free Citizens Party. His approach to the spread of libertarian ideas is diametrically different from mine, but this does not stand in the way of mutual respect, because we both strive for the same thing.
As this is the first episode with a guest, I would appreciate it if you could comment on whether you think this format is better or worse than when we talk only with Terezka.

– Roman Cross; minarchist, head of the Libertarian Institute, member of the Free Citizens Party

title: About probability
text:
We know the term "probability" from mathematics and everyday life; at this level we can intuitively work with it. However, the problem arises when these planes begin to intersect; then mere conjectures and opinions can become proofs and facts in the eyes of others.
What is the probability that humans are causing climate change? Can such a thing be calculated? If so, how?

title: Freeport Studio: The Right to Self-Determination
text:
I think we talked about Barcelona a few times in the video and meant Madrid, for which we apologize (at least I realize I did, Urza; I don't know how Terezka).
Catalan separatists received heavy penalties for holding a referendum on Catalan independence, which contradicted the Spanish constitution. But what about the right to self-determination?
What about other territories seeking secession? How are Catalonia, Tibet or Kosovo related? We will also mention Crimea. But mainly we will look at separation and the right to self-determination from an anarcho-capitalist point of view.

title: Urza vs Bratříček
text: A few months ago, the YouTuber Bratříček started an ankap (and me) on his channel; his and my listeners responded to this and wished for our clash of opinions. And since we both cater to our subscribers, do you have our very long debate. Quite possibly this will not be the last debate.

title: Ankap in the Cherubín teahouse
text: I accepted an invitation to the cozy Cherubín teahouse, where I had the opportunity to give a lecture on ankapa next to the Buddha holding a pumpkin. The audience was very nice and calm; really nice place, so i guess this is not my last event there.

title: Scio conference on the future
text: I accepted an invitation to the Scio conference on the future; here is the record. I apologize for the noises in the audio track (but they are not there all the time), which is also the reason why the next debate that followed this introduction was not published (virtually nothing can be heard from it).

title: Freeport Studio: Taxes and Duties for Schools
text:
With our money, Berňák created the Taxes and Duties for Schools project, within the framework of which he will indoctrinate the youngest through the education system. A whole lot of economic and logical nonsense will be heard as part of the teaching of "financial literacy"; and a plurality of opinions is certainly not desirable where it would mean real criticism of the state.
In addition, you can listen to the introductory five-minute clip on the topic of monopoly; what about them on the free market?

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Freedom to Learn
text:
One planned lecture at the (de)Centrála club became a regular cycle (every first Wednesday of the month) due to great interest; the latter to some extent follows the cycle Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis, although the format changes a little. I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.
Come start the school year with a lecture on anarcho-capitalism on the appropriate topic; In my opinion, education and the educational system are absolutely key aspects of our society. Although I have already dedicated two lectures of the Anarcho-Capitalism cycle to education (and each was significantly different), I believe that it certainly deserves even more; and another new view.

title: Freeport Studio: Drought and subsidies in agriculture
text:
Drought has been a theme in recent years; we would also like to comment on it from the point of view of anarcho-capitalism and state distortion of the market. We will also discuss agricultural subsidies and their justification, or unjustifiability.
Among other things, we will also mention the current topic of the Koněv statue, and at the end there will be a popular five-minute short that we forgot about last time.

title: Mises Academy 2019: Anarcho-Capitalism
text: We were honored for the third time to accept an invitation to the Mises Academy of the Liberal Institute, where we were asked to give a lecture on anarcho-capitalism. The audience consisted primarily of people with some interest in libertarian ideas, to which we adapted the content and composition of the lecture. The topic was not only ankap, but also state propaganda in schools.

title: Mises Academy 2019: Defending the Indefensible
text:
It was with great joy that we accepted the third invitation to the summer Mises Academy of the Liberal Institute. In addition to the lecture on anarcho-capitalism, we discussed with all the participants the chapter "Rogue cop" from the book "Defending the Indefensible" by Walter Block, who I consider to be one of the most logical anarcho-capitalists.
There is no image from the debate, only audio, the quality of which is also infamous, for which I apologize, but I cleaned it up as best I could.

title: Studio of the Free Port: Freedom of learning and the new school year 2019 / 2020
text:
Another school year has begun, the Freeport is back in full operation; and our first video belonged precisely to the educational system, education and a certain overlap in the upbringing of children, which, in our opinion, is closely related to the kind of free society we will live in.
Write us your opinions in the comments, especially disagree; we will be happy If you find the video useful, please share it!

title: Urza at Worldschooling Retreat 2019
text:
Sorry for my English; but the only way to learn this better is just to do it xD

Worldschooling Retreat is a specific format for meeting supporters of self-directed learning, which is also its main focus – not a program of concrete activities, although it is usually varied. The main task for the organizers is to take care of the atmosphere of the safe and incentive environment in which children and adults have the opportunity to discover and search for their own self and without fear of being themselves.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: The Libertarian Constitution
text:
One planned lecture at the (de)Centrála club became a regular cycle (every first Wednesday of the month) due to great interest; the latter to some extent follows the cycle Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis, although the format changes a little. I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.
A libertarian constitution? An oxymoron, many would say. And they might be right. However, when I was given the task of creating one, I thought I would do the best I could and then see how happy I was with the result. He pleasantly surprised me; and besides, I realized other interesting connections during the creation, which I would like to share.

title: Tereza about drugs in the Nebe bar
text:
My wife Terezka and I again accepted the invitation to the Nebe bar, where we were to talk about drugs and weapons; unfortunately, I couldn't attend, so the discussion was only with Teresa, who did a great job, because the legislation surrounding drugs and the use of drugs in medicine (especially psychiatry) are her favorite topics.
Perhaps we will also organize a discussion or lecture on drugs and weapons at the same time, because there are a number of interesting parallels between the regulations of these two goods.

title: Freeport Studio: Vaccinating the Poor
text:
In the last pre-holiday video, Tereza addresses the question of who would pay for vaccinations for the poor in a stateless society on the free market.
Thanks for your patronage and enjoy your summer!
We will look forward to the next video - again with Urza.

title: Ankap in the Tucan cafe (Valmez)
text: When the owner of the Tucan cafe in Valmez learned that I was going to give a lecture at the gymnasium there, he did not hesitate and approached me to ask if I would also speak in his cafe, which I gladly accepted when I was already there. The audience reacted peacefully, the part with questions was calm and non-confrontational.

title: Lecture for František Palacký High School in Valmez
text: I was very pleased to be invited to Valemzu, not only because of the famous Moravian hospitality, but above all because of another opportunity to talk about anarcho-capitalism on the grounds of the school. Even former graduates came to see, the atmosphere was incredibly pleasant for me; and I think you as viewers will appreciate good questions from the audience!

title: Freeport Studio: State Against the Poor
text:
Today's topic was how the state harms the poor and weak, which it should declaratively defend. How do large corporations gain power at the expense of small businesses? How does the state harm employees?
You will learn this and much more in the tenth volume of the Free Port Studio. Write your opinions in the comments!

title: Jiří Vestfy, Martin Lux and Urza on various topics (read description)
text:
ATTENTION: Please read this description before deciding whether to watch the video.
Jiří Vestfy invited me for the second time as a guest on the Anežka and Jiřík channel; this time, however, I still had an opponent - a socialist.
At first we debated various economic issues, the function of money and the like; it subsequently turned out that the socialist in question was not describing the current world, but some futuristic concept of full automation of everything, which he did not say in advance.
Subsequently, we deviated from the topic and discussed everything from emotions to artificial intelligence.
If you are interested in a long-winded debate on many topics (not always economic or social), I definitely recommend; otherwise rather not.

title: Freeport studio: The results of the European elections and the double quality of food
text:
Euro elections are over, Babiš won again; and you will hear a short summary from us. What we are satisfied with, what we are not; and why? This will be followed by a popular five-minute show.
And then we will get into the main topic of today's episode, which is the so-called double quality of food! Are we the "trash bin of Europe" as some politicians claim? What can be done with such a condition? And is there anything to be done at all? Come think with us and write us your opinions in the comments!

title: Tereza on drugs for the Folou initiative in Brno
text: The Brno folou association organized a lecture on the prohibition of psychoactive substances and their potential use in science and medicine; and since they chose Tereza Urzová as the speaker, you can find the recording here, on the Free Port Channel.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: An Economic Calculus
text:
One planned lecture at the (de)Centrála club became a regular cycle (every first Wednesday of the month) due to great interest; the latter to some extent follows the cycle Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis, although the format changes a little. I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.
Economic calculation - or rather its impossibility in central planning - is a very neglected topic; I therefore decided to devote the entire lecture to her. I will explain it from several aspects (my favorite from the point of view of consumers, but also Mises's from the point of view of producers), in general and using examples. If you know any socialists, bring them along!

title: Night at Hollar 2019
text: IKSŽ students invited me to a discussion about anarcho-capitalism as part of their Night on Hollar with the subtitle Limits of Anarchy; although it was nice outside, an interesting debate broke out in the lecture room. I will be very happy if you add your opinions to the comments.

title: Freeport Studio: Euro Elections 2019
text:
Since you've been asking us a lot lately about who to vote for in the Euro elections, we decided to make a video on this topic. We discuss a number of candidates there from a libertarian point of view; we even address the question of whether it is worth going to the elections at all.
But definitely don't take our opinions as dogma; even the two of us don't agree on a lot of things, so we expect a lot of libertarians to have even more completely different views.

title: Interview for the student magazine Ars
text:
The student magazine Ars asked me for a video interview; I agreed, and in return they gave me permission to publish it on the Freeport Channel.
Although the questions are related to ankap, they have a certain overlap in other aspects of life, for example faith and the like.

title: Freeport Studio: EU, Russia, Propaganda and Information War
text:
In the eighth volume of the Free Port Studio, we deal with the information and propaganda war between the EU and Russia; we speculate on the possibilities of further development after a possible Czexit and think about what it actually means when a state falls under someone's "sphere of influence".
How to fight misinformation? But above all, how not to fight so that it is not counterproductive? And who should pay for this fight?

title: Education Night 2019
text: I accepted the invitation to the Night of Education event in Olomouc; I had the opportunity to discuss with the students of the Faculty of Education, which was certainly interesting. Two listeners were very confrontational, on the other hand, I think that the vast majority left with an interesting topic to think about, which I was also convinced by the interviews with those in question after the end of the event.

title: Freeport Studio: The Venus Project
text:
In the seventh part of the Freeport Studio, we deal with economic calculation, cybersocialism and The Venus Project. Why does the resource-based economy not work? What is economic calculation good for? Why does socialism inevitably fail? What is the main function of money and prices? You can hear that and much more in this video.
At the end, we focus on how people perceive entrusting their personal data to the state versus a private entity.

title: Whistleblower - hero or crackpot?
text: I accepted the invitation to the debate of the Endowment Fund against Corruption; it was a two-hour panel discussion with eight people, so I didn't say much. Nevertheless, quite interesting opinions were heard from people who work on the anti-corruption law; unfortunately, he may soon expand the Czech legislation.

title: Freeport Studio: Planned Obsolescence (Kurvítka)
text:
In the sixth volume of the Free Port Studio, we deal with planned obsolescence components (colloquially called "kurvítka") built into products whose lifespan is to be reduced in order to stimulate consumption and ensure further purchase. Do manufacturers actually use these practices? Why? What economic sense does it make? And why does it usually no longer make sense to repair appliances?
We will be happy for all your comments on the video, comment on the content and form!

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Right to Live, Right to Die
text:
One planned lecture at the (de)Centrála club became a regular cycle (every first Wednesday of the month) due to great interest; the latter to some extent follows the cycle Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis, although the format changes a little. I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.
I won't be lecturing this time, but Tereza! The topic will be abortion, euthanasia and other issues related to the right to make decisions about one's own life. Everything will be discussed from the point of view of the NAP, but at the same time, Tereza will also analyze the possible differences between the NAP and real free market law, which in these areas could most likely manifest themselves in a stateless society...

title: Freeport Studio: Housing Crisis
text: In the fifth part of the Free Port Studio, we deal with the housing crisis, rent prices, expensive housing in Prague, but also the expropriation of apartments in Berlin. We will be glad for your opinions in the comments, as well as for any feedback!

title: Ankap for the Folou initiative in Brno
text: I gladly accepted the invitation of the Folou initiative and came to give a lecture in Brno; the lecture was very successful, the participation was several times higher than expected. However successful I was in the presentation itself, in my opinion I failed a little in the debate, but judge for yourself.

title: Ankap and social "policy" for Caritas Voš
text: I accepted an invitation to give a lecture for Caritas, a higher professional school of social work in Olomouc; and I must say it was quite a challenge. Come and talk about the free market to people who are studying social work, so they are clear enough that certain things just have to be done by the state. I think I took the whole thing quite mildly, sensibly, and got a lot of people thinking; I liked how some initially hostile faces in the audience melted over time.

title: Liberty Evening (SfL) in Olomouc
text:
At the Liberty Evening in Olomouc, Lucka Komárková and I talked about the basics of ankap; the audience was thoughtful, so interesting questions were asked. I'm still fine-tuning the lecture on the basics of anarcho-capitalism, so you've never heard two alike, but if you already know ankap, you probably won't learn anything new.

– Lucie Komárková; author of articles for the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of Students for Liberty

title: Freeport Studio: Patriotism and support of local entrepreneurs
text:
In the fourth part of the Studio, we dealt with patriotism, support of local entrepreneurs, customs and protectionism of all kinds! Write us your thoughts on the topic in the comments; you can also suggest other topics...
Unfortunately, I managed to accidentally burn the sound; I'll do better next time, maybe I'll hit the golden mean.

title: Urza in Svobodom, February 2019
text: It was a great honor for me to speak at the Svobodome, where we organized another winter stay with the Freedom of Learning. The very informal discussion mainly concerned the differences between oppression by the state and the influence of powerful companies on the free market. Can something like this be compared? The debate was quite emotional.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Polycentric Law
text:
One planned lecture at the (de)Centrála club became a regular cycle (every first Wednesday of the month) due to great interest; the latter to some extent follows the cycle Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis, although the format changes a little. I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.
The topic of the lecture and discussion is polycentric law in the free market. Although I have already lectured on free-market justice and law enforcement, there was quite a lot of theory in the lectures, within which perhaps the answer to the questions: "Who and according to what law will decide disputes without the state? And who will enforce these decisions?" Let's try to model several such hypothetical situations...

title: Freeport Studio: Freedom (on) the Internet
text:
In the third part of the Free Port Studio, we deal with the issue of freedom on the Internet; in particular we will deal with the EU copyright directive and its problematic articles 11 and 13, but we will not stop there xD
Hopefully we've fixed the audio glitch, but surely our recordings will suffer from a whole host of other flaws, so any feedback would be appreciated; and when we solve all the problems in the recording, we will start streaming in time!

title: Freeport Studio: Migration
text:
In the second part of the Free Port Studio, we address the issue of migration in the state and on the free market; and also a lot of other topics we get to because of the constant digressions xD
Hopefully we've fixed the audio glitch, but surely our recordings will suffer from a whole host of other flaws, so any feedback would be appreciated; and when we solve all the problems in the recording, we will start streaming in time!

title: Freeport Studio: Introduction
text:
The Freeport Studio is starting to "broadcast"!
We put the word "broadcast" in quotation marks because we are currently recording, we are not interactive, and you can certainly find a lot of other shortcomings. Getting a studio up and running is a harder task than one might expect, so please be patient with us, but also be sure to write all (especially negative) feedback; we want and need to improve!
Sorry for the audio skipping, we don't know the reason, we will fix it.

title: Debate Club: Urza and Zálom about Ankap and Objectivism
text: As a huge fan of Debate Club, having followed it since its very beginnings, I was delighted to be invited back; I debated with Luboš Zálom about anarcho-capitalism and objectivism. I am posting the entry on the Freeport Channel with the creator's kind permission; you can visit the website of the debate club here: https://debatniklub.webnode.cz/; YouTube channel here: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC9sFfo8pVvYGikaeZdkllTQ.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: The Consequences of Drug Prohibition
text:
One planned lecture at the (de)Centrála club became a regular cycle (every first Wednesday of the month) due to great interest; the latter to some extent follows the cycle Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis, although the format changes a little. I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.
I will not be lecturing on drug prohibition this time, but Tereza! He will talk about alcohol prohibition and its consequences, but also about how the war on drugs has similar effects on the whole society. With regard to her specialization - medicine - she will also focus on the possible use of drugs in medicine and how the current stigmatization hinders them. Substances that we have known for decades have still not been sufficiently explored...

title: Debate on education at ScioŠkole
text: In the name of Freedom of Learning, I accepted an invitation to a panel discussion at the ScioSchool in Dejvice; we talked about different methods of education; the panel discussion was followed by the division of the panelists into individual rooms, where those who were interested in their opinions went to talk with each of them. I think both debates were useful and interesting.

title: Ankap in the Nový svět bar in Zlín
text: This time I came to give a lecture on the basics of ankap in Zlín; I took it a little differently than ever before (but of course I am based on what the audience already knows). The lecture was followed by a really long and quite nourishing debate; perhaps more valuable than the lecture itself.

title: Debate club: Urza, Joch and Semin about ankap
text: As a huge fan of Debate Club, having followed it since its very beginnings, I was delighted to be invited back; we debated with Mr. Joch and Mr. Semín about anarcho-capitalism. I am posting the entry on the Freeport Channel with the creator's kind permission; you can visit the website of the debate club here: https://debatniklub.webnode.cz/; YouTube channel here: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC9sFfo8pVvYGikaeZdkllTQ.

title: Debate Club: Questionnaire
text: As a huge fan of Debate Club, having followed it since its very beginnings, I was delighted to be invited too; we started with a questionnaire about anarcho-capitalism. I am posting the entry on the Freeport Channel with the creator's kind permission; you can visit the website of the debate club here: https://debatniklub.webnode.cz/; YouTube channel here: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC9sFfo8pVvYGikaeZdkllTQ.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Inequality
text:
One planned lecture at the (de)Centrála club became a regular cycle (every first Wednesday of the month) due to great interest; the latter to some extent follows the cycle Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis, although the format changes a little. I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.
We will discuss an often inflected topic with anarcho-capitalism - inequality. Where does it come from? Is it possible to somehow remove her from the world? Why do socialists and all other egalitarians constantly focus only on wealth inequality? Are inequalities bad at all? Should we fight them? And if so, is the state the right fighter? You will learn the answers to these and many other questions at this lecture!

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: Free Speech and Public Space
text: In this piece, we focused on two seemingly unrelated, but actually closely connected topics: freedom of speech and public space. How are these two things related?

title: Lecture for the Teplice High School
text: I gladly accepted the invitation to the lecture at the Teplice High School; this surprised me with a seriously beautiful building, but above all, one of the best audiences I've met so far. Really good questions were asked and the discussion took place in a civilized, decent manner, without unnecessary emotions; after all, judge for yourself.

title: Anarcho-capitalism on the front lines: Firemen
text: In this part, we focused on firefighters in a stateless company. How would the market solve the problem of black passengers? What would be the availability of firefighting services outside the big cities?

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: Culture
text: In this piece, we focused on culture and art in anarcho-capitalism. Would any works of art be created at all without state support? What about the protection of historical monuments? Who would protect them in a free market?

title: Lecture for the Libomudravna association
text: The association of philosophers Libomudravna from Hradec Králové invited Mr. and Mrs. Urza to lecture on anarcho-capitalism; the organizer and I agreed on a very short lecture, which served rather as an introduction to the subsequent debate. The discussion was really beneficial and the questions were very interesting; after all, judge for yourself.

title: Freeport 2018
text:
Towards the end of the year, Terezka and I made a little balance. What happened in Freeport? And what will happen next? Stay with us and you will know everything. If our work makes sense to you and you want to support it, continue to https://opristavu.urza.cz/.
Thanks a lot and happy new year!

title: Urza Against the Current
text: With the kind permission of Dan Tržil, I am publishing on the Free Port Channel a recording of his program Proti Proudu, where he invited me as a guest; he asked interesting questions and we had a good discussion, even if we were interrupted during the siren test. I will be glad if you write your views on this interview in the comments.

title: Debate on education at the Jan Kepler High School
text: After a successful debate on anarchy, I was immediately invited again to debate at the Jan Kepler Gymnasium; this time about education. My opponent was (for the second time) Bob Kartous, however this time we debated in a much more friendly and less confrontational spirit; not to mention the students asked good questions.

title: Teresa in the Reefer Madness debate
text: Students for Liberty organized a debate in Ostrava about the pro-criminal anti-drug policy and its effects on our society; in addition to Tereza, the following participated: Jan Horák (Renarkon), Jakub Frydrych (Director of the National Drug Control Center) and Lukáš Bechyně (Say NO to drugs – Say YES to life).

title: Debate on anarchy at the Jan Kepler High School
text: The students of Jan Kepler Gymnasium invited me to a panel discussion at Symposion 2018; the topic was supposed to be anarchy, left-wing anarchists were also invited, but they refused, so in the end I debated alone with Ilona Švihlíková. I think that it was still an interesting panel with good questions from the audience, but above all from the presenters, who confided in me before the discussion that they had never moderated anything before, but they definitely performed their roles well.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: The Road to Anarcho-Capitalism
text: In this part, we focused on the transition to an anarcho-capitalist society from today's state-run society. How to achieve something like this? How long can such a transformation take?

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Intellectual Property
text:
One planned lecture at the (de)Centrála club became a regular cycle (every first Wednesday of the month) due to great interest; the latter to some extent follows the cycle Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis, although the format changes a little. I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.
The topic of the lecture and discussion will be intellectual property, which loosely follows the principle of non-aggression, which we talked about last time. How does intellectual property relate to property rights? And how might its enforcement differ today and in a stateless society? The lecture will require full attention, as the issue of intellectual property in anarcho-capitalism is often misinterpreted.

title: Interview for Svobodné universum: Forward to the past
text:
The lovely Martina Kociánová did this great interview with me, in which she proved to be a very capable presenter. With her kind permission, I am then publishing the recording on the Freeport Channel. You can find all parts of the interview (here they are combined into one) here:
https://www.kupredudominulosti.cz/host/urza/

title: Anarcho-capitalism in Rakovník
text: Petr Smidrkal, one of the generous funders of the Free Port, invited me to a lecture in his hometown Rakovník; this time I tried to introduce people to anarcho-capitalism in a slightly different way than before. And I think it was successful; after all, judge for yourself!

title: Kinolab Film Festival: Folk Art in Cyberspace
text: Kinolab.cz invited me to the panel discussion "Folk art in cyberspace"; the central theme was intellectual property. In the debate, I brought anarcho-capitalist views between the three lawyers, which was quite unconventional; the discussion was not confrontational, but I found it very interesting (especially thanks to my opponents).

title: Interview for the program Štrunc!
text:
E15 (info.cz) invited me to their program Štrunc! They were kind enough to allow me to publish the recording of the interview on the Freeport Channel, for which I thank them here. Above all, however, anarcho-capitalism is becoming known to the wider public; for that, thank you to everyone who participates or supports us.
#makeAncapMainstream

title: Jana Kozlová and Urza on the state, laws and education
text: Nonviolent communication lecturer Jana Kozlova and I differed on the law prohibiting physical punishment for children, which was presented in France; although none of us physically punishes children, neither of us likes it, but I am convinced that the state should not interfere in such a thing at all.

title: Lecture for Budějovická Gymnasium
text: After two years, I was invited again to the Budějovická Gymnasium; but I did not enter the same river a second time. Whereas anarcho-capitalism was unknown there last time, this time the awareness was much deeper; and there were even sympathizers and even readers of my book among the students. #makeAncapMainstream

title: Students for Liberty: Is the State Legitimate? Backa versus Urza
text: Students for Liberty: How are taxes different from protection money? Is it legitimate for the state to force citizens to do something they have not consented to? We will seek answers to these and other questions in the context of the debate between the propagator of anarcho-capitalism Urza and the lawyer Jakub Backa as part of the Liberty Evening.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: The Non-Aggression Principle (NAP)
text:
One planned lecture at the (de)Centrála club became a regular cycle (every first Wednesday of the month) due to great interest; the latter to some extent follows the cycle Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis, although the format changes a little. I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.
The topic of the lecture and discussion will be the increasingly asked and mentioned non-aggression principle (NAP). We will explain in detail what it actually is, what it is good for, but also mainly what it is definitely not good for; we will also touch on topics such as psychological violence or animal rights, about which there are heated discussions in connection with the NAP.

title: Lecture for JiPiCe
text: The lecture on anarcho-capitalism was also requested by the Pirate Party; although I am not exactly a fan of them, I believe that it is always good to have a dialogue, so I gladly accepted. In the end, Terezka also lectured with me; you can watch its premiere in this recording.

title: On a knife's edge: Democracy
text: Parlamentní Listy and TV Praha invited me to the program Na ostří nože; my opponent in the duel was Lukáš Jelínek and the topic was democracy. You can watch the full uncut version of the entire debate here; you saw less than half in the Parliamentary Papers.

title: Talk at HAD KLUB
text: HAD KLUB is a student club in Liberec, where I was invited to discuss anarcho-capitalism. There was a great atmosphere in the place and I have to say that some of the best questions ever were asked; it's rare that there are so many people sitting in the audience with such a desire to learn something.

title: Anarchist party at Dark Velvet
text: Cafebar Dark Velvet organized an anarchist evening; in addition to the author's reading, debates and a bit of poetry, my short lecture with a subsequent debate was also on the program. The recording is only of this part of the evening; however, it was certainly not the last event of this type in Dark Velvet, next time you can come too!

title: Urza in Svobodom, October 2018
text: It was a great honor for me to speak at the Svobodome, where we organized an autumn stay with the Freedom of Learning. The speech and the subsequent debate naturally concerned primarily freedom in education, but subsequently also anarcho-capitalism as a whole and the possibilities of how far we can go with freedom in individual branches of human activity; does it make sense to want freedom for yourself, but at the same time deny it to others?

title: Urza versus Antonín Dolák at Stigura about monopolies
text: In the last debate with Stigur, we did not have time to discuss monopolies and agreed to do a sequel; Stigur (https://www.twitch.tv/stigur_cz) invited my critic Antonín Dolák (https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCetB9vSWnvoUV3s_OOv0BHA?view_as=subscriber) to it and he himself decided on the role of moderator.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: Law Enforcement
text: In this piece, we tackled one of the most difficult topics, namely free market law enforcement; we dealt with what happens if someone damages someone else and refuses to take any responsibility for it.

title: Interview for Urban XP
text: I was approached by Petr Höhn with his Urban XP project, where he conducts interesting interviews with various people; I was very happy to answer his questions about anarcho-capitalism. He was kind enough to allow me to upload the result to the Freeport Channel.

title: Synergeticum: The Different Faces of Anarchy III
text: The collectivist anarchist Tibor Moravčík invited me to his radio show; and I find it extremely interesting to discuss anarchy from two completely opposite perspectives and approaches. Anarcho-capitalists use logic, collectivist anarchists more emotion; before i would have said logic is just better, today i just don't know. I am an anarcho-capitalist, but I respect anarchists of other schools.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: A School for Authoritarianism
text:
One planned lecture at the (de)Centrála club became a regular cycle (every first Wednesday of the month) due to great interest; the latter to some extent follows the cycle Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis, although the format changes a little. I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.
The topic of the lecture and discussion will be education and education for obedience, discipline, authoritarianism and totalitarianism. In contrast to the lecture on education in Parallel Polis, I will deal in detail throughout with the mechanisms by which state education leads people to conformity and indoctrinates them with statism; and not only on a conscious basis, which I have already talked about so many times, but above all subliminally.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: Judiciary and Law
text: In this piece, we addressed one of the most difficult topics; specifically, the free market judiciary; we discussed polycentric law, but not yet its enforcement, which you can look forward to next time.

title: Lecture at the Eccentric Club
text: Eccentric Club is a very interesting and free place; I've been a member of this club for a while, a few weeks ago I was asked to give a talk on the basics of anarcho-capitalism with a discussion, which I was really happy to accept. The discussion was ultimately (and during) very interesting, which you can judge for yourself.

title: Ankap in Bar Nebe (punk debate over beer)
text: Markéta Čermáková organized a discussion about anarcho-capitalism in the Nebe bar; and thanks to her incredible enthusiasm for the cause, we gladly accepted! The talk was very punk, the listeners drank and hollered, so the discussion looked like that in places; anyway, it was an interesting evening. Watch the video at your own risk xD

title: Mises Academy 2018: Peace with drugs?
text:
I was honored to be invited to the Liberal Institute's Mises Academy, where I gave two lectures.
This is a record of the second of them - on drugs; the audience was overwhelmingly made up of libertarians who already know a lot about the given topic, to which the lecture was tailored. You can find almost the same lecture in the list of videos "Anarchocapitalism in Polis" under the title "Anarchocapitalism, part eight: Drugs" (for those who have seen it, this one may be a waste of time).

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: The Environment
text: In this piece we focused on the environment; we also discussed negative externalities, waste, contamination of the landscape and various catastrophic scenarios xD

title: Mises Academy 2018: Anarcho-Capitalism
text:
I was honored to be invited to the Liberal Institute's Mises Academy, where I gave two lectures.
This is the record of the first of these – on anarcho-capitalism; the audience consisted of people interested in freedom and libertarianism, to which the lecture was tailored. A more detailed treatment of this topic aimed at a wider public can be found in the list of videos "Anarchocapitalism in Polis".

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Human Rights
text:
One planned lecture at the (de)Centrála club became a regular cycle (every first Wednesday of the month) due to great interest; the latter to some extent follows the cycle Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis, although the format changes a little. I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.
The topic of the lecture and discussion will be human rights in anarcho-capitalism. How do anarcho-capitalists approach them when only property rights are sacred to them? Does the non-aggression principle (NAP) protect human rights? And to what extent? What is the difference between positive and negative rights? Are positive rights "better"? If you are interested in answers - not only to these questions - do not hesitate to come!

title: Lecture for SŠINFIS in Pilsen
text: Students invited me to the Secondary School of Informatics and Financial Services; and since the teachers didn't pick it up (which happens in most cases), it was a pleasure to get them to talk about anarcho-capitalism. On the one hand, I took a trip to my beloved Pilsen, but above all, lectures in schools are the highest priority for me.

title: Anarcho wedding
text:
We got engaged in the air, said our YES (and recorded it in the blockchain) on the ground... and a little bit in the water; at the end of the video you will then see the bride spitting fire.
We love life, we love each other; we are even happier together than before, besides we complement each other wonderfully, but above all we learn from each other. We want to share this endless joy with you, our dear viewers.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: Linear Infrastructure (Roads)
text: In this part, we devoted ourselves to linear infrastructure, especially roadways, or the popular question: "Who would build roads without the state?"

title: On anarcho-capitalism with Matthias
text:
Matthias – one of the authors of Stok Freeport and the Ludwig von Mises Institute – wanted to discuss anarcho-capitalism with me; I was very happy to accept his offer. Unfortunately, the quality of the recording is not the best, for which I apologize; and I will be happy for any feedback on the content (we will definitely work on the technique).

– Matthias; anarcho-capitalist; author of Stok Freeport and the Ludwig von Mises Institute

title: Synergeticum: The Different Faces of Anarchy II
text: The collectivist anarchist Tibor Moravčík invited me to his radio show; and I find it extremely interesting to discuss anarchy from two completely opposite perspectives and approaches. Anarcho-capitalists use logic, collectivist anarchists more emotion; before i would have said logic is just better, today i just don't know. I am an anarcho-capitalist, but I respect anarchists of other schools.

title: We about the Scouts about AKTP
text:
The spies - Martin Rota and Patrik Kořenář - made a video about the AKTIP case; we more or less agree with them, but we would probably solve the problem in a significantly different way. The interesting thing is that they themselves see that the state is failing here, but instead of accepting it, they call for a state solution. Statism is pervasive and unfortunately affects even skeptics; and to some extent actually anarchists.

– Tereza Urzová; creator of Freeport; head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of Students for Liberty

title: Urza at TEDx
text: It was a huge honor to give a talk on anarcho-capitalism at TEDx; and the huge challenge was the new format – I had to fit in 18 minutes. Having never done anything like this before, it didn't go perfectly; and next time I would do it a little differently. Either way it was a great experience; and I hope I get the chance to do it again and better.

title: Urza and Jiří Vestfy (not only) about anarcho-capitalism
text: Jiří Vestfy published his criticism of anarcho-capitalism in his channel Anežka and Jiřík; and because she was reasonable, we agreed to debate. In the end, she didn't really stick to the topic, but especially towards the end we (especially me) digressed a bit. I hope you don't mind; please let me know if you welcome such a format or what you think about it.

title: Anarcho-capitalism in České Budějovice
text: I gladly accepted the invitation to another lecture on the foundations of anarcho-capitalism; this time I came to České Budějovice. Again, I tried to talk about the same topic in a slightly different way, so I will be happy for your feedback. I try to analyze people's reactions and adjust my performances accordingly.

title: Polycentric law and its enforcement
text: Classical liberal Andrej Poleščuk invited me to his stream, where we discussed decentralized law and its enforcement. The debate is very advanced, we go into much more detail than I have ever allowed myself to in lectures, so it is more of a listening session for people who already know a lot about anarcho-capitalism; I would like to point out that for those who are just getting to know anarcho-capitalism, it can be uninteresting, unnecessarily detailed and possibly even misleading, because in the discussion we build on a lot of things that you may not even know.

title: Anarcho-capitalism on the front lines: Monopoly
text: In this part, we focused on monopolies, cartels and "unfair" economic competition in the free market; how could we defend against them without a state?

title: 4D: No smoking
text:
Four reasons why the state should not ban smoking in restaurants!

– Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD); creator of Freeport; head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of Students for Liberty

title: Synergeticum: The Different Faces of Anarchy I
text: The collectivist anarchist Tibor Moravčík invited me to his radio show; and I find it extremely interesting to discuss anarchy from two completely opposite perspectives and approaches. Anarcho-capitalists use logic, collectivist anarchists more emotion; before i would have said logic is just better, today i just don't know. I am an anarcho-capitalist, but I respect anarchists of other schools.

title: Anarcho-capitalism in the Brno Impact Hub
text: Svobodní invited me to give a lecture at the Impact Hub in Brno about the very foundations of anarcho-capitalism. Although I did not expect that many people would come, because libertarian lectures are not so popular in Moravia, they filled the whole large hall, about a hundred of them came; and many of them didn't know ankap at all, they came to me after the lecture and said that they are becoming interested because it makes sense to them, which is the best appreciation of my work.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: Drugs
text: In this part, we focused on drugs and their regulation. What would happen if all regulations disappeared and drugs could be bought without any restrictions?

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: Monopolization
text:
One planned lecture at the (de)Centrála club became a regular cycle (every first Wednesday of the month) due to great interest; the latter to some extent follows the cycle Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis, although the format changes a little. I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.
The topic of both the lecture and the discussion will be something that, in connection with the growing popularity of anarcho-capitalism, is increasingly coming under fire, namely monopolization in the free market. Will monopolies and cartel agreements arise without state supervision and antitrust authorities? How does the Austrian school of economics view monopoly? What about mainstream economics? Without a state, do we have anything to fear? If you are interested in answers - not only to these questions - do not hesitate to come!

title: SKAV: What values does the school teach?
text: As many of you probably know, as part of my anarcho-capitalist and libertarian activities, I focus primarily on education. As a member of Freedom of Learning, I represent the Freedom of Learning Association in SKAV (Permanent Conference of Associations in Education). SKAV organizes Round Tables (panel discussions), of which I found this one absolutely essential, so I am making its recording available. Please note that this is far more an educational and professional debate than a libertarian one, so it's different than what you're used to.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: Weapons
text: In this part, we focused on weapons and their regulations. What would happen if all regulations disappeared and guns and ammunition could be purchased without any restrictions?

title: Interview for Ecofin
text:
Lukáš Kovanda interviewed me for Ecofin; I think he did very well, but judge for yourself. It's about bringing anarcho-capitalism to people who may never have heard of it, which is something I'm still learning, but I'm making progress; I will be very happy for any (especially negative) feedback.
I am publishing the recording of the interview on the Free Port Channel with the kind permission of Lukáš Kovanda; Thanks.

title: ART ECON high school lecture
text: I gladly accepted the invitation of the manager of the ART ECON private school to give a lecture about free education and its connections with anarcho-capitalism. Although it didn't say much to some students, it clearly appealed to others, they came to chat even after the lecture and asked about this channel; I salute them!

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: Wars and the Military
text: In this part, we focused on the army and warfare. How will the anarchist territory hold up in the fight against the state? And how will wars be fought in the future? Why is it so easy to wage war nowadays?

title: Polycentric versus centralized law
text: Classical liberal Andrej Poleščuk invited me to his stream, where we discussed centralized and decentralized law. At first we dealt with classic evolutionary arguments, but towards the end we got to some interesting analyses; in the record you will also find a theoretical justification for why polycentric legal systems converge to the NAP (however, it is a very advanced chapter, we go deeper than in the Polis judiciary lecture).

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: Cryptocurrencies
text: In this part, we focused on cryptocurrencies. We were not so much technical, but more concerned with the economic side of things; and cryptocurrencies as the money of the future.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: The Labor Market
text: In this part, we focused on the labor market without regulations. Who do they actually help? And who does employee protection protect? On the contrary, who does it harm?

title: Anarcho-Capitalism: General Basics for Everyone
text: I was contacted by the owner of the Centrála club - which some jokingly and aptly call Decentralá with respect to the other program - and asked for a lecture: Ankap for beginners. If you have no idea what this is all about, this lecture explains the absolute basics of this school of thought. I tried to lecture in such a way that absolutely everyone could understand; I hope I managed to do it at least in general.

title: Conference Education for the Future
text: Mensa CR, the World of Education, the National Institute for Further Education and the Fraus Publishing House jointly organized the Education for the Future conference, which took place on Friday, March 2, 2018 and Saturday, March 3, 2018 in Prague. I gladly accepted their invitation to lecture as well; I chose the complete separation of education from the state as a topic, which probably won't surprise anyone.

title: Anarcho-capitalism on the front lines: Healthcare
text: In this part, we focused on free market healthcare, pharmaceutical production, regulations in medicine and healthcare certifications.

title: Urza in Stigur's Darth Night Show
text: Pavel Stigur Novák watched my stream with Zvědátory; then he made an unflattering comment on him on his show. I offered him if he would do the same, if I could oppose him; he agreed. The stream ended up being quite beneficial, we focused on a few topics in depth, which is actually great. We discussed teachers and education, then the death cycle of democracy and how state protection of the irresponsible creates more irresponsible. I think the footage is definitely worth watching.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part Nineteen: In the Broader Context...
text: How to go from a huge omnivorous state to anarcho-capitalism? And where does the road definitely not lead? We will also talk about this at the last regular lecture of this cycle. Many of you have rightly noted that most of the lectures were "one-of-a-kind" in the sense of applying the same principle to various branches of human endeavor. I would like to clarify and formulate this principle in general terms; especially for those who didn't notice it. And finally, we will place anarcho-capitalism in some context of the other anarchist schools, of which there are many and about which you will certainly hear a lot more.

title: Scouts: Anarcho-Capitalism
text:
My favorite YouTuber (and probably the only one I follow) Martin Rota invited me to the program Zvědátoři, which he has been doing for a long time with Patrik Kořenář; the topic was - how else but - anarcho-capitalism!
And I have to say, it was a great discussion for me; Martin Rota is a logician, he has great arguments and overall he is one of the best opponents. Plus, I think live is even better than online. So I hope you enjoy watching the video at least half as much as I enjoyed making it.

title: Lecture for the Gymnasium on the Victory Plain
text: I accepted an invitation to a lecture at Gymnasium Na Vítězné pláni to tell the students there something about anarcho-capitalism. A surprisingly large number of students came to the lecture; although they had many lectures to choose from, there weren't enough chairs in the end, so they had to sit on the furniture. They asked great questions; I consider the whole debate to be very constructive. Above all, in the end it turned out that almost everyone learned something new!

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: Social Issues
text: In this piece, we addressed the devastating effects of the welfare state on our society; and how would we be without him?

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Volume Eighteen: The Army
text: As difficult as the free market provision of justice and internal security is, defense against an external enemy and, by extension, international relations represent by far the greatest challenge for a stateless anarcho-capitalist society. Can free people without a state defend themselves against aggressive conquerors? And if not, what will happen in the conquered territory? How does the control of a conquered anarchist territory differ from the control of a conquered state? Can the common survive without the state? Minarchists do not believe this; anarcho-capitalists do. Don't miss a lecture with a discussion on this interesting topic.

title: Anarcho-capitalism on the front lines: Education
text: In this part, we focused on education and its complete separation from the state, but also its function as a powerful propaganda tool.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Volume Seventeen: Law Enforcement
text: If the lecture on the judiciary was controversial, it is doubly so for law enforcement. While last time we only dealt with disputes in which both parties more or less cooperate, this time we will talk about cases of criminals and desperadoes who violate property rights and actively try to avoid the administration of justice. How will the free market deal with them? Isn't the state really needed here? This lecture is one of the three most "advanced" of the series and is a bone of contention between the anarcho-capitalists and the minarchists; so don't miss it.

title: Launch of the book Anarchocapitalism
text:
Something I believe in has become more real and tangible because of me; I was able to celebrate this alongside my beloved wife, surrounded by people who believe in the same ideals, peacefully participate in their promotion, and without whom what is happening right now could never have happened, because without their hard work and support, all my efforts would have meant nothing. Thanks; thanks to all of you.

– Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD); creator of Freeport; head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of Students for Liberty

title: Senseless imprisonment
text: An 18-year-old girl got behind the wheel, recorded and streamed her actions until she killed her own sister live. There is no need to comment on how devastating this idea was, after all, she herself described it very aptly: "I killed my own sister just because I wanted to look cool." What about her now? Six years in prison! That's not much for a wasted life. But what good does it do?

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: Economic Calculation
text: In this part, we focused on economic calculation, its impossibility in central planning and some principles of the Austrian school of economics.

title: CZPodcast
text: Roman Pichlík and Jiří Fabián invited me to their podcast; although the latter is almost always about programming, this time they wanted to talk about anarcho-capitalism, which of course pleased me and I gladly accepted. I really enjoyed getting to know them; it was interesting. In the discussion I was opposed by Karel Holub, whom I appreciate for his calm insight. I wish everyone a pleasant listening experience!

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: Money and Banking
text: In this installment we covered money and banking; we also touched lightly on economic calculation and the function of money.

title: Jail, lose for all
text: On my way to work, I heard a message on the radio that I wanted to respond to immediately, so this recording was created; it was taken directly in the car, so I apologize for the slightly worse quality, but I think you can understand them. Two people committed something that was unfortunately not a victimless crime and were also guilty in terms of the NAP; on the other hand, I don't even agree with their imprisonment. Why? You will find out when you play the video.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: An Introduction
text: In this work, we focused on the roots of anarcho-capitalism, its foundations and general principles; we also lightly honed in on specific topics, which we will certainly get to in more detail over time.

title: Cryptocurrencies and Anarcho-Capitalism
text: I accepted the invitation of the Prague Business Club for a lecture and discussion about cryptocurrencies and anarcho-capitalism. Interesting debates accompanied the whole evening; I would like to share a recording of one of its parts with you here. Unfortunately, the picture and sound starts from a third of the recording, for which I apologize; the reasons are bizarre (related to the line: "Teresa, please turn off that microphone." xD). I wish you a pleasant listening.

title: NAP and cryptocurrency ownership
text: It was an honor to speak at the Bitcoin is Retro! Slovak Parallel Polis, Progressbar and Students for Liberty organized a great event and asked me to give a lecture on a purely theoretical topic, which really suited me - an old theoretician. Then followed a great discussion with an ending that you can look forward to (probably for a few months).

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part Sixteen: The Judiciary
text: How could a free market without states ensure a functioning judiciary? Who would appoint a judge? And would it be possible to appeal against the judgment? Is there any way to prevent the courts from favoring rich and wealthy clients? I will try to answer these - and many other - questions during the lecture; but first of all we get to the most interesting part: What would the courts decide if there was no central authority with a monopoly on legislation? This lecture is one of the three most "advanced" of the series and is a bone of contention between the anarcho-capitalists and the minarchists; so don't miss it.

title: Anarcho-capitalism: a public cause
text: Anarcho-capitalism is finally being talked about! We are overwhelmed with questions and comments, the topic has already reached Jakub Janda from European values. A lot of people who don't know anything about anarcho-capitalism are also commenting now, but that's only good; please stay with us, be patient and help us spread the ideas of freedom!

title: Anarcho-Capitalism Volume Fifteen: The Environment
text: Do we need states in order not to devastate nature and the environment? If our society is only "managed" by the free market, will we leave our descendants with more than just contaminated water, air and soil? Without the state, who would protect endangered animal species? And how to promote sustainable development without the state? To explain this interesting issue, I will make considerable use of the knowledge of the Austrian school of economics, which we discussed (mostly repeatedly) in previous lectures; I highly recommend refreshing them again.

title: Anarcho-capitalist revolution?
text: Left-wing anarchists are often revolutionaries; anarcho-capitalists typically do not. However, we are individualists, as a matter of principle we do not group together and we are united, among other things, by our reluctance to blindly obey authorities, so there are exceptions to each of our "typicals". On the one hand, this is great, but on the other hand, in this particular case, I consider it extremely important to say a few words about it...

title: Urza in StandaShow
text: Youtuber Standa invited me to his online streaming show; and it was definitely an interesting interview. We talked about anarcho-capitalism; in the end, the audience could also ask their questions. Unfortunately, we didn't have time to go too deep, but thousands of people saw it, which I'm really happy about.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Volume Fourteen: Healthcare
text: When the word "free market health care" is mentioned, most people immediately think of exorbitant amounts of money for medical procedures that the common mortal simply cannot afford to pay, leaving him with no choice but to live in sickness; or even die. Without the government, how could we afford to pay for medical care? Who would supervise the quality? How to overcome the enormous information asymmetry between doctor and patient in the market? Isn't free market healthcare an antisocial and horrible system through which the powerful can squeeze the powerless and sick? You will learn the answers to these and many other questions when you come to the lecture; and you can ask your own questions in the subsequent discussion.

title: Crowdfunding
text:
https://kniha.urza.cz/

Thank you for your amazing support that makes the project so successful; we posted more rewards and we still haven't heard back from all the donors.

title: Where does statism come from?
text:
Where do states get their power? Power is where one believes it to be; it's a trick, a shadow on the wall. And not only the shadow, but also the coat of arms, the image of the president and other religious symbols; we are all exposed to indoctrination by state propaganda from an early age...
Screenplay: Urza
Reads: Urza
Graphics: Tereza Vyslužilová

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Volume Thirteen: The Labor Market
text: Do you think that without the state and its regulations, employees would have no standing, so employers could screw them over? In that case, this lecture is just for you! We will show why a free and unregulated labor market would not only not harm employees, but would, on the contrary, improve their situation in many ways; because the state provides its "protection" to employees as a bit of a disservice.
