Seeing exactly how and why this is so is not at all difficult; just come to the lecture, where we will talk about child labor and many other interesting things, among other things.

title: Panel Discussion "Anarcho-Capitalists and Elections"
text:
In Parallel Polis, five anarcho-capitalists (four panelists and a moderator) gathered for a panel discussion about elections. I find the debate very interesting and beneficial; it contained arguments for and against participation in the elections, all from the position of staunch opponents of the state. Unfortunately, due to a technical fault, the last third of the recording is missing.

Discussing: Alice Eliška Hrazdilová, Pavol Lupták, Jan Hubík and Urza.
Moderator: Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD)

title: Media campaign
text:
https://kniha.urza.cz/

Through the first Czech book on anarcho-capitalism, we are working to get this topic into the media and thus spark a public discussion about a stateless society. Please help us get libertarian ideas to the people! Thank you

title: Drugs and Liberty (SfL): Peace on Drugs
text:
Presentation Peace on Drugs at Drugs and Liberty conference organized by Students for Liberty.
The global war on drugs has failed, with devastating consequences for individuals and societies around the world. Make peace on drugs then!

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part Twelve: The Social System
text: Without the state, not only would there be no social benefits and unemployment support, but above all there would be no pension system as we know it now. What would that mean? In a free market society, would the poor starve to death on the streets? What would old people do without the state? I am going to answer these and many other questions at the twelfth lecture from the Anarchocapitalism cycle; subsequently we can talk about these topics in a discussion.

title: Lecture for the OKO Society
text:
The OKO association asked Freedom of Learning (with a capital S) for a lecture on the topic of Freedom of Learning (with a small s). The parents of the schoolchildren, but even the representatives of the city, arrived at the lecture; the reactions were surprisingly positive.
Although it was already possible to arrange the sound in such a way that I could be understood well, unfortunately, the same cannot be said about the questions from the audience, for which I apologize. The presentation on the wall was glossy, so it couldn't be caught on camera; making videos is not as easy as it might seem.

– Urza for Freedom of Learning

title: The book "Anarcho-Capitalism"
text:
Support the first Czech book on anarcho-capitalism:
http://kniha.urza.cz/

title: HCPP17: Liberate education from the state!
text:
Compulsory school attendance is not only immoral, but it also represents the initial reason for our economic lack of freedom; State education costs money, also it's a source of state propaganda and statist indoctrination. This is the main cause of the conviction of people that the free market fails in so many areas, so we need the state authority to replace it. Why don't they teach us anything about the impossibility of economic calculation in the central planning? How easily can the authority of a teacher be replaced by the state authorities? And how can we keep the freedom when we spend the most important years of our lives in the jail?
Sorry for my horrible English; it is not so good in general and moreover I felt physically quite bad this time.

Presenting: Zdeňka Staňková and Urza (www.urza.cz) of Freedom of Learning (www.svobodauceni.cz).

title: Prague Business Club: Who would build roads?
text:
I was asked by entrepreneurs from the Prague Business Club to give a private lecture on transport infrastructure in the free market; I gladly accepted the offer and adapted the presentation to this target group, although the topic of course overlaps to a large extent (not completely) with the eleventh volume of the series Anarcho-capitalism from Polis.
If you are a skeptic and a practitioner of everyday reality, the lecture may be a little too optimistic and "visionary" for your taste; in that case, I recommend watching the lecture of the same name from the series Anarchocapitalism instead. Either way, the direction of the questions in the discussion is very different in both cases.

title: The Fight for Democracy (Urza vs. Bob Kartous)
text: Freedom of Learning hosted an unmoderated discussion between Bob Kartous and Urza on the topic of democracy in the education system in Paralelní Polis. We wish you a pleasant listening, although the debate was a bit heated in places and went into details.

title: A minor parallel
text: The state appears to be an indestructible entity that has been with us as far back as history, so that no reason can be seen why it should not endure forever; but a similar institution, of which one could assume exactly the same thing, was already there - and how do you think it turned out?

title: Mises Academy 2017: Anarcho-Capitalism
text:
I was honored to be invited to the Liberal Institute's Mises Academy, where I gave two lectures.
This is a record from the second of them - about anarcho-capitalism; the audience consisted of people interested in freedom and libertarianism, to which the lecture was tailored. A more detailed treatment of this topic aimed at a wider public can be found in the list of videos "Anarchocapitalism in Polis".

title: Mises Academy 2017: Freedom to Learn
text:
I was honored to be invited to the Liberal Institute's Mises Academy, where I gave two lectures.
This is the record of the first of these—of free education; the audience was overwhelmingly made up of libertarians who already know a lot about the given topic, to which the lecture was tailored. You can find a lecture on a similar topic aimed at a wider public in the video list "Anarchocapitalism in Polis" under the title "Anarchocapitalism, part seven: Education".

title: "LGBT Pride Week" Panel Discussion
text: Parallel Polis organized a discussion on "LGBT Pride Week"; so it was originally called something else, but there were legal threats due to the trademark. Both proponents and opponents attended and there were many interesting views; you can find their montage in this video.

title: About pedophilia and pedophiles
text: Although there are many statists in the LGBTQ community who try to push their agenda through state power, they are right about some things. We do not agree with violence through the state and restrictions on freedom of speech, because we are convinced that the right way is enlightenment.

title: About science and evidence
text:
During the lecture at the gymnasium in Holice, I mentioned that the theory of evolution is not proven; reactions were strong and often shocking.
In discussing this topic online and in person with a number of people, I realized that it would be a good idea to make a video explaining what scientific evidence actually means and the difference between it and a mere experiment that does not disprove a theory.

title: Engagement between heaven and earth
text: We've been on vacation, paragliding, engaged (in the air); we have an amazing life and we want to live it together. Even in this rather personal video you will find some anarcho-capitalist ideas, although this time they are exceptionally not the main topic.

title: Matěj Stropnický talks about weapons
text: After a long time, our MPs did something exceptionally, for which we even praised them; on the other hand, the chairman of the Greens, Matěj Stropnický, unsurprisingly sees it differently. And since he did not respond to the invitation to the discussion, we commented on his statement in the video.

title: Lecture at the gymnasium in Holice
text:
The students of the gymnasium in Holice invited me to the day of personalities to give them a lecture about anarcho-capitalism, freedom (and Freedom) of learning, education and the state; I gladly accepted and came, although the date conflicted with an invitation to the same event of another gymnasium.
Not only students and teachers arrived for the lecture, but to my surprise some parents too; in the end, an interesting debate was sparked, with the result of which I am certainly satisfied, but judge that for yourself.
Unfortunately, this is only an audio recording recorded on the phone, there is no picture, and the sound quality does not exactly allow for the most luxurious listening, for which I apologize; however, I find it listenable.

title: Panel Discussion "The Sharing Economy"
text:
Parallel Polis organized a discussion on the topic "Sharing economy" - a phenomenon of today's time, an idol and a scarecrow. In-demand services that defeat established companies and scare the state with their success among users. 
Urza was invited as a guest, Tereza selected interesting moments from the discussion and added her commentary.

title: State versus innovation
text: Innovation can take place - and has for millennia - based on the voluntariness of resourceful and enterprising people; such a state is more than desirable and thanks to it our society continues to flourish. In addition, we unfortunately have an unrelenting, ravenous and expansive state that takes resources from the people against their will under the threat of using violence against them; even as a result of his interventions, various innovations arise, but at what cost?

title: Panel discussion "Anti-smoking law"
text:
Parallel Polis organized a discussion on the topic "Anti-Smoking Law"; is the government supposed to "protect our health" or should no one be forced to conform the rules of their business to the orders of the powerful?
Urza was invited as a guest, Tereza selected interesting moments from the discussion and added her commentary.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part Eleven: Who Would Build the Roads?
text: "If we had no state, who would build the roads?" So goes the most common question in libertarian jokes and one of the first reactions of statists to the mention of a stateless society; I am going to answer this very question at the lecture. And not only that! We will also talk about road traffic rules; would these differ from road to road if each road had its own private owner? After the lecture, as always, there will be a (perhaps heated) discussion; I look forward to hearing from you, especially if you disagree with me!

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part Ten: Public Space and Freedom of Speech
text: In the tenth lecture from the Anarcho-Capitalism series, we will focus on public spaces and places "for all"; how could such spaces exist in a stateless society based on respect for property rights? Who would manage them, why and for what? Would all parks disappear in cities? Would we live in concrete jungles without a bit of greenery? In addition, we will talk about freedom of speech; how does it relate to the topic? We will show that very closely. As always, the lecture will be followed by a discussion; I hope you will oppose me!

title: Election of the (French) President
text: Today we are thinking about the election of the French president (and we certainly do not envy the French that choice), the last election of the Czech president and, above all, what is the point of having a president (anywhere)...

title: Panel discussion "State versus Labor"
text:
Parallel Polis organized a discussion on "State versus Labor"; should the government protect Czech workers from cheap labor from the east?
Urza was invited as a guest, Tereza selected interesting moments from the discussion and added her commentary.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism Volume Nine: Weapons
text: The topic of the ninth lecture from the cycle Anarchocapitalism will be weapons and their regulation; we will talk about what the disarmament of society leads to and what is the main difference between a community of people with and without weapons. We will also look back in history and focus on a time and place when and where guns were virtually unregulated; what were the consequences? As always, the lecture will end with a discussion, in which you will be able to ask anything and, ideally, even oppose me.

title: Optimistic spring ride
text: Since we at FREEPORT CHANNEL usually rain fire and brimstone on the state, this time we decided to be positive, nice and share with you, dear viewers, a little happiness from a beautiful spring day; come for a ride with us xD

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Volume Eight: Drugs
text: At the eighth lecture from the Anarchocapitalism series, we will talk and discuss drugs; on the one hand, we will talk about the drugs themselves, but above all about the state's relationship to them and our freedom to deal with our own bodies as we see fit. We will also discuss the war on drugs that has been raging for decades; what did it actually cost us and what are its results? As usual, the lecture will be followed by a discussion, in which I will gladly try to answer all the questions you ask me.

title: Who is Marek Novák?
text:
Who is Marek Novák? Our most persistent and notorious troll.
Do you want to know his identity? Watch this video!

title: LibertyCon 2017
text:
From March 17th to 19th LibertyCon took place in Prague, which we participated in and we bring you a short compilation of videos we shot there; the whole event was absolutely phenomenally divine.
We hope to see you there next year!

title: LibertyCon 2017: State Education System
text:
Presentation of Freedom to Learn at LibertyCon 2017.
The government is indoctrinating our kids with propaganda of statism and evil; the solution is the separation of state and education!

Presenting: Urza (www.urza.cz) and Zdeňka Staňková of Freedom of Learning (www.svobodauceni.cz).

title: Anarcho-capitalism, part seven: Education
text: I consider this lecture to be the most important of the entire series on Anarcho-Capitalism; we will talk about the state education system as a powerful tool used to massively spread state propaganda. We will reveal the roots and effects of how current education works. Of course, there will also be an insight into how (and why) education could (and should) take place in a free market; and this time we will not only dwell on why it would not be such a horror as most people assume, but we will also look at the origin of those assumptions themselves. As always, the lecture will be followed by a discussion where I will answer all your questions and objections. Be sure to come this time!

title: Whitebeard votes but doesn't read
text:
Member of Parliament Pavel Bělobárdek has publicly admitted that he does not read the laws he approves because we would like too much, after all, they are clouds of text.
We fear that the nature of the problem goes far beyond this case.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Volume Six: Democracy
text: The topic of the sixth lecture from the Anarchocapitalism cycle will be democracy, its harmfulness, but also a reflection on why it is so deified and, on the contrary, its criticism is considered something so inappropriate; we will also talk about why democracy quite naturally leads to socialism and how by supporting the irresponsible we create more irresponsible ones. As always, the lecture will be followed by my much-loved discussion; come and bring your friends who you think might be interested in this controversial topic.

title: School Junk-Food Ban (Snack Ordinance)
text:
School snack decree: The state will decide what can and cannot be sold in schools for food...
...and that is unfortunately one of the minor problems.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Volume Five: Culture
text: The topic of this lecture from the series Anarchocapitalism will be culture and art in the hands of the state and how they could function without it in the free market; although most people are convinced of the necessity of the state's role in this area, I believe that things are far from clear-cut. In addition to the creation of new art, we will also devote ourselves to the protection of already existing works of art and cultural monuments; can this also be provided on the market? As always, there will be an opportunity for discussion after the lecture.

title: Panel discussion on EET
text:
The Parallel Polis openly rejected the EET; organized a panel discussion on the topic.
Urza was invited as a guest, Tereza selected interesting moments from the discussion and added her commentary.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part Four: Firemen
text: In the next lecture from the Anarcho-Capitalism cycle, we will discuss why and how firefighters could function in the free market; for what reason should the state not provide this service? Would maximum travel times for sparsely populated areas be guaranteed even in the free market? Shouldn't firefighters only rescue paying customers from burning houses and leave others to perish in the flames? As always, there will be an opportunity for discussion after the lecture.

title: Bitcoin
text:
Bitcoin recently crossed the 1 BTC per $1000 mark...
...and what exactly is Bitcoin? You can find out in this video.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Volume Three: Money
text: In this lecture from the Anarcho-Capitalism cycle, you have the opportunity to learn and then discuss the most important and absolutely fascinating function of money and prices, which without exaggeration makes them one of the most important discoveries in human history. We will also talk about how states are gradually devaluing this wonderful discovery through their interventions. You will be able to get an idea of fractional banking and find out why and how states cause cyclical economic crises through banks.

title: Reaction to Dominik Feri's Myths of the EU
text:
In his video (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=olXYASGkNfM), Dominik Feri refuted alleged myths about the EU...
...we refute the myths of Dominik Feri xD

title: Anarcho-capitalism, part two: The state is a bad servant but a bad master
text: In the first lecture from the Anarcho-Capitalism cycle, we talked about why the state is immoral. Come to the second lecture to hear why the state is even more inefficient. Anarcho-capitalism stands on two main pillars – natural law and the Austrian school of economics, the foundations of which will be presented at the lecture. But don't expect a dry talk about economics, we'll show everything with examples from the real world - for example, why does a top soccer player earn more than a firefighter who saves lives?

title: No smoking
text:
During 2017, the ban on smoking in pubs and restaurants will come into force...
...and what about us? We went to smoke (someone's first time xD).

title: Merry Christmas 2016
text:
Wishing everyone a very Merry Christmas 2016...
...and we attach two short reflections and an anarchocoura xD

title: Run the state like a business?
text:
For some time we have been hearing everywhere that it would be desirable to run the state like a business; and Babiš is far from promoting it alone.
It sounds quite "right-wing" and sympathetic; what do we say to that? We are not excited; watch the video to find out why.

title: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part One: The State Is Immoral
text: Come and listen to the introductory lecture from the series Anarchocapitalism! We talk about state funding and taxes; we will criticize the concept of taxes and their collection from the point of view of ethics. We will think through the consequences of what is behind every regulation and every law; how can their violent enforcement by the police be morally justified? And finally, we will say something about state propaganda and indoctrination; reasons why the state can basically do whatever it wants.

title: Introduction
text:
There are two of us. We love freedom. We love anarchy. We love capitalism. We love each other xD
We are talking about a free market stateless society; yes, we know how it looks, even we thought the idea was absurd at first...
However, try to give her a chance; you can always refuse it.
Motto: "Good people don't follow bad laws."

title: Story one
text: Tereza picked up her pace because she was getting cold.

title: Story one
text: Dusk fell on the city, so she tried not to linger anywhere unnecessarily. After a while, however, she stopped to look into the light of a street lamp and watch the falling snow. And it was... gorgeous. She wondered when she had last seen something like this. She remembered. Back then in the mountains, still as a little girl. Right there she saw flakes so big and falling so much that it resembled falling feathers.

title: Story one
text: The surrounding park was covered in snow and glistened beautifully in the lamplights. Tereza felt the flakes tickle her cheek and let herself drift away in nostalgia for a while longer. Still, when she exhaled and a puff of steam rose from her mouth, she snapped back to reality. To that reality where it freezes in the winter and the tips of the fingers freeze.

title: Story one
text: She shook the snow from her coat and hair and wanted to set off again, but at that moment she was overcome with anxiety. It was just a moment. As a warning. Something just wasn't right.

title: Story one
text: Maybe it was the surrounding silence. Silence, as if all life had suddenly passed away. But something told her that she was not alone.

title: Story one
text: She set off towards home with a quick step.

title: Story one
text: Girl, don't worry, she was calming down. Once you have enough money with you, you are immediately nervous and see crooks around every corner.

title: Story one
text: Nevertheless, she accelerated and continued at a very brisk pace. After a while she wasn't even cold anymore. A few more minutes of walking and she would be home...

title: Story one
text: She heard footsteps.

title: Story one
text: Or was she just imagining it? She looked back and saw a stocky man trudging off the footpath. He wasn't going straight to her, and there was still quite a distance between them, but if they both continued walking like they had been, their paths would soon cross. The idea suddenly made her extremely uncomfortable. And that creeping feeling.

title: Story one
text: She added to her stride again. She almost ran. Was she imagining it, or did the stranger also speed up?

title: Story one
text: Dammit, stop being so dramatic, she thought. You need to calm down.

title: Story one
text: After all, nothing is happening at all. She stopped and began searching her pockets for cigarettes. The man continued walking, but Teresa did not, so unless something unexpected happened, he would miss her by a considerable distance. She was relieved. At least a little.

title: Story one
text: She pulled out a box, a cigarette and a lighter, and inhaled her favorite smoke. She was calming down. That was the job of nicotine. Even the fact that the guy went his own way and didn't pay attention to her at all.

title: Story one
text: Tereza suddenly found the whole situation absurd. What was she crazy about? She has been here almost daily and has never had anything happen to her, nor does she know of anyone else who has experienced anything bad here. She was never afraid here. And today someone should rob her just because she has a bundle of money with her, which no robber has any idea about? She doesn't have it written on her forehead, so what are the chances that...

title: Story one
text: Someone put a hand on her shoulder. She immediately flinched, turned, and cowered in sheer terror.

title: Story one
text: There were two thugs standing in front of her. One unusually small and stocky. A massive mustache under his nose, the ends of which flowed loosely into a long black beard. He was wearing a leather biker outfit that looked like he'd been through a lot; as well as its owner, who was certainly no more than thirty years old. His dark eyes measured Tereza with a hard look that did not bode well.

title: Story one
text: The age of the other would perhaps be impossible to guess for an ignorant observer. He could easily be in his fifties, but he didn't have to be any older than his partner. When someone takes drugs so often and for so long that they sell their soul to them and they become everything to them, you don't even know how old they are. He was tall, thin, and his sunken cheeks were covered by badly shaved stubble. He was apparently missing several teeth. Not to mention his clothes... They looked like they were pulled out of a trash can, although he didn't stink now in winter. His gaze was empty and watery, which frightened Tereza even more than the darkness in his companion's eyes.

title: Story one
text: "Good evening. Wouldn't you have some spare change, lady?" whined the junkie. His voice was as blank as his gaze; and most likely life.

title: Story one
text: "Good evening. I don't have any. Sorry. Goodbye," answered Tereza neutrally and was about to leave.

title: Story one
text: No sooner had she turned than she felt that terrible hand on her shoulder again. She hated being touched by a stranger, and this was especially unpleasant. She tried to shake her hand off, but it gripped her and turned her around – the little biker was obviously a big strong man.

title: Story one
text: "Leave me!" she hissed. There was defiance in the way she said it, but also a desperation that the bearded man didn't miss. His eyes sparkled, but he withdrew his hand.

title: Story one
text: "And a cigarette? Wouldn't you have one?" wheezed the tall man, as if nothing had happened. That man, or rather what used to be man, had sunk so low that he no longer cared.

title: Story one
text: It dawned on Teresa that getting rid of them might not be so easy. By looking for cigarettes, whose location she knows precisely because she has just finished smoking, she can at least buy time to think about what to do next. She immediately appreciated the idea - that's when she thought to find pepper spray in her purse and hide it in the palm of her hand. She regretted not having a revolver with her. Either way, she would try to avoid any conflict; she wouldn't provoke them too much and could play for time—sooner or later someone might walk by even in this little-frequented area.

title: Story one
text: After a while, she handed over the entire box to the rascal in an attempt to appease them and be left alone. "Keep it, there's a lighter in there too. Take care."

title: Story one
text: "Kind of generous, isn't she? Why, I guess?" a dwarf joined the conversation. His voice sounded ominous. He wanted to instill fear in her. He wasn't after the loot so much, he was just enjoying it. He wasn't broken like his buddy, but sadistic and evil.

title: Story one
text: She didn't answer and tried to clear the field when she felt that strong hand on her shoulder again. This time she turned without resistance.

title: Story one
text: "Leave it!" she said firmly, trying not to show her fear.

title: Story one
text: "Then behave yourself and don't turn your back when I talk to you," said the little one, almost mockingly.

title: Story one
text: She didn't know what to answer. She pressed the pepper spray in her hand and prepared to use it.

title: Story one
text: "I asked you a question, as far as I know..."

title: Story one
text: "Excuse me, for what?" The trace of hopelessness in her voice that had inadvertently escaped her pleased him.

title: Story one
text: "Why are you so generous?" he asked in a kindly tone that irritated and frightened her.

title: Story one
text: "I guess I am," she sneered.

title: Story one
text: "Then you'll surely find a little spare change too, right?" the junkie rejoined the conversation. His voice sounded condescending and condescending, not at all matching what was going on around him. He perceived the whole situation obscurely, as if the body he inhabited was acting independently of his will. But it didn't matter to him anymore, he just wanted another dose, everything else was secondary to him.

title: Story one
text: She decided to leave without saying a word. And if he tries to hold her again... She gripped the pepper spray. She felt that intrusive hand on her shoulder again. A wave of anger shot through her.

title: Story one
text: That's enough! No one will touch me!

title: Story one
text: She quickly turned around. She raised her hand to counterattack. However, the dwarf was faster. He sensed her intentions. He grabbed her wrist and gripped it so hard that she dropped her weapon. She screamed. He jerked her hand downwards. She lost her balance and was heading for the ground. At the last moment she stopped her fall with her knee. There was a pain in the leg. She tried to fight back with her other hand, but the attacker caught that as well. She was at her wits end. The little robber continued to push her hands to the ground and she had no choice but to kneel down.

title: Story one
text: "Help!" she called.

title: Story one
text: "Shut up!"

title: Story one
text: "Somebody help me!" she did not give up and screamed as hard as she could.

title: Story one
text: The assailant grabbed both of her wrists with one hand while reaching for the knife with the other.

title: Story one
text: "Will you shut up now?"

title: Story one
text: This time, Tereza obeyed the call.

title: Story one
text: "Please don't hurt me."

title: Story one
text: "We'll see," smiled the burly man. "Take her things," he said towards the long man.

title: Story one
text: She knew resistance was futile. She knelt on the cold ground, feeling the wet snow. She tried not to notice the roving hands of the junkie, which were expertly going through her pockets, taking out all the valuables from them and casually throwing them into her purse, which the robbers were about to leave with.

title: Story one
text: If I don't cause trouble, maybe they'll let me live, she thought. She even hoped no one would walk by and scare the guy with the knife. He might panic and use it.

title: Story one
text: “Good girl,” the smaller assailant interrupted her thoughts with a mischievous smile on his lips. Meanwhile, the taller one finished the search and held the loot firmly in his hands.

title: Story one
text: The dwarf suddenly jerked her hands violently, which she didn't expect. She crumpled to the ground.

title: Story one
text: Luckily, she heard the two men running away. The shadows on the path beside her faded away.

title: Story one
text: For a long time she lay on the ground exactly as the vagabond had thrown her, recovering and not wanting to move. She would have called someone, but she also lost her phone... And most of all, she lost a wad of money.

title: Story one
text: She regretted her decision to cut her way through the park; however, she could not change anything with regret. She sat down, then stood up. She wasn't in much pain, the snow cover was soft, although wet and cold. On the one hand, she thought that it could have turned out worse, on the other hand, she was really sorry and upset about losing so much money. She looked around and slowly - still a little in shock - limped her way home.

title: Story one
text: A crescent moon shone in the sky.

title: Story two
text: Rosalie smiled at the departing guest, "Take care and come again."

title: Story two
text: "You too, and thanks," he replied. He always enjoyed coming back and left a decent tip each time.

title: Story two
text: Rosalie had a rather short-tempered and impatient nature. In her small tavern, however, she was basically nice, attentive and listened to customers. Every morning she promised herself in front of the mirror that today she would be even more professional than yesterday. She just happened to be behind the counter, a completely different world opened up in front of her, and she had it all in the palm of her hand. At that moment, it didn't matter how she felt or what her mood was. There was only one thing - to do her job precisely.

title: Story two
text: She demanded the same from her employees. "Show your guests only the best of you," she used to say.

title: Story two
text: She knew she was there for her visitors and they were there for her. Her smile, kind word, friendly environment - all these were the reasons why they came back again and again; well this and good beer to be exact.

title: Story two
text: Such was the source of her livelihood. And she wanted to earn it.

title: Story two
text: "Well gentlemen, we're closing," she said cheerfully to the table of regulars and looked around the place; most people were already gone. In addition to the regular guests, there was one more couple and a kind of strange patron at a table in the corner.

title: Story two
text: "Come on, Rouzí, bring us one more," demanded one of the regular customers.

title: Story two
text: "Well, what shall I do with you?" she smiled. "One last thing and off to bed, okay?"

title: Story two
text: "Thanks, you're the best!" a wave of joy rose from the table.

title: Story two
text: "Every woman is the best when you've been drinking..." she interjected with a smile.

title: Story two
text: She poured six beautifully dewy beers, took three in each hand and carried them to the table. Then she cashed in on a young couple who also wanted to pay. However, the weirdo in the corner made no move to leave.

title: Story two
text: She walked up to him with a smile and asked, "We're closing slowly. Can I bring you the bill?"

title: Story two
text: He fixed her with a thoughtful and unusually penetrating look. He was clean-shaven, balding, but the remnants of his hair were carefully trimmed and combed back. He didn't smile. It occurred to Rosalie that he hadn't smiled once in all that time. In fact, he didn't even speak! He also ordered the beer with a wave of his hand.

title: Story two
text: So maybe that's why I found him strange, she thought. And he's a bit scary. Did he even understand what I was telling him? Of course he did... Why wouldn't he? I highly doubt this particular guy is out of it. So why didn't he answer? And why is he still watching me?

title: Story two
text: That moment seemed absurdly long to her. At that he shook his head.

title: Story two
text: He reached into the pocket of the jacket he was still wearing. He didn't take them off the whole time; even though it was warm here. He took out a leather wallet and a banknote from it, which he placed on the table with a vigorous movement. The owner and waitress in one person started hunting for money back in her purse. The man shook his head, picked up the banknote he had placed there earlier, and handed it to the waiter. His gesture was utterly convincing and confident, which Rosalie liked; and let's be honest, she liked such a generous tip just as much.

title: Story two
text: "Thank you very much," she said with a slight blush and moved away from the stranger. She didn't know what to think of him.

title: Story two
text: The table of regulars gradually paid - some in cash, others on a tab. The guests began to rise and gradually disappear into the night. Rosalie said goodbye to each of them individually, she had known them for a long time and over time she grew to like them. But she already saw herself in bed, so she completely forgot about the mysterious stranger while saying goodbye to the noisy group.

title: Story two
text: As she closed the door, the person reminded her in an ice-cold voice, "So we're left here alone."

title: Story two
text: She was startled; she nearly jumped out of her skin. "Shit!" she exclaimed.

title: Story two
text: Then she hesitated a little. "Sorry, you startled me," she said conciliatoryly and even with a hint of a smile.

title: Story two
text: The stranger said nothing, but remained seated behind the table. It didn't look like he was about to leave.

title: Story two
text: "Thank you for visiting, but unfortunately I'm closing now."

title: Story two
text: "Close up. At least we'll have peace and quiet," he replied slowly.

title: Story two
text: "Quiet for what? Look, sir, I'm working tomorrow, I need to get some sleep, so if you..." she gestured to leave.

title: Story two
text: "Calm down for a business meeting," he measured every word.

title: Story two
text: "I don't know what you're offering or what you're looking for, but I'm not interested right now. We can meet tomorrow, okay?"

title: Story two
text: "Take a seat with me. In your own interest. It won't be long," came the uncompromising voice from the corner table.

title: Story two
text: She thought for a few seconds.

title: Story two
text: This guy certainly doesn't act like someone who came to whitewash my cash register. He doesn't look nervous, he drew attention to himself and also wanted me to sit next to him. A thief would use the element of surprise, wouldn't he? But the fear of him is nothing, she thought. What the hell could he want from me? Anyway, probably the fastest way to get rid of him is to talk to him.

title: Story two
text: "Fine, but only five minutes," she said conciliatoryly as she sat down at the table.

title: Story two
text: "I don't even need that much time," came the icy voice.

title: Story two
text: He waited for her to sit down before continuing.

title: Story two
text: "I have an offer for you from my employer. It offers protection to your business."

title: Story two
text: "Protection from what?" she was playing for time. She didn't like where their conversation was going.

title: Story two
text: "To the criminals. He only wants ten percent of your profits for it," he hung on every word.

title: Story two
text: "So you came here for protection money? Get out of my establishment immediately and don't come back, you scumbag!" she slipped. She herself was immediately frightened. She knew it wasn't wise to make him angry, but the audacity of a man who had come to threaten Rosalia in her own pub really made her angry.

title: Story two
text: The mobster smiled. He was clearly amused by her reaction. This made her even more upset.

title: Story two
text: There was a glimmer of something human in his voice for the first time, perhaps the smile was to blame. "Think about it. Mr. Bogdanov is one of the most respected businessmen. It is an honor to work with him."

title: Story two
text: She folded her arms over her chest and measured him with a hostile look.

title: Story two
text: "But it's also a big mistake not to do business with him," he said so slowly and coldly that it sent a chill down her spine.

title: Story two
text: He suddenly stood up and she instinctively pulled away.

title: Story two
text: He ignored it and said goodbye, "I'll come for an answer tomorrow. I hope you won't refuse. It would be a shame. Goodbye," he said firmly.

title: Story two
text: When the door closed behind him, Rosalie was still sitting behind the table, visibly upset.

title: Story two
text: She didn't sleep much that night, she still had to think about the events of the day.

title: Story two
text: How serious is this goon? What actually happens if I don't pay? Is the Russian mafia really threatening me? Or just a few dogs who bark but don't bite? But the poor guy didn't look twice for that. He had an expensive tailored suit and acted like someone who knew exactly what he was doing... But what if it was just a show? Maybe he's a clever con artist. Anyway, I'm not going to pay someone just because they scare me! It's all absurd! I could call the cops too, but what would I tell them? And what could they do for me? You can't rely on them even in much simpler cases, I've already tried that and got burned badly. Moreover, if it is really a mafia, then they can have the police somehow "solved". Oh well, if that gangster comes again, I'll send him to hell.

title: Story two
text: With that she concluded her thoughts shortly before falling asleep.

title: Story two
text: The next day passed quite calmly. Rosalie was mainly troubled by lack of sleep in combination with the usual hustle and bustle in the pub. She put her mobster out of her head for the job itself. After all, she had already decided that night that she would not give him anything. Evening came and he was still nowhere.

title: Story two
text: He walked through the door just before it closed and headed with a slow step towards the table in the corner. The owner blocked his way.

title: Story two
text: "You are no longer welcome here," she stated forcefully, trying not to show her fear.

title: Story two
text: "As you wish, I won't bother," the man replied without any emotion.

title: Story two
text: He turned to the door. He took a step. Then he stopped, reached into his pocket, and handed Rosalia a small piece of paper. "What if you happen to find out that you do need protection after all..."

title: Story two
text: She hesitantly accepted it from him. The man walked away without another word.

title: Story two
text: "This is not good," she said to herself almost inaudibly.

title: Story two
text: If he threatened, pressured, or tried to convince her, she would probably feel more at ease. A dog that barks does not bite. But he just left ominously.

title: Story two
text: That means he's probably not done with me; if so, he would probably try something else, she thought.

title: Story two
text: She opened her palm. There was a business card.

title: Story two
text: She hesitated. Shouldn't I call him? No! After all, I'm not going to pay anyone who starts unleashing horror. It is my hard earned money; and I won't give you to any fool.

title: Story two
text: After closing the pub, she went up the stairs to her small apartment, where she headed straight for the covers. As soon as she lay down, she immediately fell asleep. It was no wonder. She desperately needed sleep.

title: Story two
text: Even today, however, she was not allowed a thorough rest. She couldn't estimate how long she had been asleep when she was awakened by the sound of glass clinking followed by a noise coming from downstairs. From her business!

title: Story two
text: Firemen's horns rang out on the street. She threw on a robe and quickly ran down the stairs.

title: Story two
text: Smoke was billowing from the premises...

title: Story two
text: In the end, the damage was minimal. She learned from the firemen that someone probably started the fire on purpose, but she was lucky in the accident. Someone called for help just in time; given how little had burned, it would seem - if it wasn't nonsense - that the call was recorded on the emergency line perhaps even before the fire broke out.

title: Story two
text: The police wrote a report. For a moment, Rosalie considered telling the lawmen about her situation and turning to them for help. However, that quickly passed her by when she realized that she was the main suspect and the police consider insurance fraud to be the most likely motive for the arson.

title: Story two
text: Seriously kiss my ass with that, you idiots, Rosalie thought.

title: Story three
text: Katina dipped a sponge in soapy water and went to scrub the sign from the window.

title: Story three
text: Although she didn't have to, she wanted to leave a nice clean up after her. In addition, the inscription symbolized the end of her enterprise:

title: Story three
text: SALE! 90% OFF!

title: Story three
text: She needed to get rid of the supplies, she had no further use for them. When the glass was clean, she smiled involuntarily, as she hated dirt and washed things made her happy.

title: Story three
text: She climbed down from the window, poured out the black water, and began to slowly load the rolls of leftover canvas that were still left in the store into the car. While doing so, she nostalgically looked around the place where she went to work almost every day for the past eight years, because she really liked sewing and selling the fabrics themselves.

title: Story three
text: Her business has worked for a long time, but now it is necessary to move on. She was a little sad, on the other hand, she knew how to take life as it is. She certainly had no regrets, and even at this moment she was glad she had gone into business then. Those were beautiful years...

title: Story three
text: She started - like most entrepreneurs - in the red, barely making ends meet and sometimes even sleeping in her small shop so she could open early in the morning. She closed late in the evening and sewed after nights, which was her "extra service" that she tried to differentiate from the competition and stand out.

title: Story three
text: It worked. Customers were happy with what they bought in her little shop, so word of her opening spread pretty quickly. Katina's business slowly began to flourish. Sometimes she did better, sometimes worse. One time she made a lot of money, the other time she was happy to cover the expenses. Over time, she also accumulated some savings for worse times, which gave her peace of mind.

title: Story three
text: In the last year, however, it all took a bad turn - customers slightly decreased and they spent less in her store, which turned out to be a rather fatal problem in combination with the rising cost of rent. At first, profits only fell, then the company began to find itself more and more often at a loss. Katina did what she could, but the savings were slowly and inexorably melting away. Like many entrepreneurs who have experienced good times and bad times, she always believed that things would get better again and did not want to close her business.

title: Story three
text: But one day she reached the point where she simply couldn't pay for everything anymore. So she paid the suppliers, as well as the rent, but did not pay the VAT. The tax office will just have to wait. After all, she had been paying outrageous sums to the state for many years.

title: Story three
text: When the situation still did not improve, she did what she had been putting off for so long - closed the shop for good. She didn't owe anything to the suppliers or the owner, that would have made her very sorry, but she didn't pay VAT to the state for two quarters - there was nothing to pay it from. She received a call to pay some time ago, but she did not respond to it. If she doesn't have it, she simply doesn't have it, she closed the shop and the tax office is out of luck. In any case, she paid a lot of money to the state in all kinds of levies during that time and she never wanted anything from him, so she herself had no conscience about the unpaid tax.

title: Story three
text: While these and many other thoughts raced through her mind, she loaded the car with everything that was left of her small business. She walked in and took one last look around the shop. It was completely empty and she thought it looked sad. She remembered a similar sight when she first rented it, but it didn't look sad then; rather full of hope. She smiled slightly.

title: Story three
text: "Thanks, shop, it was nice. Hopefully my successor will have better luck," she sputtered. At the same time, she shed a tear.

title: Story three
text: She went outside, closed the shutters, which also served as a grille, and locked them. She got into the car, looked back one more time and waved. She headed towards home.

title: Story three
text: Over the next few days, she was thinking about what she wanted to do - probably sewing again - so she sent out a few resumes, and also did some paperwork. One afternoon someone rang the bell. Katina quite nonchalantly opened the door, only to be startled by two men.

title: Story three
text: "Good afternoon, Miroslav Dráb, Financial Office for the Central Bohemian Region, regional office Kladno," the first introduced himself.

title: Story three
text: "Good day, Vojtěch Sebral, also the tax office," said the other.

title: Story three
text: "I hereby deliver to you a writ of distraint (seizure order) for the sale of movable property. Please sign it here," Dráb spoke again.

title: Story three
text: Katina was startled and slammed the door in their faces.

title: Story three
text: "Come on, madam, be sensible."

title: Story three
text: "Go away!" she replied desperately.

text: "We can, but we'll come again. You can't avoid it."

text: She didn't answer. She was scared and didn't know what to do.

title: Story three
text: "Well, as you wish," he grumbled. Then she heard them both leave.

title: Story three
text: She stood outside the door for a moment in utter shock. She looked through the peephole and saw an empty hallway. She unfastened the latch and opened the door. She just wanted to make sure they were really gone. When she was sure, she closed the door and tried to fasten the latch, but her hand was shaking.

title: Story three
text: She slumped into her chair and tried not to burst into tears. This was her nightmare. Problems with official authority and everything connected with it.

title: Story three
text: Before, she naively believed that the authorities were there for her, but as she did business, she gradually began to realize that it was all a little different. She does not represent a customer to the officials. If only that! She is not even a sheep to be sheared for them, because many of them do not even realize that they live on her taxes. No, they mostly just treated her like a troublesome insect. This position, combined with having to deal with them, seemed infinitely humiliating to her.

title: Story three
text: If she had something, she would have paid, but she basically had nothing. And not at all as much as they demanded. Of course, she could try to negotiate with the tax office, but her resistance to that was too strong. As long as her business flourished, she paid the state every crown it demanded. After all... what was left for her if she didn't want to end up exactly the way she ended up. But when she had nothing to give, the tax office sent bailiffs on her.

title: Story three
text: She knew that what she was doing was not helping herself. It was perfectly clear to her that this couldn't go well. But she simply couldn't overcome the disgust that the tax office's hyenism evoked in her at that moment.

title: Story three
text: If she did nothing all the time and just lived on support, the state would not only want nothing from her, but would even give her money. For the fact that she ran a business, thanks to which many people could buy the fabrics of their dreams and which supported not only her, but also the state, she now has people on her neck who want to take even the little she has left. She tried to push the whole thing out, it was too stressful.

title: Story three
text: However, they appeared again in a few days. She pretended not to be home.

title: Story three
text: Just let it ring, she thought.

title: Story three
text: "We know you're home. Open!"

title: Story three
text: She remained silent.

title: Story three
text: "We have a locksmith with us, he will open the door."

title: Story three
text: She looked through the peephole—and indeed; the bailiffs stood in the corridor accompanied by another man. It was bad. However, Katina did not want to let them in. She suspected it wasn't wise, but letting strangers invade her privacy and take her things was an absolutely unbearable thought for her.

title: Story three
text: "As you wish," replied the enforcer.

title: Story three
text: Immediately she heard the locksmith getting to work.

title: Story three
text: After a while, the lock loosened, but the door didn't even move, as it was secured from the inside by a massive latch.

title: Story three
text: "Have a mind and open for us! We'll get there eventually anyway," said the bailiff, less confidently.

title: Story three
text: She was as quiet as a mouse, and when she heard the three men leave, she felt a certain - if short-lived - relief.

title: Story three
text: She didn't even know how much time had passed when there was a sharp voice behind her door: "This is the Police of the Czech Republic. In the name of the law, open the door!"

title: Story three
text: She didn't know what to do, despair was taking over her, but she didn't want to open the door. The state had already taken so much money from her and had such a thorough overview of every item in her accounting that she had had enough. The idea that this rabble would rummage through her personal belongings made her sick!

title: Story three
text: "Open the door or we'll be forced to kick it out."

title: Story three
text: She didn't answer. The whole situation was so desperately unpleasant and absurd that the clueless Katina withdrew into herself and shut out what was happening in front of her apartment.

title: Story three
text: And suddenly a BANG! The door flew open. Policemen and bailiffs burst in. They legitimized her. She didn't protest. She also signed the seizure order in the end. What else did she have left? The police officers commented on the broken door and instructed her that she should have opened it. Enforcement officers from the tax office began to tape things up. Katina just stood quietly, unable to resist, watching everything as if in a dream and wondering what she had actually done so terrible... Yes, she probably could have handled the situation more actively and sensibly, but who did she hurt to deserve this? She went to the window, looked out, sang softly to herself, and let the uninvited guests do what they wanted in her house.

title: Anarcho-capitalism
text: Three stories. The first about foul robbers who robbed a defenseless woman; the second about mobsters threatening violence, instilling fear and collecting protection money; however, the third is different, as it is about an unsuccessful small business woman who got into trouble through her own fault and subsequent laxity. At least that's how most people perceive these stories. Are you among them? Then this book was written just for you; I would like to offer a different point of view for consideration, which you don't have to agree with, but I will be very happy if you at least think about it - if possible without prejudices and pre-formed conclusions, for which you only look for arguments in retrospect.

title: Anarcho-capitalism
text: I hope everyone will agree when I say that the actions of the robbers and the mafia are reprehensible. But let's ask ourselves the question - why is this so? For what reason do we reject looting and the collection of protection money? Well, we consider it wrong to appropriate someone else's resources by force (or the threat of violence) against the will of their owner, because whoever spends his time and energy to get something deserves to enjoy the fruits of his labor in peace; no one should have the right to take them from him just because he has more power at a given time and place. Of course, it happens sometimes and there will always be similar incidents, but it is important to condemn such behavior and stand against it.

title: Anarcho-capitalism
text: But what are taxes? Unfortunately, the same thing; people have to give their resources to someone (the state) under the threat of violence. It is not so clearly visible at first glance, because the state violence is somewhat hidden; while in the first story the use of force was quite explicit, in the second less so, and in the third the force was actually used only after the victim had been given many chances to solve the situation differently. However, these are technical differences, not moral ones; in all cases, the attacker claims foreign resources and uses force to obtain them if they are not given to him. In general, the stronger a robber is, the more chances he can afford to give his victim: the vagabonds in the park had to turn Teresa around right away, because if they let her go, they would lose the loot; the mob could have given Rosalia some time to think, but when that didn't help, they resorted to intimidation; the state could afford to give Katina many chances, because when she didn't take any of them, he just robbed her in broad daylight without anyone saying anything.

title: Anarcho-capitalism
text: I'm not saying there aren't differences between park pickpockets, the mob, and the state; I am merely pointing out that although there are many differences of a technical nature between robbery, extortion, and taxation, ethically it is still the same thing: The strong threatens the weak and demands that they pay him; if he does not pay, violence will be used against him, which will eventually force him to pay anyway. I fully understand that this sounds absurd in the case of the state, and you may well be tapping your forehead now; however, all of history is full of cases of obvious atrocities that were considered normal or even right at the time. If someone defended the accused during the witch trials by saying that their blasphemy didn't hurt anyone because witchcraft doesn't exist, he might very well end up at the stake himself. And what about the violence of the master against the slave? If any one in a slave society were to declare that it was morally as bad as violence to a free man, he would be laughed at by all; after all, something like this cannot be compared at all! Just like you can't compare robbers, the state and the mafia...

title: Anarcho-capitalism
text: One might argue that the state provides various services to citizens for the money it collects; on the other hand, when the robber buys something with the victim's stolen money (perhaps all of it), his robbery hardly ceases to be a robbery (the Japanese yakuza mafia sometimes helps victims during natural disasters; this does not excuse its crimes, however). It is also true that in a (democratic) state, people voted and enacted taxes; but just because people vote and legalize something, it does not automatically become justified and legitimate (then we would have to admit that everything that has ever happened with the sanctification of a sufficient number of people was in order - for example, although not only, the democratic election of Hitler to power or the subsequent holocaust, which was also in accordance with the law of the time). Someone can also argue that the state clearly declares its intentions to tax and there are rules for this; certainly yes, however, when the mafia declares its intention to collect protection money as clearly as it does, it is difficult to call it legitimate. For a similar reason, the argument that the taxpayer can move out if he doesn't like it doesn't hold up; so can the protection money payer.

title: Anarcho-capitalism
text: Good; but even if we morally reject the state, who will build roads, educate children, care for the poor, heal the sick, protect the environment, catch criminals, adjudicate disputes and guard borders against enemies? Paradoxically, it was the search for answers to these questions and the search for the most effective way to solve the above (and other) problems that led me years ago to reflect on the ethics of the functioning of the state; I strongly resisted it, I didn't like the idea at all, but long discussions, in which my goal was to show the necessity and necessity of the state establishment, finally convinced me that morality and efficiency go hand in hand, but in complete opposition to the state. I became an anarcho-capitalist.

title: Anarcho-capitalism
text: What does that mean, you ask? What is anarcho-capitalism? Although most people associate anarchy with egalitarians, communists and the left in general, there are also anarchist schools based on respect for property rights and the free market, which they believe could replace all functions of the state, as absurd as that sounds; and anarcho-capitalism is one such school. Like all other anarchists, anarcho-capitalists passionately love freedom and heartily hate the state; however, our reasons (and means) are different - the highest value for us is freedom and the responsibility that is inextricably linked to it, while we - unlike most other anarchists - believe that real freedom can be achieved through respect for private property and property rights, because in our eyes, a free person is one who can enjoy the fruits of his own work and make his own decisions about life, without anyone forcing him to do something or taking from him what is his. The state then represents the greatest usurper and aggressor, ordering people how they should and should not live, not to mention forcing them to hand over to it most of what they earn. All of this is done under the threat of violence, because whoever does not obey, does not pay the protection money (loosely called taxes) and defends his property against the aggressor, will end up behind bars at best, or underground at worst.

title: Anarcho-capitalism
text: Anarcho-capitalism is by no means a heartless materialistic ideology reducing people to mere numbers in an accounting without any rights. On the contrary, I personally believe that people should help each other, so I donate part of my income to the poor who, in my opinion, need it. Anarcho-capitalists are certainly not against solidarity (in fact, on the contrary; I would describe most of the ones I know as very compassionate and kind people), they just believe that it should be voluntary and no one should be forced into it under threat of violence (which is exactly what the state does). We are not indifferent to human rights either; the difference from how they are perceived by the state, which restricts the freedom of its citizens in order to enforce them, is that we define them using property rights - for example, we derive the "right to life" from the principle of self-ownership, according to which people are the owners of their bodies, so attacking them is a violation of their property rights.

title: Anarcho-capitalism
text: Anarcho-capitalists are not social engineers, eager to plan people's lives; on the contrary, we are convinced that everyone can make the best decisions about their own lives, because no politician (or anyone else) knows what is best for others. It is not our interest to dictate to anyone how to live, we only consider it right not to force anyone to do anything, as long as the person in question looks after his own and does not attack others in any way; and even if the majority democratically votes to intervene against him, it will not turn a bad thing into a good one.

title: Anarcho-capitalism
text: We just want to live freely in peace and quiet; we want to love, have fun, work, decide for ourselves. We do not want and need someone who will forcefully take most of the fruits of our labor and "for a reward" dictate to us what we can and cannot say publicly, what we can and cannot sell and buy, under what conditions we can and cannot work. We want to make our own decisions and, of course, bear all the consequences. We want to raise our children without our rulers deciding which values we should lead them to more and which ones less or when, in what way and in which institutions they should be educated. Because that's freedom.

title: Anarcho-capitalism
text: "It's a nice fairy tale, but without the state, our society simply wouldn't function," you think? Well, such an objection is perfectly natural, and I should be surprised if no one made it; after all, it was the first thing that came to mind when I first heard about anarcho-capitalism. And it's no wonder, because this is exactly what we've all been presented with since elementary school; after all, it is the state that determines what is taught in schools. On the other hand, a century or two ago slavery was perfectly normal, an institution thousands of years old. Before it was abolished in many countries, the most common arguments for its preservation were something like this: "The abolition of slavery is a nice fairy tale, but without slaves, society simply wouldn't work because there wouldn't be enough people to work." Doesn't that sound familiar? At that time it was also absolutely clear to most people that the abolition of slavery was pure utopia. But today?

title: Anarcho-capitalism
text: History is paved with huge mistakes of humanity, which sometimes take hundreds or thousands of years to correct; and I am not asserting anything here other than that states are just another such error in a series. I know very well how difficult it is to think constructively and dispassionately about theses that question the very foundations of what was instilled in us from a young age, so I ask the reader to be patient and open-minded when reading a book about how a free stateless society might one day function. I do not claim that everything must necessarily look exactly as I describe, because it is realistically impossible to predict exactly where human creativity will take us; perhaps reality far exceeds my expectations. However, when I first read about anarcho-capitalism, I could not imagine how the market could replace all the functions of the state; so in this book I deal with individual areas in which the state operates and try to describe how state laws could be replaced by free market principles.

title: A few words in the introduction
text: Sixteen chapters will now follow. The first four contain certain general principles. Twelve others describe how individual areas managed by the state today (such as education, healthcare, judiciary, police and many others) could function in a free market. Finally, you can look forward to a few bonus chapters and quick answers to some common objections to a stateless society.

title: A few words in the introduction
text: Since the first four chapters mainly contain theory, they may not be very readable for some (although I tried not to be too boring); however, those who want to read straight away about how this or that could work without the state can skip to the fifth chapter (about money). However, it should be taken into account that throughout the book I refer to the first four theoretical chapters in the explanation - especially the second one.

title: A few words in the introduction
text: When reading about how individual industries could function in a free market, one must always remember that when I mention an alternative to providing certain services without state intervention, I am certainly not claiming that this is the only possible non-state way. It is absurd to think that none of the millions of businessmen could devise the provision of that service better than I outline it here (or as any handful of the best politicians could); just imagine what this world looked like just a hundred years ago, and how the brilliant ideas and diligence of many people exceeded even the assumptions of the most daring visionaries of the time. The free market simply cannot be predicted; if so, he would go to plan centrally, which is not possible, as we will soon show. These are only possible variants of how such a world could (but might not) look like.

title: A few words in the introduction
text: Because state-controlled schools convince us of the necessity of the state and the correctness of democracy from an early age, when our minds and opinions are just beginning to form, I write my texts as an opposition to such claims. But my opponents have one huge advantage; they started much earlier (within the state education system) and have already planted in most people's heads in advance that the ideas I advocate are absurd, unrealistic, undesirable and meaningless. Hand on heart: Who among you, dear readers, is already negative about the idea of a stateless society? And who of you who do have seriously and open-mindedly entertained the idea for some time? I know many will reject this book; however, I would like to ask you not to do so based on "arguments" such as: "Everyone knows that wouldn't work," but after mature - and if possible unbiased - reasoning.

title: A few words in the introduction
text: It is possible that you will find chapters in the book that will make sense to you, but also some that you will definitely not be able to identify with; that's perfectly fine. I'm not proclaiming a revolution, there's no need to abolish the state overnight, for now it's more than enough to reduce it. Even if, after reading this book, you come to the conclusion that we need the state, but there is even a single industry that you previously thought should be managed, but you have changed your mind, I consider that a great success. And if that doesn't happen either, I will be very happy if you at least think about the necessity or dispensability of the state.

title: 1. Scarce resources and the price system
text: Everyone has probably heard of the invisible hand of the market; some refer to it, others ridicule it. However, not everyone knows that this is a relatively old phrase; and even fewer people suspect that this label was first used in the eighteenth century by the British thinker Adam Smith in his work "The Wealth of Nations". However, it is sometimes surprising how little many - and sometimes even people with a diploma certifying their economic education - imagine under this term; very often their awareness ends with the fact that the author probably wanted to metaphorically indicate that the market will somehow arrange everything.

title: 1. Scarce resources and the price system
text: The truth is that Adam Smith probably really meant to say what the market will arrange; however, this is no vague "somehow" - there is a perfectly clear and comprehensive theory of how and why this happens. Two centuries later, this idea of his was further developed and, above all, much better described by the outstanding economist of the Austrian school of economics, Ludwig von Mises (and his student Friedrich August von Hayek, who received the Nobel Prize in Economics in 1974 for his work, continued this). Its essence, which applies to each of us, can be summarized as follows: If I do something for people that pleases them, they will gladly pay me for it. Therefore, wealth in a free market is a measure of how much a person has done for others according to their own rankings of values. But let's start from the beginning.

title: 1. Scarce resources and the price system
text: When people hold discussions on the topic of what the proper social order should be, how society should be organized, some propose anarchy, others minarchy, others monarchy, some democracy/socialism... But what are they really talking about? What is the difference between these – and other – systems? It is primarily a matter of deciding how to use what we only have a limited amount of - i.e. labor force, natural resources, means of production, material. Collectively, we call such goods "scarce resources" and by this we mean (simplistically) anything that is limited in quantity, so that people must share it (when one person uses something, no one else can use it at the same time).

title: 1. Scarce resources and the price system
text: Rare resources are for example: meat, computer, cow, operating surgeon's work, iron ore mine, miner's work, mine cart, steel ingot. On the contrary, rare resources in normal conditions are not: air (by breathing, you do not limit anyone else's breathing - so, for example, in a submerged submarine or a space shuttle in orbit, air is a rare commodity) or sunlight. Using the example of air, we can see beautifully that the rarity of resources can change over time and space.

title: 1. Scarce resources and the price system
text: The utility of scarce resources is subjective. For me, for example, a juicy steak is of more use than a head of cabbage; for a vegetarian it will probably be the opposite. And it is the subjectivity of utility that is the basis for voluntary exchange. If I have cabbage and a veggie steak, we can exchange it, increasing the utility of what we own for both of us (it's also worth noting that this transaction makes people better off without anything being produced; voluntary exchanges generally increase the utility of all participants in this way). Now let's imagine that there will be someone else standing next to him who is willing to give the vegetarian two heads for that piece of meat. Presumably, the vegetarian's utility from two heads of cabbage exceeds his utility from a single head, so he will prefer this exchange to the exchange with me.

title: 1. Scarce resources and the price system
text: Therefore, if a vegetarian knows someone with whom meat can be exchanged for cabbage, meat begins to have value for him as well. The value is also subjective and corresponds to either the direct benefit from the given good or the benefit of what can be exchanged for this good. In the second case, we still have to calculate that the exchange costs some time, always carries with it certain risks, and we are never completely sure that it will take place. These are all factors that reduce value - we'll get to the implications of that later. For now, it is important to realize that the value of goods is assigned by individual people (so it is subjective), either according to the direct benefit they bring to them, or what they can exchange them for.

title: 1. Scarce resources and the price system
text: A small complication occurs when I have cabbage to exchange, I want a steak, but my vegetarian friend (who owns meat) doesn't feel like a head at the moment, but he would rather have bread. In that case, I have to look for someone to trade bread for cabbage. If the transactions are more complicated in this way, another problem arises: If the vegetarian trades meat only for heads, it is immediately clear to him which store will end up with the most heads; however, if he exchanges indirectly through other people through completely different goods, comparing the advantages of individual trades is difficult or impossible. This led to people choosing some suitable commodity (typically precious metals) to use as a universal medium of exchange (called money); then it was not necessary to determine ratios between countless different goods, the ratio of each good to money was always sufficient, with the help of which the exchange ratio between any goods could be easily determined.

title: 1. Scarce resources and the price system
text: We call the exchange rate of some good and money the price. One basic observation can be made about price: In a group of people who trade with each other (we can call such a group a market), the price of a single good in different exchanges usually does not vary much; of course it changes over time, but it is usually almost the same for different sellers in the same period within the same market. Why? Every buyer tries to buy as cheaply as possible, every seller wants to sell as expensive as possible; while each buyer has a maximum (and each seller a minimum), above which (or below which) the price will no longer go, because their subjective benefit would not increase with such a deal, but would decrease. Buyers then tend to buy from sellers with the lowest prices; sellers want to be bought from them, so they lower the price (compete), but not so much that they lose. In this way, the price stabilizes at a level acceptable to everyone who participates in the exchanges - and we can call such a stable price the market price.

title: 1. Scarce resources and the price system
text: All the findings stated so far are quite trivial and each of us probably understands them (at least on a subconscious basis) - but we stated and described them precisely so that we could draw further consequences from them. First of all, it is necessary to realize what circumstances affect the prices of goods. When consumers are a little more interested, or when something starts to run out on the seller's side, it becomes rarer, so sellers can raise prices without losing customers (if they kept the original price, the item would simply sell out immediately). On the other hand, when the demand for something falls, or if there is a way to get/produce much more of it for the same effort, the price will fall, because sellers can afford to lower the price (to attract as many customers as possible).

title: 1. Scarce resources and the price system
text: What will happen if a natural resource starts to run out, or if its further acquisition becomes expensive? From the above it follows that its price will increase; as well as the price of products made from it. And the consequences of this price increase? First, consumers begin to buy less of it (because it is expensive, they begin to look for alternatives to do without it), thus saving something that is itself scarce. And secondly (probably most importantly) the increased price will attract other entrepreneurs to enter the industry and look for better solutions (use of other raw materials, more efficient mining, more economical production, production of substitutes, and so on). Prices serve as a great carrier of information about the world: We don't even need to know what happened where, why something is in short supply, we just need to try to maximize our utility (which we do anyway) and it's likely that we won't waste; we don't have to invent any solutions to remote problems at all, we don't have to have a cure for everything, we just have to wait and the natural desire of entrepreneurs for profit will solve those problems: The greater the lack of something, the more it is missing, the more people are motivated to deal with it, because they can get rich from it.

title: 1. Scarce resources and the price system
text: Conversely, when a resource becomes more available (and again it doesn't matter for what reason; most people may not know about it at all - it will still affect their behavior, this information will be transmitted to them through prices), producers can lower prices to lure customers away from competitors. They will proceed in this way as long as possible, so that they can make a profit from it, for which it is still worthwhile for them to do it. If the product becomes cheaper, people will tend to buy more of it and possibly replace it with other more expensive substitutes (thus, what is abundant is used a lot, but what is scarce is not wasted). A similar situation occurs if consumers simply begin to demand less of the given goods. Some sellers will go down in price (if they can), others will change their supply, and others will go bankrupt, which is correct (there is a surplus of the good, so it must be stopped, which is exactly what happens if some producers change their supply and those who don't go bankrupt).

title: 1. Scarce resources and the price system
text: The following also follows from the last two paragraphs: Those who make the best use of scarce resources, i.e. transform them into something that is even more beneficial to society, become rich. On the contrary, those who waste precious resources, i.e. transform them into something that has less value for society than the resources they use for it, become poor and subsequently go bankrupt. To solve all problems like "how/if to provide a service" or "how/if to make a product" just let thousands and millions of entrepreneurs just try it. Those of them who do it wrong (= differently than people want) will go bankrupt (and go do something that will benefit society more). On the contrary, those who do it right (= as people wish) will prosper. Every service (even product) can be provided in several correct ways (if different groups of people prefer different ways, quality and price); then those firms that fulfill consumers' wishes (i.e. follow any of the "correct" paths) will remain on the market.

title: 1. Scarce resources and the price system
text: Although almost all the insights we have presented in this chapter are rather intuitive and clear, I ask the reader to let them go through their heads and think about what interesting consequences for the organization of society follow from them.
