section: Aktivity spekulantů ožebračují slušné lidi; o peníze, které spekulant svými obchody vydělal, musel někoho jiného připravit!
title: The activities of speculators impoverish decent people; he had to rob someone else of the money the speculator made from his trades!
text: Hatred of speculators stems from Ricardo's long-overdue cost theory of value, which was refuted by Carl Menger as early as 1870, when he came up with the subjective theory of value; however, many still mistakenly believe that the value of goods is fixed. In reality, however, it is attributed to them by people, ergo it is subjective and changes over time. Things can gain and lose value without changing in any way.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Ekonomie
section: Aktivity spekulantů ožebračují slušné lidi; o peníze, které spekulant svými obchody vydělal, musel někoho jiného připravit!
title: The activities of speculators impoverish decent people; he had to rob someone else of the money the speculator made from his trades!
text: Speculators use this feature to enrich themselves; they buy cheap to sell at a higher price later. Does it harm others? To answer this question it is necessary to realize why the prices of goods fall and rise; a decrease means their excess, an increase, on the contrary, a shortage. Therefore, in order to make a profit, the speculator must buy surplus goods and sell shortages; what are the consequences of such action?

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Ekonomie
section: Aktivity spekulantů ožebračují slušné lidi; o peníze, které spekulant svými obchody vydělal, musel někoho jiného připravit!
title: The activities of speculators impoverish decent people; he had to rob someone else of the money the speculator made from his trades!
text: In times of surplus, speculators help producers not go bankrupt; in times of need, in turn, they supply shoppers with scarce goods, thereby reducing their price. In essence, they "smooth out" price fluctuations over time. That is what those of them who earn do; they help society and are rewarded for it. The losers, on the other hand, do harm (for which they themselves pay the most); and strangely so much anger is not borne on their heads.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Ekonomie
section: Aktivity spekulantů ožebračují slušné lidi; o peníze, které spekulant svými obchody vydělal, musel někoho jiného připravit!
title: The activities of speculators impoverish decent people; he had to rob someone else of the money the speculator made from his trades!
text: The market is not a zero sum game! The gain of one does not mean the loss of another; this would be true if the prices of goods were objectively given. But this is not the case, because in a voluntary business transaction, each party values what it gains more than what it gives up (otherwise the trade would not take place); therefore, when one gains something, it does not follow that another has lost. Speculators do not make money at the expense of others.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Ekonomie
section: I kdyby trh ve všem ostatním fungoval, neumí si dobře poradit s problémem veřejných statků; nutně potřebujeme (demokratický) stát v otázce jejich poskytování a zajišťování plateb.
title: Even if the market were to work in everything else, it cannot deal well with the problem of public goods; we absolutely need a (democratic) state in the matter of providing them and securing payments.
text: Public goods are those that benefit everyone, whether they pay for them or not; Take public lighting as an example. The problem arises when the following way of thinking of individuals becomes widespread: Public lighting will benefit me, whether I pay for it or not; however, I will save money by not paying, and the chance that there will be no lighting in the end due to the absence of my contribution is minimal.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Ekonomie
section: I kdyby trh ve všem ostatním fungoval, neumí si dobře poradit s problémem veřejných statků; nutně potřebujeme (demokratický) stát v otázce jejich poskytování a zajišťování plateb.
title: Even if the market were to work in everything else, it cannot deal well with the problem of public goods; we absolutely need a (democratic) state in the matter of providing them and securing payments.
text: Financing goods, from the consumption of which it is difficult to exclude black passengers, can be difficult in the free market (although solvable, since everything is privately owned); the state is claimed to be able to "solve" this problem. On the one hand, this is not true (those who have nothing, do not pay taxes and are black passengers of the state), but above all, the state "solution" causes far greater difficulties; especially in a democracy.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Ekonomie
section: I kdyby trh ve všem ostatním fungoval, neumí si dobře poradit s problémem veřejných statků; nutně potřebujeme (demokratický) stát v otázce jejich poskytování a zajišťování plateb.
title: Even if the market were to work in everything else, it cannot deal well with the problem of public goods; we absolutely need a (democratic) state in the matter of providing them and securing payments.
text: The big problem with democratic elections is that in order for a citizen to make an informed decision about who to vote for, he would have to spend an enormous amount of time studying electoral programs, both in terms of practical implications and credibility; and even if the voter spends that time, the chances of his vote making a difference are slim to none, ergo a smart strategy is to not care about the election if he doesn't enjoy it.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Ekonomie
section: I kdyby trh ve všem ostatním fungoval, neumí si dobře poradit s problémem veřejných statků; nutně potřebujeme (demokratický) stát v otázce jejich poskytování a zajišťování plateb.
title: Even if the market were to work in everything else, it cannot deal well with the problem of public goods; we absolutely need a (democratic) state in the matter of providing them and securing payments.
text: Does this remind you of anything? A relatively high price must be paid for the slim chance that a person can make an impact; this, of course, makes many individuals prefer not to pay the price (whether it is dozens of hours of studying political party programs or a contribution to public lighting). So democracy offers only the transformation of a relatively small problem (public goods) into a huge one (the whole government), but not its solution.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Historie
section: Všechny ty anarchokapitalistické teorie jsou sice hezké, ale ukažte mi jedinou reálnou fungující anarchistickou společnost; taková nikdy existovat nemůže.
title: All those anarcho-capitalist theories are nice, but show me a single real working anarchist society; such can never exist.
text: Anarchy has already proven itself in history. Take Iceland as an example, which has been an anarchy for almost a thousand years since its settlement; although it was formally annexed by Norway and Denmark after a few centuries, the population there actually lived in anarchy. Although the Icelandic National Assembly Althing is sometimes referred to as the first European parliament, it was more of a "council of elders" that did not issue laws applicable to all residents.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Historie
section: Všechny ty anarchokapitalistické teorie jsou sice hezké, ale ukažte mi jedinou reálnou fungující anarchistickou společnost; taková nikdy existovat nemůže.
title: All those anarcho-capitalist theories are nice, but show me a single real working anarchist society; such can never exist.
text: Another example of functioning anarcho-capitalism was the United States during the period of colonization. Despite what westerns show, crime at that time was significantly lower than it is today; not only in absolute numbers, but also in per capita terms. The colonizers got along well with the natives (they bought land from them and made treaties that were respected) until the European states sent an army there.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Historie
section: Všechny ty anarchokapitalistické teorie jsou sice hezké, ale ukažte mi jedinou reálnou fungující anarchistickou společnost; taková nikdy existovat nemůže.
title: All those anarcho-capitalist theories are nice, but show me a single real working anarchist society; such can never exist.
text: Another example is medieval Ireland, although there is some debate as to whether this society can be described as anarchist. On the one hand, there was no Irish central government, but on the other, many different territories were ruled by local warlords at different times, with the degree of freedom of the people in these areas varying greatly - sometimes really high, sometimes not.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Historie
section: Všechny ty anarchokapitalistické teorie jsou sice hezké, ale ukažte mi jedinou reálnou fungující anarchistickou společnost; taková nikdy existovat nemůže.
title: All those anarcho-capitalist theories are nice, but show me a single real working anarchist society; such can never exist.
text: Until recently, the most famous anarchy was Somalia; the truth is that compared to modern and developed states, Somalia has no chance to succeed. On the other hand, no judgmental anarchist claims that arbitrary anarchy is better than arbitrary state; it's just that in every time and place anarchy is better than the state, which is also confirmed by Somalia: The situation on its territory without a government was significantly better than with it (though worse than here, for example).

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Historie
section: Všechny historicky známé anarchie fungovaly pouze za specifických podmínek; to ale neznamená, že by anarchokapitalismus mohl být funkční dnes, v současném světě.
title: All historically known anarchies functioned only under specific conditions; but that does not mean that anarcho-capitalism could be functional today, in the contemporary world.
text: This objection is no doubt quite valid; it is just an objection to an argument that does not defend anarcho-capitalism. The assumption of the functioning of anarcho-capitalism in today's world results from elaborate and still unproven theories, which are based on several axioms (resulting from economics - praxeology - and ethics), from which they are derived using pure logic.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Historie
section: Všechny historicky známé anarchie fungovaly pouze za specifických podmínek; to ale neznamená, že by anarchokapitalismus mohl být funkční dnes, v současném světě.
title: All historically known anarchies functioned only under specific conditions; but that does not mean that anarcho-capitalism could be functional today, in the contemporary world.
text: Examples of functioning anarchies in the past certainly support these theories, but they do not form their basis; nor does anyone try to construct those historical anarchies as proof that anarcho-capitalism could be feasible even today. The theories of anarcho-capitalism are certainly not based on the fact that sometimes anarchy worked well somewhere.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Historie
section: Všechny historicky známé anarchie fungovaly pouze za specifických podmínek; to ale neznamená, že by anarchokapitalismus mohl být funkční dnes, v současném světě.
title: All historically known anarchies functioned only under specific conditions; but that does not mean that anarcho-capitalism could be functional today, in the contemporary world.
text: It is also true that all functioning anarchies of the past had certain common features, which include low population density (however, this is also due to the fact that in the past the overall population density was practically everywhere much lower than today), or a relatively "remote" geographical location; however, it does not follow that anarcho-capitalism could not function in other conditions.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Historie
section: Všechny historicky známé anarchie fungovaly pouze za specifických podmínek; to ale neznamená, že by anarchokapitalismus mohl být funkční dnes, v současném světě.
title: All historically known anarchies functioned only under specific conditions; but that does not mean that anarcho-capitalism could be functional today, in the contemporary world.
text: Furthermore, it must be realized that things cannot be declared impossible just on the basis that they are not currently realized anywhere; if so, nothing new could ever arise, because we would dismiss everything as pointless, since there is no real example on which the functionality of that idea can be demonstrated (and this very argument prevents the creation of such an example).

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Lidské jednání
section: Podnikatelé sledují jen krátkodobé cíle a činí pouze investice s krátkou dobou návratnosti; pro skutečně dlouhodobé projekty potřebujeme vládu.
title: Entrepreneurs only pursue short-term goals and only make investments with a short payback period; for really long term projects we need government.
text: First of all, it should be mentioned that with politicians it is not exactly a win in the long term, as they are typically elected for four years and their interests usually do not extend beyond that; if they invest for the long term, then mainly because the money they invest is not theirs - so the decision about what to invest in does not depend so much on the necessity of this step, but rather on how many votes it will get the politician.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Lidské jednání
section: Podnikatelé sledují jen krátkodobé cíle a činí pouze investice s krátkou dobou návratnosti; pro skutečně dlouhodobé projekty potřebujeme vládu.
title: Entrepreneurs only pursue short-term goals and only make investments with a short payback period; for really long term projects we need government.
text: The problem with long-term investments lies mainly in the fact that it is very difficult to know which ones are "right" and which ones are not; and since it's possible to invest in a plethora of different things, it's probably the most sensible thing to leave it to free people to decide what they want to finance with their money and what not - after all, it's their money that they've been able to earn, so they can hopefully spend it.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Lidské jednání
section: Podnikatelé sledují jen krátkodobé cíle a činí pouze investice s krátkou dobou návratnosti; pro skutečně dlouhodobé projekty potřebujeme vládu.
title: Entrepreneurs only pursue short-term goals and only make investments with a short payback period; for really long term projects we need government.
text: People sometimes think that the more "long-term" an investment is, the better; this may not always be true. In general, the higher the current wealth, the more it "pays off" to invest in the long term, which applies both to individuals and to society (when we "don't have anything to do", we usually save less for retirement than when we live in abundance); however, there is no need to "manage" it in any way, people behave this way completely naturally.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Lidské jednání
section: Podnikatelé sledují jen krátkodobé cíle a činí pouze investice s krátkou dobou návratnosti; pro skutečně dlouhodobé projekty potřebujeme vládu.
title: Entrepreneurs only pursue short-term goals and only make investments with a short payback period; for really long term projects we need government.
text: An example of such a failed "long-term investment" is the decades-long massive subsidy support for biofuels in the fight against global warming, which led to deforestation (which its authors could have foreseen if they had not been incentivized to the contrary); such a waste of resources is typical when the funds are "public", so the one who decides about them is not the one to whom they belong.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Lidské jednání
section: Kdyby stát nefinancoval některé projekty, nikdy by nevznikly, neboť by na ně lidé sami od sebe dobrovolně nepřispěli; stát tedy musí tyto projekty subvencovat!
title: If the state did not finance some projects, they would never have been created, because people would not voluntarily contribute to them; so the state must subsidize these projects!
text: The first possible response to this objection is that the statist in question who raises it is simply wrong; many projects that are generally considered to simply have to be financed by the state in order not to disappear, have already existed in history without state intervention. It is, of course, in the interest of the state to claim that this is not the case, as it is a very good way to maintain a corresponding monopoly without anyone objecting.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Lidské jednání
section: Kdyby stát nefinancoval některé projekty, nikdy by nevznikly, neboť by na ně lidé sami od sebe dobrovolně nepřispěli; stát tedy musí tyto projekty subvencovat!
title: If the state did not finance some projects, they would never have been created, because people would not voluntarily contribute to them; so the state must subsidize these projects!
text: The second possibility is that the statist who raises the above objection is right; that project would really disappear without state support. What does this mean? Well, only so much that people are simply not interested in the project in question, or rather they want to invest their money in something else that they consider more important, and no one other than the person concerned can properly judge this importance.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Lidské jednání
section: Kdyby stát nefinancoval některé projekty, nikdy by nevznikly, neboť by na ně lidé sami od sebe dobrovolně nepřispěli; stát tedy musí tyto projekty subvencovat!
title: If the state did not finance some projects, they would never have been created, because people would not voluntarily contribute to them; so the state must subsidize these projects!
text: Therefore, if the state implements a project that would not have been created without it, it actually does the people a disservice, because it takes their savings and invests them in something, instead of which the people in question would rather buy something else that is more important to them (if this were not the case, the project would have been created even without state intervention); therefore, it is a simple waste of resources on less important things at the expense of the more important ones.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Lidské jednání
section: Kdyby stát nefinancoval některé projekty, nikdy by nevznikly, neboť by na ně lidé sami od sebe dobrovolně nepřispěli; stát tedy musí tyto projekty subvencovat!
title: If the state did not finance some projects, they would never have been created, because people would not voluntarily contribute to them; so the state must subsidize these projects!
text: A common counterargument is this: "People want the project, but they're struggling with poverty, so they just can't afford it." On closer reflection, however, we come to the fact that this is all the more in line with what was described above: The people in question are poor, so they prefer to buy food and other basic things with their money, and so then they cannot afford the given project; by the state forcing them to buy it anyway, it certainly won't help them.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Lidské jednání
section: Stát musí lidem zajišťovat věci, které si oni sami nechtějí platit dobrovolně (v dané míře); jedná se například o dotace hromadné dopravy, hasičů a záchranářů, některých druhů umění a podobně.
title: The state must provide people with things that they themselves do not want to pay voluntarily (to a given extent); these are, for example, subsidies for mass transport, firefighters and rescuers, certain types of art, and the like.
text: First of all, it must be said that statist scaremongering on the topic of what would not exist without the state is indeed a very popular pastime of some people, but it is rarely based on any real basis; if we look into historical anarchies, we will find that many services that the general public thinks cannot function without the state have already been provided without the state in the past.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Lidské jednání
section: Stát musí lidem zajišťovat věci, které si oni sami nechtějí platit dobrovolně (v dané míře); jedná se například o dotace hromadné dopravy, hasičů a záchranářů, některých druhů umění a podobně.
title: The state must provide people with things that they themselves do not want to pay voluntarily (to a given extent); these are, for example, subsidies for mass transport, firefighters and rescuers, certain types of art, and the like.
text: This is due to the fact that if there is a demand for a service in society and people are really willing to pay for such a service, an opportunity arises for entrepreneurs who can provide that service and make money from it; thus, an offer is created for each demand, and the more urgent the demand, the more people are willing to pay, which correspondingly increases the motivation of the bidders.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Lidské jednání
section: Stát musí lidem zajišťovat věci, které si oni sami nechtějí platit dobrovolně (v dané míře); jedná se například o dotace hromadné dopravy, hasičů a záchranářů, některých druhů umění a podobně.
title: The state must provide people with things that they themselves do not want to pay voluntarily (to a given extent); these are, for example, subsidies for mass transport, firefighters and rescuers, certain types of art, and the like.
text: It is important to realize that in the event that a service provided by the state does not actually arise on the free market, it means only one thing: There is no interest in such a service, because its operation and provision costs more resources than how much benefit it brings to people, which means that if these resources were invested in another (earning) way, the benefit of society would increase without providing such a service.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Lidské jednání
section: Stát musí lidem zajišťovat věci, které si oni sami nechtějí platit dobrovolně (v dané míře); jedná se například o dotace hromadné dopravy, hasičů a záchranářů, některých druhů umění a podobně.
title: The state must provide people with things that they themselves do not want to pay voluntarily (to a given extent); these are, for example, subsidies for mass transport, firefighters and rescuers, certain types of art, and the like.
text: This, by the way, refutes a favorite argument that statists like to use to defend various social experiments (often in transportation, but not only): "Even if it saves just one single human life, it's worth it." Not necessarily; resources are limited and another investment could save more lives or benefit people in some other way.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Lidské jednání
section: Jen pohleďte na „obyčejné lidi“, ti stát prostě potřebují, aby se o ně postaral; dělají spoustu hloupých rozhodnutí a nebýt státu, pomřou hlady na ulicích.
title: Just look at the "ordinary people", they just need the state to take care of them; they make a lot of stupid decisions and if it wasn't for the state, they would starve to death in the streets.
text: The fact is that some people behave irresponsibly and often do not think much about their actions. But the reason why they are so is mainly because they can afford it, because they rely on the protection of an all-powerful state; and the more the state convinces them that it provides them with "safety" and "certainties", the less will be the need for these people to take care of themselves and bear responsibility.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Lidské jednání
section: Jen pohleďte na „obyčejné lidi“, ti stát prostě potřebují, aby se o ně postaral; dělají spoustu hloupých rozhodnutí a nebýt státu, pomřou hlady na ulicích.
title: Just look at the "ordinary people", they just need the state to take care of them; they make a lot of stupid decisions and if it wasn't for the state, they would starve to death in the streets.
text: The state inculcates in its citizens from a very young age, from school age, that one of the tasks of a proper state is to take care of the weak, the old, the helpless and all those who "were not lucky in life"; in this way, the state practically confirms to its citizens that if they have a problem, it will take care of them and provide for them, thereby actually taking over their responsibility for their own lives, and thus making them individuals without autonomy.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Lidské jednání
section: Jen pohleďte na „obyčejné lidi“, ti stát prostě potřebují, aby se o ně postaral; dělají spoustu hloupých rozhodnutí a nebýt státu, pomřou hlady na ulicích.
title: Just look at the "ordinary people", they just need the state to take care of them; they make a lot of stupid decisions and if it wasn't for the state, they would starve to death in the streets.
text: The sad truth is that if the state in any way mitigates the consequences of any type of irresponsible behavior, it also motivates people to this behavior; being irresponsible and not worrying about anything is of course very convenient (compared to building savings and providing for bad times), so people will not happily do it if someone promises to do it for them (obviously with other people's money).

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Lidské jednání
section: Jen pohleďte na „obyčejné lidi“, ti stát prostě potřebují, aby se o ně postaral; dělají spoustu hloupých rozhodnutí a nebýt státu, pomřou hlady na ulicích.
title: Just look at the "ordinary people", they just need the state to take care of them; they make a lot of stupid decisions and if it wasn't for the state, they would starve to death in the streets.
text: People are not incapable of taking care of themselves. With a strong state behind them, they just don't have much reason to even attempt such a thing; until the state took responsibility for the people, they took care of themselves, even in conditions far worse than the ones we live in now. People aren't self-righteous idiots, they're just naturally comfortable and most don't want to take responsibility when they don't have to.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Peníze a bankovnictví
section: Banky musí být regulovány státem, aby držely nějaké frakční rezervy; kdyby takto regulovány nebyly, emitovaly by neomezené množství peněz (ostatně by bez státních zákonů mohl peníze tisknout každý).
title: Banks must be regulated by the state to hold any fractional reserves; if they were not regulated in this way, they would issue an unlimited amount of money (after all, without state laws, anyone could print money).
text: The reason why this fallacy is relatively widespread is extremely sad. It consists in the fact that the state has already distorted most people's idea of the essence and meaning of money to such an extent that almost no one can even imagine free market and non-state money; this confusion then results in ideas that private money could not work because everyone could print it.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Peníze a bankovnictví
section: Banky musí být regulovány státem, aby držely nějaké frakční rezervy; kdyby takto regulovány nebyly, emitovaly by neomezené množství peněz (ostatně by bez státních zákonů mohl peníze tisknout každý).
title: Banks must be regulated by the state to hold any fractional reserves; if they were not regulated in this way, they would issue an unlimited amount of money (after all, without state laws, anyone could print money).
text: The catch, of course, is that the state has established some currency as official and forces people to accept it, so if anyone were to be able to issue this money without any restrictions, it would be a disaster. However, in a free market there is no forced currency, the acceptance of which is enforced by force, ergo untrustworthy money that is created by someone simply will not be accepted in the market.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Peníze a bankovnictví
section: Banky musí být regulovány státem, aby držely nějaké frakční rezervy; kdyby takto regulovány nebyly, emitovaly by neomezené množství peněz (ostatně by bez státních zákonů mohl peníze tisknout každý).
title: Banks must be regulated by the state to hold any fractional reserves; if they were not regulated in this way, they would issue an unlimited amount of money (after all, without state laws, anyone could print money).
text: Another reason why banks in the free market cannot afford to keep fractional reserves too low is so-called hostile clearing, which is a form of competition between banks that buy as many of their competitor's banknotes as possible, then ask them to exchange these notes for gold - it is actually an artificially induced run on the rival bank; when the latter does not have enough gold, it goes bankrupt.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Peníze a bankovnictví
section: Banky musí být regulovány státem, aby držely nějaké frakční rezervy; kdyby takto regulovány nebyly, emitovaly by neomezené množství peněz (ostatně by bez státních zákonů mohl peníze tisknout každý).
title: Banks must be regulated by the state to hold any fractional reserves; if they were not regulated in this way, they would issue an unlimited amount of money (after all, without state laws, anyone could print money).
text: Even in history, free market banks functioned well, private money did not cause problems; as long as the currency was hedged, there were no business cycles. An example is the "Bank of Scotland" and the "Royal Bank of Scotland", which in the eighteenth century kept gold reserves very high without any regulation (due to hostile clearing), thereby preventing economic crises that affected neighboring England.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Peníze a bankovnictví
section: Banky musí být silně regulované, neboť jejich deregulace způsobila hospodářskou krizi; tato krize je navíc ukázkou selhání volného trhu.
title: Banks must be heavily regulated because their deregulation caused the economic crisis; this crisis is also an example of the failure of the free market.
text: If there is any law that restricts the free market and individual freedom, it is a regulation. If another law then comes into being that limits the first law in some way, this law can be described as deregulation. And if the government then introduces a third law that limits the validity of the second law, this law is again regulation, not deregulation.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Peníze a bankovnictví
section: Banky musí být silně regulované, neboť jejich deregulace způsobila hospodářskou krizi; tato krize je navíc ukázkou selhání volného trhu.
title: Banks must be heavily regulated because their deregulation caused the economic crisis; this crisis is also an example of the failure of the free market.
text: With the first law, the state forced the people to adopt a single national currency, a completely illegitimate act of violence that governments mostly justified as the need to finance war activities (which are typically nothing more than another needless violence); selected banks were granted the privilege by the state to print and create this currency (based on some rules). So it was about regulation.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Peníze a bankovnictví
section: Banky musí být silně regulované, neboť jejich deregulace způsobila hospodářskou krizi; tato krize je navíc ukázkou selhání volného trhu.
title: Banks must be heavily regulated because their deregulation caused the economic crisis; this crisis is also an example of the failure of the free market.
text: With another law, the state set stricter rules for banks to issue new money and make loans; although some label this law as regulatory and so-called "pro-market", however, considering that it is a limitation of the power of the banks given to them by the state despite the free market, this label is completely misleading. This law is therefore deregulatory.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Peníze a bankovnictví
section: Banky musí být silně regulované, neboť jejich deregulace způsobila hospodářskou krizi; tato krize je navíc ukázkou selhání volného trhu.
title: Banks must be heavily regulated because their deregulation caused the economic crisis; this crisis is also an example of the failure of the free market.
text: Finally came a law that loosened the rules for banks to issue more money and make more loans; however, if the free market currency is typically 100% bullion-backed, while the state currency is only a fraction, a further reduction in the level of this backing is certainly no deregulation, no step toward the free market. Ergo, the laws that caused the economic recession were regulations, not deregulations.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Peníze a bankovnictví
section: Libertariáni tak často obhajují ten přežitý a staromódní zlatý standard; kdybychom se k němu vrátili, měli bychom opět začít nosit měšce a platit zlatem?
title: Libertarians so often defend the outmoded and old-fashioned gold standard; if we went back to it, should we start carrying pouches and paying in gold again?
text: A gold or silver backed currency is certainly not something that "has long since been outgrown and discarded as a bad concept"; the hedged currency was not actually abandoned by free people, but was forcibly abolished by states that needed to print unhedged money to finance their war appetites (often with politicians promising to return to the gold standard after the war).

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Peníze a bankovnictví
section: Libertariáni tak často obhajují ten přežitý a staromódní zlatý standard; kdybychom se k němu vrátili, měli bychom opět začít nosit měšce a platit zlatem?
title: Libertarians so often defend the outmoded and old-fashioned gold standard; if we went back to it, should we start carrying pouches and paying in gold again?
text: Even if we leave aside the fact that by issuing money the state through banks is robbing its subjects (and thus doing practically the same thing as illegal counterfeiters), so that it is actually another form of taxation (from which this time the banks also profit), nothing changes the fact that a fiat currency is the cause of economic cycles and depressions (they only started to occur with a fiat currency; for the justification, look for the word "ABCT" on the Internet).

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Peníze a bankovnictví
section: Libertariáni tak často obhajují ten přežitý a staromódní zlatý standard; kdybychom se k němu vrátili, měli bychom opět začít nosit měšce a platit zlatem?
title: Libertarians so often defend the outmoded and old-fashioned gold standard; if we went back to it, should we start carrying pouches and paying in gold again?
text: There is in principle no reasonable reason why the state should hold the currency; unlike other sectors of the market, where there are various pseudo-reasons centered on "protecting ordinary people", there is no such thing in the case of money (apart from the popular labeling of a hedged currency as a "long outdated concept"). A currency backed by precious metals (even a private one) worked for hundreds of years without problems around the world.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Peníze a bankovnictví
section: Libertariáni tak často obhajují ten přežitý a staromódní zlatý standard; kdybychom se k němu vrátili, měli bychom opět začít nosit měšce a platit zlatem?
title: Libertarians so often defend the outmoded and old-fashioned gold standard; if we went back to it, should we start carrying pouches and paying in gold again?
text: After the (re)introduction of the gold standard, it would of course not be necessary for all payments to be made by counting gold grains (although coins, especially silver ones, would probably find their place); in today's age of modern technology, of course, it would be possible to store gold in banks that would manage our accounts, allow card payments and the like, only the units would not be crowns, but grams of gold.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: V anarchokapitalismu mohou nastávat situace, ve kterých dochází k nespravedlnosti, neefektivitě, bezpráví a vůbec všelijakým špatnostem; nebude to tedy až tak skvělé společenské uspořádání.
title: In anarcho-capitalism, situations can arise in which injustice, inefficiency, injustice and all kinds of evils occur; so it won't be such a great social arrangement.
text: Similar phenomena will naturally occur in anarcho-capitalism; similarly as in any social arrangement. Nobody offers a recipe for a perfect and ideal world, and anarcho-capitalists are no exception. It does not make sense to look for hypothetical situations in which some social arrangement can fail, but rather to look for an arrangement in which these situations occur least often.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: V anarchokapitalismu mohou nastávat situace, ve kterých dochází k nespravedlnosti, neefektivitě, bezpráví a vůbec všelijakým špatnostem; nebude to tedy až tak skvělé společenské uspořádání.
title: In anarcho-capitalism, situations can arise in which injustice, inefficiency, injustice and all kinds of evils occur; so it won't be such a great social arrangement.
text: No judgmental anarchist sees anarcho-capitalism as a panacea for all the world's problems; they claim only that anarcho-capitalism is a better social order than an arbitrary state. It is therefore of little use to merely point out the potential faults of anarcho-capitalism without mentioning another system (either the current one or some hypothetical one) that would be able to deal with these faults better.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: V anarchokapitalismu mohou nastávat situace, ve kterých dochází k nespravedlnosti, neefektivitě, bezpráví a vůbec všelijakým špatnostem; nebude to tedy až tak skvělé společenské uspořádání.
title: In anarcho-capitalism, situations can arise in which injustice, inefficiency, injustice and all kinds of evils occur; so it won't be such a great social arrangement.
text: There may even be anarcho-capitalist societies whose overall condition is worse than that of some state-controlled societies; if poor and uneducated barbarians live in anarchy, their standard of living will be lower than that of educated and wealthy people who live in a state, but both societies can be assumed to function better without a state than with it.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: V anarchokapitalismu mohou nastávat situace, ve kterých dochází k nespravedlnosti, neefektivitě, bezpráví a vůbec všelijakým špatnostem; nebude to tedy až tak skvělé společenské uspořádání.
title: In anarcho-capitalism, situations can arise in which injustice, inefficiency, injustice and all kinds of evils occur; so it won't be such a great social arrangement.
text: Simply pointing out the faults of anarcho-capitalism without mentioning any social order that can solve this problem better (and at the same time not cause other and worse problems) is practically equivalent to comparing anarcho-capitalism with an ideal - non-existent - society that solves all the world's problems that can potentially arise.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: Anarchokapitalismus není nic než sociální inženýrství; a to je třeba jednoznačně odmítnout, neboť jde o pěkné svinstvo.
title: Anarcho-capitalism is nothing but social engineering; and this must be unequivocally rejected, because it is a nice piece of crap.
text: If anarcho-capitalism is social engineering, then social engineering must be the design of an arbitrary social order. To build a state is to manipulate people through social engineering into submission to the state; if people are manipulated by the theories of anarcho-capitalism for anything, then only to be free and responsible for themselves.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: Anarchokapitalismus není nic než sociální inženýrství; a to je třeba jednoznačně odmítnout, neboť jde o pěkné svinstvo.
title: Anarcho-capitalism is nothing but social engineering; and this must be unequivocally rejected, because it is a nice piece of crap.
text: Social engineering is typically used to manipulate people in order to benefit someone in particular by making the manipulated masses do what that person wants, which is most often to submit, let themselves be ruled by them, pay money for something they would not want to pay for without this manipulation, or change their behavior for the supposed "benefit of the whole" or "the welfare of society".

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: Anarchokapitalismus není nic než sociální inženýrství; a to je třeba jednoznačně odmítnout, neboť jde o pěkné svinstvo.
title: Anarcho-capitalism is nothing but social engineering; and this must be unequivocally rejected, because it is a nice piece of crap.
text: Anarcho-capitalism is the exact opposite; people will not be ruled by anyone, they will be free and take responsibility for themselves. The so-called "benefit of society" is the sum of the benefits of all its members, which, however, is best ensured by each individual, because only he knows best what he actually wants. There is no need for anyone to rule such a society and whom the supposed social engineering should serve.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: Anarchokapitalismus není nic než sociální inženýrství; a to je třeba jednoznačně odmítnout, neboť jde o pěkné svinstvo.
title: Anarcho-capitalism is nothing but social engineering; and this must be unequivocally rejected, because it is a nice piece of crap.
text: The term "social engineering" can have many different meanings, and it cannot be ruled out that for some, anarcho-capitalist theories also fall under this term; however, if this is the case, it must consistently include practically any proposal to change our social order, so in principle it probably cannot be anything bad.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: Anarchokapitalismus je sice krásná teorie, ale to byl ostatně komunismus také; v realitě by nefungovalo ani jedno.
title: Anarcho-capitalism is a beautiful theory, but so was communism; in reality neither would work.
text: First of all, it must be said that communism is definitely not a good theory, because it is entirely based on the teachings of Karl Marx, who was based on Ricardo's cost theory of value, which was refuted by Carl Menger as early as 1870, when he came up with the subjective theory of value; that this fact was ignored by those who were still trying to build bright tomorrows a hundred years later does not make communism a good theory.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: Anarchokapitalismus je sice krásná teorie, ale to byl ostatně komunismus také; v realitě by nefungovalo ani jedno.
title: Anarcho-capitalism is a beautiful theory, but so was communism; in reality neither would work.
text: Communism is no example of a system that works well in theory but is unworkable in practice; the theory of Communism was debunked long before a group of ignoramuses tried to put it into practice. Anarcho-capitalism has not yet been refuted on a theoretical level; yes, it can happen, however, until it does, we should treat it as an unproven theory and not compare it to communism.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: Anarchokapitalismus je sice krásná teorie, ale to byl ostatně komunismus také; v realitě by nefungovalo ani jedno.
title: Anarcho-capitalism is a beautiful theory, but so was communism; in reality neither would work.
text: Although anarchist societies have existed throughout history, they have been stable and successful; an example can be medieval Iceland, but also the USA at the time of colonization or medieval Ireland (in the latter case, there are doubts as to whether it was really anarchy; some call the given state anarchy, others claim that it was a large number of mini-states in a small area).

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: Anarchokapitalismus je sice krásná teorie, ale to byl ostatně komunismus také; v realitě by nefungovalo ani jedno.
title: Anarcho-capitalism is a beautiful theory, but so was communism; in reality neither would work.
text: One can understandably object that it was a long time ago and today there is no modern functioning anarchy; this is true, but it does not invalidate the anarcho-capitalist theory in any way and does not put it on the level of the refuted communist theory (communism has always failed in practice, anarchy does not exist in modern society, but we do not know of any case of its failure; historically, on the contrary, it worked).

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: Tradice států sahá tisíce let do minulosti; kdyby byl anarchokapitalismus lepší uspořádání společnosti, někde by už existoval; evoluce však jasně ukazuje nadřazenost státu nad anarchií.
title: The tradition of states goes back thousands of years; if anarcho-capitalism were a better order of society, it would already exist somewhere; however, evolution clearly shows the superiority of the state over anarchy.
text: It is only a few hundred years since the same could be said of slavery; slave societies had a tradition at least as long as states, they existed absolutely everywhere, slavery was quite common and nobody questioned it. And not only that! No one could even imagine a society in which there were no masters and slaves; slavery seemed to be a completely natural and unchangeable part of the world.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: Tradice států sahá tisíce let do minulosti; kdyby byl anarchokapitalismus lepší uspořádání společnosti, někde by už existoval; evoluce však jasně ukazuje nadřazenost státu nad anarchií.
title: The tradition of states goes back thousands of years; if anarcho-capitalism were a better order of society, it would already exist somewhere; however, evolution clearly shows the superiority of the state over anarchy.
text: Everyone knew that "a negro can't take care of himself without a master"; just like today, it is clear that "man cannot take care of himself without the state". It was also (or is) obvious that we also need slavery (or the state) from an economic point of view, because otherwise it wouldn't work. Also, if slavery was so bad, how could it be so widespread? After all, there would be societies without slaves.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: Tradice států sahá tisíce let do minulosti; kdyby byl anarchokapitalismus lepší uspořádání společnosti, někde by už existoval; evoluce však jasně ukazuje nadřazenost státu nad anarchií.
title: The tradition of states goes back thousands of years; if anarcho-capitalism were a better order of society, it would already exist somewhere; however, evolution clearly shows the superiority of the state over anarchy.
text: And when someone then compared the violence of a master to a slave to the same violence to a free man, it was completely absurd, and everyone knew at once that it could not be compared, since it was something completely different; just as everyone knows today that comparing taxes to protection money does not make sense, because they are completely different. Just read some texts from that time; similar arguments seriously failed.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: Tradice států sahá tisíce let do minulosti; kdyby byl anarchokapitalismus lepší uspořádání společnosti, někde by už existoval; evoluce však jasně ukazuje nadřazenost státu nad anarchií.
title: The tradition of states goes back thousands of years; if anarcho-capitalism were a better order of society, it would already exist somewhere; however, evolution clearly shows the superiority of the state over anarchy.
text: What came next? It only took a few hundred years for the institution of slavery, with a tradition dating back thousands of years, to fall in almost all countries of the world. In the beginning, however, someone had to stand up, start talking about it, be ridiculed and considered a dreamer building castles in the air that have no connection with reality; yet he persevered, spread the idea, didn't give up and inspired others... Until finally freedom won.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: Anarchokapitalistické teorie předpokládají, že se k sobě budou lidé chovat hezky, případně alespoň vždy logicky; takoví ale lidé nejsou, pomíjíte skutečné lidské vlastnosti.
title: Anarcho-capitalist theories assume that people will treat each other nicely, or at least always logically; but people aren't like that, you're missing out on real human qualities.
text: I have encountered the objection that anarcho-capitalist theories attribute to people different qualities than they actually have countless times; but no one has ever been able to list for me which specific properties they are, and to show in any of my texts (or the texts of anarcho-capitalist authors to which I refer) where I assume some unrealistic properties or neglect real ones.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: Anarchokapitalistické teorie předpokládají, že se k sobě budou lidé chovat hezky, případně alespoň vždy logicky; takoví ale lidé nejsou, pomíjíte skutečné lidské vlastnosti.
title: Anarcho-capitalist theories assume that people will treat each other nicely, or at least always logically; but people aren't like that, you're missing out on real human qualities.
text: Sometimes someone objects that I do not account for human selfishness, but he is unable to show me exactly where; no wonder, as few things are further from the truth. After all, the free market and its functioning are largely based on the selfishness and greed of entrepreneurs who try to make money by providing people with services they are interested in.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: Anarchokapitalistické teorie předpokládají, že se k sobě budou lidé chovat hezky, případně alespoň vždy logicky; takoví ale lidé nejsou, pomíjíte skutečné lidské vlastnosti.
title: Anarcho-capitalist theories assume that people will treat each other nicely, or at least always logically; but people aren't like that, you're missing out on real human qualities.
text: Sometimes one can also meet with the objection that people do not always behave so logically that it fits into the usual economic theories about perfect competition and the like. Of course they don't breed! After all, this was one of the great objections of Ludwig von Mises and the entire Austrian school of economics, on which anarcho-capitalism is built, against mainstream economics, which rejects anarcho-capitalism.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Polemika
section: Anarchokapitalistické teorie předpokládají, že se k sobě budou lidé chovat hezky, případně alespoň vždy logicky; takoví ale lidé nejsou, pomíjíte skutečné lidské vlastnosti.
title: Anarcho-capitalist theories assume that people will treat each other nicely, or at least always logically; but people aren't like that, you're missing out on real human qualities.
text: So before you condemn anarcho-capitalist theories on the basis that they "do not take into account real people", please try to answer for yourself the question of whether such a thing actually happens, or which specific theses are based on such assumptions; if you really find such a specific place in anarcho-capitalist theories, I would be very happy if you let me know.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Přirozené právo
section: Lidé někdy vraždí, loupí, nerespektují vlastnictví a iniciují násilí; dokud bude princip neagrese porušován, anarchokapitalismus nemůže nikdy fungovat.
title: People sometimes murder, rob, disrespect property, and initiate violence; as long as the principle of non-aggression is violated, anarcho-capitalism can never work.
text: It is true that anarcho-capitalism is based on respect for property rights, but it does not require their 100% observance always and everywhere; it is understandable that there will always be people who do not respect the property of others, but if there are not too many such people, anarcho-capitalism will not significantly disrupt this (and if there are so many, then no state will save them either).

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Přirozené právo
section: Lidé někdy vraždí, loupí, nerespektují vlastnictví a iniciují násilí; dokud bude princip neagrese porušován, anarchokapitalismus nemůže nikdy fungovat.
title: People sometimes murder, rob, disrespect property, and initiate violence; as long as the principle of non-aggression is violated, anarcho-capitalism can never work.
text: Although, for example, democracy is based on the fact that every citizen meeting certain criteria (typically age) has the right to participate in elections, even if someone accidentally denies someone this right (for example, locks them in a cellar and does not let them out), the elections will not be repeated because of this, and this system will still be called a democracy; nor will anarcho-capitalism disappear through a single violation of the principle of non-aggression.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Přirozené právo
section: Lidé někdy vraždí, loupí, nerespektují vlastnictví a iniciují násilí; dokud bude princip neagrese porušován, anarchokapitalismus nemůže nikdy fungovat.
title: People sometimes murder, rob, disrespect property, and initiate violence; as long as the principle of non-aggression is violated, anarcho-capitalism can never work.
text: Anarcho-capitalists do not assume that people will turn into saints out of nowhere and will observe the principle of non-aggression out of love for their neighbor, but rather that the function of protection against criminal elements will not be performed by the state, but by private companies (and as you know, private companies typically provide their services better than the state) and by the people themselves (whom the state will no longer prevent from arming).

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Přirozené právo
section: Lidé někdy vraždí, loupí, nerespektují vlastnictví a iniciují násilí; dokud bude princip neagrese porušován, anarchokapitalismus nemůže nikdy fungovat.
title: People sometimes murder, rob, disrespect property, and initiate violence; as long as the principle of non-aggression is violated, anarcho-capitalism can never work.
text: A society in which property rights are respected is, on the whole, a better place for most of its members to live than a society in which the principle of non-aggression is not respected, which is related to the fact that, in the long run, trade is typically more beneficial to most people than war, which is expensive; countries go to war so much, among other things, because those who declare and conduct wars do not pay for them from their own money.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Přirozené právo
section: Anarchisté jsou násilníci a touží po krvavé revoluci!
title: Anarchists are violent and want a bloody revolution!
text: Some do; however, there are many anarchist schools. Some of them indeed preach violent revolution, but by no means all; anarcho-pacifists, for example, reject any violence (including defensive violence). Anarcho-capitalists allow violence only to remedy a situation where someone's property rights are being violated. So, from their point of view, is it legitimate to use violence against the state and plan a revolution?

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Přirozené právo
section: Anarchisté jsou násilníci a touží po krvavé revoluci!
title: Anarchists are violent and want a bloody revolution!
text: Although defense against an aggressor is undoubtedly permissible, and states represent the greatest aggressors of today, it is certainly not legitimate to take an action that will make the situation worse as a result and in addition harm a lot of innocent people; and I claim that violent revolution is exactly such an action. Even if I were to ignore the ethical side of the matter, I will not support a violent revolution; for it cannot lead to success.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Přirozené právo
section: Anarchisté jsou násilníci a touží po krvavé revoluci!
title: Anarchists are violent and want a bloody revolution!
text: People can be forced to do anything; however, freedom cannot be imposed on them by force. Let us imagine that I should succeed in taking power and abolishing the state against the will of the people; what then? Either I will give them liberty, which they will immediately dispose of by forming a new state; or I will forbid it to them, which will make me a state myself (because I will limit their freedom by force). Either way, the result will be the state, not anarcho-capitalism.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Přirozené právo
section: Anarchisté jsou násilníci a touží po krvavé revoluci!
title: Anarchists are violent and want a bloody revolution!
text: What is the solution to this situation? The only way is to convince people that they don't need the state. When that happens, there will be no need for a violent revolution, because they can then peacefully vote democratically to abolish the state; however, as long as the states will, the revolution is completely meaningless for the reasons described above. So don't worry about anarcho-capitalists, we are not thugs; we fight with words, not with Molotov cocktails.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Přirozené právo
section: Anarchokapitalisté úplně ignorují lidská práva a nic krom vlastnictví jim není svaté; tento přístup je naprosto nepřijatelný a nelidský.
title: Anarcho-capitalists completely ignore human rights, and nothing but property is sacred to them; this approach is completely unacceptable and inhumane.
text: Although it is true that anarcho-capitalism is built on private property and the principle of non-aggression, it is not quite true that anarcho-capitalists ignore human rights, they only derive them from property rights; the huge advantage of human rights defined in this way is that they do not contradict each other, they do not go against each other and there is no dispute about what is still a human right and what is not.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Přirozené právo
section: Anarchokapitalisté úplně ignorují lidská práva a nic krom vlastnictví jim není svaté; tento přístup je naprosto nepřijatelný a nelidský.
title: Anarcho-capitalists completely ignore human rights, and nothing but property is sacred to them; this approach is completely unacceptable and inhumane.
text: So how are human rights described by property rights? So, for example, the right to life follows from the fact that when someone kills someone, they violate the victim's property rights to their body; freedom of speech is ensured in such a way that everyone can say what they want on their land (or with the consent of the owner of another's land); it is the same with freedom of religion, education and the like.

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Přirozené právo
section: Anarchokapitalisté úplně ignorují lidská práva a nic krom vlastnictví jim není svaté; tento přístup je naprosto nepřijatelný a nelidský.
title: Anarcho-capitalists completely ignore human rights, and nothing but property is sacred to them; this approach is completely unacceptable and inhumane.
text: Property rights do not ensure human rights exactly in the form in which they are written, for example, in the inconsistent Charter of Fundamental Rights and Freedoms, because all rights that can be derived from property rights are negative rights, not positive; one can assert negative rights even without initiating violence against someone else (positive rights cannot; therefore LZPS is inconsistent).

chapter: AMEN: analýza mnohých etatistických námitek › Přirozené právo
section: Anarchokapitalisté úplně ignorují lidská práva a nic krom vlastnictví jim není svaté; tento přístup je naprosto nepřijatelný a nelidský.
title: Anarcho-capitalists completely ignore human rights, and nothing but property is sacred to them; this approach is completely unacceptable and inhumane.
text: Examples of negative and positive rights: the negative right to education means that no one can stop me from getting an education; a positive right to education means that someone will be forced to provide me with an education; the negative right to housing means that no one can forbid me to have a home; a positive right to housing means that someone must provide housing for me. Only negative rights result from property rights.

title: Preface
text: Thirteen years after writing more than twenty texts that eventually resulted in the book Anarchocapitalism, in which I describe a free free market stateless society, I again felt the need to write a book. On its pages, I deal with the reasons why we do not live in such a society today, but above all, I propose - first a theoretical, then a practical - way how we could get closer to freedom. First, I identify how we lose our freedom (which typically occurs from childhood); then I derive the consequent logical effects on our civilization. Finally, I return to the individual again and present concrete practices of how we can liberate ourselves in the everyday of our lives.

title: Preface
text: I would like to appeal primarily to the reader for whom freedom is at least a somewhat important value; although it is not absolutely necessary that it be the alpha and omega of his life, I am speaking primarily to the one to whom it is not completely indifferent. For those who do not think about freedom or do not feel that they need it for something specific, I would rather refer to the book Anarchocapitalism. In it, I explain why a free, unregulated society is, among other things, significantly more effective in meeting the needs of those who live in it.

title: Preface
text: Today, many politicians flaunt freedom in their election campaigns. We read about it on billboards, hear about it on TV and on the Internet, and even make up parts of the names of political parties. For many of those who use the word, however, it is nothing more than a cheap way to appeal to voters; also as a result of this emptying of the concept of freedom, there is a centralization of society and an increase in the number of regulations and legal norms that aim to govern practically all aspects of our lives. How to get out of this legislative jungle?

title: Preface
text: Even if we were to admit that social change is not yet in sight, there are a number of concrete steps towards freedom that anyone who cares about can take today - despite external restrictions. Furthermore, I am deeply convinced that any attempt to change society by social engineering "from above" is most likely to fail, just like any central planning. Changes "from below", that is, in the everyday lives of individuals, are therefore the only functional tools for achieving freedom anyway. Want to know more about them? I want to share them with you on the following pages.

title: 1. Freedom
text: Freedom is my lifelong theme; I've been researching it since I was a kid. I looked for it in democracy, various (centralized) utopias, enlightened monarchies (with simple legislation and draconian punishments) and in a small state, until about twenty years ago the desire for knowledge led me to study anarchism (primarily anarcho-capitalism). I strongly rejected it at first, until my search for arguments against it led me to (reluctantly at first) accept it. Thanks to this, I also discovered the first comprehensive definition of freedom that made sense to me: A person is free precisely when no one violates his negative rights. These are equivalent to property rights, primarily to the body (self-ownership), but also to all physical property. The so-called principle of non-aggression is based on respect for property; the latter consists in not initiating violence (not even in the sense of threatening such actions), and therefore in using physical force exclusively for defense. These are different ways to describe what we can simply express with the words: Live and let live.

title: 1. Freedom
text: The preceding paragraph discusses the freedom of the individual from oppression caused by other people. However, the more intensively I dealt with this issue, the less I found this - however fundamental and valid - concept to be sufficient, since it does not deal with the demons within ourselves. Is a drug addicted, unhappy, broken and hateful person free just because no one initiates violence towards them? In a sense, yes; however, despite the absence of external limitations, he may not have the determination to realize his purpose in life (whatever it may be). On the other hand, there are stories of people from gulags or concentration camps that were not broken even by sadistic jailers, with whom these prisoners could even sympathize. These and similar examples led me to the need to distinguish between external freedom (that is, the absence of the oppression of aggressors, which I wrote about above) and internal freedom (that is, the willingness and determination to do what really makes sense to a person).

title: 1. Freedom
text: In the beginnings of my research, although I perceived and felt inner freedom, I could not describe it more precisely; it was only after several years that I was able to formulate a satisfactory definition: Inner freedom means the absence of fear or the ability to work with fear when it is present. It is therefore not a binary quantity, but a scale - the degree of our fear (or inability to manage it) corresponds to the degree of our inner lack of freedom.

title: 1. Freedom
text: This concept is based on the belief that, ultimately, it is fear – whether of failure, pain, loss, the darkness within ourselves, or anything else – that holds us back from doing what we find meaningful and fulfilling. Although at first glance it may seem that there are other reasons, I believe that in the end, fear is always hidden behind them - for example, of material hardship, what others will think of us or ourselves, that something will not work out for us, how it will harm us or our loved ones, and so on. Those who are not afraid have no reason not to try to do something that fulfills them and gives them meaning. Even behind what may initially appear to be, for example, laziness, upon closer examination we find precisely fear (perhaps from discomfort). Since many people question this principle, I spent a lot of time analyzing the examples they used to try to disprove it; despite this, I am not aware of any (even hypothetical) situation in which some form of fear is not behind the causes of someone's resignation to fulfilling the meaning of life.

title: 1. Freedom
text: An attentive reader may have noticed that I am talking about the determination, willingness or effort to do something in connection with internal freedom, or rather the absence of aggression in the case of external freedom, while I am not at all concerned with the results of a free person's actions. Because I consider it important to distinguish between the freedom to act and the real possibility of achieving something in the real world. These states are commonly confused; for example, "What good is the freedom to travel if I don't have the money anyway?" The author of such a sentence may feel unfree because he does not have the means to fulfill his needs; however, I believe that confusing (lack of) freedom with (lack of) options or resources is rather unfortunate - we could then come to rather absurd conclusions such as that we are not free if we do not have a time machine, a teleporter, a dragon or a date with our idol.

title: 1. Freedom
text: We rarely hear someone say that they are not free because they can't do magic (or at least make beautiful music). More often we can hear someone complaining that their freedom is limited by a lack of (typically financial) resources. Why? Because we tend to constantly compare ourselves to others: Many people feel unfree when they cannot afford even a cheap holiday at home, while their neighbors travel around the world; At the same time, almost no one considers the fact that they do not have a spacecraft capable of interstellar flights as a detriment to their freedom, since no one (yet) owns one. However, if everyone had ships capable of intergalactic travel, they would easily begin to see even interstellar as insufficient. If someone finds the previous sentence hard to believe, they can try to compare the availability and quality of owner-occupied housing for young families today and a hundred (or several hundred) years ago; nevertheless, today's (albeit better) state is found to be completely intolerable by society as a whole.

title: 1. Freedom
text: If we want to understand freedom universally, we cannot derive it from where the grass is greener, whose neighbor's goat died - or, more generally, from the technological level of civilization and our socio-economic position in it. In other words, it doesn't make sense that the same abilities, resources, and opportunities make us free in a poor society (where we have, say, the only car) while unfree in a rich one (where we own the same car, but everyone else already has private helicopters); for that would mean that we lose our freedom just because others get rich, even if they otherwise did nothing to us and did not limit us in anything.

title: 1. Freedom
text: Similar examples can be used to illustrate the difference between real unfreedom and the feeling of unfreedom; it can also stem from the fact that we do not have the opportunity to fulfill our needs, even if we are free at the given moment. Even if we desperately want something that everyone around us has and we just lack it, we need not therefore be unfree; and it does not give us any claim to the property of others. People sometimes call for a "dignified life" and basically mean that they want to have similar opportunities and resources as those they compare themselves to; at the same time, they forget that the feeling of dignity comes from ourselves and from our inner set-up. Why should exactly the same conditions (for life, housing or anything else) be "decent" at one moment, but perhaps in a hundred(s) years from now only because the standard of living of other people has increased? At the same time, it does not have to be only about material goods; I would like to illustrate this with an example from my own life to show that I stand by my words, even when the going gets tough.

title: 1. Freedom
text: Some time ago, after a serious accident with twenty-five broken bones, I was confined to bed for several months, then to a wheelchair, and still sometimes need crutches; I will probably never get rid of the pain and I won't be able to walk or even run normally. I think I might see the situation as a restriction of freedom if I hadn't spent so much time studying it in the past. Since I had fortunately already experienced that my external freedom can only be violated by others, while the internal one can only be violated by my own attitude, I was able to feel free even with a broken spine, unable to even drink or defecate without help. This not only helped me in the given situation (my regeneration far exceeded all expectations thanks to my approach stemming from inner freedom), but above all in practice it confirmed the theoretical starting points that I present in this book.

title: 1. Freedom
text: But what if we long to fulfill our dreams, but lack the means to do so? I am convinced that if we are internally free, i.e. we are not held back by fear (for example of failure), and we have determination, we can always do our best to obtain those resources. This may not be successful, but if we act with the sincere belief that this is truly our path, we fulfill our life's mission. Of course, we have the possibility at any time to decide to go a different way, to start fulfilling completely different needs or goals; and even if we are not aware of them, we can start working precisely to reveal them. It means it's never too late to start - we can always do our best for what makes sense to us (even if we don't even know it at the time).

title: 1. Freedom
text: However, sometimes life is so difficult that our strength may not be enough. Then it can be tempting to reach for a shortcut, the abundance of which has unfortunately been normalized by the states. Where our willingness or determination to face fear is lacking, the paternalistic state comes in, like the devil in a moment of weakness, offering us a "solution" - tempting and easy; with one catch - someone else (but ultimately ourselves) will pay for it, and that's the price of freedom. We often hear people calling for freedom where they feel confident and on solid ground: Those who can make money usually ask for economic freedom; good shooters or drivers often reject restrictions on guns or automobile traffic. On the contrary, blanket regulations are typically demanded by those who do not feel strong about something: Former or quit smokers formed one of the strongest voices for a ban on smoking in Czech pubs; the poor keep demanding legislation to redistribute the rich's money and such.

title: 1. Freedom
text: We could observe the combination of both phenomena (the demand for legislative restrictions and freedom) a few years ago in the public debate about the regulation of social networks: Before Elon Musk bought Twitter, a lot of conservatives called for state intervention in the then progressive-tuned platforms; those of us who opposed that the market would solve the situation, then those in question sharply attacked - until the market really solved it - so that the same conservatives would then start rejecting the same state interventions, because the tables were turned and, among other things, because of the X network, the Republican candidate became the president of the USA.

title: 1. Freedom
text: I perceive a great difference between the principled advocates of universal freedom for everyone and the people who call for it only when it suits them as a means to achieve a certain (their) end. And although I wish it from the bottom of my heart to absolutely everyone, I fear that those who are willing to sacrifice (especially other people's) freedom for the promise of fulfilling their needs will eventually lose it (even for themselves) to a much greater extent than they expected; and they may not even be aware of it. Why is that so? And how to defend against it? Before we answer these questions, let's look at when and how we start to lose our freedom...

title: 2. Education
text: For millions of years of the evolution of the human species, children naturally learned everything necessary for life from their parents and other members of the pack, later also of larger societies; a few centuries ago, however, a drastic change took place - the mass expansion of education. Today, we could divide a person's life in terms of learning into three stages: The first years after birth, he decides more or less on his own what he learns (typically he acquires speech, walking and other skills when he sees fit); then comes the turning point in the form of starting school (not to mention the fact that the current Czech legislation also imposes a mandatory year of kindergarten) - it is shaped in the critical years of adolescence at the discretion of teachers, respectively politicians and officials of the Ministry of Education; after finishing school, he returns to what he has been doing since birth - he decides for himself what he needs to know, be familiar with, or be able to do (including when and how he will learn).

title: 2. Education
text: Full autonomy in deciding the time, content, methods or intensity of learning (self) - so-called self-directed education - is of fundamental importance for every person. Thanks to self-management, he/she not only acquires new knowledge and skills, but above all becomes aware of responsibility for his/her education, and therefore also his/her entire life. This happens regardless of the method (and even the intention) of learning, which is ongoing. Although we cannot explain what and why we learn, and we do not even call our actions learning, it occurs (thanks to the neuroplasticity of the brain) in every moment of our waking lives (and probably even in our sleep). The more autonomous we are in this process, the stronger we strengthen our awareness of responsibility for our lives in addition to developing specific abilities; at the same time, we may not be able to describe such a thing or be aware of it at all, yet it inevitably happens - because we constantly bear the consequences of our decisions, and the less external influences enter into them (for example, orders and prohibitions from parents or teachers), the more clearly we perceive this principle.

title: 2. Education
text: As parents or teachers, thanks to life experiences, we sometimes know ways of learning that can be (at least for us) more effective than those we observe in "our" children; then of course we can share our experience with them, if they are interested. However, the problem arises when we start to elevate these experiences and methods (albeit time-tested) above the approach of others (perhaps much younger) and force them to learn as we see fit. Coercion tends to have negative effects on interpersonal relationships, however, if the given experience is suitably transferable to another person, it can help them to acquire a certain skill more effectively or faster. However, in no case can we avoid the fact that by limiting the autonomy of the person in question, we always delay at least a little from realizing the responsibility for our life.
